meaning: ~ is ~
structure: Noun + は + Noun / い-Adj / な-Adj + です

examples.japanese: 私は学生です。
examples.english: I am a student.

examples.japanese: これは本です。
examples.english: This is a book.

examples.japanese: 彼女は親切です。
examples.english: She is kind.

notes: は (wa) marks the topic of the sentence. です is the polite copula. Negate with ではありません or じゃないです.

meaning: There is / There are
structure: Place + に + Thing/Person + が + あります (inanimate) / います (animate)

examples.japanese: テーブルの上に本があります。
examples.english: There is a book on the table.

examples.japanese: 公園に子供がいます。
examples.english: There are children in the park.

examples.japanese: 冷蔵庫にジュースがありますか。
examples.english: Is there juice in the fridge?

notes: Use あります for non-living things (objects, plants, buildings) and います for living things (people, animals).

meaning: Please do ~
structure: Verb[て] + ください

examples.japanese: ここに名前を書いてください。
examples.english: Please write your name here.

examples.japanese: もう一度言ってください。
examples.english: Please say it one more time.

examples.japanese: 静かにしてください。
examples.english: Please be quiet.

notes: A polite request. For closer relationships or children, dropping ください makes it more casual: 書いて。

meaning: Please don't do ~
structure: Verb[ない] + でください

examples.japanese: 写真を撮らないでください。
examples.english: Please don't take photos.

examples.japanese: ここで食べないでください。
examples.english: Please don't eat here.

examples.japanese: 心配しないでください。
examples.english: Please don't worry.

notes: The negative counterpart of 〜てください. Used for polite prohibitions or reassurances.

meaning: Let's ~ / Shall we ~
structure: Verb[stem] + ましょう / ましょうか

examples.japanese: 一緒に行きましょう。
examples.english: Let's go together.

examples.japanese: 休みましょうか。
examples.english: Shall we take a break?

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強しましょう。
examples.english: Let's study Japanese.

notes: ましょう proposes an action. ましょうか is a softer suggestion or offer to do something for someone.

meaning: Want to do ~
structure: Verb[stem] + たい

examples.japanese: 日本に行きたいです。
examples.english: I want to go to Japan.

examples.japanese: 寿司が食べたい。
examples.english: I want to eat sushi.

examples.japanese: もっと休みたいです。
examples.english: I want to rest more.

notes: Expresses the speaker's desire. For a third person's desire, use 〜たがっている. The object can be marked with を or が.

meaning: Is doing ~ / Has done ~ (resultant state)
structure: Verb[て] + います

examples.japanese: 今、勉強しています。
examples.english: I am studying right now.

examples.japanese: 彼は結婚しています。
examples.english: He is married.

examples.japanese: 雨が降っています。
examples.english: It is raining.

notes: With action verbs, expresses ongoing action (progressive). With change-of-state verbs (結婚する, 死ぬ), expresses the resulting state.

meaning: From ~ / Because ~
structure: [Time/Place] + から (from) / [Sentence] + から (because)

examples.japanese: 9時から授業があります。
examples.english: Class starts from 9 o'clock.

examples.japanese: 東京から来ました。
examples.english: I came from Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 眠いから、寝ます。
examples.english: I'm sleepy, so I'll sleep.

notes: Two separate uses: marking start point (time/place) or giving a reason. As a reason marker it follows plain-form verbs.

meaning: Until ~ / Up to ~
structure: [Time/Place] + まで

examples.japanese: 5時まで働きます。
examples.english: I work until 5 o'clock.

examples.japanese: 駅まで歩きました。
examples.english: I walked to the station.

examples.japanese: いつまで日本にいますか。
examples.english: Until when are you in Japan?

notes: Often paired with から: 〜から〜まで (from … to …). まで marks the end point in time or space.

meaning: Have ever done ~
structure: Verb[た] + ことがある

examples.japanese: 富士山に登ったことがあります。
examples.english: I have climbed Mt. Fuji.

examples.japanese: 刺身を食べたことがありますか。
examples.english: Have you ever eaten sashimi?

examples.japanese: 一度も外国に行ったことがない。
examples.english: I have never been abroad.

notes: Expresses past experience. The negative is 〜たことがない / ありません.

meaning: Do things like ~ and ~
structure: Verb[た] + り + Verb[た] + り + する

examples.japanese: 週末は映画を見たり、本を読んだりします。
examples.english: On weekends I do things like watch movies and read books.

examples.japanese: 泣いたり笑ったりした。
examples.english: I laughed and cried.

examples.japanese: 天気がよくなったり悪くなったりしている。
examples.english: The weather keeps getting better and worse.

notes: Used to give a non-exhaustive list of representative actions. At least two verbs are typically listed, and the pattern ends with する.

meaning: Probably ~ / Right?
structure: Plain form + でしょう

examples.japanese: 明日は雨でしょう。
examples.english: It will probably rain tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼は来ないでしょう。
examples.english: He probably won't come.

examples.japanese: 知っているでしょう？
examples.english: You know, right?

notes: Expresses the speaker's conjecture. With a rising intonation it seeks confirmation. The casual equivalent is だろう.

meaning: I think that ~
structure: [Plain form sentence] + と思います

examples.japanese: 彼は来ないと思います。
examples.english: I think he won't come.

examples.japanese: これは難しいと思います。
examples.english: I think this is difficult.

examples.japanese: 日本語は面白いと思います。
examples.english: I think Japanese is interesting.

notes: と is the quotation particle. The verb before と must be in plain form. 〜と思っています implies an ongoing belief.

pattern: 〜が好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手
meaning: Like / Dislike / Good at / Bad at
structure: Noun + が + 好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手 + です

examples.japanese: 私は音楽が好きです。
examples.english: I like music.

examples.japanese: 彼は運転が上手です。
examples.english: He is good at driving.

examples.japanese: 私は料理が下手です。
examples.english: I am bad at cooking.

notes: These な-adjectives take が, not を, for their objects. 大好き (love) and 大嫌い (hate) are intensified versions.

meaning: ~ too / ~ also / Even ~
structure: Noun + も

examples.japanese: 私も日本語を勉強しています。
examples.english: I am also studying Japanese.

examples.japanese: コーヒーもお茶も飲みます。
examples.english: I drink both coffee and tea.

examples.japanese: 子供でもできます。
examples.english: Even a child can do it.

notes: Replaces は, が, or を to add the meaning 'also/too'. When repeated with two items (AもBも), it means 'both A and B'.

meaning: topic marker
structure: present + い | present negative + くないくありません | past + かった | past negative + くなかったくありませんでした

meaning: out of this group, [A] is best
structure: [A] + が/は + いちばん | いちばん + [A]

examples.japanese: 彼がいちばん働いた。
examples.english: He worked the hardest.

examples.japanese: 秋が一番好きな季節です。
examples.english: Fall is my favorite season.

examples.japanese: 私はブロッコリーが一番嫌いだ。
examples.english: I hate broccoli the most.

examples.japanese: 午前中が一番調子がいい。
examples.english: I feel best in the morning.

examples.japanese: 一番前に座っている人は誰ですか？
examples.english: Who is that sitting in the very front?

examples.japanese: 一番早く予約できる日はいつですか？
examples.english: When is the earliest day we can make a reservation?

meaning: together with; at the same time as; as well as ~
structure: often preceded with と

examples.japanese: 一緒に日本語を勉強しましょう。
examples.english: Let's study Japanese together.

examples.japanese: 今夜、カラオケに一緒に行こう。
examples.english: Let's go to karaoke together tonight.

examples.japanese: ずっと彼と一緒にいたい。
examples.english: I want to be together with him forever.

examples.japanese: 明日の朝、一緒にジムに行きませんか？
examples.english: Do you want to go to the gym together tomorrow morning?

examples.japanese: 今朝、友だちと一緒に図書館に行きました。
examples.english: I went to the library together with my friend this morning.

examples.japanese: うちの犬と一緒に散歩するのが好きです。
examples.english: I like walking together with my family's dog.

meaning: ongoing action or current state
structure: Can be used mid-sentence and also to start a new sentence

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも元気ですね。
examples.english: He is always energetic.

examples.japanese: 妹はいつも寝ている。
examples.english: My younger sister is always sleeping.

examples.japanese: いつも夜10時に寝ます。
examples.english: I always go to bed at 10 o'clock.

examples.japanese: 昼ご飯はいつも納豆を食べます。
examples.english: I always have natto (fermented soybeans) for lunch.

examples.japanese: 仕事に行く前にいつもジムに行きます。
examples.english: I always go to the gym before going to work.

examples.japanese: いつも自転車で学校に来ますが今日は歩きました。
examples.english: I always go to school by bike, but today I walked.

meaning: right?; isn't it?
structure: presentnegative + casualじゃないではないpoliteじゃありませんではありません | pastnegative + casualじゃなかったではなかったpoliteじゃありませんでしたではありませんでした

examples.japanese: あなたは一人じゃない。
examples.english: You are not alone.

examples.japanese: 危険じゃないの？
examples.english: Isn't it dangerous?

examples.japanese: そんなつもりじゃなかった。
examples.english: That wasn't my plan/intention.

examples.japanese: ごめんなさい！わざとではありませんでした。
examples.english: I'm so sorry! It wasn't intentional.

examples.japanese: 肉はあまり好きじゃないです。
examples.english: I don't really like meat.

examples.japanese: 若いころはやさいが好きじゃなかった。
examples.english: I didn't like vegetables when I was younger.

meaning: or
structure: end of sentence + か

examples.japanese: 何ですか？
examples.english: What?

examples.japanese: すみません、あなたも学生ですか。
examples.english: Excuse me, are you also a student?

examples.japanese: あなたの名前は何ですか。
examples.english: What is your name?

examples.japanese: 元気ですか。
examples.english: How are you?

examples.japanese: 彼は何才ですか。
examples.english: How old is he?

examples.japanese: 大丈夫ですか？
examples.english: Are you alright?

meaning: after doing ~
structure: meaning 1: because; since | Verb + から | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective + い | meaning 2: from; since | Noun + から

examples.japanese: 天気がいいから、外に行きたい。
examples.english: Since the weather is nice, I want to go outside.

examples.japanese: 私はすぐ戻るから、ここでちょっと待ってください。
examples.english: I'll return shortly, so please wait here just a moment.

examples.japanese: これからもよろしくお願いします。
examples.english: From now on, let's have a good relationship (I'll be counting on you).

examples.japanese: ここからあの駅まで歩いてどれぐらいかかりますか？
examples.english: How long does it take to walk from here to that station?

examples.japanese: お店は何時から何時まで開いていますか？
examples.english: What are the shop's opening hours?

meaning: had better; it'd be better to; should ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 方かた

examples.japanese: パソコンの使いかたがわかりません。
examples.english: I don't know how to use a computer.

examples.japanese: ケーキの作り方を知っていますか？
examples.english: Do you know how to make a cake?

examples.japanese: おはしの使い方が上手ですね。
examples.english: You're very good at using chopsticks (you will be told this all the time in Japan)

examples.japanese: あの先生の教え方はとてもわかりやすいです。
examples.english: That teacher's way of teaching is very easy to understand

examples.japanese: 彼の生き方は、かっこいいです。
examples.english: His way of living is really cool.

examples.japanese: この漢字の読み方を教えてください。
examples.english: Please teach me how to read this kanji character.

meaning: but; however; although ~
structure: Use between 2 contradicting ideas

examples.japanese: 仕事は辛いけど楽しい。
examples.english: Work is tough, but fun.

examples.japanese: 金はないけど夢はある。
examples.english: I don't have money, but I have dreams.

examples.japanese: スポーツは上手じゃないけど、好きです。
examples.english: I'm not good at sports, but I like them.

examples.japanese: 悪いけど、明日のパーティーに行けません。
examples.english: Sorry, but I can't make it to tomorrow's party.

examples.japanese: 眠いけど、まだ宿題があるから寝られません。
examples.english: I'm sleepy, but I still have homework to do so I can't go to sleep yet.

examples.japanese: たくさん勉強したけど、テストの点はよくなかったです。
examples.english: Although I studied a lot, my test score wasn't very good.

meaning: but; however; although ~
structure: Use between 2 contradicting ideas

examples.japanese: 外はさむいけれど、家の中は暖かいです。
examples.english: It’s cold outside, but inside the house it is warm.

examples.japanese: 彼は若いけれども経験がある。
examples.english: Although he is young he has experience.

examples.japanese: 眠いけれど、まだ宿題があるから寝られません。
examples.english: I'm sleepy but still have homework to do so I can't go to bed yet.

examples.japanese: このカメラは高かったけれど、すぐ壊れてしまいました。
examples.english: This camera was really expensive, but it broke right away.

examples.japanese: 雪が降っているけれども、スーパーに行きます。
examples.english: Although it is snowing outside, I'm going to the grocery store.

examples.japanese: お金はあまり持っていません。けれども、毎日幸せです。
examples.english: I don't have much money. But I am happy every day.

meaning: have not yet ~
structure: まだ + Verb (ている)Verb (ていない) | Noun

examples.japanese: まだですか？
examples.english: Is it ready yet? / are we there yet? / Still...?

examples.japanese: まだまだ暑いだ。
examples.english: It's still hot out. (mada can be used twice in a row for extra emphasis)

examples.japanese: 先生はまだ来ていない。
examples.english: Our teacher still hasn't come.

examples.japanese: もう10時ですが弟がまだ寝ている。
examples.english: It's already 10 am, but my younger brother is still sleeping.

examples.japanese: まだ1時間もあるよ。
examples.english: We still have one hour.

examples.japanese: あきらめるのはまだ早い！
examples.english: It's still too early to give up!

meaning: still; not yet
structure: まだ + Verb (てない) *spokenVerb (ていない)Verb (ていません)

examples.japanese: バスはまだ来ていません。
examples.english: The bus still hasn't come.

examples.japanese: まだ、決まっていません。
examples.english: It hasn't been decided yet.

examples.japanese: 私はまだ朝ごはんを食べていません。
examples.english: I still haven't eaten breakfast yet.

examples.japanese: 今週の新しい単語をまだ覚えていません。
examples.english: I still haven't memorized this week's new vocabulary.

examples.japanese: 父はまだ帰ってきていない。
examples.english: My father still hasn't come home yet.

examples.japanese: まだ宿題をやっていない。
examples.english: I haven't done my homework yet.

meaning: by; by the time; indicates time limit
structure: Noun + まで

examples.japanese: 昨日までお休みでした。
examples.english: I was on vacation until yesterday.

examples.japanese: ここからそこまでは遠いですよ。
examples.english: That's really far from here!

examples.japanese: 駅まで行きたいんですが、どう行ったらいいですか。
examples.english: How can I get to the station?

examples.japanese: 最後までがんばってね！
examples.english: Do your best all the way until the end!

examples.japanese: 家まで車で送ります。
examples.english: I'll take you home by car.

examples.japanese: 朝から夜までずっとかんじを勉強しました。
examples.english: I studied kanji all day from morning until night.

meaning: shall I ~; used to offer help to the listener
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + ましょう

examples.japanese: 行きましょう！
examples.english: Let's go!

examples.japanese: 駅で会いましょう！
examples.english: Let's meet at the station!

examples.japanese: もうご飯の時間だよ、早く食べましょう！
examples.english: It's already dinner time, let's hurry up and eat!

examples.japanese: 帰る前に教室をきれいにしましょう。
examples.english: Before we go home, let's clean up the classroom.

examples.japanese: 一緒に日本語を勉強しましょう！
examples.english: Let's study Japanese together!

examples.japanese: もう暗くなったから、帰りましょう。
examples.english: It's gotten dark already, so let's head home.

meaning: I think; it seems; probably; right?
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + ましょうか

examples.japanese: マドを開けましょうか。
examples.english: Shall I open the window?

examples.japanese: 手伝いましょうか。
examples.english: Do you want some help?

examples.japanese: 荷物を持ちましょうか。
examples.english: Shall I help carry your luggage?

examples.japanese: タクシーを呼びましょうか。
examples.english: Shall I call a taxi for you?

examples.japanese: 私がお皿を洗いましょうか？
examples.english: Shall I wash the dishes?

examples.japanese: 写真を取りましょうか。
examples.english: Shall I take a picture for you?

meaning: still; not yet
structure: See examples below

examples.japanese: もう昼ご飯の時間だ。早く食べましょう！
examples.english: It's lunch time already, let's hurry up and eat.

examples.japanese: 宿題はもう終わった？
examples.english: Did you already finish your homework?

examples.japanese: ビールもう一杯ください！
examples.english: One more beer please!

examples.japanese: 飲み物は全部飲みました。もうありません。
examples.english: We drank all of the drinks. There aren't any left.

examples.japanese: もう少し待ってください。
examples.english: Please wait a little while longer.

examples.japanese: コーヒーはもう飲まないことにしました。
examples.english: I've decided to not drink coffee anymore.

meaning: change noun into na-adjective or adverb
structure: present + な / だ | present negative + じゃないではない | past + だったでした | past negative + じゃなかったではありませんでした

meaning: isn't it? right? eh?
structure: end of sentence + な(あ)

examples.japanese: たくさんの人がいるなあ。
examples.english: Wow, there's a lot of people here.

examples.japanese: これ、美味しいなあ。
examples.english: This is really delicious.

examples.japanese: 暑くなってきたなあ。
examples.english: It's starting to get hotter.

examples.japanese: それは本当かな。
examples.english: I wonder if that's true...

examples.japanese: 明日は晴れるかなあ。
examples.english: I wonder if the weather will clear up tomorrow...

examples.japanese: トイレはどこかな。
examples.english: I wonder where the restroom is...

meaning: please don't do ~
structure: Verb-A (ない form) + で + Verb-B

examples.japanese: コーヒーには、いつもさとうを入れないで飲みます。
examples.english: I always drink coffee without putting any sugar in it.

examples.japanese: 彼女はカサを持たないで出てしまった。
examples.english: She left without bringing an umbrella.

examples.japanese: 昨日は疲れていて、電気を消さないで寝てしまった。
examples.english: Yesterday I was so tired I fell asleep without turning off the lights.

examples.japanese: 今朝、朝ごはんを食べないで仕事に来ました。
examples.english: I came to work today without eating any breakfast.

examples.japanese: 昨日、お風呂に入らないで寝てしまった。
examples.english: I went to bed yesterday without taking a bath/shower.

examples.japanese: 明日は試験なので、今夜は寝ないで勉強します。
examples.english: Tomorrow is test day, so I'm gonna stay up all night and study without sleep.

meaning: please give me ~
structure: Verb (ない form) + で + ください

examples.japanese: 泣かないでください。
examples.english: Please don't cry.

examples.japanese: このパソコンを使わないでください。
examples.english: Please don't use this computer.

examples.japanese: 明日の予定を忘れないでください。
examples.english: Don't forget about our plans tomorrow!

examples.japanese: 私のことを心配しないでください。
examples.english: Please don't worry about me.

examples.japanese: 道の邪魔をしないでください。
examples.english: Please don't block the street.

examples.japanese: 事務所で食べないでください。
examples.english: Please don't eat in the office.

meaning: must do; need to do
structure: Verb (ない form) + と + いけないいけませんダメです

examples.japanese: そろそろ寝ないといけない。
examples.english: I have to sleep soon.

examples.japanese: 私は家に帰らないといけない。
examples.english: I have to go home.

examples.japanese: 今から勉強をしないといけない。
examples.english: I have to study now.

examples.japanese: 明日から働かないといけない。
examples.english: I have to work from tomorrow.

examples.japanese: この薬を飲まないといけませんか。
examples.english: Do I have to take this medicine?

examples.japanese: 私は今から仕事を始めないといけません。
examples.english: I must start my work now.

meaning: is OK to ~; is alright to ~; may I ~?
structure: Verb (ない form) ない + くてもいい

examples.japanese: 明日は休みだから、学校に行かなくてもいい。
examples.english: Tomorrow is a day off, so I don't need to go to school.

examples.japanese: 空港まで来なくてもいいよ。
examples.english: You don't have to come all the way to the airport.

examples.japanese: 好きじゃないなら、食べなくてもいいですよ。
examples.english: If you don't like it, you don't need to eat it.

examples.japanese: 来なくてもいいですよ。私一人で行くから。
examples.english: You don't need to come. I'll go by myself.

examples.japanese: 無理しなくてもいいですよ。
examples.english: You don't need to push yourself too hard.

examples.japanese: 明日は授業がないから大学に行かなくてもいいです。
examples.english: I have no classes tomorrow so I don't need to go to university (campus).

meaning: must do; need to do
structure: Verb (ない form) ない + くちゃくちゃダメくちゃいけないくちゃいけませんくちゃならないくちゃなりません

examples.japanese: 行かなくちゃ。
examples.english: I gotta go.

examples.japanese: もう寝なくちゃ。
examples.english: I have to go to bed already.

examples.japanese: 新しい車を買わなくちゃね。
examples.english: You need to buy a new car..

structure: Verb (dictionary form) + のが上手のがじょうず

examples.japanese: 今日試験があるから、遅刻してはいけない。
examples.english: There's a test today, so you can't be late.

examples.japanese: 室内でタバコを吸ってはいけませんよ。
examples.english: No smoking inside!

meaning: but; however; though ~
structure: Verb (て form) + もいい（です） | Noun + で | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: トイレに行ってもいいですか？
examples.english: May I go to the restroom?

examples.japanese: うん、行ってもいいですよ！
examples.english: Sure, go a head!

examples.japanese: 明日でもいいですか？
examples.english: Is tomorrow OK?

examples.japanese: どっちの日でもいいですよ。
examples.english: Either day would be all right with me.

examples.japanese: それを食べてもいいですか。
examples.english: Can I eat that?

examples.japanese: 私も一緒に行っていい？
examples.english: Can I go with you?

meaning: and; or; connecting particle
structure: phrase + と

examples.japanese: お母さんと買い物に行った。
examples.english: I went shopping with my mom.

examples.japanese: 彼女と仲がいいです。
examples.english: She and I get along well.

examples.japanese: あなたと話したくない。
examples.english: I don't want to talk to you.

examples.japanese: これとそれは違います。
examples.english: This and that are different.

examples.japanese: 彼はベトナム人と結婚している。
examples.english: He's married to a Vietnamese person.

examples.japanese: 犬と遊ぶのが大好きです。
examples.english: I love playing with dogs.

meaning: always; usually; habitually
structure: Verb (casual form) + とき | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: 分からないときは、早く先生に聞きましょうね。
examples.english: Whenever you don't understand, hurry up and ask the teacher.

examples.japanese: 道を渡るとき、車に気をつけてください。
examples.english: When crossing the street, be careful with the cars.

examples.japanese: 時間がないときは、朝ごはんを食べません。
examples.english: When I have no time, I don't eat breakfast.

examples.japanese: 体の調子が悪いとき、温かいお茶を飲みます。
examples.english: When I'm not feeling well, I drink warm tea.

examples.japanese: 眠いとき、いつもチョコレートを食べます。
examples.english: I always eat chocolate whenever I'm feeling sleepy.

examples.japanese: 図書館で本を借りる時、カードがいります。
examples.english: When you borrow a book from the library, you need a card.

meaning: too much
structure: とても + Adjective / Verb

examples.japanese: 今日はとても暑いですね。
examples.english: Today is very hot, isn't it?

examples.japanese: 1月と２月はとても寒いです。
examples.english: January and February are very cold.

examples.japanese: このカレーはとても辛いですね。
examples.english: This curry is very spicy!

examples.japanese: 彼らはとても似ている。
examples.english: They look very alike.

examples.japanese: 両親のことをとても愛している。
examples.english: I really love my parents.

examples.japanese: 昨日見た映画はとても面白かった。
examples.english: The movie I watched yesterday was very interesting.

meaning: plan to, intend to
structure: Verb (dictionary form)Verb (ない form) + つもりだつもりです | つもりはないつもりはありません

examples.japanese: 今日はラーメンを食べるつもりだ。
examples.english: Today, I plan to eat ramen.

examples.japanese: あなたたちも行くつもりですか？
examples.english: Are you guys also planning to go?

examples.japanese: 大学に入って日本語を勉強するつもりです。
examples.english: I plan on studying Japanese once I enter university

examples.japanese: 何度聞かれても、あなたに教えるつもりはありません。
examples.english: No matter how many times you ask, I have no plans to tell you.

examples.japanese: いつ日本に留学するつもりなの？
examples.english: When do you plan on studying abroad in Japan?

examples.japanese: ばれたら、どうするつもり？
examples.english: What are you planning to do if you get caught?

meaning: destination particle; in; at; on; to
structure: See below

examples.japanese: 私はジョンです。
examples.english: "I" am John.

examples.japanese: それは面白い。
examples.english: "That" is interesting.

examples.japanese: 今日は電車で来ました。
examples.english: "Today" I came by train.

examples.japanese: 金曜日は空いていますか？
examples.english: How about "Friday", are you free?

examples.japanese: 運動をするのは嫌です。
examples.english: I hate "exercising".

examples.japanese: 好きな食べ物は何ですか？
examples.english: What kind of "food" do you like?

meaning: [2] is more than [1]
structure: Noun-1 + は + Noun-2 + より + Adj +です

examples.japanese: 本は映画より面白いです。
examples.english: Books are more interesting than movies.

examples.japanese: 今日は昨日より忙しいです。
examples.english: Today is busier than yesterday.

examples.japanese: 電車はバスより速いです。
examples.english: Trains are faster than buses.

examples.japanese: アメリカ人は日本人より背が高いです。
examples.english: Americans are taller than Japanese.

examples.japanese: 北海道は台湾より大きいです。
examples.english: Hokkaido is bigger than Taiwan.

examples.japanese: エベレスト山は富士山より高いです。
examples.english: Mt. Everest is taller than Mt. Fuji

meaning: why; for what reason; how
structure: Noun + はどうですか

examples.japanese: 明日はどうですか。
examples.english: How about tomorrow?

examples.japanese: 日本はどうですか？
examples.english: How do you like Japan?

examples.japanese: 天気はどうですか。
examples.english: How is the weather?

examples.japanese: 買い物に行くのはどうですか。
examples.english: What do you say to going shopping?

examples.japanese: 日本語の勉強はどうですか。
examples.english: How are your Japanese studies going?

examples.japanese: 私の日本語の発音はどうですか？
examples.english: How is my Japanese pronunciation?

meaning: and; with; as; connecting particle
structure: Noun + や + Noun

examples.japanese: 毎朝、パンやベーコンなどを食べています。
examples.english: Every morning I eat bread and bacon and so on.

examples.japanese: スーパーで肉や野菜を買いました。
examples.english: I bought some meat and vegetables (and so on) from the supermarket.

examples.japanese: あなたのおすすめの音楽や本を私に教えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me your recommended music or books.

examples.japanese: 電車やバスでの旅は好きです。
examples.english: I like traveling by train and bus (and so on).

examples.japanese: 私はアメリカやイギリスのテレビドラマを見るのが好きです。
examples.english: I like watching American and British dramas (among others).

examples.japanese: 冬休みは家族で長野や北海道へ行きます。
examples.english: During winter vacation my family often goes to places like Nagano or Hokkaido.

meaning: isn't it? right? eh?
structure: end of sentence + よ

examples.japanese: 行くよ。
examples.english: Let's go!

examples.japanese: ちょっと、待ってよ！
examples.english: Wait a second!

examples.japanese: 元気を出せよ。
examples.english: Cheer up.

examples.japanese: 愛しているよ。
examples.english: I love you!

examples.japanese: 頑張るよ。
examples.english: I'll do my best!

examples.japanese: 寝る時間ですよ。
examples.english: It's time for bed.

meaning: had better; it'd be better to; should ~
structure: Verb-1 + より + Verb-2 + ほうが ~ | Noun-1 + Noun-2 + の | な-adj-1 + な-adj-2 +な | い-adj-1 + い-adj-2

examples.japanese: 私は猫より、犬のほうが好きです。
examples.english: I like dogs more than cats.

examples.japanese: 昨日より今日の方が暑いです。
examples.english: It's hotter today than it was yesterday.

examples.japanese: 彼女より、君の方がきれいだよ。
examples.english: You're more beautiful than she is.

examples.japanese: 日本語を読むより、話す方が上手だ。
examples.english: I'm better at speaking Japanese than I am at reading it.

examples.japanese: 遅く寝るより、早く寝た方がいいですよ。
examples.english: Going to bed earlier is better than going to bed late.

examples.japanese: 台湾より、北海道の方が大きいです。
examples.english: Hokkaido is bigger than Taiwan.

meaning: In order to ~ / For the purpose of ~
structure: Verb[dict] / Noun + の + ために

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強するために、毎日練習しています。
examples.english: I practice every day in order to study Japanese.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、野菜を食べています。
examples.english: I eat vegetables for my health.

examples.japanese: 試験に合格するために、頑張ります。
examples.english: I will work hard in order to pass the exam.

notes: Expresses purpose or goal. Do not confuse with 〜から (reason/cause). The subject of both clauses is usually the same.

meaning: While doing ~ / At the same time as ~
structure: Verb[stem] + ながら

examples.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
examples.english: I study while listening to music.

examples.japanese: 歩きながら電話をしないでください。
examples.english: Please don't talk on the phone while walking.

examples.japanese: 笑いながら話した。
examples.english: She spoke while laughing.

notes: Both actions are done simultaneously by the same subject. The main action comes after ながら. The secondary (background) action is expressed by the ながら clause.

meaning: Try doing ~
structure: Verb[て] + みる

examples.japanese: この料理を食べてみてください。
examples.english: Please try eating this dish.

examples.japanese: 新しいカフェに行ってみた。
examples.english: I tried going to the new café.

examples.japanese: 日本語で話してみます。
examples.english: I'll try speaking in Japanese.

notes: みる comes from 見る (to see), but here means 'to try and see'. Implies attempting something with some uncertainty about the outcome.

meaning: End up doing ~ / Do completely (with regret or finality)
structure: Verb[て] + しまう

examples.japanese: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I ended up forgetting my homework.

examples.japanese: ケーキを全部食べてしまった。
examples.english: I ate all the cake.

examples.japanese: 財布をなくしてしまった。
examples.english: I went and lost my wallet.

notes: Two nuances: (1) regret or unintended result, (2) completion of an action. The contracted forms てしまう → ちゃう and でしまう → じゃう are common in casual speech.

meaning: Do in advance / Do and leave it that way
structure: Verb[て] + おく

examples.japanese: 会議の前に資料を準備しておきます。
examples.english: I'll prepare the materials in advance of the meeting.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けておいてください。
examples.english: Please leave the door open.

examples.japanese: メモしておいた方がいいよ。
examples.english: You should write it down (for future reference).

notes: Implies doing something in preparation or leaving something in a ready state. The contracted form ておく → とく is common in casual speech.

pattern: 〜てあげる / くれる / もらう
meaning: Giving and receiving verbs
structure: Verb[て] + あげる / くれる / もらう

examples.japanese: 友達に本を貸してあげた。
examples.english: I lent a book to my friend (as a favor).

examples.japanese: 先生が説明してくれた。
examples.english: The teacher explained it to me (as a favor).

examples.japanese: 母に料理を作ってもらった。
examples.english: I had my mother cook for me.

notes: あげる = speaker gives to someone; くれる = someone gives to the speaker's in-group; もらう = speaker receives. These verbs encode the direction and social relationship of a favor.

meaning: If ~ / As long as ~ (conditional)
structure: Verb[ば-form] / い-Adj[ければ] / な-Adj[なら] / Noun[なら]

examples.japanese: 早く起きれば、間に合う。
examples.english: If you wake up early, you'll make it in time.

examples.japanese: 安ければ、買います。
examples.english: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.japanese: 雨が降らなければ、出かけます。
examples.english: If it doesn't rain, I'll go out.

notes: Expresses a hypothetical condition. Often used for general truths or advice. The result clause usually expresses the speaker's will, desire, or a natural consequence.

meaning: If ~ / When ~ (conditional)
structure: Verb[た] + ら / い-Adj[かった] + ら / な-Adj/Noun + だったら

examples.japanese: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
examples.english: When you arrive at the station, please call me.

examples.japanese: お金があったら、旅行したい。
examples.english: If I had money, I'd want to travel.

examples.japanese: 試験が終わったら、遊ぼう。
examples.english: Once the exam is over, let's hang out.

notes: Very versatile: can express 'when' (sequential events) or 'if' (hypothetical). The event in the main clause happens after or as a result of the たら clause.

meaning: Might ~ / Maybe ~
structure: Plain form (Verb / Adj / Noun+かも) + しれない

examples.japanese: 明日は雨が降るかもしれない。
examples.english: It might rain tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼女は知っているかもしれません。
examples.english: She might know.

examples.japanese: もう遅すぎるかもしれない。
examples.english: It might already be too late.

notes: Expresses possibility or uncertainty. Weaker than でしょう (probably). The polite form is かもしれません.

meaning: Should be ~ / Expected to be ~
structure: Plain form + はずだ / はずです

examples.japanese: 彼はもう来るはずです。
examples.english: He should be arriving soon.

examples.japanese: この薬は効くはずだ。
examples.english: This medicine should work.

examples.japanese: そんなはずはない。
examples.english: That can't be right.

notes: Based on logical expectation or prior knowledge. 〜はずがない / はずはない means 'there's no way that ~' (strong denial).

meaning: Looks like ~ / Seems like ~ (based on observation)
structure: Verb[stem] / い-Adj[stem] / な-Adj[stem] + そうだ

examples.japanese: 雨が降りそうだ。
examples.english: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.japanese: このケーキはおいしそうです。
examples.english: This cake looks delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼は疲れそうだ。
examples.english: He looks tired.

notes: Based on direct visual evidence. Do not confuse with 〜そうだ (hearsay), which follows plain form and means 'I heard that ~'.

meaning: Too ~ / Excessively ~
structure: Verb[stem] / い-Adj[stem] / な-Adj[stem] + すぎる

examples.japanese: 食べすぎて、気分が悪い。
examples.english: I ate too much and feel sick.

examples.japanese: この荷物は重すぎます。
examples.english: This luggage is too heavy.

examples.japanese: 彼は真面目すぎる。
examples.english: He is too serious.

notes: The resulting noun is 〜すぎ (e.g., 食べすぎ = overeating). Often carries a negative nuance.

meaning: Apparently ~ / I hear that ~ / Typical of ~
structure: Plain form + らしい (hearsay) / Noun + らしい (typical of)

examples.japanese: 彼は転職するらしい。
examples.english: Apparently he's changing jobs.

examples.japanese: 彼女らしい答えだ。
examples.english: That's a very her kind of answer.

examples.japanese: 男らしい人が好きです。
examples.english: I like a manly man.

notes: Two uses: (1) hearsay — based on indirect evidence or information; (2) 'typical of / befitting'. Compare with 〜ようだ (direct observation) and 〜そうだ (visual appearance).

meaning: It is that ~ / (explanation/emphasis)
structure: Plain form + んです / のです

examples.japanese: どうして遅刻したんですか。
examples.english: Why is it that you were late?

examples.japanese: 実は、体調が悪いんです。
examples.english: The truth is, I'm not feeling well.

examples.japanese: これは日本語なんです。
examples.english: This is (in fact) Japanese.

notes: Adds explanatory nuance — providing or seeking an explanation. Very common in conversation. の is the nominalizer; ん is its contracted spoken form.

meaning: Make an effort to ~ / Try to make sure ~
structure: Verb[dict / ない] + ようにする

examples.japanese: 毎日運動するようにしています。
examples.english: I make an effort to exercise every day.

examples.japanese: 遅刻しないようにしてください。
examples.english: Please make sure not to be late.

examples.japanese: 野菜を食べるようにしている。
examples.english: I'm trying to make a habit of eating vegetables.

notes: Describes a conscious ongoing effort to do or not do something. Compare with 〜ようになる (a change has come about naturally).

meaning: Can ~ / Be able to ~
structure: Verb[dict] + ことができる

examples.japanese: 日本語を話すことができます。
examples.english: I can speak Japanese.

examples.japanese: ここで写真を撮ることができますか。
examples.english: Can I take photos here?

examples.japanese: 彼女は自転車に乗ることができない。
examples.english: She cannot ride a bicycle.

notes: More formal than the potential verb form (e.g., 話せる). Interchangeable in most contexts.

meaning: Had better ~ / It is better to ~
structure: Verb[た] + ほうがいい / Verb[ない] + ほうがいい

examples.japanese: 早く寝たほうがいいですよ。
examples.english: You had better go to sleep soon.

examples.japanese: 甘いものを食べないほうがいい。
examples.english: You had better not eat sweets.

examples.japanese: 医者に行ったほうがいいと思います。
examples.english: I think you had better see a doctor.

notes: Gives advice or recommendation. Positive advice uses た-form; negative advice uses ない-form. Blunter than 〜てください.

meaning: Called ~ / Named ~ / Known as ~
structure: Noun + という + Noun / [Quote] + という

examples.japanese: 「鬼滅の刃」というアニメを知っていますか。
examples.english: Do you know an anime called 'Demon Slayer'?

examples.japanese: 東京という都市は大きい。
examples.english: The city called Tokyo is big.

examples.japanese: 彼は来ないということを聞いた。
examples.english: I heard that he won't be coming.

notes: Used to introduce or identify by name. Also used as a quotation linker (というのは = 'the thing called', というわけで = 'so that's why').

meaning: it must be; it should be (expectation)
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + はずがないはずがありません | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: そんなはずがない。
examples.english: That can't be true.

examples.japanese: 彼女の話は本当のはずがない。
examples.english: Her story can't be true.

examples.japanese: 彼はそんなことを言うはずがない。
examples.english: He would never say such a thing.

examples.japanese: ジョンが嘘をついているはずがない。
examples.english: There's no way that John is lying.

examples.japanese: そんな大きな量を全部食べられるはずがない。
examples.english: There's no way you're going to be able to eat all of that.

examples.japanese: そのうわさが本当のはずがない。
examples.english: That rumor cannot be true.

meaning: need; necessary
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 必要がある必要がない

examples.japanese: 彼らは休む必要がある。
examples.english: They need to rest.

examples.japanese: もっと勉強する必要がある。
examples.english: I need to study more.

examples.japanese: 私の弟は今日学校に行く必要がない。
examples.english: My younger brother doesn't need to go to school today.

examples.japanese: 俺にはもう必要がない。
examples.english: I have no need for this anymore.

examples.japanese: 何でそんなことをする必要があるんですか？
examples.english: Why is it necessary to do that?

examples.japanese: 医者は彼にタバコをやめる必要があると言った。
examples.english: The doctor told him that he needs to quit smoking.

meaning: let's ~; shall we ~
structure: see conjugation rules below...

examples.japanese: 今日から自転車で出勤しよう。
examples.english: Let's start commuting by bicycle from today!

examples.japanese: もう11時だ。早く寝よう。
examples.english: It's already 11pm, let's hurry and go to sleep.

examples.japanese: 重たそうだね。手伝おうか。
examples.english: That looks heavy, shall I give you a hand?

examples.japanese: 今日は食堂で昼食を食べよう。
examples.english: Let's eat lunch at the dining room today.

examples.japanese: 図書館で一緒に勉強しよう。
examples.english: Let's study together at the library.

examples.japanese: 明日は週末ですから、飲みに行こう。
examples.english: Tomorrow is the end of the week, so let's go out for some drinks.

meaning: to be, to exist (the polite form of いる/ある)
structure: いる (changes to)来る (changes to)行く (changes to) + いらっしゃる | Verb (て form) + + いらっしゃる

examples.japanese: 質問のある方はいらっしゃいませんか。
examples.english: Does anyone have any questions?

examples.japanese: 校長先生は図書館にいらっしゃいます。
examples.english: The headmaster is in the library.

examples.japanese: 私たちと一緒にいらっしゃいませんか？
examples.english: Wouldn't you like to come with us?

examples.japanese: 先生、何時まで学校にいらっしゃいますか。
examples.english: Teacher, until what time will you remain at school?

examples.japanese: 先生はあなたを信じていらっしゃる。
examples.english: Our teacher believes in you.

examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーにいらっしゃいますか。
examples.english: Will you go to the party tomorrow?

meaning: to decide on
structure: する (changes to) + いたす | します (changes to) + いたします | お/ご + Verb ます (stem) + いたします

examples.japanese: 失礼いたします。
examples.english: Excuse me.

examples.japanese: この仕事は私がいたします。
examples.english: I will do this job.

examples.japanese: お席にご案内いたします。
examples.english: I’ll take you to your seat.

examples.japanese: 新幹線の予約は私がいたします。
examples.english: I’ll book the shinkansen bullet train tickets.

examples.japanese: 荷物は私が明日にお届けいたします。
examples.english: I’ll send the luggage tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 必要な教材のリストを同封いたします。
examples.english: Please find enclosed a list of all necessary teaching equipment.

meaning: to not be (am not; is not; are not)
structure: phrase + じゃないか

examples.japanese: 行こうじゃないか。
examples.english: Let's go, shall we?

examples.japanese: ダメじゃないか。
examples.english: You should know that's no good / you can't do that.

examples.japanese: だから言ったじゃないか！
examples.english: I told you so! (didn't I?)

examples.japanese: 今夜外食しようじゃないか。
examples.english: Let's go out for dinner tonight, shall we?

examples.japanese: 今日は元気そうじゃないか。
examples.english: Well aren't you looking quite energetic today?

examples.japanese: お祝いに一杯やろうじゃないか。
examples.english: Let's have a drink in celebration (shall we?)

meaning: aside from; apart from; except for; whether or not ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + かどうか | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.english: I don't know if the weather will be clear or not tomorrow.

examples.english: I'm not sure if that is correct or not.

examples.english: We won't know if it's good or not until we eat it.

examples.english: Please check again whether or not you wrote the name.

examples.english: I'm worried whether or not we'll be able to succeed with this plan.

structure: phrase + かしら

examples.english: I wonder if he is serious.

examples.english: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

examples.english: I wonder if this book will sell.

structure: Verb (casual form) + かな | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.english: I wonder if she's doing well.

examples.japanese: 雨が降るかな。
examples.english: I wonder if it's going to rain.

examples.japanese: 外は寒いかな。
examples.english: I wonder if it's cold outside.

examples.japanese: もう食べていいかな。
examples.english: I wonder if it's OK to start eating.

examples.japanese: 一緒に映画を見るのはどうかな？
examples.english: What do you think about going to see a movie together?

examples.japanese: ここに座ってもいいかな？
examples.english: Do you mind if I sit here?

structure: Noun + から + 作る作られる (passive form)作られている | Noun + で

examples.english: Wine is made from grapes.

examples.english: Paper is made from wood.

examples.english: Sake (Japanese alcohol) is made from rice.

examples.japanese: このつくえは木で作られています。
examples.english: This desk was made from wood.

examples.english: Can you make cheese from milk?

examples.japanese: この橋は石から作られている。
examples.english: This bridge was made from stones.

structure: きっと + eventaction

examples.english: You studied really hard, so I'm sure tomorrow's test will be fine!

examples.english: It will most likely be sunny tomorrow.

examples.english: He's my best friend, so I'm positive he will help me.

structure: Noun (time) + ごろ (around; about) | Verb (casual) + ころ (when) | Noun + の | Adjective

examples.english: Can you come by my place around eight p.m.?

examples.english: Did you ever experience bullying when you were a child?

examples.japanese: 夕食は何時ごろになさいますか？
examples.english: Around what time will you be expecting dinner?

meaning: It has been decided that..; it turns out that..
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + こと

examples.english: I like to read books.

examples.japanese: 私は料理を作ることが下手です。
examples.english: I am bad at cooking food.

examples.japanese: 私はゲームをすることが大好きです。
examples.english: I love playing games.

examples.english: There are many things that we think about.

examples.english: My hobby is cooking.

examples.japanese: 毎日ウォーキングをすることにしている。
examples.english: I go walking every day.

meaning: there are times when
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことができることができないことができますことができません

examples.english: I can speak Japanese.

examples.english: She can sing.

examples.japanese: このナイフはどんなものでも切ることができるよ。
examples.english: This knife can cut through anything.

examples.english: I'm not able to tell a lie.

examples.japanese: 私は日本語を学ぶことができない。
examples.english: I can't learn Japanese.

structure: Verb (dictionary form)Verb (ない form) + ことになる

examples.english: The entrance ceremony will be held on April 1st.

examples.japanese: どうしてそれを学ぶことになったの？

examples.english: I've decided to go to Okinawa over summer break with my friends.

structure: い-adjective い + くするくしますくして

examples.english: Make it better with music.

examples.english: I'll buy it if you make it 500 yen cheaper.

examples.english: She raised her voice.

examples.english: This room is a bit hot so I'll turn on the air conditioning to make it cooler.

examples.japanese: 運動をして、体を強くしましょう。
examples.english: Let's workout and make our bodies stronger.

structure: 急に + Phrase

examples.english: It suddenly got a bit cooler today.

meaning: until; as far as; to (an extent); even ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + までに | Noun

examples.japanese: 彼は夕食のことなどすっかり忘れた。

examples.japanese: なぜわざわざわたしに警告なんかなさるの？

examples.japanese: 私があなたのメールに気がついたのが昨日でした。
examples.english: Yesterday was when I noticed your email.

structure: Verb (て form) + 見えるみえる | Verb (casual, non-past) + ように | Noun +（のよう）に | な-adjective + に | い-adjective + いく

examples.japanese: 同じに見える。
examples.english: They look the same.

examples.japanese: 彼はアメリカ人に見える。
examples.english: He looks like he is American.

examples.japanese: 彼女は先生にみえる。
examples.english: She looks like a teacher.

examples.japanese: その人はとてもお金持ちにみえる。
examples.english: That person appears to be very rich.

examples.japanese: 寝てないように見える。
examples.english: You look like you didn't sleep much.

examples.japanese: 彼女は結婚してからとても幸せそうに見える。
examples.english: Since getting married, she seems very happy.

meaning: to make something ~
structure: な-adjective な + にするにしますにしてにした

examples.japanese: もう少し、静かにしてください。
examples.english: Please be a bit more quiet.

examples.japanese: この写真を大切にする。
examples.english: I will treasure this picture.

examples.japanese: 歯医者は私の歯をきれいにした。
examples.english: The dentist cleaned my teeth.

examples.japanese: 先生は、テストをもっと簡単にしました。
examples.english: The teacher made the test easier.

examples.japanese: この絵は彼女を有名にするでしょう。
examples.english: This picture will probably make her famous.

examples.japanese: 最近元気にしていますか？
examples.english: Are you doing well lately?

meaning: difficult to do ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + にくい

examples.japanese: この質問には答えにくいです。
examples.english: This question is difficult to answer.

examples.japanese: この本は字が小さくて読みにくいです。
examples.english: This books print is too small, it's difficult to read.

examples.japanese: この漢字は覚えにくいです。
examples.english: This kanji is difficult to remember.

examples.japanese: この自転車は古くて乗りにくいです。
examples.english: This bicycle is old and difficult to ride.

examples.japanese: 魚は骨が多くて食べにくいだ。
examples.english: Fish have a bunch of bones and are difficult to eat.

examples.japanese: 彼の説明が難しくて分かりにくいだった。
examples.english: His explanation was complicated and difficult to understand.

meaning: out of this group, [A] is best
structure: Noun + の中で

examples.japanese: 心の中ではこれを分かっていた。
examples.english: I know this in my heart.

examples.japanese: 病院の中で、待ちますか。
examples.english: Will you wait inside the hospital?

examples.japanese: 私は今日は車の中で寝ました。
examples.english: I slept in my car today.

examples.japanese: 私は頭の中でも日本語で考える。
examples.english: I even think in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 私は季節の中で秋が好きです。
examples.english: Out of all the seasons, I like autumn.

examples.japanese: あなたはまだ夢の中でしょう。
examples.english: You're probably still dreaming.

meaning: although; despite the fact that; even though ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + のに | Noun + な | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: まだ20時なのに、とても眠い。
examples.english: I'm really tired even though it's still only 8PM.

examples.japanese: なぜ、彼らは冬なのに泳ぐのでしょうか？
examples.english: Why will they swim even though it's winter?

examples.japanese: 約束をしたのに、彼女は来ませんでした。
examples.english: Even though she promised, she didn't come..

examples.japanese: 今日は日曜日なのに、働かなければなりません。
examples.english: I have to work today even though it is Sunday..

examples.japanese: 彼女がきれいなのに彼氏がいません。
examples.english: Although she is very beautiful, she doesn't have a boyfriend.

examples.japanese: この携帯は高いのに、すぐに壊れた。
examples.english: Even though this cell phone was really expensive, it broke right away.

meaning: hence; for that reason; because of ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + のに

examples.japanese: 始めるのに遅すぎることはない。
examples.english: It's never too late to start.

examples.japanese: 家に帰るのに3時間かかりました。
examples.english: It took 3 hours to return home.

examples.japanese: 本を読むのに時間がかかる。
examples.english: Reading books takes time.

examples.japanese: 勉強するのに、それが必要だ。
examples.english: I need it to study.

examples.japanese: 考えるのにも疲れたし。
examples.english: I am tired of thinking.

examples.japanese: その仕事をするのにどのくらいの時間が必要ですか。
examples.english: Around how much time do you need to do that job?

meaning: hence; for that reason; because of ~
structure: Verb (casual) + のは + ～だ～です | Noun + な | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 毎日、新しい単語を覚えるのは大変です。
examples.english: It is difficult to memorize new vocabulary every day.

examples.japanese: 私たちは結婚を決めたのは子どもができたからです。
examples.english: We decided to get married because we were going to have a baby.

examples.japanese: 私が生まれたのは北海道の小さな村です。
examples.english: I was born in a small village in Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: このメンバーの中に独身なのは田中さんだけです。
examples.english: From these members, the only one who is single is Tanaka.

examples.japanese: 会議が始まるのは10時です。忘れないようにメモしたほうがいいよ。
examples.english: The meeting begins at 10 o'clock. It would be best to write a memo so you don't forget.

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強するとき、一番難しいのは漢字だ。
examples.english: When studying Japanese, the most difficult part is kanji.

meaning: please do; could you please…; I ask of you to ~
structure: お + Verb ます (stem form) + ください | お/ご + Noun (action)

examples.japanese: ここでお待ちください。
examples.english: Please wait here.

examples.japanese: ここにお名前をお書きください。
examples.english: Please write your name here.

examples.japanese: それを水と一緒にお飲みください。
examples.english: Take that together with water.

examples.japanese: あちらからお入りください。
examples.english: Please enter from over there.

examples.japanese: このボールペンをお使いください。
examples.english: Please use this ball pen.

examples.japanese: どうぞお座りください。
examples.english: Please be seated.

meaning: please do ~ (honorific)
structure: お + Verb ます (stem form) + になるになります | お/ご + Noun

examples.japanese: 何をお飲みになりますか。
examples.english: What would you like to have to drink?

examples.japanese: お座りになりませんか。
examples.english: Do you want to sit down?

examples.japanese: 先生は何時ごろお戻りになりますか?
examples.english: Teacher, around what time will you return?

examples.japanese: 何をお食べになるのですか。
examples.english: What will you have to eat?

examples.japanese: どうか、ぜひお入りになってください。
examples.english: Do come in, please.

examples.japanese: 部長はたばこをお吸いになりません。
examples.english: Our manager does not smoke.

meaning: when; at this time
structure: Noun (measurable) + おきに

examples.japanese: 電車は5分おきに走っています。
examples.english: The trains run every five minutes.

examples.japanese: このバスは15分おきに出ている
examples.english: This bus leaves every 15 minutes.

examples.japanese: 彼は数日おきに来る。
examples.english: He comes here every few days.

examples.japanese: この道には5メートルおきに木が植えられている.
examples.english: Trees align this road every 5 meters.

examples.japanese: この薬は2時間おきに飲んでください。
examples.english: Take this medicine every 2 hours.

examples.japanese: 私は一ヶ月おきに故郷へ帰ります。
examples.english: I return to my home town every month.

meaning: until; as far as; to (an extent); even ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 終わる終わらない終わったetc..

examples.japanese: みんなが朝食を食べ終わるまで待ちましょう。
examples.english: Let's wait until everyone has finished eating breakfast.

examples.japanese: そのゲームをやり終わるまでに5時間くらいかかる。
examples.english: It takes about 5 hours to finish that game.

examples.japanese: 彼が話し終わるとみんな黙っていた。
examples.english: There was silence when he finished speaking.

examples.japanese: 仕事をし終わったらすぐ行く。
examples.english: I'll go/come as soon as I finish work.

examples.japanese: パソコンを使い終わったら、シャットダウンをしてください。
examples.english: Once you've finished using the computer, please turn it off.

examples.japanese: 宿題の作文を書き終わったのでテレビを見ます。
examples.english: I've finished writing my essay for homework and now am going to watch some TV.

meaning: passive form; passive voice
structure: Ru-verb + る -> られる | U-verb + change "u" to "e" + る | やる + やれる | する + できる | くる + こられる

examples.japanese: そんなことを信じられない。
examples.english: I am not able to believe such a story..

examples.japanese: そこにあるいちごはすべて食べられる。
examples.english: You can eat any of the strawberries in there.

examples.japanese: 今日は忙しすぎて、朝ごはんを食べられなかった。
examples.english: Today I was so busy and wasn't able to eat breakfast.

examples.japanese: 納豆が食べられるの？
examples.english: Are you able to eat natto? (fermented soybeans)

examples.japanese: 夜は寒くて寝られない。
examples.english: The nights are too cold to sleep.

examples.japanese: 私はここにあまり長くいられない。
examples.english: I can't stay here for too long.

meaning: as if; as though; just like ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + らしいらしくらしくない | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 雨らしい。
examples.english: It looks like rain / looks like it's gonna rain.

examples.japanese: 男らしい。
examples.english: Manly (like a man)

examples.japanese: 女らしい。
examples.english: Womanly; feminine (like a woman)

examples.japanese: 学生らしくもっと勉強しなさい。
examples.english: Study more like a real student.

examples.japanese: 今日は君らしくないな。
examples.english: You don't seem like yourself today.

examples.japanese: 遅刻するなんて彼らしくない。
examples.english: It's not like him to be late like this.

meaning: like, similar to ~
structure: な-adjective + さ | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: 背の高さはどれぐらいですか？
examples.english: How tall are you?

examples.japanese: 私は、ワサビの辛さが大好きです。
examples.english: I love the spiciness of wasabi.

examples.japanese: この池の深さはどのぐらいですか？
examples.english: How deep is this pond?

examples.japanese: 新しい橋の長さは3,911メートルです。
examples.english: The length of the new bridge is 3,911 meters.

examples.japanese: 彼女の部屋の広さは畳で６畳くらいです。
examples.english: The space of her room is about 6 tatami mats (unit of measurement for Japanese rooms).

examples.japanese: この料理の美味しさを皆さんに紹介したいです。
examples.english: I want to introduce to everyone the deliciousness of this food.

meaning: before; in front of ~
structure: さっき + Sentence

examples.japanese: さっきまで天気がよかったですが、今は大雨です。
examples.english: The weather was fine just a moment ago, but now there's heavy rain..

examples.japanese: さっき起きたばかりで、まだ眠いです。
examples.english: I just woke up, but am still sleepy.

examples.japanese: あなたはさっき何か言ったでしょうね。聞こえなかったからもう一回教えてくれる？
examples.english: What did you say earlier? I couldn't hear you, so could you tell me one more time?

examples.japanese: さっき覚えた漢字を、もう忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I've already forgotten the kanji I just memorized not too long ago.

examples.japanese: ハサミが見あたらない。さっき見たときは、机の上にあったはずなのに。
examples.english: I can't find the scissors.. I saw them just a little while ago on top of the desk, but...

examples.japanese: あの二人、さっきまで喧嘩していたかと思ったらもう仲良くしている。
examples.english: I thought those 2 were fighting just a moment ago, but they seem to have already made up.

meaning: causative form; to make/let somebody do something
structure: Verb (causative form させる) + られる | くる + こさせられる | やる + やらせられる

examples.japanese: 仕事を辞めさせられた。
examples.english: I was forced to quit my job.

examples.japanese: 息子は退学させられた。
examples.english: My son was expelled from school.

examples.japanese: 彼女に2時間も待たせられた。
examples.english: She made me wait over 2 hours.

examples.japanese: その映画は考えさせられる。
examples.english: That movie makes you think.

examples.japanese: 毎日母に野菜を食べさせられる。
examples.english: Every day, my mother forces me to eat vegetables.

examples.japanese: フィアンセのお父さんにお酒を飲ませられた。
examples.english: My fiance's father made me to drink alcohol with him.

meaning: please let me do
structure: Ru-verb + る -> させる | U-verb + (ない form) ない -> せる | する + させる | やる + やらせる | くる + こさせる

examples.japanese: 母は私に自分の部屋を片付けさせた。
examples.english: My mother made me clean up my own room.

examples.japanese: この仕事は部下にやらせます。
examples.english: I'll make one of my subordinates do this task.

examples.japanese: 君を泣かせるつもりはなかった！
examples.english: I didn't mean to make you cry!

examples.japanese: 僕にやらせてください
examples.english: Please allow me to do it.

examples.japanese: 息子はアニメを見たがっていますが、宿題が終わっていないので、見させません。
examples.english: My son wants to watch anime, but he hasn't finished his homework, so I won't let him watch it..

meaning: causative form; to make/let somebody do something
structure: Verb(causative て form) + ください

examples.japanese: 質問させてください。
examples.english: Please allow me to ask you a question.

examples.japanese: 私のことをあなたに話させてください。
examples.english: Please let me tell you about myself.

examples.japanese: ちょっと調子が悪いので、早く帰らせてください。
examples.english: I'm not feeling well, so please let me head home early.

examples.japanese: 返事をする前にちょっと考えさせてください。
examples.english: Please let me think a bit before I give you my answer.

examples.japanese: 私に何かお手伝いさせてください。
examples.english: Please let me help with something.

examples.japanese: 彼女は今日病気なのでお休みさせてください。
examples.english: She is sick today so please allow her to have the day off.

meaning: very; quite; pretty; rather; just not ~
structure: さすが + に + Verb | の + Noun + (も)

examples.japanese: さすがに大都市だけあって、たくさんの高いビルがある。
examples.english: As expected of a large city, there are many tall buildings.

examples.japanese: 彼はさすがに出勤初日は緊張していました。
examples.english: He was understandably nervous on his first day of work.

examples.japanese: さすがにこういうところには住みたくないな。
examples.english: Just as I thought, I don't want to live in this kind of place.

examples.japanese: 彼がさすがにおどろきを隠せなかった。
examples.english: He really couldn't hide his surprise.

examples.japanese: さすがの私も泣きました。
examples.english: Even I cried.

examples.japanese: ピストルを見るとさすがの彼も動けなかった。
examples.english: When he saw the pistol, even he couldn't move.

meaning: do such things as A and B
structure: Verb (casual) + し | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: このコートは色がきれいだし、好きなデザインだし。買いたいですよ。
examples.english: This coat has a beautiful color and I like the design. I really want to buy it.

examples.japanese: 今日は週末だったし、天気が良かったので、公園は人が多かったです。
examples.english: It's the weekend and the weather is nice so the park was packed with people

examples.japanese: 彼は勉強ができるしスポーツも上手だし、私の好きなタイプだ。
examples.english: He's smart and good at sports, definitely my type.

examples.japanese: 彼女は料理は上手いし、性格はいいし、理想の奥さんだ。
examples.english: She cooks well and has a good personality, she's the ideal wife.

examples.japanese: お腹が空いたし、のどがかわいたし、何か食べたいです。
examples.english: I'm hungry and thirsty, I want to eat something.

examples.japanese: 友だちと遊びたいし、宿題はしなくてはいけないし、どうしよう。
examples.english: I want to hang out with my friends, but I need to do my homework.. What should I do!?

meaning: so much… that
structure: そんなに + Verb | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 昨日はそんなに忙しくなかった。
examples.english: Yesterday was not so busy.

examples.japanese: 日本語はそんなに難しくないよ。
examples.english: Japanese is not that difficult..

examples.japanese: 肉はそんなに好きではありません。
examples.english: I don’t like meat that much.

examples.japanese: そんなにがっかりするな。もう一度やり直しなさい。
examples.english: Don’t be so disappointed. Try again one more time.

examples.japanese: 私のことがそんなに大切なの？
examples.english: Do I really mean that much to you?

examples.japanese: ええ、そんなに暑いのですか？エアコンを付けようか？
examples.english: Is it really that hot? Shall we turn on the AC then?

meaning: ... or something; how about~
structure: Phrase 1 + それでも + Phrase 2

examples.japanese: それでもいいですか？
examples.english: Is that still OK with you?

examples.japanese: それでもあなたのことが好き。
examples.english: I still love you anyway.

examples.japanese: 外は大雨だ。それでも出かけないといけない。
examples.english: There's heavy rain outside, but even so I still need to head out.

examples.japanese: 彼はテストの準備をしていなかった。それでも合格した。
examples.english: He didn't prepare for the test, but even so he still passed..

examples.japanese: あの大学は絶対無理だと言われた。それでも僕は受けるつもりだ。
examples.english: Everyone says that university is impossible to get into. Even so, I plan to apply.

examples.japanese: みんなに反対されている。それでも私は彼と結婚したい。
examples.english: Everyone is against it, but even so I still want to marry him.

meaning: and; and then; thus; and now ~
structure: それに + Phrase

examples.japanese: チーズバーガー、それにフライドポテトをお願いします。
examples.english: I'd like a cheeseburger and fries please.

examples.japanese: このアニメはとても人気がある。それに、音楽がいい。
examples.english: This anime is very popular. In addition, it has good music.

examples.japanese: それに、私は日本語あまりが話せません。
examples.english: Furthermore, I can't speak a lot of Japanese.

examples.japanese: これはとても美味しい、それに値段もいい。
examples.english: This is very tasty, and the price is also good.

examples.japanese: 母は料理をする。それに、父は皿を洗う。
examples.english: My mother cooks and my father washes the dishes.

examples.japanese: 朝ご飯はご飯、みそ汁、それに、魚ですよ。
examples.english: Breakfast is rice, miso soup, and fish.

meaning: seems like; looks like ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + そうだそうです | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事をやめるそうだ。
examples.english: I heard that he will be quitting his job.

examples.japanese: 彼は金持ちだそうだ。
examples.english: He is said to be rich.

examples.japanese: 先生によると、来週の試験はむずかしいそうだ。
examples.english: According to our teacher, next week's test is going to be very hard.

examples.japanese: 彼女は今、入院中だそうだ。
examples.english: I heard she's in the hospital now.

examples.japanese: 彼女は有名だそうです。
examples.english: I heard she is famous.

examples.japanese: 彼はまだ独身だそうだ。
examples.english: I hear he's still single.

meaning: seems like; looks like ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + そうそうだそうです | な-adjective | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: いまにも、雨が降りそうだ。
examples.english: It seems like it's gonna start raining any moment.

examples.japanese: その人は倒れそうです。
examples.english: That person looks like they're about to fall over.

examples.japanese: そろそろ雨がやみそうなので、もう少し待ちましょう。
examples.english: It seems like the rain is going to stop soon, so let's wait a little bit more.

examples.japanese: どうしたの？眠そうだね。
examples.english: What's wrong. You look pretty sleepy..

examples.japanese: わぁ、おいしそうな料理がたくさんありますね。
examples.english: Wow, there's a lot of really good looking food here!

examples.japanese: 彼女が料理を作ってくれたが、見た目が悪くてまずそうだ。
examples.english: My girlfriend cooked some food for me, but the appearance was really bad and looked very unappetizing.

meaning: only; nothing but ~
structure: Verb (た form) + ばかり

examples.japanese: 私は今起きたばかりです。
examples.english: I've only just woken up.

examples.japanese: この仕事を始めたばかりです。
examples.english: I've only just recently started this job.

examples.japanese: さっき昼ごはんを食べたばかりです。
examples.english: I just finished eating lunch.

examples.japanese: 田中さんは先月にこの会社に入ったばかりです。
examples.english: Tanaka san just entered the company last month.

examples.japanese: このパソコンを買ったばかりなのにとても遅い！
examples.english: Even though I just bought this new computer, it's really slow!

examples.japanese: たった今その事故を見たばかりだ。
examples.english: I only just saw the accident now.

meaning: just about to; on the verge of doing something
structure: Verb (た form) + ところ

examples.japanese: 今起きたところです。
examples.english: I just woke up.

examples.japanese: 昼ごはんを食べたところです。
examples.english: I was just eating lunch.

examples.japanese: アメリカから日本に戻ったところです。
examples.english: I just returned to Japan from America.

examples.japanese: 駅に着いた時、ちょうど電車が出たところでした。
examples.english: I arrived at the station just as the train left.

examples.japanese: あなたのことを話したところだよ。
examples.english: We were just talking about you.

examples.japanese: 図書館にあなたを探しに行ったところです。
examples.english: I was just heading to the library to look for you.

meaning: passive form; passive voice
structure: see rules below

meaning: to show signs of; to appear; to feel, to think ~
structure: Verb (たい form) たい + がるがっているがったがらない

examples.japanese: その子が家に帰りたがっている。
examples.english: That kid seems like he wants to go home.

examples.japanese: 木村さんが、あなたに会いたがっていましたよ。
examples.english: Kimura-san wanted (wants) to see you.

examples.japanese: 娘は新しいi-phoneを買いたがっています。
examples.english: My daughter wants to buy the new i-phone.

examples.japanese: 息子が塾に行きたがらない。
examples.english: My son is reluctant to go to cram school.

examples.japanese: 息子はアニメを見たがっていますが、宿題が終わっていないので、見させません。
examples.english: My son wants to watch anime, but he hasn't finished his homework, so I won't let him watch it..

examples.japanese: 彼女は仕事を辞めたがっていますが、転職先が見つからず、なかなか辞めることができません。
examples.english: She wants to quit her job, but is unable to find a new job so she can't quite do it yet.

meaning: why don't you; how about ~ (used to give advice)
structure: Verb (た form) + ら | Noun + だった | な-adjective + だった | い-adjective + いかった

examples.japanese: お金があったら、旅行します。
examples.english: If I had money, I would go travel.

examples.japanese: 一口食べたら、きっと好きになるよ。
examples.english: Taste one bite, and you will surely like it!

examples.japanese: 時間がなかったら、テレビを見ません。
examples.english: If I had no time, I wouldn't watch any TV.

examples.japanese: 安かったら、パソコンを買いたいです。
examples.english: If it's cheap, I'd like to buy a computer.

examples.japanese: 暇だったら、手伝ってください。
examples.english: If you're free, please help me out.

examples.japanese: いい天気だったら、散歩しませんか。
examples.english: If the weather is nice, would you like to go for a walk?

meaning: how about; how is
structure: Verb (た form) + らどう

examples.japanese: 一緒に来たらどうですか？
examples.english: How about coming together with us?

examples.japanese: 静かにしたらどうですか。
examples.english: How about being quiet?

examples.japanese: 先生に聞いてみたらどうですか？
examples.english: Why don't you try asking the teacher?

examples.japanese: 彼に電話したらどうですか。
examples.english: Why don't you give him a call?

examples.japanese: 君もやってみたらどうか？
examples.english: Why don't you also give it a try?

examples.japanese: 友だちとそこに行ってみたらどう？
examples.english: Why don't you try going there with your friends?

meaning: if; after; when ~
structure: Verb (た form) + らいいですか

examples.japanese: どうしたらいいですか？
examples.english: What should I do?

examples.japanese: どこに行ったらいいですか。
examples.english: Where should I go?

examples.japanese: 何を食べたらいいですか。
examples.english: What should I eat?

examples.japanese: この本はいつまでに返したらいいですか。
examples.english: When do you need me to return this book to you?

examples.japanese: 私はどの駅で降りたらいいですか？
examples.english: Which station should I get off at?

examples.japanese: ホテルの予約をキャンセルしたいんですが、どうしたらいいですか。
examples.english: I'd like to cancel my hotel reservation, what should I do? (can you help me?)

meaning: and; with; as; connecting particle
structure: Verb (て form) | Noun +で (usually bad things) | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: 最近は忙しくてあまり運動をしていない。
examples.english: Lately, I've been busy and so I haven't been working out.

examples.japanese: 自転車のカギをなくして、家まで歩いて帰った。
examples.english: I lost the key to my bicycle, so I walked home.

examples.japanese: あの教室のドアは古くて開けにくいです。
examples.english: The door in that classroom is old and hard to open.

examples.japanese: パソコンの調子が悪くて、仕事ができなかった。
examples.english: My computer was acting up and I wasn't able to do any work.

examples.japanese: 日本に来てから半年をたった。家族に会えなくて寂しい。
examples.english: A half-year has passed since I came to Japan. Since I can't see my family, I am a little lonely.

examples.japanese: 娘は調子が悪くて、晩ご飯を食べなかった。
examples.english: My daughter is not feeling well, so she didn't eat her dinner.

meaning: to do for; to do a favor (casual)
structure: Verb (て form) + あげるあげたあげないあげます

examples.japanese: 母にセーターを買ってあげた。
examples.english: I bought my mother a sweater.

examples.japanese: いいよ，僕がやってあげるよ。
examples.english: No problem, I'll do it for you.

examples.japanese: 車に君を乗せてあげる。
examples.english: I'll give you a ride (by car).

examples.japanese: 君に見せてあげたかったよ。
examples.english: I wanted to show it to you.

examples.japanese: 私はあなたにそれを教えてあげない。
examples.english: I won't tell you that.

examples.japanese: あなたがそれを読んだら別の本を貸してあげます。
examples.english: Once you finish reading that I'll lend you another book.

meaning: want to do something
structure: Verb (て form) + ほしい欲しい | Verb (ないで form)

examples.japanese: 日本語を教えてほしいです。
examples.english: I want you to teach me Japanese.

examples.japanese: 先生には、もっとゆっくり話してほしいです。
examples.english: I wish the teacher would speak more slowly

examples.japanese: あなたに見てほしい写真を持っています。
examples.english: I have a picture I want you to see.

examples.japanese: ぜひ私と一緒に来てほしい。
examples.english: I'd love for you to come with me.

examples.japanese: 私に何をしてほしいのですか?
examples.english: What do you want me to do?

examples.japanese: あなたに家に来てほしくない。
examples.english: I don't want you to come to my house.

meaning: to do… and come back; to become; to continue; to start ~
structure: Verb (て form) + いくいきますいったいきました

examples.japanese: 歩いていく。
examples.english: to walk / to go by walking / to start walking

examples.japanese: 彼は毎日駅まで歩いていきます。
examples.english: He walks to the station every day.

examples.japanese: 船は港を出ていった。
examples.english: The ship pulled out of the harbor.

examples.japanese: 彼は京都へ引っ越していった。
examples.english: He moved to Kyoto.

examples.japanese: 今年はあっという間に過ぎていく。
examples.english: This year is going by really fast.

examples.japanese: 何も言わずに部屋を出ていきました。
examples.english: I left the room without saying anything.

meaning: could you please ~
structure: Verb (て form) + いたいました

examples.japanese: 彼女はオレンジを食べていた。
examples.english: She was eating an orange.

examples.japanese: 今日は家でゆっくりしていました。
examples.english: I relaxed at home today.

examples.japanese: 私は一晩中泣いていた。
examples.english: I cried all night.

examples.japanese: 彼はこのニュースを心配していた。
examples.english: He was worried about this news.

examples.japanese: 今朝、自分の部屋を掃除していました。
examples.english: I cleaned my room this morning.

examples.japanese: あなたは休日は何をしてたのですか。
examples.english: What did you do on your day off?

meaning: to get somebody to do something
structure: Verb (て form) + いただけませんか

examples.japanese: 写真を取っていただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you take a picture please?

examples.japanese: ちょっと待っていただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please wait a moment?

examples.japanese: もう少しゆっくり話していただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please speak a little bit more slowly?

examples.japanese: いい先生を紹介していただけませんか？
examples.english: Could you please introduce me to a good teacher?

examples.japanese: 荷物を持ってきていただけませんか？
examples.english: Could you please carry my luggage?

examples.japanese: お金を貸していただけませんか？
examples.english: Could you please lend me some money?

meaning: to get somebody to do something
structure: Verb (て form) + くれるくれますくれないくれたくれました

examples.japanese: 手伝ってくれる？
examples.english: Will you help me?

examples.japanese: 彼ならやってくれる。
examples.english: We can count on him to help us.

examples.japanese: 母は僕に毎日弁当を作ってくれる。
examples.english: My mom makes my bento lunch for me every day.

examples.japanese: 手を貸してくれますか？
examples.english: Will you please help me out?

examples.japanese: 私に日本語を教えてくれますか？
examples.english: Will you please teach me Japanese?

examples.japanese: すみません、写真を取ってくれませんか？
examples.english: Excuse me, could you please take a photo for me?

meaning: to start; to continue; to go on
structure: Verb (て form) + くるきたきますきました

examples.japanese: 見えてくる。
examples.english: To come into view (to start coming into view/ to continue coming into view)

examples.japanese: 雨が降ってきた。
examples.english: It started raining.

examples.japanese: 戻ってきたよ!
examples.english: I'm back!

examples.japanese: お腹がすいてきた。
examples.english: I'm hungry / I'm starting to get hungry.

examples.japanese: ここまで歩いてきました。
examples.english: I came here by foot.

examples.japanese: 私は彼を連れてくる。
examples.english: I will bring him / pick him up.

meaning: is/has been done (resulting state)
structure: Verb (て form) + みるみますみたい

examples.japanese: やってみる！
examples.english: I'll give it a shot! / Here goes nothing!

examples.japanese: これを使ってみる。
examples.english: I'll try using this.

examples.japanese: やってみないと分からない。
examples.english: You'll never know until you try.

examples.japanese: いつか海外に行ってみたいな。
examples.english: One day I'd like to try going abroad.

examples.japanese: おいしいかどうかわからないので、試しに食べてみます。
examples.english: I don't know if this is tasty or not, so I'm gonna give it a try.

examples.japanese: とにかく、彼女の予定を聞いてみます。
examples.english: Anyway, I'll try asking her about her plans.

meaning: to do for; to do a favor
structure: Verb (て form) + もらうもらいますもらいたいもらわないもらいません

examples.japanese: 彼に来てもらう。
examples.english: I will have him come.

examples.japanese: 先生に作文を直してもらう。
examples.english: I'll have my teacher check my writing/essay.

examples.japanese: あなたにぜひ見てもらいたいものがある。
examples.english: There's something I want you to look at.

examples.japanese: 彼は病院でみてもらう必要がある。
examples.english: He requires hospital care.

examples.japanese: 母に車で送ってもらった。
examples.english: I had my mom drive me there.

examples.japanese: あなたに日本語を教えてもらいたい。
examples.english: I want you to teach me Japanese.

meaning: is/has been done (resulting state)
structure: Verb (て form) + おくおきますおいて

examples.japanese: お弁当を作っておいたよ。
examples.english: I made your bento (lunch box) already.

examples.japanese: 出かける前に何か食べておこう。
examples.english: Let's eat something before we head out.

examples.japanese: 旅行の前に切符を買っておきます。
examples.english: I will buy the tickets before the trip.

examples.japanese: お母さんには内緒にしておくね。
examples.english: I will keep it a secret with mom, okay?

examples.japanese: 来週の試験のため、漢字を勉強しておきました。
examples.english: I studied my kanji in preparation for next week's exam.

examples.japanese: 友だちが遊びに来るので、部屋をきれいにしておきます。
examples.english: I will clean my room since my friend is coming over.

meaning: to finish; to end~
structure: Verb (て form) + しまうしまいますしまった | Verb (て form) + ちゃうちゃった | Verb (で form) + じゃうじゃった

examples.japanese: 仕事は全部終わってしまいました。
examples.english: I've finished with all of my work.

examples.japanese: 疲れが出たので、寝ちゃった。
examples.english: I was tired and so I fell asleep.

examples.japanese: パスポートをなくしてしまいました。
examples.english: I've lost my passport..

examples.japanese: 漢字の宿題はもうやってしまいました。
examples.english: I've already finished my kanji homework.

examples.japanese: 明日までに宿題をしちゃいます。
examples.english: I will finish my homework by tomorrow.

examples.japanese: ごめん！ジュースを全部飲んじゃった！
examples.english: Sorry, I drank all the juice!

meaning: to do something by accident, to finish completely
structure: Verb (て form) + すみません

examples.japanese: 遅れてすみません。
examples.english: I'm sorry for being late.

examples.japanese: 心配をかけてすみません。
examples.english: I apologize for causing you concern.

examples.japanese: 電話に出れなくてすみません。
examples.english: I am sorry that I couldn't answer the phone.

examples.japanese: あなたのお弁当を食べてすみません。
examples.english: I’m sorry for eating your lunch box.

examples.japanese: 返事が遅くなってすみませんでした。
examples.english: I'm sorry for replying so late.

examples.japanese: 朝早くにお電話してすみません。
examples.english: I'm sorry for calling so early in the morning.

meaning: is OK to ~; is alright to ~; may I ~?
structure: Verb (て form) + よかった

examples.japanese: 行ってよかった！
examples.english: I'm glad I went!

examples.japanese: これを買ってよかった。
examples.english: I'm glad I bought this.

examples.japanese: 私はあなたと出会えてよかった。
examples.english: I am glad that I was able to meet you.

examples.japanese: 財布を見つかってよかったですね。
examples.english: It's a good thing you found your wallet, eh?

examples.japanese: 君が無事に帰ってよかった。
examples.english: I'm glad you returned home safely.

examples.japanese: 君と連絡できてよかった。2時間遅れて心配したよ。
examples.english: I'm glad I was able to get in contact with you. I was really worried with the 2 hour delay.

meaning: just about to; on the verge of doing something
structure: Verb (て form) + いるところ

examples.japanese: 彼は入院しているところです。
examples.english: He is being hospitalized now.

examples.japanese: 今料理をしているところです。
examples.english: I am cooking now.

examples.japanese: 私は今、家で日本語を勉強しているところです。
examples.english: I'm currently studying Japanese at home.

examples.japanese: 姉は電話をかけているところだ。
examples.english: My older sister is in the middle of a phone call.

examples.japanese: 子どもを産んだばかりなので、うちで休んでいるところです。
examples.english: I just gave birth to my child so I’m currently resting at home.

examples.japanese: 彼女はお茶を飲みながら雑誌を読んでいるところです。
examples.english: She’s currently reading a magazine while drinking tea.

meaning: but; however; though ~
structure: Verb (て form) + も | Noun + で | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: たくさん食べても、お腹が空きます。
examples.english: Even if I eat a lot, I still feel hungry.

examples.japanese: 日曜日でも、働きます。
examples.english: I work even on Sundays.

examples.japanese: 子どもでもできることよ。
examples.english: Even children can do this.

examples.japanese: 必要なので、高くても買います。
examples.english: I need this, so I'll still buy it even if it's expensive.

examples.japanese: これは多いですよ。がんばっても食べ切れない。
examples.english: There is too much.. Even if I give it my all I can't eat everything.

examples.japanese: 安くても、私はグループ旅行が好きじゃない。
examples.english: Even if it's cheaper, I don't like traveling in a group.

meaning: and; with; as; connecting particle
structure: Verb (dictionary / ない form) + と | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: ラーメンを毎日食べると太りますよ。
examples.english: If you eat ramen everyday, you're gonna gain weight.

examples.japanese: 寝る前に甘い物を食べると虫歯になります。
examples.english: If you eat sweets before going to bed, you will get a cavity.

examples.japanese: 私の彼氏は酒を飲むと顔が赤くなる。
examples.english: Whenever my boyfriend drinks, his face gets red.

examples.japanese: 勉強するの場所が静かだとよく集中できます。
examples.english: When the place I study at is quiet, I am able to concentrate very well.

examples.japanese: このボタンを押すと、両方のドアが開きますよ。
examples.english: If you press this button, both doors will open.

examples.japanese: 最初の角を右に曲がると、銀行が見えます。
examples.english: If you turn right at the first corner, you will be able to see the bank.

meaning: – It is said; called thus.
structure: phrase + と言ってもいいといっても

examples.japanese: それはよい買い物だったといってもいいでしょう。
examples.english: I'd say it was a good buy.

examples.japanese: 彼はやさしいが，だまされやすいといってもいい。
examples.english: He's a kind person, but could be said to be a bit easy to be deceived.

examples.japanese: それはいい考えだ。いや，すばらしいといってもいいだろう。
examples.english: That's a good idea, even brilliant I might say..

examples.japanese: それまでの中で一番の旅だったと言ってもいいでしょう。
examples.english: I'd say that was the best trip I had ever taken.

examples.japanese: 彼女はネイティブと言ってもいいくらい日本語が上手だ。
examples.english: Her Japanese is so good you could say she's like a native speaker.

examples.japanese: 彼は死んだと言ってもいいくらいのものだ。
examples.english: You could say he's as good as dead.

meaning: convert phrase into noun
structure: Noun + と言うというと言いますといいます | Phrase

examples.japanese: この犬はバディーという名前です。
examples.english: This dog is called "Buddy".

examples.japanese: 昨日、トムという人に会いました。
examples.english: Yesterday, I met a person called Tom.

examples.japanese: 明日という日もある。
examples.english: There's always tomorrow.

examples.japanese: あなたにとって日本という国はどういう国ですか？
examples.english: What kind of country is Japan to you?

examples.japanese: 英語で「宿題」は、なんといいますか？
examples.english: How do you say "shukudai" (homework) in English?

examples.japanese: 猫みたいだという人もいる。
examples.english: Some people think he is like a cat.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Verb (casual) + ということ | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: あなたが私の声が好きだということがとても嬉しいです。
examples.english: I'm so glad you like my voice.

examples.japanese: あなたが会社をやめるということは本当ですか。
examples.english: Is it true that you're quitting the company?

examples.japanese: 彼は怖いということを知らない。
examples.english: He does not know what fear is.

examples.japanese: つまり、あなたは同じ本をまた読みたいということ？
examples.english: Do you mean you want to read the same book again?

examples.japanese: 彼は友だちができるかということを心配している。
examples.english: I'm worried about if he will be able to make friends.

examples.japanese: 私は彼が信用できない人だということが分かった。
examples.english: I realized he was an unreliable person.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Verb (casual, past) + と言われている | Noun + だ | Adjective (standard, past)

examples.japanese: 彼は天才だと言われている。
examples.english: He is said to be a genius.

examples.japanese: 彼は来月に退職すると言われている。
examples.english: It's being said that he will quit next month.

examples.japanese: 女性は男性より長生きだと言われている。
examples.english: It is said that women live longer than men.

examples.japanese: 彼女の母親は有名な作家だと言われている。
examples.english: Her mother is said to be a famous writer.

examples.japanese: 彼は若い時には体が弱かったと言われている。
examples.english: It is said that he had a weak body when he was young.

examples.japanese: 彼らは今年中に結婚すると言われている。
examples.english: It is said that they are going to get married by the end of the year.

meaning: appears; seems; looks as if ~
structure: Phrase + と聞いたときいた

examples.japanese: 彼がお父さんになったと聞いた。
examples.english: I heard that he became a father.

examples.japanese: この映画が面白いと聞いたことがあります。
examples.english: I heard that this movie is interesting.

examples.japanese: 彼が帰ってくると聞いた。
examples.english: I heard that he will be coming back.

examples.japanese: あなたの日本語がうまくなっていると聞いた。
examples.english: I heard your Japanese is getting better.

examples.japanese: あれはとても良い街だと聞いたことがあります。
examples.english: I've heard that is a very nice town.

examples.japanese: あなたが今日アメリカに帰ると聞いた。
examples.english: I heard you will be going back to America today.

meaning: thinking of doing; planning to ~
structure: Verb + と思うと思いますと思わないと思いません | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: きれいだと思わない？
examples.english: Don't you think it's beautiful?

examples.japanese: それはかなりむずかしいと思います。
examples.english: I think that is extremely difficult.

examples.japanese: 今日は午後から雨が降ると思います。
examples.english: I think it will rain today from the afternoon.

examples.japanese: この問題、テストに出ると思いますか。
