examples.english: Do you think this problem will be on the test?

examples.japanese: 日本に留学しようと思っています。
examples.english: I'm thinking to go study abroad in Japan.

examples.japanese: 仕事を続けるのはむりだと思う。
examples.english: I don't think I can continue on with this job.

meaning: such as; things like ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + とか + Verb (dictionary form) + とか | Noun + とか + Noun + とか

examples.japanese: 趣味とかありますか？
examples.english: Do you have any hobbies (or anything else you do)

examples.japanese: 私はおすしとかラーメンとか日本料理が好きです。
examples.english: I love Japanese food, like sushi, ramen, etc.

examples.japanese: このイベントでは、バーベキューとかゲームとかをします。
examples.english: At this event we will do things like barbecue and play games.

examples.japanese: 毎日、5分とか、10分とかでもいいので、運動をしたほうがいいですよ。
examples.english: You should work out every day, even just 5 to 10 minutes is OK.

examples.japanese: 毎日、仕事とか、会議とかでとても忙しい。
examples.english: I'm busy every day with (things like) work and meetings.

examples.japanese: 彼は英語だけじゃなくて、中国語とかスペイン語とかも話せるんだよ。
examples.english: He not only speaks English, but can also speak Chinese, Spanish, etc..

meaning: just finished doing, was just doing
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + ところ

examples.japanese: 今、出かけるところです。
examples.english: I am just about to leave.

examples.japanese: これから料理を作るところです。
examples.english: I am about to start cooking.

examples.japanese: 今からお風呂に入るところです。
examples.english: I am about to take a bath.

examples.japanese: もう少しで信じるところだった。
examples.english: I was really close to believing it.

examples.japanese: 「昼ごはんはもう食べましたか。」「いいえ、これから食べるところです。」
examples.english: "Have you eaten luch already?""Nope, I'm about to eat from now."

examples.japanese: 「宿題したの？」「ちょうど今からするところですよ。」
examples.english: "Did you do your homework?""I'm about to start now."

meaning: ongoing action or current state
structure: Verb (ます stem) ます + 続ける続けている続けた

examples.japanese: 昨日から雨が降り続けている。
examples.english: It's been raining nonstop since yesterday.

examples.japanese: 父からもらった自転車を今も使い続けています。
examples.english: I still use the bicycle that my father gave to me even now.

examples.japanese: 彼女は彼氏の話をしゃべり続けた。
examples.english: She continued talking about her boyfriend.

examples.japanese: それをやり続けたほうがいいのかもしれない。
examples.english: It might be better for me to keep doing that.

examples.japanese: どんなに大変だったとしても、やり続けることが大切です。
examples.english: No matter how tough things get, it's important to stay consistent with what you're doing.

examples.japanese: 一週間雨が降り続けた。
examples.english: It kept raining for a full week.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Noun + ってっていう

examples.japanese: これはたい焼きっていう食べ物だよ。
examples.english: This is a food called "taiyaki".

examples.japanese: コストコってスーパーに行ったことがありますか。
examples.english: Have you ever been to the supermarket (called) Costco?

examples.japanese: みんなの日本語って教科書がだれでも知っているね。
examples.english: Everyone knows the Japanese textbook "minna no nihongo", right?

examples.japanese: これは日本語でじゃんけんっていうゲームだよ。
examples.english: This is a game called "janken" in Japanese.

examples.japanese: ドラゴンボールっていうマンガが一番好きだ。
examples.english: Dragon Ball is my favorite manga.

examples.japanese: トムさん、さっき山田さんって人が探してたよ。
examples.english: Tom was just looking for a person called Yamada.

meaning: please let me do
structure: Ru-verb + る -> られる | U-verb + (ない form) ない -> れる | する + される | くる + こられる

examples.japanese: ケーキが誰かに食べられた！
examples.english: The cake was eaten by somebody!

examples.japanese: みんなに変だと言われます。
examples.english: Everyone tells me that I am strange.

examples.japanese: この本は多くの人に読まれている。
examples.english: This book is being read by many people.

examples.japanese: 私は先生にほめられました。
examples.english: I was praised by the teacher.

examples.japanese: こんな遅い時間に来られても困ります。
examples.english: It's a bit inconvenient for me if you come over this late.

examples.japanese: 友人に彼氏を取られた。
examples.english: My boyfriend was stolen by my best friend.

meaning: in comparison to; rather than; more than ~
structure: Noun-1 + は + ～が + Noun-2 + は…

examples.japanese: ひらがなは書けますが、漢字は書けません。
examples.english: I can write hiragana, but I cannot write kanji.

examples.japanese: 私は猫が好きですが犬はあまり好きじゃない。
examples.english: I like cats, but I don't really like dogs.

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人だが頭は良くない。
examples.english: She is beautiful but not very smart.

examples.japanese: 彼は才能があるが、経験はほとんどない。
examples.english: He has talent, but almost no experience.

examples.japanese: 日本に来たときは寂しかったが、今は友達ができて楽しくなりました。
examples.english: I was lonely when I came to Japan, but now I have some friends and it has become fun.

examples.japanese: 今の仕事は忙しいですが、給料は高いから頑張って続けます。
examples.english: My current job is busy, but my salary is high so I will keep working hard.

meaning: tend to; tendency to; frequently; often; to do something easily
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + やすい

examples.japanese: 日本語は分かりやすいです。
examples.english: Japanese is easy to understand.

examples.japanese: 先生の声が聞きやすいです。
examples.english: The teacher's voice is easy to hear / easy to listen to.

examples.japanese: ひらがなは漢字より書きやすいです。
examples.english: Hiragana is easier to write than kanji.

examples.japanese: 光に感じやすい。
examples.english: To be sensitive to light.

examples.japanese: 彼女はカゼを引きやすいです。
examples.english: She is prone to getting colds.

examples.japanese: 彼は説得しやすい。
examples.english: He is easy to persuade.

meaning: finally; at last; in the end ~
structure: やっと + phrase

examples.japanese: やっとレポートを書き上げた。
examples.english: I finally finished writing my report.

examples.japanese: 私はやっと家に帰ることが出来る。
examples.english: I can finally return home!

examples.japanese: 社長の長い話がやっと終わった。
examples.english: The company president's long story finally ended.

examples.japanese: やっと自転車に乗れるようになりました。
examples.english: I finally learned how to ride a bicycle!

examples.japanese: 『おはようございます。今日はいい天気ですね。』『おはよう。やっと晴れたね。』
examples.english: "Good morning! Today's weather is nice, isn't it?""Morning. Indeed, the sun finally came out."

examples.japanese: 明日までの宿題がやっと終わりました。
examples.english: I finally finished my homework due tomorrow.

meaning: [2] is more than [1]
structure: [A]より[B] | OR より + adjective

examples.japanese: 今日は昨日より暑いです。
examples.english: Today is more hot than yesterday.

examples.japanese: 最近、円はドルより安い。
examples.english: Lately the Yen is cheaper than the dollar.

examples.japanese: 今は恋愛より仕事だ。
examples.english: I'm more interested in work than love right now.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、私より料理が上手。
examples.english: She's better at cooking than I am.

examples.japanese: それより安くは売られません。
examples.english: I can't sell it for any less (more cheap) than that.

examples.japanese: 今朝はいつもより早く学校へ来ました。
examples.english: I came to school this morning earlier than usual.

meaning: plan to ~; intend to ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 予定だよていだ | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 私はデートに行く予定だ。
examples.english: I'm going on a date.

examples.japanese: 私は友だちと遊ぶ予定だった。
examples.english: I was planning to hang out with my friends.

examples.japanese: 6時に起きる予定だった。
examples.english: I planned to wake up at 6.

examples.japanese: 7月の終わりにドイツへ出張する予定です。
examples.english: I am planning to go on a business trip to Germany in July.

examples.japanese: 旅行は１週間ぐらいの予定です。
examples.english: I'm planning to travel for about 1 week.

examples.japanese: 来週に中国に行く予定です。
examples.english: I am planning to go to China next week.

meaning: I heard...
structure: Verb (casual) + ようだ | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 雨のようだ。
examples.english: It looks like rain..

examples.japanese: そのようだ。
examples.english: It seems to be that way.

examples.japanese: 今日は寒くなるようだ。
examples.english: It looks like it's gonna get pretty cold today.

examples.japanese: 彼女はうれしくないようだ。
examples.english: She doesn't seem happy.

examples.japanese: だいぶ変わったようだな。
examples.english: (it) seems to have changed considerably

examples.japanese: 教室に来たけど誰もいない。今日は授業がないようだ。
examples.english: I came to the classroom, but nobody was there. It seems like there's no class today.

meaning: to try to; to make sure that ~
structure: Verb (casual) + ようにような | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 犬のように働いている。
examples.english: I'm working like a dog

examples.japanese: その二人は燃えるような愛がありますね。
examples.english: Those two seem to have a smoldering-like love for each other.

examples.japanese: 彼は家族のためだけに生きていたように思える。
examples.english: He seemed to live only for his family in my opinion.

examples.japanese: 見えるように、このパソコンはとても古いですがまだ使われている。
examples.english: As you can see, this computer is very old, but it's still being used.

examples.japanese: 私を子どものように扱わないで。
examples.english: Don't treat me as a kid.

examples.japanese: 日本語で新聞が読めるように、漢字の勉強をしています。
examples.english: I'm studying kanji so that I can read the newspaper in Japanese.

meaning: to try to; to make sure that ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ようになる | Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 大きくなったら分かるようになるよ。
examples.english: When you get older, you'll understand.

examples.japanese: 毎日練習すれば、泳げるようになります。
examples.english: If you practice everyday, you'll eventually be able to swim.

examples.japanese: やっと自転車に乗れるようになりました。
examples.english: I finally learned how to ride a bicycle!

examples.japanese: たくさん勉強したので、日本語を話せるようになりました。
examples.english: I studied a lot and became able to speak Japanese.

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んで、よく寝られるようになりました。
examples.english: I was able to sleep well after taking some medicine.

examples.japanese: それをいつ使えるようになるのか教えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me when I will start being able to use that.

meaning: to decide on
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ようにするようにしますようにしているようにしています | Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 明日早く起きるようにする。
examples.english: I'll try to wake up early tomorrow.

examples.japanese: それを忘れないようにする。
examples.english: I'll be sure to remember that.

examples.japanese: 明日から仕事に行く前に毎日ラニングをするようにします。
examples.english: From tomorrow I'm going to try to go running before work every day.

examples.japanese: 今日からお酒を飲まないようにします。
examples.english: I'm going to not drink alcohol anymore from today.

examples.japanese: 毎日歩くようにしている。
examples.english: I'm trying to walk every day.

examples.japanese: 夜は10時に寝るようにしている。
examples.english: I'm trying to go to bed at 10.

meaning: in such a way that ~
structure: Verb (volitional form)(よう form) + と思うとは思わないと思いますと思っている

examples.japanese: 日本に留学しようと思っています。
examples.english: I'm thinking to go study abroad in Japan.

examples.japanese: 大学で働こうと思っています。
examples.english: I'm thinking to work at the University.

examples.japanese: 今度の休みに海へ行こうと思う。
examples.english: I think I will go to to the beach during my next holiday.

examples.japanese: 子どもができたからタバコを辞めようと思う。
examples.english: Since I will be having a kid, I'm planning to quit smoking.

examples.japanese: 今から書店へ行こうと思っています。
examples.english: I think I'll go to a bookstore now.

examples.japanese: 彼は外国で働こうと思っています。
examples.english: He is thinking of working in a foreign country.

meaning: please do
structure: ぜひ是非 + Phrase

examples.japanese: 私はぜひそこで働きたい。
examples.english: I would really like to work there.

examples.japanese: ぜひ、今度うちへ遊びに来てください。
examples.english: Definitely please come over to hang out sometime.

examples.japanese: 彼女はぜひそこへ行きたいと言った。
examples.english: She said that she was eager to go there.

examples.japanese: 日本に来きたら、ぜひ連絡してください。
examples.english: If you ever come to Japan, be sure to let me know!

examples.japanese: ベトナムに旅行したら、ぜひフォーを食べてみたいです。
examples.english: If I ever go to Vietnam, I would like to try eating Pho noodles.

examples.japanese: ぜひその映画を見るべきです。
examples.english: You really must go see that movie!

meaning: difficult to do ~
structure: Verb (ます stem) ます + づらい

examples.japanese: この質問には答えづらいです。
examples.english: This question is difficult to answer.

examples.japanese: この本は字が小さくて読みづらいです。
examples.english: This books print is too small, it's difficult to read.

examples.japanese: 彼女はつき合いづらい人だ。
examples.english: She's a difficult person to get along with.

examples.japanese: 彼の説明がむずかしくて分かりづらいだった。
examples.english: His explanation was complicated and difficult to understand.

examples.japanese: この漢字は覚えづらいです。
examples.english: This kanji is difficult to remember.

examples.japanese: この道は狭くて、車も多いので、運転しづらいです。
examples.english: This road is really narrow, and there's lots of cars, so it's difficult to drive on.

meaning: It seems ~ / It appears ~ (based on evidence)
structure: Plain form + ようだ / Noun + の + ようだ

examples.japanese: 彼女は疲れているようだ。
examples.english: She seems to be tired.

examples.japanese: 外は雨のようです。
examples.english: It appears to be raining outside.

examples.japanese: まるで夢のようだ。
examples.english: It's just like a dream.

notes: Based on the speaker's direct observation or evidence. Also used for comparisons with まるで (just like). The written/formal counterpart is 〜ように見える.

meaning: Looks like ~ / Seems like ~ (casual)
structure: Plain form + みたいだ / Noun + みたいだ

examples.japanese: 彼は風邪を引いたみたいだ。
examples.english: Looks like he caught a cold.

examples.japanese: まるで子供みたいだ。
examples.english: You're just like a child.

examples.japanese: 試験は難しかったみたいです。
examples.english: The exam seems to have been difficult.

notes: Casual equivalent of 〜ようだ. Very common in spoken Japanese. Also used for comparisons.

meaning: Just did ~ / Only ~ / Nothing but ~
structure: Verb[た] + ばかり (just did) / Noun + ばかり (only)

examples.japanese: 日本に来たばかりです。
examples.english: I just arrived in Japan.

examples.japanese: 彼はゲームばかりしている。
examples.english: He does nothing but play games.

examples.japanese: 卒業したばかりの新入社員。
examples.english: A new employee who just graduated.

notes: 〜たばかり means 'just did (very recently)'. Noun/Verb + ばかり means 'only/nothing but' (often with a critical nuance).

meaning: Not only ~ but also ~
structure: Noun / Plain form + だけでなく + [Noun / Phrase] + も

examples.japanese: 彼は英語だけでなく、フランス語も話せる。
examples.english: He can speak not only English but also French.

examples.japanese: 勉強するだけでなく、スポーツも大切だ。
examples.english: Not only studying, but sports are also important.

examples.japanese: 値段だけでなく、品質も考えてください。
examples.english: Please consider not only the price but also the quality.

notes: Adds emphasis by saying something goes beyond what is expected. Similar patterns: 〜のみならず (more formal), 〜はもちろん (of course … but also).

meaning: Thanks to ~ / Because of ~ (positive result)
structure: Plain form + おかげで / Noun + の + おかげで

examples.japanese: 先生のおかげで合格できました。
examples.english: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to pass.

examples.japanese: 毎日練習したおかげで、上手になった。
examples.english: Thanks to practicing every day, I got better.

examples.japanese: 君のおかげです。
examples.english: It's all thanks to you.

notes: Always expresses a positive result. The negative counterpart (bad result) is 〜せいで.

meaning: Because of ~ / Due to ~ (negative result / blame)
structure: Plain form + せいで / Noun + の + せいで

examples.japanese: 電車が遅れたせいで、遅刻した。
examples.english: Because the train was delayed, I was late.

examples.japanese: 君のせいだ！
examples.english: It's your fault!

examples.japanese: 雨のせいで試合が中止になった。
examples.english: Due to the rain, the game was cancelled.

notes: Always carries blame or a negative nuance. Contrast with 〜おかげで (positive). 〜せいか is softer: 'perhaps because of ~'.

meaning: According to ~
structure: Noun + によると / によれば

examples.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうです。
examples.english: According to the weather forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼女によると、彼はもう辞めたらしい。
examples.english: According to her, he apparently already quit.

examples.japanese: ニュースによれば、事故があったようだ。
examples.english: According to the news, it seems there was an accident.

notes: Quotes an information source. Often followed by 〜そうだ or 〜らしい since both indicate reported information.

meaning: Towards ~ / Against ~ / In contrast to ~
structure: Noun + に対して / に対する + Noun

examples.japanese: 先生に対して失礼なことを言った。
examples.english: I said something rude to the teacher.

examples.japanese: この問題に対して、解決策が必要だ。
examples.english: A solution is needed for this problem.

examples.japanese: 彼が賛成なのに対して、彼女は反対だ。
examples.english: While he is in favor, she is against it.

notes: Three uses: (1) target of an action or attitude; (2) subject of consideration; (3) contrast ('whereas'). に対する precedes nouns attributively.

meaning: Not as ~ as ~ / Less ~ than ~
structure: Noun + ほど + Adjective / Verb + ない

examples.japanese: 思ったほど難しくなかった。
examples.english: It wasn't as difficult as I thought.

examples.japanese: 彼女ほど歌が上手な人はいない。
examples.english: There is no one who sings as well as she does.

examples.japanese: 東京ほど大きい街はない。
examples.english: There is no city as large as Tokyo.

notes: ほど sets a standard of comparison. Positive: Noun₁はNoun₂ほど〜ない (A is not as ~ as B). Can also express degree: 〜するほど (to such an extent that ~).

meaning: Decide to ~ / Choose to ~
structure: Verb[dict / ない] + ことにする

examples.japanese: 毎朝ジョギングすることにした。
examples.english: I decided to jog every morning.

examples.japanese: 肉を食べないことにしました。
examples.english: I decided not to eat meat.

examples.japanese: 旅行に行くことにしよう。
examples.english: Let's decide to go on a trip.

notes: Expresses a personal decision. 〜ことになる (N3) expresses a decision or outcome that has been reached by circumstances or others.

meaning: It has been decided that ~ / It turns out that ~
structure: Verb[dict / ない] + ことになる / ことになっている

examples.japanese: 来月から東京に転勤することになりました。
examples.english: It has been decided that I will transfer to Tokyo from next month.

examples.japanese: この部屋では禁煙ということになっています。
examples.english: It is the rule that this room is non-smoking.

examples.japanese: 彼女が担当することになった。
examples.english: It turned out that she will be in charge.

notes: Implies an outcome determined by circumstances, rules, or outside forces — not a personal choice. ことになっている describes an established rule or arrangement.

meaning: On the other hand ~ / While ~ (contrast)
structure: Plain form / Noun + の + 一方で

examples.japanese: 日本語が上手になった一方で、英語を忘れてしまった。
examples.english: On one hand my Japanese improved, but on the other I forgot my English.

examples.japanese: 彼は勤勉な一方で、少し頑固だ。
examples.english: While he is diligent, he is also a bit stubborn.

examples.japanese: 物価が上がる一方だ。
examples.english: Prices keep rising.

notes: Two uses: (1) contrast between two aspects; (2) 〜一方だ / 〜一方である describes a continuing trend in one direction.

meaning: Taking the opportunity to ~ / While you're at it
structure: Verb[dict / た] + ついでに / Noun + の + ついでに

examples.japanese: 買い物のついでに、銀行に寄った。
examples.english: While I was shopping, I stopped by the bank.

examples.japanese: 図書館に行くついでに、DVDを返してきた。
examples.english: On the way to the library, I returned the DVD.

examples.japanese: 散歩のついでに写真を撮った。
examples.english: I took photos while out on a walk.

notes: The secondary action (after ついでに) is done opportunistically while already doing the main action. The main event is mentioned before ついでに.

meaning: If only ~ / As long as ~
structure: Noun + さえ + Verb[ば] / い-Adj[ければ]

examples.japanese: お金さえあれば、旅行できるのに。
examples.english: If only I had money, I could travel.

examples.japanese: あなたさえいれば十分だ。
examples.english: As long as I have you, that's enough.

examples.japanese: これさえすれば大丈夫だ。
examples.english: As long as you do this, it will be fine.

notes: さえ is an emphasis particle meaning 'even/only'. Combined with a conditional, it expresses a minimum sufficient condition.

meaning: Even if ~ / Even though ~
structure: Verb[て] + も / い-Adj[くて] + も / な-Adj/Noun + でも

examples.japanese: 雨が降っても、試合は続ける。
examples.english: Even if it rains, the game will continue.

examples.japanese: 高くても、買いたい。
examples.english: Even if it's expensive, I want to buy it.

examples.japanese: 何回試みても、うまくいかない。
examples.english: No matter how many times I try, it doesn't work.

notes: Grants a concession — the result occurs regardless of the condition. 〜ても + negative means 'no matter how much you ~, it won't happen'.

meaning: only; just; as much as ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + だけ | Noun | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 食べたいだけ食べなさい。
examples.english: Eat as much as you like.

examples.japanese: 私はそれをできるだけ早くいただけますか。
examples.english: Would I be able to get that as soon as possible?

examples.japanese: できるだけ早く返事をいただけると助かります。
examples.english: I would appreciate it if you could reply to me as soon as possible.

examples.japanese: 食べ放題だから、食べれるだけ食べてくださいね。
examples.english: It's all you can eat, so eat as much as you can!

examples.japanese: 二度とここに戻れないから、読めるだけ本を読みたいです。
examples.english: I will never be able to come back here, so I want to read as much as I can.

examples.japanese: 試験が終わったら、好きなだけ遊びたい。
examples.english: After the exam is finished, I want to relax and hang out as much as I want.

meaning: not limited to; not only… but also ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + だけでなく | Noun (である) | な-adjective + な/である | い-adjective

examples.japanese: ここのレストランはどれも安いだけでなく、美味しい。
examples.english: Not only is everything cheap at this restaurant, it is all delicious.

examples.japanese: この公園では、子供だけではなく大人も楽しむことができる。
examples.english: This park is enjoyable for not only kids, but for adults as well.

examples.japanese: 彼女は日本語が上手なだけでなく、英語もペラペラだ。
examples.english: She is not only good at Japanese, but also fluent in English.

examples.japanese: 君だけでなく僕も悪かった。
examples.english: It isn't just you, I am also to blame.

examples.japanese: 彼は知識だけではなく、経験も豊かである。
examples.english: Not only does he have knowledge, but he also has an abundance of experience.

examples.japanese: 肉だけでなく野菜も食べなさいよ。
examples.english: Make sure to eat not just the meat, but the vegetables as well.

meaning: [A] but [B]; however; comparison
structure: Verb (casual) + んだ/のだ + けど | Noun + だ/だった/ですNoun + なんだ/なのだ | な-adjective + だ/だったな-adjective + なんだ/なのだ | い-adjective + い/いかったい-adjective + いんだ/いのだ

examples.japanese: スキー行きたいんだけど、お金が全然ないよ。
examples.english: I want to go skiing, but I have no money.

examples.japanese: 彼女はかわいいんだけど僕のタイプではない。
examples.english: She's cute, but not my type.

examples.japanese: 今週は暇だけど、来週は忙しい。
examples.english: I am free this week, but next week I am busy.

examples.japanese: 彼に電話したんだけど、話し中で通じなかった。
examples.english: I called him, but he was busy and I couldn't get through.

examples.japanese: そうだといいんだけど。
examples.english: I hope that's true, but...

examples.japanese: 母:「ちょっと、手伝ってくれない？」娘:「今、勉強してるんだけど…」
examples.english: Mother: Can you give me a hand?Daughter: I'm studying now... (may express irritation)

meaning: no matter how ~
structure: どうしても + phrase

examples.japanese: 私はどうしても自分の家がほしい。
examples.english: I really want to have my own house (to the point I'd do anything).

examples.japanese: どうしても車が動かなかったので私たちは歩いて行くことにした。
examples.english: No matter what we tried the car wouldn't start, so finally we decided to go on foot.

examples.japanese: どうしても彼女の電話番号が思い出せない。
examples.english: I can't for the life of me remember her phone number.

examples.japanese: 他の問題はできたのだが、この問題だけはどうしても解けない。
examples.english: I was able to do the other problems, but this one I cannot solve no matter how hard I try.

examples.japanese: どうしても来られないときは連絡してください。
examples.english: Please contact me when you are not able to come.

examples.japanese: あなたはそれがどうしても必要なら再度連絡をください。
examples.english: If you need that no matter what, please contact me again.

meaning: abruptly; suddenly; all of a sudden; without warning
structure: ふと + action

examples.japanese: ふと街で彼に会った。
examples.english: I met him in the street by chance.

examples.japanese: 学校に行く途中、ふと今日は母の誕生日だったことを思い出した。
examples.english: On my way to school I suddenly remembered that today was my mother's birthday.

examples.japanese: 財布がないのにふと気がついた。
examples.english: He suddenly realized he had lost his wallet.

examples.japanese: 私はあの店で珍しいものをふと見つけた。
examples.english: I came across a rare item at that store.

examples.japanese: 素晴らしい考えがふと心に浮かんだ。
examples.english: A brilliant idea just occurred to me.

examples.japanese: 彼はわざとそうしたのだとふと私は思った。
examples.english: It just occurred to me that he had done it on purpose.

meaning: personality (someone tends to; has a tendency to; has a sensitivity to ~)
structure: Noun + がち | Verb ます (stem form)

examples.japanese: 私は、仕事でミスしがちです。
examples.english: I tend to make a lot of mistakes at work.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、学校をサボりがちです。
examples.english: She's always skipping school.

examples.japanese: ずっと曇りがちの天気が続いている。
examples.english: The constant cloudy weather keeps continuing.

examples.japanese: パソコンの使いすぎで目が疲れがちです。
examples.english: My eyes tend to get tired from using computers too much.

examples.japanese: 一人暮らしなので、コンビニ弁当ばかり食べがちだ。
examples.english: I live alone, so I tend to only eat meals from the convenience store.

examples.japanese: 最近、彼女は仕事を休みがちだ。
examples.english: She has been taking a lot of days off of work recently.

meaning: difficult to do ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + がたい

examples.japanese: 信じがたいことだが、これは事実だ。
examples.english: This may be hard to believe, but this is the truth.

examples.japanese: 許しがたいことです。
examples.english: This is an unforgivable act.

examples.japanese: 彼の話は信じがたい内容でした。
examples.english: His story's contents were impossible to believe.

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人だから近寄りがたい。
examples.english: She's so beautiful, It's impossible for me to approach her.

examples.japanese: 子どもに対する犯罪は許しがたい。
examples.english: Crimes against children are unforgivable.

examples.japanese: これは正解ではないが、間違っているとも言いがたい。
examples.english: This isn't the correct answer, but I can't say it's a mistake either.

meaning: seems like; somewhat; -ish; easily does; often does ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 気味ぎみ | Noun

examples.japanese: 彼は人の名前を忘れ気味である。
examples.english: He tends to forget people's names.

examples.japanese: 昨夜、彼は風邪気味だった。
examples.english: He had a bit of a cold last night.

examples.japanese: 風邪気味で、熱っぽいんだ。
examples.english: I feel like I'm catching a cold, and I'm a bit feverish.

examples.japanese: 残業続きで疲れ気味だ。
examples.english: I'm feeling a bit tired due to continued overtime work.

examples.japanese: 新入社員は緊張気味の顔をしています。
examples.english: The new employee looks a little bit nervous.

examples.japanese: 彼女は遠慮気味にそう言った。
examples.english: She said that hesitantly.

meaning: is not as… as ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + 程ほど | Noun | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 君ほど美しい人はいません！
examples.english: There is no one that rivals your beauty.

examples.japanese: 死ぬほどのどがかわいている。
examples.english: I'm so thirsty I could die..

examples.japanese: 今年ほど雨の降った年はなかった。
examples.english: It rained more this year than any other year.

examples.japanese: 年をとるほど体が弱くなる。
examples.english: My body becomes weaker as I grow older.

examples.japanese: ビックリするほど大きい赤ちゃん。
examples.english: The child was surprisingly large.

examples.japanese: JLPT先生ほど、生徒のことを大切に思っている先生はいません。
examples.english: There is no teacher that cares as much about their students as JLPT Sensei.

meaning: while; besides; at the same time; in addition
structure: 一度に + phrase

examples.japanese: 彼は一度にクッキーを3つ取った。
examples.english: He took 3 cookies at once.

examples.japanese: 一度に３冊の本を借りることが出来ます。
examples.english: You can borrow three books at a time.

examples.japanese: 一度に全部はできないよ。
examples.english: You can't do everything at once.

examples.japanese: 彼は一度に６個の箱を運んだ。
examples.english: He carried six boxes at once.

examples.japanese: その薬品は一度に全部使用しなければなりません。
examples.english: You must use all of that medicine at the same time.

examples.japanese: 私はそれらを一度にまとめて注文したい。
examples.english: I want to order those all together.

meaning: no matter what; at any cost; after all ~
structure: いくら + Verb (ても form) | Noun + でも | な-adjective + でも | い-adjective + いくても

examples.japanese: お金はいくらあっても困りません。
examples.english: You can never have too much money.

examples.japanese: これはいくら安くても、買いたくない。
examples.english: No matter how cheap this is, I don't want to buy it.

examples.japanese: いくら調べても分からなかったので、先生に聞いた。
examples.english: I could not understand no matter how much I studied, so I asked my teacher.

examples.japanese: これは必要なので、いくら高くても買います。
examples.english: I need it so I’ll buy it now matter how expensive it is.

examples.japanese: いくら好きでも、それを伝えなければ始まらない。
examples.english: No matter how much you may like them, if you don't let them know nothing will ever start.

examples.japanese: 生活のために仕事はいくら嫌いでもやらなければならない。
examples.english: No matter how much you may hate your job, you have to do it to maintain your livelihood.

meaning: on one hand, on the other hand; although ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 一方だ

examples.japanese: 最近、この町の人口は減る一方だ。
examples.english: Recently, this town's population continues to decrease.

examples.japanese: 日本に来る外国人の数は増える一方だ。
examples.english: The number of foreigners coming to Japan continues to increase.

examples.japanese: 交通事故は増える一方だ。
examples.english: Traffic accidents are continuing to increase.

examples.japanese: 私は全然勉強していないので、成績は下がる一方だ。
examples.english: I never study and so my grades just keep dropping.

examples.japanese: 日本の人口はこのままだと減少する一方だと思います。
examples.english: With Japan's population situation as it is, I think it will just continue to decline.

examples.japanese: 広告を出しているのに、お客さんは減る一方だ。
examples.english: Despite advertising, the number of customers is decreasing.

meaning: ask a question in a polite way
structure: 一体いったい + question

examples.japanese: 一体どこで彼に会ったんだ。
examples.english: Where on earth did you meet him?

examples.japanese: あなたは一体何をしていますか？
examples.english: What exactly are you doing?

examples.japanese: あの人は一体何の者だ？
examples.english: Who in the world is that?

examples.japanese: 彼女は一体どこに住んでいるだろう。
examples.english: Where in the world does she live?

examples.japanese: 一体誰が彼女にそんなことを言ったのか？
examples.english: Who could have said such a thing to her?

examples.japanese: この騒ぎは一体なんですか?
examples.english: What is this fuss all about?

meaning: in the case of~; assuming~; if A then B
structure: Phrase + じゃない

examples.japanese: トムさんも来るじゃない？
examples.english: Tom will surely come as well?

examples.japanese: あそこにいる人って、田中先生じゃない？
examples.english: Isn't that person over there Mr. Tanaka?

examples.japanese: やればできるじゃない。
examples.english: I didn't think you had it in you.

examples.japanese: 彼は今度も来ないんじゃないかな。
examples.english: I don't think he'll come this time either.

examples.japanese: ちょっと！危ないじゃない。
examples.english: Be careful, that's dangerous!

examples.japanese: リモコン？テーブルの上にあるんじゃない？
examples.english: The remote control? Isn't it on top of the table?

meaning: how…!; what…!
structure: Noun + か何か

examples.japanese: 彼は病気か何かだろう。
examples.english: He must be sick or something.

examples.japanese: オレンジジュースか何か欲しいな。
examples.english: I want some orange juice or something.

examples.japanese: 私はアイスクリームか何か食べたいです。
examples.english: I want to eat ice cream or something.

examples.japanese: 帰りは寒いから上着か何か持っていった方がいいよ 。
examples.english: It will be cold when you come back, so you'd best bring a jacket or something.

examples.japanese: 昼ご飯はサンドイッチか何かを作ってあげましょうか。
examples.english: I'll fix a sandwich or something for your lunch?

examples.japanese: お急ぎでなかったら、お茶か何かいかがですか。
examples.english: If you’re not in a hurry, how about cup of tea or something?

meaning: over (a period); through; concerning; regarding ~
structure: Noun-1 + から + Noun-2 + にかけて

examples.japanese: 東京から京都にかけて新幹線で行くのは何時間かかるの？
examples.english: How long does it take to get from Tokyo to Kyoto by bullet train?

examples.japanese: 午前から夕方にかけて昼寝をした。
examples.english: I took a nap from morning until evening.

examples.japanese: 日本では、大学の入学試験は、普通２月から３月にかけて行われる。
examples.english: In Japan, university entrance exam is usually held from February to March.

examples.japanese: 明日は昼から夕方にかけて雨でしょう。
examples.english: Tomorrow it will rain from noon through late afternoon.

examples.japanese: 六月から七月にかけて、日本は梅雨のシーズンです。
examples.english: From June to July is Japan's rainy season.

examples.japanese: この服は、春から夏にかけて多くの人に着られています。
examples.english: This clothing is worn by many people from spring to summer.

meaning: instead of; replacing; on behalf of ~
structure: Verb (casual) + 代わりに | Noun + の | その

examples.japanese: 私が部長の代わりに出張に行きます。
examples.english: I will go on a business trip on behalf of my manager.

examples.japanese: 今朝はコーヒーの代わりにお茶を飲んだ。
examples.english: This morning, I drank tea instead of coffee.

examples.japanese: 昨日残業した代わりに、今日は少し早く帰っていいと言われた。
examples.english: In exchange for working overtime yesterday, I was told I could leave a little earlier today.

examples.japanese: 今日は仕事へ車で行く代わりに自転車で行った。
examples.english: Today, instead of going to work by car, I went by bicycle.

examples.japanese: お箸がないので、その代わりにフォークを使う。
examples.english: Since I do not have any chopsticks, I will use a fork instead

examples.japanese: 車で来たので、ビールの代わりにコーラをください。
examples.english: Since I came by car, I will have a cola instead of beer.

meaning: end up; in the end; as a result (negative)
structure: Verb (casual, past) + 結果けっか | Noun + の | その

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事をサボった結果として首になった。
examples.english: As a result of him skipping work, he was fired.

examples.japanese: みんなで相談した結果、今回は参加しないことにした。
examples.english: After consulting with everyone, I've decided to not participate this time.

examples.japanese: ほとんど勉強をしなかった。その結果、試験に落ちてしまった。
examples.english: I barely studied. As a result, I failed my exam.

examples.japanese: これは君の努力の結果だと思います。
examples.english: I think this is a result of your hard effort.

examples.japanese: 毎日ご飯の量を減らした結果、1ヶ月で3キロ体重が減った。
examples.english: As a result of reducing the amount of food I eat every day, I lost 3 kilograms after 1 month.

examples.japanese: 半年ダイエットを続けた。その結果、10キロをやせた。
examples.english: I continued to diet for half a year. As a result, I lost 10 kilos.

meaning: as a result of; after ~
structure: (phrase) + 結局（は） + conclusion

examples.japanese: 結局彼はそれを買わなかった。
examples.english: He didn't buy it in the end.

examples.japanese: 友人から何度も誘われたが、結局行かないことにした。
examples.english: I was invited by my good friend countless times, but ultimately decided not to go.

examples.japanese: 私たちは結局この試合に負けてしまった。
examples.english: In the end, we lost this match.

examples.japanese: 彼は働きすぎて、結局は病気になってしまった。
examples.english: He worked so hard that eventually he made himself ill.

examples.japanese: お昼は何を食べようかと考えていたけど、結局ハンバーガーにした。
examples.english: I was thinking about what I should eat for lunch, but ended up getting a hamburger.

examples.japanese: 2時間も会議をしたのに、結局何も決まらないで終わってしまった。
examples.english: We had a meeting for 2 hours, but it ultimately ended with nothing being decided..

meaning: to do something completely to the end
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 切れない

examples.japanese: この部屋に100人は入り切れない。
examples.english: This room cannot fit 100 people.

examples.japanese: 彼は使い切れないほど金がある。
examples.english: He has more money than he can spend.

examples.japanese: このお酒は強すぎて、飲み切れなかった。
examples.english: This liquor is too strong, I couldn't finish drinking it all.

examples.japanese: いっぱい注文しないで、二人で食べ切れないから。
examples.english: Don't order so much, we won't be able to eat it all with just the 2 of us.

examples.japanese: 明日のテストまでには、全ての文法は勉強し切れないな。
examples.english: I won't be able to finish studying all of the grammar before tomorrow's test.

examples.japanese: ご飯の量が多くて食べ切れないよ。
examples.english: I can’t finish the rice because there is too much.

meaning: only; just; as much as ~
structure: Verb (た form) + きりっきり | Noun

examples.japanese: 私は一人きりで暮らすのが嫌だ。
examples.english: I don't want to live all alone.

examples.japanese: 二人っきりで話をしたいです。
examples.english: I want to talk privately with you, just the two of us.

examples.japanese: 彼女に会ったのは１回きりです。
examples.english: I've only met her one time.

examples.japanese: 今日は寒いから、Ｔシャツ一枚きりで外に出たら寒いよ。
examples.english: It's cold out today, so if you go out with just one t-shirt you're gonna be cold.

examples.japanese: 彼女とは別れたきり、一度も会っていない。
examples.english: I haven't met with her at all since we broke up.

examples.japanese: その男の人は、森に入ったきり、帰ってきませんでした。
examples.english: That man hasn't come back since he entered the woods.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Verb + っけ | Noun + (だ / だった) | な-adjective + (だ / だった) | い-adjective + いかった

examples.japanese: 次のテストっていつだっけ？
examples.english: When is the next test again?

examples.japanese: あなたの誕生日、いつだったっけ？
examples.english: When was your birthday again?

examples.japanese: どこに住んでいるんだっけ？
examples.english: Where did you live again?

examples.japanese: 自己紹介したっけ？
examples.english: Have I already introduced myself?

examples.japanese: 何の話をしていたっけ？
examples.english: What were we talking about again?

examples.japanese: 誰だっけ？
examples.english: Who were you again? (I can't seem to remember)

meaning: do something together
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 込むこむ

examples.japanese: この紙に必要な情報を書き込んでください。
examples.english: Please write the necessary information on this paper.

examples.japanese: あなたの口座にお金を振り込んだよ。
examples.english: I transferred the money to your account.

examples.japanese: すみません、この商品をどこに入れ込んだほうがいいですか。
examples.english: Sorry, where should I put this product?

examples.japanese: クレジットカードで支払ったら、ここにカードを差し込んでください。
examples.english: If you will pay by credit card, insert your card here.

examples.japanese: この薬の使い方は鼻から吸い込むことです。
examples.english: This medicine is used by breathing it in through your nose.

examples.japanese: 今日は１時間走り込んだ。
examples.english: Today I ran for 1 hour.

meaning: precisely because ~
structure: Noun + こそ

examples.japanese: これこそ望むところです。
examples.english: This is the very thing I want.

examples.japanese: こちらこそありがとうございます。
examples.english: It is I that should be saying thank you.

examples.japanese: 今年こそJLPTに受かりたい。
examples.english: This year I want to finally pass the JLPT.

examples.japanese: これこそ私がずっと探していたものです。
examples.english: I've been searching forever for this!

examples.japanese: 今度こそ試合に勝ちたいです。
examples.english: This time for sure I want to win this match!

examples.japanese: ゆっくりした方法こそ安全な方法だ。
examples.english: The slow way is the safe way.

meaning: how…!; what…!
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + こと | Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 大声を出さないこと。
examples.english: Don't speak with a loud voice.

examples.japanese: 晩ごはんの前にデザートを食べないこと。
examples.english: No eating dessert before dinner.

examples.japanese: お金を大切にすること。
examples.english: Use your money wisely.

examples.japanese: 休むときは、必ず学校に連絡すること。
examples.english: You must contact the school when you want to take a day off.

examples.japanese: どうしても必要な場合以外には使わないこと。
examples.english: It should not be used unless absolutely necessary.

examples.japanese: 学校の規則を守ること。
examples.english: You must follow school rules.

meaning: how…!; what…!
structure: Verb (casual) + ことから | Noun + である/だった | な-adjective + である/だった | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 道路が濡れていることから、雨が降ったということが分かる。
examples.english: Considering the ground is wet, I know that it must have rained.

examples.japanese: 教室で席が隣だったことから友人になった。
examples.english: We became good friends from the fact that our seats were right next to each other in the classroom.

examples.japanese: 日本語能力試験のN3に合格していないことから、彼は日本に行くことができない。
examples.english: From the fact that he hasn't passed the JLPT N3, he is not able to go to Japan.

examples.japanese: 毛の色が白いことからシロという名前がつけられる犬や猫は多い。
examples.english: Many dogs and cats are named "Shiro" (white) from the fact that their fur color is white.

examples.japanese: この問題は緊急性が低いことから、今まであまり注目されてこなかった。
examples.english: From the fact that this problem is of low urgency, it has not been given much attention until now.

examples.japanese: ガラスが割れていることから、どろぼうが家に入ったと分かりました。
examples.english: Because the glass was broken, I knew that a burglar had entered the house.

meaning: emphasize speaker's feelings; to my (surprise/etc)
structure: Verb (dictionary form)Verb (ない form) + ことになっていることになっています | Noun + という

examples.japanese: この図書館では2週間まで本が借りられることになっています。
examples.english: At this library, you can borrow books for up to 2 weeks.

examples.japanese: 日本では、車は左側を走ることになっている。
examples.english: In Japan, cars drive on the left side of the road.

examples.japanese: 授業中は、携帯電話を使ってはいけないことになっている。
examples.english: Cellphones are not allowed to be used during class.

examples.japanese: 60点以上が合格ということになっている。
examples.english: Over 60 points is a passing score.

examples.japanese: この部屋には、関係者以外入ってはいけないことになっている。
examples.english: Only authorized personnel are allowed to enter this room.

examples.japanese: 燃えるゴミは、毎週の月曜日と木曜日に捨てることになっています。
examples.english: Burnable garbage is to be thrown out every week on Mondays and Thursdays.

meaning: there is no need to; unnecessary; no match for ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことはない

examples.japanese: 謝ることはないよ。
examples.english: There is no need for you to apologize

examples.japanese: 明日のテストは簡単だから、心配することはないよ。
examples.english: Tomorrow's test will be easy, so it's nothing to worry about.

examples.japanese: 何も怖がることはない。
examples.english: You have nothing to fear.

examples.japanese: 時間は十分あるから急ぐことはない。
examples.english: There is plenty of time so there is no need to rush.

examples.japanese: 自分を責めることはない。
examples.english: There's no need to blame yourself..

examples.japanese: ただの風邪ですから、心配することはないよ。
examples.english: It's just a basic cold, so there is no need to worry.

meaning: but; although; despite ~
structure: Verb (casual) + ことは + same verb + が | な-adj. + な + same な-adj. | い-adj. + same い-adj.

examples.japanese: パーティーは行けることは行けるが、たぶん1時間くらい遅刻する。
examples.english: I can go to the party, but I will probably be about 1 hour late.

examples.japanese: N3の勉強をしたことはしたが、合格できるか自信がない。
examples.english: Although I studied for the JLPT N3, I don't have confidence I can pass...

examples.japanese: 新しいゲームも面白いことは面白いが、昔のゲームのほうが好きだ。
examples.english: New games are still interesting, but I prefer older games.

examples.japanese: 日本語は話せることは話せるんですが、日常会話しかできません。
examples.english: I can speak Japanese, but can only do daily conversation stuff.

examples.japanese: このレストランの食事はおいしいことはおいしいが、値段が高すぎる。
examples.english: Although the food in this restaurant is delicious, the prices are too high.

examples.japanese: 彼女のことは好きなことは好きだが、結婚したいほどではない。
examples.english: Although I love her, it’s not like I want to marry her.

meaning: it seems like; I heard; apparently ~
structure: まるで + Verb (casual form) + よう | Noun + のよう

examples.japanese: 合格した！まるで夢のようだ。
examples.english: I passed! It’s like a dream!

examples.japanese: すごい！まるで魔法のようだ！
examples.english: Amazing! It's just like magic!

examples.japanese: あの女の人は、美しくて、優しくて、まるで天使のようだ。
examples.english: That lady is beautiful and kind like an angel.

examples.japanese: 彼の日本語はまるで日本人が話しているように聞こえる。
examples.english: His Japanese is so natural that he sounds like a native speaker.

examples.japanese: 最近できたロボットは、まるで本物の人間のように動きます。
examples.english: Recently made robots move just like real humans.

examples.japanese: あの二人はまるで兄弟のようによく似ている。
examples.english: Those two look so much alike that they could be twins.

meaning: cannot be (impossible)
structure: まさか + Negative clause

examples.japanese: まさかそうなるとは思わなかった。
examples.english: That's the last thing I expected.

examples.japanese: 僕はまさかそんなことはできないよ。
examples.english: I could never do such a thing.

examples.japanese: 私はまさかここで彼に会えるとは思わなかった。
examples.english: I never thought that I could see him here.

examples.japanese: まさかカギをなくしたのではないでしょうね！
examples.english: You surely haven't lost the key!

examples.japanese: まさか彼女がそんなことを言ったとは思えない。
examples.english: She could not possibly of said such a thing.

examples.japanese: まさかあれは私たちの探している家じゃないだろう。
examples.english: Surely that wouldn't be the house we're looking for.

meaning: not really, not particularly
structure: めったに + Verb (ない form) | Noun + は + めったにない

examples.japanese: 彼はめったに本を読まない。
examples.english: He rarely reads books.

examples.japanese: 彼女はめったに遊びに来ない。
examples.english: She rarely comes to see me.

examples.japanese: 彼はめったに泣かない。
examples.english: He rarely cries.

examples.japanese: このところでは滅多に雪が降りません。
examples.english: It rarely snows in this area.

examples.japanese: 忙しくて滅多に休みが取れない。
examples.english: I’m so busy that I can hardly take time off work.

examples.japanese: 彼女は週末に出勤することは滅多にない。
examples.english: She seldom works weekends.

meaning: let alone; not to mention; needless to say ~
structure: Noun-1 + も + Verb（ば form) + Noun-2 + も | Noun + なら | な-adj + なら | い-adj + いければ

examples.japanese: 本を読むのが好きな人もいれば、嫌いな人もいます。
examples.english: If there are people who like to read books, there will also be people who dislike it.

examples.japanese: 学生の態度もわるければ教師の態度もわるい。
examples.english: If the student's attitude is bad, then the teacher's attitude will also be bad.

examples.japanese: 人生は楽しいこともあれば、苦しいこともある。
examples.english: In life, there are both ups and downs.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語もできれば英語もできる。
examples.english: He can speak both English and Japanese.

examples.japanese: あのメキシコ料理屋の食べ物は、値段も安ければ味もいいです。
examples.english: That Mexican restaurant has cheap prices and also the food tastes good.

examples.japanese: 私の彼氏はタバコも吸わなければ、お酒も飲まない。
examples.english: My boyfriend neither smokes nor drinks.

meaning: might; perhaps; indicates possibility
structure: もしかしたらもしかすると + phrase + かもしれない

examples.japanese: もしかしたら、明日行けないかもしれない。
examples.english: I might not be able to come tomorrow.

examples.japanese: もしかしたら病気かもしれない。
examples.english: I might be sick.

examples.japanese: もしかしたら彼は気が変わるかもしれません。
examples.english: He might change his mind.

examples.japanese: もしかすると彼の話はうそかもしれない。
examples.english: It's possible his story may be a lie.

examples.japanese: もしかするとあそこに座っている人は有名な人かもしれない。
examples.english: That person sitting there could be a celebrity.

examples.japanese: もしかしたら彼は会社をやめたかもしれない。
examples.english: Perhaps he has quit his job.

meaning: in the event of; in the case that ~
structure: もしも + Verb (た form) + ら

examples.japanese: もしも明日は晴れたらピクニックに行きましょう。
examples.english: If it's sunny tomorrow, let's go out for a picnic.

examples.japanese: もしも日本に行けたら、大阪の友達に会いたいです。
examples.english: If I could go to Japan, I would like to meet my friends in Osaka.

examples.japanese: もしも試験を受けたら、合格したいです。
examples.english: In the case that I take the exam, I would like to pass.

examples.japanese: もしも地震が起きたら、この家は丈夫だから倒れない。
examples.english: In the case that an earthquake happens, this house is strong and will not collapse.

examples.japanese: もしも日本へ留学しなかったら、今ごろは結婚しているかもしれない。
examples.english: If I hadn't gone to study abroad in Japan, I might have been married by now.

examples.japanese: もしも時間があったら、ダンスを習いたいです。
examples.english: If I had the time, I would like to learn to dance.

meaning: suitable for ~
structure: Noun + 向けむけ

examples.japanese: 初心者向けのコースがありますか。
examples.english: Do you have a course for beginners?

examples.japanese: この映画は子供向けなので、大人は見てもつまらない。
examples.english: That movie is targeted for children, so it will be boring for adults who watch it.

examples.japanese: この家は、部屋が多くて、ファミリー向けだ。
examples.english: This house has a lot of rooms and is targeted towards families.

examples.japanese: 最近は、男性向けの料理教室が人気だ。
examples.english: Lately, cooking classes for men are popular.

examples.japanese: ピアノ初心者向けのいい曲を知りませんか。
examples.english: Do you know any good songs suitable for beginner piano players?

examples.japanese: 子供向けの絵本コーナーは、１３番の棚にあります。
examples.english: The children's picture book corner is at shelf number 13.

meaning: intended for; aimed at ~
structure: Noun + 向きむき

examples.japanese: この本は初心者向きである。
examples.english: This book is suitable for beginners.

examples.japanese: その映画は子供向きだ。
examples.english: This movie is suitable for children.

examples.japanese: このスキー場は初心者向きです。
examples.english: This ski resort is suitable for beginners.

examples.japanese: このプレゼントは10歳の女の子向きだ。
examples.english: This present is suitable for a 10 year old girl.

examples.japanese: 若い女性向きの小説を書いています。
examples.english: I'm writing a short novel for young women.

examples.japanese: こういう本は若い読者向きではない。
examples.english: These kinds of books are not suitable for young readers.

meaning: also; let alone; from the beginning
structure: むしろ + phrase

examples.japanese: 私はむしろ一人で行きたい。
examples.english: I would rather go alone.

examples.japanese: 私はむしろ電車で行くだろう。
examples.english: I would likely rather go by train.

examples.japanese: この商品は、女性をターゲットに作られたが、実際は、むしろ男性に人気があるようだ。
examples.english: This product was made targeting women, but it actually seems to be more popular with men.

examples.japanese: 遅くまで残業するより、むしろ早く帰ってしっかり頭と体を休んだほうが、効率がいい。
examples.english: Rather than working late with overtime, it's more effecient to head home early and rest ones mind and body.

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも優しくないから、急に優しくなるとうれしいというより、むしろこわい。
examples.english: He's normally not nice so when he suddenly become nice, rather than feeling happy, I was more so scared.

examples.japanese: 自由な考え方が必要とされる仕事は、大人よりむしろ小さい子供の方が得意かもしれません。
examples.english: For a job that requires more freedom of thought a small child might be more suited than an adult.

meaning: while; during; as; simultaneously
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + ながら（も） | Verb (て form) + い | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 狭いながらも、このマンションは大好きだ。
examples.english: Despite it being small, I love this apartment.

examples.japanese: 残念ながらも、今日のイベントに行けません。
examples.english: Unfortunately, I will not be able to go to today's event.

examples.japanese: うちは貧しいながらも、家族の仲がいいし、幸せだ。
examples.english: Even though my family is poor, we get along well and are happy.

examples.japanese: アナちゃんは子どもながらも、いろんなことを知っている。
examples.english: Although Anna-chan is just a child, she knows quite a lot of various things.

examples.japanese: 彼女はダイエットすると言っていながら、今日もアイスを食べている。
examples.english: She says she's going to diet, but she's eating ice cream again today.

examples.japanese: 悪いことだと知っていながら、彼女は平気で嘘をつく。
examples.english: Despite knowing what she's doing is wrong, she just plain lied about it.

meaning: there are times when
structure: Verb (ない form) + ことはない | Noun + ではない/じゃない | な-adjective + ではない/じゃない | い-adjective + いくない

examples.japanese: 走れば間に合わないことはないよ。急ごう！
examples.english: We can still make it if we run. Let’s hurry up!

examples.japanese: 嬉しくないことはないが、1位が良かった。
examples.english: It's not that I'm not happy, but I would have liked to of been 1st place.

examples.japanese: 車を運転できないことはないんですが、ほとんどしません。
examples.english: It’s not that I can’t drive, I just don’t do it very often.

examples.japanese: 鶏肉は、食べないことはないですが、あまり好きではありません。
examples.english: It's not that I don't eat chicken, I just don't like it that much.

examples.japanese: できないこともないですけど、少し時間をいただきたいです。
examples.english: It's not that I can't do it, but I would like to have some more time.

examples.japanese: 私も留学したことがありますから、あなたの苦労が分からないことはありません。
examples.english: I have studied abroad so I can understand what you’re going through.

meaning: can’t help but feel; can’t help but do; must do ~
structure: Verb (ない form) + と | Noun + でない / じゃない | な-adjective + でない / じゃない | い-adjective + いくない

examples.japanese: もう行かないと...
examples.english: I have to go now...

examples.japanese: 宿題をやらないと。
examples.english: I have to do my homework.

examples.japanese: もう暗くなって、帰らないと。
examples.english: It's already gotten dark, I need to head home.

examples.japanese: 早くしないと間に合わないよ。
examples.english: If you don't hurry, you won't make it in time.

examples.japanese: 早く寝ないと、明日起きられないよ。
examples.english: If you don't go to bed early, you won't be able to get up tomorrow.

examples.japanese: この値段より安くないと買わない。
examples.english: I won't buy it unless it is cheaper than this price.

meaning: not easy to; struggling to; not able to ~
structure: なかなか + Verb | Noun | Adjective

examples.japanese: なかなか面白そうです。
examples.english: That sounds quite interesting.

examples.japanese: 彼はなかなか本を読む。
examples.english: He reads quite a lot of books.

examples.japanese: この料理はなかなか美味しいですね。
examples.english: This food is quite good.

examples.japanese: 彼らはなかなか手ごわい相手ですね。
examples.english: They are pretty tough opponents.

examples.japanese: なかなかのドレスですね。君にとても似合うと思うよ。
examples.english: It's quite a nice dress, I think it suits you well.

examples.japanese: 車のエンジンがなかなかかからない。
examples.english: I can't seem to get the car to start.

pattern: なんか / なんて / など
meaning: such as; things like ~
structure: Noun + なんかなんてなど

examples.japanese: 試験も近いし、テレビなど見ている暇はない。
examples.english: Exams are close and I don't have time to do things like watch TV.

examples.japanese: 中国語やスペイン語など、仕事で役に立ちそうな外国語を勉強したいです。
examples.english: I want to study foreign languages that would be useful for work, like Chinese or Spanish.

examples.japanese: 彼は私なんかよりすごい人だよ。
examples.english: He is a much better man than I am.

examples.japanese: 彼は私などには目もくれようとしないだろう。
examples.english: He would never bother to notice (someone like) me.

examples.japanese: カラオケなんか行きたくない
examples.english: I don't really want to go to karaoke..

examples.japanese: 納豆なんて嫌いだ。
examples.english: I really hate natto (Japanese fermented soybean)

meaning: to do something completely to the end
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 直すなおす

examples.japanese: この作文はミスが多いから、書き直したほうがいいよ。
examples.english: This essay has a lot of mistakes, so you should do a rewrite.

examples.japanese: 彼に電話を掛け直すようにお願いしてもらえますか。
examples.english: Could you ask him to call me back?

examples.japanese: 私はその仕事をやり直すことになる。
examples.english: I ended up having to do that job over again.

examples.japanese: 家が古くなってきたので、建て直そうと思っています。
examples.english: This house is starting to get old, so I am thinking to have it rebuilt.

examples.japanese: あなたはその方法を分かりやすく書き直すべきです。
examples.english: You should rewrite that methodology so that it is easier to understand.

examples.japanese: 彼は人生をもう一度やり直す決心をした。
examples.english: He decided to start his life over again.

meaning: you could say; one might say; I'd say ~
structure: Verb (casual) + んだってんですって | Noun + な | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼、彼女ができたんだって。
examples.english: I heard he got a girlfriend.

examples.japanese: 知らないんだって。
examples.english: They said that they did not know.

examples.japanese: クリスさんがJLPTのN2合格したんだって。
examples.english: I heard that Chris passed the JLPT N2!

examples.japanese: 妹が結婚するんだって。
examples.english: I heard that my sister is going to get married.

examples.japanese: この店のカレー、美味しいんだって。
examples.english: I heard that this restaurant’s curry is delicious.

examples.japanese: 聞いた？トムさんは卒業したら国に帰るんだって。
examples.english: Did you hear? Tom is heading back to his home country after graduation.

meaning: it must be; it should be (expectation)
structure: Verb (casual form) + に違いない | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: それは痛いに違いない。
examples.english: I bet that hurts.

examples.japanese: 彼はまだ寝ているに違いない。
examples.english: I'm sure he's still sleeping.

examples.japanese: トムさんは車を７台も持っているから、お金持ちに違いない。
examples.english: Tom has 7 cars, so there's no doubt he's rich.

examples.japanese: あのレストランはいつも人が多いから、人気があるに違いない。
examples.english: That restuarant is always full of people so it's definitely a popular place.

examples.japanese: リサさんは３年も料理教室に通っているから、彼女の料理はきっと美味しいに違いない。
examples.english: Lisa has been going to cooking school for 3 years, so her food is surely delicious.

examples.japanese: 中国人は漢字をたくさん知っているから、きっと日本の漢字もすぐに覚えられるに違いない。
examples.english: Chinese people know a lot of kanji (chinese characters), so they can surely quickly learn Japanese characters as well.

meaning: compared to; in contrast to; unlike; while; whereas ~
structure: Noun + に反してに反する

examples.japanese: 彼の話は事実に反する。
examples.english: What he has said is contrary to the facts.

examples.japanese: 予想に反して彼は成功した。
examples.english: Contrary to my expectation, he succeeded.

examples.japanese: 社内でタバコを吸うのは社の規則に反する。
examples.english: Smoking in the office is against company rules.

examples.japanese: 予想に反して、試験はとても簡単だった。
examples.english: Contrary to my expectations, the test was very easy.

examples.japanese: 両親の期待に反して、彼は大学へ行かずアルバイトとして働いている。
examples.english: Contrary to the expectations of his parents, he is working a part-time job without going to University.

examples.japanese: 彼らは彼の意志に反して酒を飲ませた。
examples.english: They made him drink against his will.

meaning: through; from [A] to [B]
structure: Noun + にかけて（は）にかけて（も）

examples.japanese: テニスにかけては、彼に勝てる人はいない。
examples.english: There is no one who can beat him in tennis.

examples.japanese: マンガにかけては、私より詳しい人はいません。
examples.english: Regarding manga, there is nobody who knows as much as I do.

examples.japanese: 私はギターにかけては誰よりも詳しい。
examples.english: I am more knowledgeable about guitar than anyone.

examples.japanese: 弟は勉強はできないが、泳ぎにかけては誰にも負けない。
examples.english: Though my little brother’s not good at studying, he won’t lose to anyone at swimming.

examples.japanese: 漢字の知識にかけては誰にも負けない自信がある。
examples.english: I have confidence that I won't lose to anyone regarding knowledge of kanji.

examples.japanese: 彼はパソコンにかけて何の故障でも直せます。
examples.english: He can fix anything that's broken related to computers.

pattern: に関する / に関して
meaning: concerning; regarding; about; on ~
structure: Noun + に関して(は）に関する

examples.japanese: それに関しては彼は初心者だ。
examples.english: He is a beginner in regards to that.

examples.japanese: 配送に関して希望はありますか？
examples.english: Do you have any requests regarding delivery?

examples.japanese: 給料に関しては不満はない。
examples.english: I have no complaints regarding my salary.

examples.japanese: 彼の新しい小説は、日本文化に関するものだった。
examples.english: His latest novel was related to Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: この本には、交通規則に関することが書いてあります。
examples.english: This book is about traffic rules.

examples.japanese: 事故の原因に関して、現在調査が進められている。
examples.english: We are currently conducting the investigation regarding the cause of the accident.

pattern: にかわって / にかわり
structure: Noun (person) + にかわってにかわり

examples.japanese: 弟は、母にかわってご飯を作った。
examples.english: My little brother made dinner instead of my mom.

examples.japanese: 部長にかわり、私は会議に参加しました。
examples.english: I participated in the meeting instead of my manager.

examples.japanese: DVDにかわり、ブルーレイが使われるようになった。
examples.english: Bluray is starting to be used now instead of DVDs.

examples.japanese: 父にかわって一言お礼を申し上げます。
examples.english: I will say a word of thanks in place of my father.

examples.japanese: 来週の出張は大阪にかわって、京都に行くことになりました。
examples.english: Next week's business trip was changed from Osaka to Kyoto.

examples.japanese: 出張中の部長にかわって、私がごあいさつさせていただきます。

structure: Noun + に比べてに比べるとに比べればに比べ

examples.japanese: 昨日に比べて、今日は少し寒いね。
examples.english: It's a bit cold today compared to yesterday.

examples.japanese: ロンドンはパリに比べると大きい。
examples.english: London is large, compared with Paris.

examples.japanese: 以前に比べて、彼の日本語は上手になった。
examples.english: His Japanese is better than before.

examples.english: Compared with America or China, Japan is a small country.

examples.japanese: 東京に比べて、大阪のほうが物価が安い。
examples.english: In comparison to Tokyo, prices in Osaka are cheaper.

examples.japanese: アメリカでの生活は、日本に比べてどのような違いがありましたか？
examples.english: How was life in America different from life in Japan?

meaning: can; able to
structure: Noun + に慣れるになれる

examples.japanese: 私は日本の生活に慣れるまでが大変だった。
examples.english: It was tough before I got used to life in Japan.

examples.english: I am not used to getting up early.

examples.japanese: あなたはすぐに新しい大学生活に慣れるだろう。
examples.english: You'll likely quickly get used to your new college life.

examples.japanese: 彼は一人暮らしに慣れている。
examples.english: He is used to living alone.

examples.japanese: 彼は新しい会社で働くことに慣れているだろう。
examples.english: He probably is used to working at the new company.

examples.japanese: 外国人が日本の食事に慣れることは難しい。
examples.english: It is difficult for foreigners to get used to Japanese food.

pattern: において / における
meaning: concerning; regarding; about; on ~
structure: Noun + においてにおける + Noun

examples.japanese: 私は全てにおいて頑張ります。
examples.english: I do my best with everything.

examples.japanese: 当時においては、海外旅行など夢のようなことだった。
examples.english: Back then, traveling abroad was like a dream.

examples.japanese: だいたいにおいて春に雨がよく降る。
examples.english: It generally rains a lot in Spring.

examples.japanese: 今度のオリンピックは東京において開催される。
examples.english: The upcoming Olympics will be held in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 人生において一番大切なことは、後悔しないように自分がしたいことをすることだと思う。
examples.english: The most important thing in my life is to do what I want to do without regret.

examples.japanese: 車内における携帯電話のご利用はご遠慮ください。
examples.english: Please refrain from using mobile phones inside the car.

meaning: for; considering it’s (something or someone)
structure: Verb (casual) + にしても | Noun + (である) | な-adjective + (である) | い-adjective

examples.japanese: どちらにしても賛成できない。
examples.english: In either case I cannot agree.

examples.japanese: いずれにしても同じ結果になる。
examples.english: Either way, both lead to the same result.

examples.japanese: それにしても、日本は良い国ですね！
examples.english: Regardless, Japan is a great country!

examples.japanese: 何をするにしても、よく考えてから行動しなさい。
examples.english: Regardless of what you do, make sure you think carefully before you take action.

examples.japanese: 今回の試験は合格したにしても、点数はあまりよくないと思う。
examples.english: Even if I pass this test, I don’t think I’ll have a high score.

examples.japanese: 誰がやったにしても、私たち全員で責任を取らなければならない。
examples.english: Regardless of who did it, we must all take responsibility.

meaning: regardless of whether ~
structure: Verb (casual) + にしては | Noun

examples.japanese: 今４月にしては、ちょっと暑いですね。
examples.english: It's a bit hot for April.

examples.japanese: 初めてケーキを作ったにしては、上手にできましたね。
examples.english: You did a good job with the cake considering it was your first time.

examples.japanese: あの人は５０歳にしては、ずいぶん若く見える。
examples.english: That person looks considerably young for 50.

examples.japanese: 外国人にしては日本語が上手だ。
examples.english: For a foreigner, his Japanese is very good.

examples.japanese: この子は小学生にしてはずいぶんしっかりしている。
examples.english: For an elementary school student, this kid sure has himself in order.

examples.japanese: 彼は勉強しなかったにしては、いい点が取れた。
examples.english: For someone who didn't do their homework, he still managed to get a decent score.

meaning: against; contrary to; in contrast to ~
structure: Noun + に対して

examples.japanese: 彼は女性に対しては優しい。
examples.english: He is kind towards her.

examples.japanese: お客さんに対して、そのような言葉遣いをしてはいけません。
examples.english: You must not speak towards customers that way.

examples.japanese: 私の先生は男の子に対して厳しいが、女の子に対しては優しい。
examples.english: My teacher is strict with boys but gentle with girls.

examples.japanese: 目上の人に対して敬意を示さなければなりません。
examples.english: We must show respect to our superiors.

examples.japanese: 子供に対して短気を起こしてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't be impatient with children.

examples.japanese: 彼の意見に対して、反対の人は手をあげてください。
examples.english: Raise your hand if any of you are opposed to his opinion.

meaning: whenever; every time ~
structure: Noun + にとって（は/も）

examples.japanese: 私にとって、漢字の勉強はとても楽しい。
examples.english: For me, studying kanji is a lot of fun!

examples.japanese: あなたにとって、一番大切な物は何ですか？
examples.english: What is the most important thing for you?

examples.japanese: 家族は私にとって、一番大切な物です。
examples.english: For me, the most important thing is family.

examples.japanese: 水は人間の体にとって必要なものだ。
examples.english: Water is essential for the human body.

examples.japanese: スポーツ選手にとって、健康管理はとても重要です。
examples.english: For athletes, health management is extremely important.

examples.japanese: 転校は、子どもにとって大きな変化だ。
examples.english: Changing schools is a big change for a child.

meaning: towards; against; regarding; in contrast with​ ~
structure: Noun + について

examples.japanese: この問題についてどう思いますか。
examples.english: What do you think about this problem?

examples.japanese: あなたの国についていろいろと教えてください。

examples.japanese: その事件について、知っていることを全部話してください。
examples.english: Please tell me everything you know regarding that incident.

examples.english: I had my doctor explain to me about the medicine I am taking now.

examples.japanese: 大学では国際ビジネスについて研究したいと思っています。
examples.english: I am thinking about studying international business in university.

examples.japanese: 明日、私は自分の国の料理について発表します。
examples.english: Tomorrow, I will give a presentation on food in my home country.

meaning: concerning; regarding; about; on ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + につれてにつれ | Noun

examples.english: As the typhoon came closer, the wind gradually got stronger.

examples.japanese: 日本語が上手になるにつれて、日本での生活が楽しくなってきた。
examples.english: As I continued to improve my Japanese, life in Japan became more enjoyable.

examples.japanese: 年をとるにつれて、髪の色が白くなるのは普通だ。
examples.english: It is normal for one's hair to turn white as they age.

examples.japanese: 子供たちが大きくなるにつれ、母親であることが楽になってきた。
examples.english: As the kids get older, being a mother gets easier.

examples.japanese: 時がたつにつれて、愛が深くなる。
examples.english: Love grows with time.

examples.japanese: 試験が近づくにつれて彼は不安になってきた。
examples.english: As the exam drew near, he became more anxious.

meaning: for; in order to; for the benefit of; because of; as a result of ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + には

examples.japanese: 日本語が上手になるには、どうしたらいいですか。
examples.english: What should I do to improve my Japanese?

examples.japanese: 図書館の本を借りるには、このカードが必要です。
examples.english: In order to borrow a book from the library, you need this card.

examples.english: I work overtime everyday to save money to get my kids into a good university.

examples.japanese: お酒を購入するには、２０歳以上であることを証明できるものが必要です。
examples.english: To buy alcohol, you need something to prove you are at least 20 years of age.

examples.japanese: 私がその口座を解約するにはどうしたらいいか。
examples.english: What should I do in order to close that account?

meaning: as; therefore; in accordance with; according to; consequently ~

examples.english: According to the weather report, tomorrow it looks like it will rain.

examples.english: According to what I heard, they have broken up.

examples.english: According to the teacher, this grammar point is unlikely to appear on the JLPT.

examples.english: According to my teacher, next year’s university entrance exam is going to be more difficult.

examples.english: According to the quick TV report, the earthquake just now was a magnitude 5.

examples.english: That medicine has strong side effects depending on the person.

examples.japanese: これは有名な作家によって書かれた小説です。
examples.english: This is a novel that was written by a famous author.

examples.japanese: 習慣は国によって異なる。
examples.english: Customs differ from one country to another.

examples.english: I wonder if it will be clear tomorrow.

examples.english: I wonder what we should do to resolve this issue?

examples.english: Sorry, Is this the correct amount of money?

examples.japanese: なぜ日本人は英語が苦手なのでしょうか？
examples.english: Why are Japanese people not good with English?

examples.english: To study Japanese with a focus on grammar.

examples.english: That story is written around her life story.

examples.english: In Tokyo, there are many tourist attractions like Tokyo Tower and so on.

examples.english: There are many interesting Japanese anime, like Dragon Ball and so on.

examples.japanese: 会議には中国をはじめ、アジアの国々が参加した。

examples.english: To help support my husband, every day I make him a lunch box full of my love.

examples.japanese: 彼女は故郷への思いを込めて、その曲を作ったそうだ。

examples.japanese: 父の日には、いつも頑張っている父に感謝の気持ちを込めてプレゼントを贈りました。
examples.english: On father's day, I sent a present full of my gratitude to my always hard-working father.

examples.japanese: 大学受験の日、息子が合格しますようにの願いを込めてお弁当を作った。

examples.japanese: 後ろのほうの人にも聞こえるよう、マイクを通して話した。

examples.japanese: 私たちは本や授業を通じて、様々な知識を得ている。
examples.english: We are gaining various information through books and class.

structure: Verb (casual) + おかげで | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んだおかげで、すっかり元気になりました。

examples.japanese: 日本語を習ったおかげで、いい仕事を見つけることができました。
examples.english: I was able to find a good job because I learned Japanese.

examples.japanese: 友達のおかげで、私は今の彼女と出会うことができました。
examples.english: Thanks to my friend, I was able to meet my current girlfriend.

examples.japanese: あの小学生は、大人っぽい。
examples.english: That elementary school student is very adult-like.

examples.japanese: 朝起きると顔が油っぽいです。
examples.english: My face is oily when I wake up in the morning.

examples.japanese: この牛乳は水っぽくて、美味しくない。
examples.english: This milk is a little watery and doesn't taste very good.

examples.japanese: この靴、デザインはいいけれど、生地が安っぽいね。
examples.english: These shoes have a nice design, but the material looks cheap.

meaning: if only; as long as ~

meaning: still; yet​; furthermore; in addition ~

examples.japanese: 彼は父親よりさらに背が高い。
examples.english: He is even taller than his father.

examples.japanese: いらっしゃい！いらっしゃい！今日はいつもよりさらにお安くなっていますよ！
examples.english: Welcome, welcome! Today everything is even cheaper than usual!

examples.japanese: こちらの料理には、すこし塩を足すと、さらに美味しくなりますよ。
examples.english: With this food, by adding a little bit of salt it will become even more delicious.

examples.japanese: 私はそれについてさらに知りたい。
examples.english: I want to know even more about that.

examples.japanese: 彼は料理を2人分も食べた。さらに、食後にケーキも食べた。
examples.english: He ate enough for 2 people. Furthermore, after that he also ate some cake.

examples.japanese: うちの近所は犬が3匹飼ったのに、さらに猫や魚も飼います。本当に動物が大好きだ。
examples.english: Our neighbors have 3 dogs. In addition, they have a cat and fish too. They really love animals.

meaning: more or less; pretty much; roughly; tentatively ~
structure: さて + clause

examples.japanese: さてどうしよう。
examples.english: What shall I do now?

examples.japanese: さてクイズの時間です。
examples.english: Now it's time for a quiz.

examples.japanese: さて、お昼にしましょう。
examples.english: Well, let's have lunch.

examples.japanese: さてこの人は誰でしょうか。
examples.english: Then, who is this person?

examples.japanese: さて本題にはいろうか。
examples.english: Well, let's get down to business.

examples.japanese: さてやってみるとなるとなかなか難しいものだ。
examples.english: When one comes to doing it, one finds it rather difficult.

meaning: thanks to; owing to; because of ~
structure: Verb (casual) + せい（で/に) | Noun + の | Adjective

examples.japanese: さっきコーヒーを飲んだせいで、なかなか寝られません。
examples.english: Because I drank coffee a little while ago, I can't seem to fall asleep.

examples.japanese: 頭が痛い。疲れたせいかな。
examples.english: My head hurts. Maybe it's because I am tired..

examples.japanese: バスが遅れたせいで、授業に遅れてしまった。
examples.english: I was late for class because my bus was late.

examples.japanese: あなたの失敗を、私のせいにしないでよ！
examples.english: Don't blame me for your mistake!

examples.japanese: 体調が悪かったせいで、試験に集中できなかった。
examples.english: As a result of not feeling well, I wasn't able to concentrate on the exam.

examples.japanese: バスが遅れたせいで、飛行機に乗れなかった。
examples.english: I missed my flight because the bus was late.

meaning: very; greatly; much; to a large extent
structure: せいぜい + Noun (period of time) | Verb

examples.japanese: せいぜい頑張ろうね！
examples.english: Let's give it our all!

examples.japanese: せいぜい楽しんで行ってください。
examples.english: Enjoy yourself to the fullest!

examples.japanese: 彼はせいぜい３０歳ぐらいだ。
examples.english: He's 30 years old at most.

examples.japanese: せいぜいがんばって練習しなさい。
examples.english: Practice as hard as you can.

examples.japanese: 彼は稼いでもせいぜい月に20万円だ。
examples.english: He earns no more than 200,000 yen a month.

examples.japanese: 桜の花は数日、せいぜい一週間しか持たない。
examples.english: Cherry blossoms last only for a few days, a week at the most.

meaning: while; during~ something happened
structure: しばらく + clause

examples.japanese: しばらくここで待てください。
examples.english: Please wait here for a while.

examples.japanese: こんにちは。しばらくですね！
examples.english: Hello, it's been a while!

examples.japanese: 私はしばらく暇です。
examples.english: I have free time for a while.

examples.japanese: しばらく考える時間をください。
examples.english: Please give me some time to think about it.

examples.japanese: しばらくお待ちくださいますか？
examples.english: Could you please wait for a moment?

examples.japanese: 来年からしばらく海外に住むつもりです。
examples.english: From next year, I plan to live abroad for a while.

meaning: to have no choice but ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + しかないしかなかったしかありません

examples.japanese: やるしかない。
examples.english: You just gotta do it.

examples.japanese: 卒業できなかったから、バイトをするしかない。
examples.english: Because I did not graduate, my only option is part time work.

examples.japanese: パソコンが直せないから、新しいのを買うしかなかった。
examples.english: My computer could not be fixed so I had no choice but to buy a new one.

examples.japanese: 電車もバスも止まってしまったから、歩くしかない。
examples.english: Since the train and bus are not working, there is no choice but to walk.

examples.japanese: あの大学に合格したかったら、毎日勉強するしかないですよ。
examples.english: If you want to get into that university, you need to study every single day.

examples.japanese: コンビニでお弁当を買ったらお箸が入ってなかったので、手で食べるしかなかった。
examples.english: I bought a bento lunch box from a convenient store, but there were no chopsticks included so I had to eat it by hand.

meaning: [A] is [B]; the reason for [A] is [B]
structure: Goal + そのため（に） + action

examples.japanese: あなたは明日、そのための時間がありますか？
examples.english: Do you have time tomorrow for that?

examples.japanese: 私はそのための時間が取れない。
examples.english: I cannot take time for that.

examples.japanese: でも、そのためには、たくさんの努力が必要です。
examples.english: However, a lot of effort is needed for that act.

examples.japanese: 私は留学したいです。そのためには、英語を学ぶ必要がある。
examples.english: I want to study abroad. To that purpose, I need to learn English.

examples.japanese: そのために英語で話せるようになりたい。
examples.english: I want to become able to speak English for that reason.

examples.japanese: 英語の教師になりたいです。そのためにいろいろな資格も取らないといけません。
examples.english: I want to become an English teacher. In order to do so, I need to obtain various certifications.

meaning: both; or; otherwise​; choice between [A] or [B]
structure: それとも + phrase

examples.japanese: 歩こうか, それとも車で行こうか？
examples.english: Shall we walk or drive?

examples.japanese: コーヒーはホットにしますか？それともアイスにしますか？
examples.english: Do you want your coffee hot, or would you prefer iced?

examples.japanese: 地下鉄で行きますか。それともJRで行きますか。
examples.english: Will you go by subway or by the JR line?

examples.japanese: 飲み物はコーヒーにしますか？それとも紅茶にしますか？
examples.english: For your drink, would you like coffee or tea?

examples.japanese: 始めましょうか。それとも、校長先生がお見えになるまでお待ちしましょうか？
examples.english: Shall we start? Or shall we wait until the headmaster arrives?

examples.japanese: 話し合って決めましょうか。それとも私が決めてしまってもいいですか。
examples.english: Shall we discuss and decide together? Or is it OK for me to decide on my own?

pattern: そうもない /そうにない
meaning: seems like; looks like ~
structure: Verb (ます stem) ます + そうもないそうにない

examples.japanese: 先生、明日までに宿題ができそうにないんですが、もう少し待っていただけませんか。
examples.english: Teacher, I won't be able to finish my homework by tomorrow, could I possibly get an extension?

examples.japanese: そんなことは起りそうもないですね。
examples.english: That does not seem likely to occur.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは一人のカでは完成できそうにない。
examples.english: With this project it doesn't look like it will be finished with only one person's power.

examples.japanese: すみません、今日中に仕事を終わりそうにないんですが、明日でもよろしいでしょうか。
examples.english: Sorry, it doesn't look like this work will be finished today. Is it alright if I get it to you tomorrow?

examples.japanese: できそうもないことを、簡単に引き受けるな。
examples.english: Don't take on things that you can't do easily.

examples.japanese: どう考えても彼と私が再会することはありそうもないのだ。
examples.english: He and I would likely never meet again.

meaning: already; now; no longer; not anymore
structure: すでに + clause

examples.japanese: 彼らはすでに外出してしまいました。
examples.english: They already went out.

examples.japanese: あなたはすでに朝ご飯を食べましたか？
examples.english: Have you already eaten breakfast?

examples.japanese: もしかしたら、彼女はすでにそれを送っているかもしれない。
examples.english: Perhaps, she may have sent it already.

examples.japanese: 彼が駅に着いたとき、列車はすでに３０分前に出発していた。
examples.english: When he arrived at the station, the train had already left 30 minutes before.

examples.japanese: 私はすでに1,000人以上からフォローされている。
examples.english: I've already been followed by more than 1,000 users.

examples.japanese: あなたはすでに明日の出張の準備をしていますか。
examples.english: Have you already prepared for the business trip tomorrow?

meaning: in other words; in summary; in short ~
structure: すなわち + phrase

examples.japanese: 妹の娘、すなわち、めいは、近所に住んでいるのでよく遊びに来ます。
examples.english: My younger sister's daughter, in other words my niece, lives nearby so I often visit.

examples.japanese: 母の父、すなわちわたしの祖父は現在６３歳です。
examples.english: My mother’s father, in other words my grandfather, is 63 years old.

examples.japanese: 夫の兄の妻、すなわち、義理の姉は料理が上手で優しい人です。
examples.english: My husband's older brother's wife, in other words my sister-in-law, is good at cooking and a nice person.

examples.japanese: このタンクには1,000ミリリットル、すなわち１リットルの水が入っています。
examples.english: There are 1,000 milliliters, in other words 1 liter of water in this tank.

examples.japanese: ４０人中１０人、すなわち、クラスの４分の１がインフルエンザで学校を休んでいます。
examples.english: 10 out of 40 people, in other words 1/4 of the class are missing school from influenza.

examples.japanese: 体力テストの持久走では、１キロメートル、すなわち１０００メートルを走らなければいけません。
examples.english: For the physical exam marathon training, you must run 1 kilometer, in other words 1,000 meters.

meaning: at least; at most ~
structure: 数量(quantity; volume; amount) + は

examples.japanese: 今日はゆっくり休むと言ったけど、１時間は仕事をしました。
examples.english: I said I would rest today, but I still worked for at least an hour or so.

examples.japanese: この映画は面白かったので、３回は見ました。
examples.english: I watched this movie at least three times now because it was interesting

examples.japanese: 毎年、１回は海外へ旅行します。
examples.english: Every year, I go travel abroad at least once.

examples.japanese: 毎日7時間は寝るようにしています。
examples.english: I make sure to sleep at least 7 hours every day.

examples.japanese: あまり時間がないだが、毎週一回はボランティア活動をしています。
examples.english: I don't have much time, but I do volunteer activities at least once a week.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、毎日30分は運動をします。
examples.english: For my health, I workout at least 30 minutes every day.

meaning: something like; something called ~
structure: Verb (た form) + ものだ

examples.japanese: 子どものころはよく川で遊んだものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, I often played at the river.

examples.japanese: 学生時代は毎日図書館へ通ったものだ。
examples.english: When I was a student, I used to go to the library everyday.

examples.japanese: 子供の時は、よく友達とテニスをしたものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, I often played tennis with my friends.

examples.japanese: 日本へ留学した時、すしをよく食べたものだ。
examples.english: When I studied abroad in Japan, I often ate sushi.

examples.japanese: 子供の頃は寝る前に母はいつも本を読んでくれたものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, my mother would always read a book to me before going to sleep.

examples.japanese: 高校生の時は、よく友達とサッカーをしたものだ。
examples.english: During my high school days, I often played soccer with my friends.

meaning: in the case of~; assuming~; if A then B
structure: Verb (た form) + とたん

examples.japanese: 家を出たとたん、雨が降ってきた。
examples.english: It started raining after I left my house.

examples.japanese: 窓を開けたとたん、強い風が入ってきた。
examples.english: As soon as I opened the window, a strong wind came in.

examples.japanese: 旅行から帰ってきたとたん、風邪を引いてしまった。
examples.english: I caught a cold just after I got back from travelling.

examples.japanese: 疲れていたので、ベッドに入ったとたん、眠ってしまった。
examples.english: I was really tired and fell asleep right after getting in bed.

examples.japanese: 夏は窓を開けたとたん、蚊が入ってくる。
examples.english: In summer, after opening the window mosquitoes will come inside.

examples.japanese: その二人は、出会ったとたんに、恋に落ちたそうです。
examples.english: Those two apparently fell in love after meeting each other.

meaning: when; at this time
structure: Noun + の + たびに | Verb (dictionary form)

examples.japanese: この曲を聞くたびに、家族を思い出す。
examples.english: Every time I hear this song, it reminds me of my family.

examples.japanese: 友人は旅行のたびにお土産を買ってきてくれます。
examples.english: Every time my friend travels, they buy me a souvenir.

examples.japanese: あの人を会うたびに用事を頼まれる。
examples.english: That person asks me for favors every time I see them.

examples.japanese: ミスをするたびに部長にしかられる。
examples.english: Every time I make a mistake my boss chews me out.

examples.japanese: 買い物のたびに、袋をたくさんもらう。
examples.english: I always get a lot of bags every time I go shopping.

examples.japanese: YouTubeを見るたびに、広告が表示されるのはうんざりだ。
examples.english: I'm sick of adds popping up every time I watch videos on YouTube.

meaning: because of; given that; since ~
structure: Verb + ため（に） | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 日本へ旅行をするために、貯金しています。
examples.english: I'm saving money to travel to Japan.

examples.japanese: 彼氏に会うために、東京に行きます。
