examples.english: I'm going to Tokyo to see my boyfriend.

examples.japanese: 今度の面接のために、このスーツを買いました。
examples.english: I bought this suit for my upcoming interview.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、毎朝に走っています。
examples.english: For my health, I go running every morning.

examples.japanese: 私たちには、皆が公平に扱われるための、明確な一連の規則が必要だ。
examples.english: We need a clear set of rules whereby everyone is treated fairly.

examples.japanese: 来週の試験のため、漢字を勉強しておきました。
examples.english: I studied my kanji in preparation for next week's exam.

meaning: surely; undoubtedly; almost certainly; most likely
structure: 確かに + phrase

examples.japanese: それは確かにそのように見えます。
examples.english: That certainly looks that way.

examples.japanese: 私は確かに少し疲れている。
examples.english: I'm certainly a little tired..

examples.japanese: 僕は、彼女の言うことが確かに正しいと思う。
examples.english: I think what she's saying is correct.

examples.japanese: 確かに君の責任ではない。
examples.english: I'm sure that's no fault of yours.

examples.japanese: 彼は確かに立派な人だと思う。
examples.english: I’m sure he’s a wonderful person.

examples.japanese: 確かに、このペンはとても書きやすいです。
examples.english: This pen is certainly very easy to write with.

meaning: to finish doing ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + たて

examples.japanese: 焼きたてのパンは美味しいよ。ちょっと食べてみる？
examples.english: Freshly baked bread is delicious. Do you want to try some?

examples.japanese: あのスーパーは取りたての新鮮な野菜を売っている。
examples.english: That supermarket sells freshly picked vegetables.

examples.japanese: やっぱり料理はできたてが美味しいね。
examples.english: As expected, freshly cooked food is delicious!

examples.japanese: これは炊きたてのご飯です。温かいうちに食べなさい。
examples.english: This is freshly made rice. Please eat while it is still warm.

examples.japanese: 母の作りたてのご飯はいい匂いがする。
examples.english: My mother's freshly made dinner smells really good.

examples.japanese: この出来たての豚かつはさくさくしていますね。
examples.english: This freshly made pork cutlet is really nice and crispy.

meaning: no matter how ~
structure: たとえ + Verb (て form) + も | Noun + でも | な-adjective + でも | い-adjective + いくても

examples.japanese: たとえ彼は忙しくても来るよ。
examples.english: Even if he is busy, he will come.

examples.japanese: たとえ明日雨が降っても私は出かけるつもりです。
examples.english: Even if it rains, I plan to go out tomorrow.

examples.japanese: たとえ君が何を言っても私の気持ちは変わらない。
examples.english: No matter what you say, my feelings won't change.

examples.japanese: 私は親にたとえ反対されても留学したいです。
examples.english: Even if my parents are against it, I want to study abroad.

examples.japanese: たとえ元気じゃなくても、家族への手紙には元気だと書きます。
examples.english: Even if I’m not well, I will write that I’m well in a letter to my family.

examples.japanese: たとえ両親に反対されても、彼と結婚します。
examples.english: I will marry him, even if my parents are opposed to it.

meaning: even if… is the case
structure: 例えばたとえば + examples

examples.japanese: 日本の食べ物は美味しいです。例えば、すしはすごく美味しい！
examples.english: Japanese food is delicious, for example, sushi is so delicious!

examples.japanese: 私にはたくさん趣味がある。例えば魚釣り、登山です。
examples.english: I have many hobbies, fishing and climbing for example.

examples.japanese: 私は例えばイタリアやスペインなど外国へ行きたい。
examples.english: I want to go abroad, for instance, to Italy and Spain.

examples.japanese: 外国、例えばアメリカへ行ったことがありますか。
examples.english: Have you visited any foreign countries, say America?

examples.japanese: 彼は不思議な生物、例えばヘビのような生物が好きです。
examples.english: He likes strange animals, things like snakes, for example.

examples.japanese: 私はうるさい音楽は好きではない。例えばロックのような。
examples.english: I don't like noisy music, such as rock.

meaning: even if; even supposing that ~
structure: Verb (casual, past) + って | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective + いく（っ）た

examples.japanese: タクシーに乗ったって間に合わないよ。
examples.english: Even if you take a taxi, you won't make it in time.

examples.japanese: いくら広くたって、駅から遠い部屋には住みたくない。
examples.english: It doesn't matter how spacious it may be, I don't want to live in a place far from the station.

examples.japanese: 今回のテストは失敗したって、また次のテストを頑張ればいいだよ。
examples.english: Even if you fail this exam, just focus on doing your best on the next one.

examples.japanese: うちの子はいくら注意したって、悪い癖が治らない。
examples.english: No matter how many times i warn my kid, he just won’t change his bad habits.

examples.japanese: この言葉はいくら調べたって、辞書には出てこないだ。
examples.english: No matter how hard I try to look up this word, it won't show up in the dictionary.

examples.japanese: いくら叫んだって、誰も来ないよ。
examples.english: No matter how much you scream, no one is coming.

meaning: continue to (go in negative direction)
structure: Verb (て form) + ばかりいる

examples.japanese: この猫は寝てばかりいます。
examples.english: This cat does nothing but sleep.

examples.japanese: あの子が泣いてばかりいる。
examples.english: That child does nothing but cry.

examples.japanese: 甘いものを食べてばかりいると、太りますよ！
examples.english: If you keep only eating sweets, you're going to gain weight.

examples.japanese: 最近彼はコンピューターを使ってばかりいる。
examples.english: Lately, he does nothing but use his computer.

examples.japanese: テレビを見てばかりいると、目が悪くなりますよ。
examples.english: If you keep watching TV all the time, your eyes are going to go bad.

examples.japanese: 息子は仕事もしないで遊んでばかりいます。
examples.english: My son doesn't work and just plays around all the time.

meaning: please do; could you please…; I ask of you to ~
structure: Verb (て form) + ごらん(なさい)

examples.japanese: もう一度やってごらん。
examples.english: Try it one more time.

examples.japanese: もう一度言ってごらん。
examples.english: Please say that once more.

examples.japanese: これは美味しいから、食べてごらん。
examples.english: This tastes really good, so please eat it.

examples.japanese: ほら、見てごらん。空に虹が出ているよ。
examples.english: Look, there's a rainbow in the sky!

examples.japanese: 分からなかったら、先生に聞いてごらん。
examples.english: If you don’t understand, you should ask your teacher.

examples.japanese: 苦くないからちょっと飲んでごらん。
examples.english: It's not bitter, try drinking some.

meaning: for example; starting with ~
structure: Verb (てform) + はじめて

examples.japanese: 日本に来てはじめてラーメンを食べた。
examples.english: I had never eaten ramen before coming to Japan.

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強してはじめて、勉強の楽しさが分かった。
examples.english: Only after I started studying Japanese did I realize the joys of studying.

examples.japanese: 試験に落ちてはじめて、ちゃんと勉強しないといけないと思った。
examples.english: I felt like I really needed to start studying seriously after failing that exam.

examples.japanese: 先生に教えていただいてはじめて、プログラミングの面白さが分かりました。
examples.english: I didn’t realize how interesting programming was until my teacher taught me.

examples.japanese: 海外に行ってはじめて、自分の世界の狭さを知った。
examples.english: Only after going abroad, did I realize how small my world was.

examples.japanese: 自分の子供が出来てはじめて、大人になった気がした。
examples.english: I did not feel like I had become an adult until I had my own child.

meaning: can’t help but feel; can’t help but do; must do ~
structure: Verb (て form) + からでないとからでなければ

examples.japanese: 親の許可をもらってからでなければ、日本への留学が出来ない。
examples.english: You must first get your parent's permission, otherwise you will not be able to study abroad in Japan.

examples.japanese: 手続きしてからでないと、図書館の本は借りられない。
examples.english: Unless you follow the procedures, you cannot borrow books from the library.

examples.japanese: この件については、上司と相談してからでないと、決められません。
examples.english: I can't decide on this without consulting my manager.

examples.japanese: この資料を完成させてからでなければ、今日は帰ることができません。
examples.english: I won't be able to head home today until I complete these materials.

examples.japanese: 実物を見てからでないと、買うかどうか決められません。
examples.english: I can't decide whether to buy or not without first seeing the item in person.

examples.japanese: 20歳になってからでないとお酒を飲むことはできません。
examples.english: You cannot drink alcohol before turning 20 years old.

pattern: てしょうがない・てしかたがない
meaning: can't help but; dying to; extremely ~
structure: Verb (て form) + しょうがないしかたがない | な-adjective + なで | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: 私はそれが気になってしょうがない。
examples.english: I can't help thinking about that.

examples.japanese: 今日は寒くてしょうがない。
examples.english: It's simply too cold today.

examples.japanese: 今日は何もすることがなくて、暇で仕方がない。
examples.english: I have nothing to do today and am very bored.

examples.japanese: お金をくれて、嬉しくてしょうがない。
examples.english: I was given some money and feel so happy.

examples.japanese: バスで行くのは、時間がかかってしょうがない。
examples.english: Going by bus takes more time, but it can't be helped.

examples.japanese: 海外で一人暮らしを始めたばかりなので、寂しくてしかたがありません。
examples.english: I feel a little lonely because I just started living abroad alone, but it cannot be helped.

meaning: get by without doing ~
structure: Verb (て form) + 済む | Noun + で | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: その夜は何の事故もなくて済んだ。
examples.english: The night passed without any accidents.

examples.japanese: 金で済む事ならいくらでも出す。
examples.english: If money can resolve this, I will give any amount.

examples.japanese: ちょうど熱が出たから、学校行かなくて済んだ。
examples.english: I had a fever and so I didn't go to school.

examples.japanese: スマホの修理に出したが、2,000円で済んだ。
examples.english: I submitted my smatphone for repairs and got by with 2,000 yen.

examples.japanese: 少しお時間いただけませんか、５分で済みますから。
examples.english: Could you please wait a little bit longer? 5 minutes should be sufficient.

examples.japanese: 予約だったら、わざわざ店に行かなくても、電話１本で済むよ。
examples.english: If you need to make a reservation, there's no need to go all the way to the shop, it can be done with just 1 phone call.

meaning: can’t afford to; unable to ~
structure: Verb (て form) + は + いけないから | Verb (dictionary form) ＋と

examples.japanese: 雨が降るといけないから傘を持って行きなさい。
examples.english: It would be no good if it rains, so please take an umbrella with you.

examples.japanese: バスに乗り遅れるといけないから、すぐ出発したほうがいい。
examples.english: You'd better head out right away so you don't miss the bus.

examples.japanese: 道に迷うといけないから、地図をもって行きなさい。
examples.english: Take a map with you in case you get lost.

examples.japanese: 彼が怒ってはいけないから本当の事は言わなかった。
examples.english: I didn't tell him the truth for fear he would be angry.

examples.japanese: 風邪を引くといけないから、マフラーをして出かけなさい。
examples.english: Please wear a scarf when you go out so that you don't catch a cold.

examples.japanese: 彼は寝てしまうといけないから、ブラックコーヒーを何杯も飲んだ。
examples.english: He drank multiple cups of black coffee so as not to fall asleep.

meaning: at once; immediately; directly; in person; automatically ~
structure: Verb (て form) + いる + 場合じゃない場合ではない

examples.japanese: 今は笑っている場合ではない。
examples.english: This is not an occasion for laughter.

examples.japanese: 今は悲しんでいる場合ではない。
examples.english: This is no time to be sad.

examples.japanese: 冗談を言っている場合じゃない！
examples.english: This is no time to be saying jokes!

examples.japanese: しっかりして！泣いている場合ではない。
examples.english: Hold yourself together! This is not a time to be crying.

examples.japanese: 今、ゆっくり休んでいる場合じゃないぞ！やることがたくさんあるんだ。
examples.english: Now is not the time to be relaxing! There are a ton of things that need to get done.

examples.japanese: 今は携帯を触っている場合じゃない。早く宿題をやりなさい。
examples.english: This is no time to be touching your smartphone. Hurry up and do your homework.

meaning: can ~; it’s okay if ~ (indicates permission or compromise)
structure: Verb (て form) + も + 始まらない

examples.japanese: 今さらそんなことを言っても始まらない。
examples.english: It is no use talking about that now.

examples.japanese: 待っていても始まらないので、もう帰りましょう。
examples.english: Waiting here isn't gonna do any good, let's just head home.

examples.japanese: その件は話し合っても始まらない。
examples.english: There is no point in discussing this matter.

examples.japanese: 自分で考えても始まらないので、先生に聞いてみよう。
examples.english: It's no good thinking about this on my own, so I'll try asking the teacher.

examples.japanese: 文句を言っても始まらないだろ。
examples.english: Complaining won't change anything.

examples.japanese: 言っておくが、私に怒っても始まらないよ。
examples.english: I'm telling you it will do you no good to be angry at me.

meaning: don't have to
structure: Verb (て form) + もかまわないもかまいません | い-adjective い + くて | な-adjective + で | Noun + で

examples.japanese: 雨が降っても構わない。
examples.english: I don't mind if it rains.

examples.japanese: 君が何をしても構わないよ。
examples.english: I don't mind what you do.

examples.japanese: 今帰っても構いませんか？
examples.english: Do you mind if I leave now?

examples.japanese: 間違いをしても構わない。
examples.english: Don't worry about making mistakes.

examples.japanese: 嫌なら来なくても構わない。
examples.english: I don't mind you not coming if you really don't want to.

examples.japanese: 私は毎日それを食べてもかまわない。
examples.english: I wouldn't mind eating that everyday.

pattern: てもしょうがない / てもしかたがない
meaning: can ~; it’s okay if ~ (indicates permission or compromise)
structure: Verb (て form) + も + しょうがないしかたがない | な-adjective + でも | い-adjective + いくても

examples.japanese: そこへ行ってもしかたがない。
examples.english: It is no use going there.

examples.japanese: こんなことをしていても仕方がないだろう。
examples.english: I don't think this will get us anywhere.

examples.japanese: どうにもならないことを、悩んでいてもしょうがないよ。
examples.english: There's no point in worrying about things beyond our control.

examples.japanese: 全然勉強していないんだから、落ちてもしかたないよ。
examples.english: I haven't been studying at all, so there's no helping it if I end up failing.

examples.japanese: そんなに健康のことを心配しても仕方がない。
examples.english: There is no sense in your worrying about your health so much.

examples.japanese: テストは明日だし、今から焦って勉強してもしかたがない。
examples.english: The test is tomorrow, so it's no use to get flustered and start studying now.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Noun + と言えばといえば

examples.japanese: ベトナムと言えば、バイクが多いですね。
examples.english: Speaking of Vietnam, there are a lot of bikes.

examples.japanese: 大阪の食べ物と言えば、たこ焼きです。
examples.english: Speaking of Osaka food, takoyaki comes to mind.

examples.japanese: 本と言えばこれを読んだか？
examples.english: Speaking of books, have you read this one?

examples.japanese: 日本の夏と言えば、とても暑いです！
examples.english: Speaking of summer in Japan, it's extremely hot!

examples.japanese: 外国語と言えば、中国語を話せますか。
examples.english: Speaking of foreign languages, can you speak Chinese?

examples.japanese: 日本と言えば、ラーメンとお寿司が名物です。
examples.english: Speaking of Japan, it's famous foods are ramen and sushi.

meaning: should; can; it’d be good if ~
structure: Verb (casual) + と + いい | Verb (た form) + ら

examples.japanese: あなたが気にいるといいな。
examples.english: I hope you like it.

examples.japanese: 見られたらいいね。
examples.english: I hope I can see it.

examples.japanese: 明日晴れるといいな。
examples.english: I hope the weather will clear up tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 旅行中は雨が降らないといいなあ。
examples.english: I hope it doesn't rain during our trip.

examples.japanese: いつか日本で出会えたらいいな。
examples.english: It would be nice if we can meet in Japan one day.

examples.japanese: 風邪ひいちゃった。早く良くなるといいんだけど。
examples.english: I caught a cold, I hope I can recover quickly.

meaning: in the case of~; assuming~; if A then B
structure: Verb (casual form) + と言ってもといっても | Noun + （だ） | な-adjective + （だ） | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 今週は忙しい、といっても先週ほどじゃない。
examples.english: I’m busy this week, but not as much as last week.

examples.japanese: 私は料理ができるといっても、卵焼きぐらいです。
examples.english: Although I said that I can cook, I can only make fried eggs.

examples.japanese: 会社の社長といっても、社員は４人だけですよ。
examples.english: Although he may be the company president, there are only 4 employees.

examples.japanese: 日本で生活したことがあるといっても、実は１ヶ月だけなんです。
examples.english: Although I have experience living in Japan, it was only for one month.

examples.japanese: 週末は旅行しました。旅行と言っても、家の近くの温泉に行っただけです
examples.english: I went traveling on the weekend. Although I said travel, we just went to our local onsen (hot spring).

examples.japanese: 私は日本語ができると言っても、簡単な会話のレベルくらいです。
examples.english: When I say I can speak Japanese, I am only at about basic conversational level.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ということだとのことだってことだ | Noun +（だ） | な-adjective +（だ） | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: ニュースによると、明日は雨が降るということだ。
examples.english: I heard on the news that it will rain tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 先ほど、山田さんから電話があって、少し遅れるとのことです。
examples.english: I heard Mr. Yamada called earlier and said he would be a bit late.

examples.japanese: 田中さんは熱があるので、明日は行けないとのことだ。
examples.english: Mr. Tanaka has a fever, so it doesn't seem like he will be able to go tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 6月は暑くなるとのことでしたが、それほど暑くなかったです。
examples.english: It seemed like it would get really hot in June, but it didn't end up being that hot.

examples.japanese: 先輩は来月で会社を辞めるとのことですが、その話は本当ですか。
examples.english: Is the story I heard that you will be quitting next month true?

examples.japanese: 物価は来月からさらに上がるということだ。
examples.english: I heard that prices will rise again even higher next month.

meaning: convert phrase into noun
structure: PhraseNoun + というのは + reasonexplanationdefinition

examples.japanese: 「コンビニ」というのはコンビニエンスストアのことだ。
examples.english: "konbini" means "convenience store".

examples.japanese: 「パソコン」というのはパーソナルコンピューターの略だ。
examples.english: "pasokon" is short for "personal computer".

examples.japanese: 「デジカメ」というのはデジタルカメラを短くした言い方です。
examples.english: "dejikame" is the shortened way to say "digital camera".

examples.japanese: 「Hello」というのは「こんにちは」という意味だ。
examples.english: "hello" is the same meaning as "konnichiwa".

examples.japanese: 禁煙というのはたばこを吸ってはいけないということです。
examples.english: The word "kinen" means no smoking is allowed.

examples.japanese: 僕は卵を食べないんです。というのは、アレルギーがあるんですよ。
examples.english: I don't eat eggs. That is to say I have an egg allergy.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Noun + と言うとというと

examples.japanese: 桜というと、花見だ。
examples.english: Speaking of cherry blossoms, flower viewing comes to mind.

examples.japanese: 人気があるアニメというと、ワンピースだ。
examples.english: Speaking of popular anime, One Piece comes to mind.

examples.japanese: 日本料理というと、すしが一番有名だ。
examples.english: Speaking of Japanese food, sushi is the most popular.

examples.japanese: どちらかというと暇です。
examples.english: If anything, I'm bored.

examples.japanese: デトロイト市と言うと、どんなイメージをしますか？
examples.english: When you think of Detroit city, what image do you have?

examples.japanese: 日本の都会と言うと、東京と大阪でしょう。
examples.english: Speaking of Japan's big cities, Tokyo and Osaka come to mind.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Verb (casual) + というより（も/は） | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼はかっこいいというよりかわいい。
examples.english: He is more cute than cool.

examples.japanese: 彼は学者というよりは教師だ。
examples.english: He is more a teacher than a scholar.

examples.japanese: 私の仕事は、仕事というより趣味に近い。
examples.english: My job is more of a hobby than a job.

examples.japanese: うちの子はこれができないというより、やる気がないと思う。
examples.english: It's not that my child can't do this, but rather they just don't have the motivation to do it.

examples.japanese: 今日は涼しいというより寒いくらいだった。
examples.english: Rather than cool, today was more on the cold side.

examples.japanese: 今はラーメンというよりうどんが食べたい気分だ。
examples.english: Now I'm more in the mood for udon than for ramen.

pattern: とみえる / とみえて
meaning: to look; to seem; to appear ~
structure: Verb (casual) + と見えるとみえるとみえて | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼は病気だとみえる。
examples.english: He appears to be sick.

examples.japanese: 彼は運が向いてきたと見える。
examples.english: Luck seems to be heading his way.

examples.japanese: 山田さんは忙しいとみえて、このごろ電話もしてこない。
examples.english: Mr. Yamada seems busy now, which may be why he hasn't called.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ったとみえて、道が濡れている。
examples.english: It seems that it just rained, as the road is wet.

examples.japanese: 彼は苦労したとみえて、実際の年齢より老けて見える。
examples.english: He seems as if he has worked very hard through his life since he looks older than his actual age.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語の勉強が真剣になってきたと見える。
examples.english: He seems to have started to get more serious with his Japanese studies.

pattern: とすれば・としたら・とすると
meaning: if; after; when ~
structure: Verb (casual) + とすればとしたらとすると | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 選ぶとすれば、僕はこれだな。
examples.english: If I were to choose, I would go with this.

examples.japanese: そこまで歩いていくとすれば、40分くらいかかるだろう。
examples.english: If we go by walking, it will likely take about 40 minutes.

examples.japanese: もし車を買い換えるとすれば、次はアメリカの車が欲しい。
examples.english: If I were to buy a new car, I would want to get an American car.

examples.japanese: 一日25時間だとしたら、何をしますか？
examples.english: If there were 25 hours in a day, what would you do?

examples.japanese: 電車で行くとしたら、時間はどのくらいかかりますか。
examples.english: Assuming we go by train, about how much time will it take?

examples.japanese: その話が本当だとしたら、嬉しいです！
examples.english: If that story is true, then I'd be really happy!

meaning: at the same time as; while; simultaneously ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + と共に | Noun

examples.japanese: 私の人生は、ギターと共にある。
examples.english: I spend my life together with my guitar.

examples.japanese: 春が近づくと共に、少しずつ暖かくなってきた。
examples.english: As spring grows nearer, it's gradually getting a bit warmer.

examples.japanese: 私は政府と共に仕事をする。
examples.english: I will work together with the government.

examples.japanese: 私は家族と共に二年間外国で暮らした。
examples.english: I lived abroad together with my family for two years.

examples.japanese: 私は共に戦ってくれる人を探している。
examples.english: I'm looking for people who will fight together with me.

examples.japanese: ゲームでは、仲間と共に敵を倒していくのが面白い。
examples.english: In games, being able to work together with my friends to defeat enemies is fun / interesting.

meaning: while; besides; at the same time; in addition
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 途中で途中に | Noun + の

examples.japanese: ごはんを食べている途中に電話がかかってきた。
examples.english: The phone rang when I was in the middle of eating (dinner).

examples.japanese: 私は駅から学校に行く途中で先生に会った。
examples.english: I saw my teacher on the way to school from the station.

examples.japanese: 彼女はテーブルまで行く途中で転んでしまった。
examples.english: She fell over on her way to the table.

examples.japanese: 彼は帰宅途中で事故があった。
examples.english: He had an accident on his way home.

examples.japanese: 学校に来る途中で、財布を忘れたのは気づいた。
examples.english: I noticed that I forgot my wallet on my way to school.

examples.japanese: 勉強の途中でお菓子を食べた。
examples.english: I ate some sweets in the middle of when I was studying.

meaning: by the way; in this connection; incidentally; (conjunction)
structure: ところで + new topic

examples.japanese: ところで、今どこにいるの？
examples.english: By the way, where are you now?

examples.japanese: ところで大阪に行ったことある？
examples.english: By the way, have you ever been to Osaka?

examples.japanese: もうすぐ卒業ですね。ところで、就職はどうしますか。
examples.english: You're about to graduate, right? By the way, what are you doing for job hunting?

examples.japanese: もうすぐ、今年も終わりですね。ところで、お正月はどうなさいますか。
examples.english: This year will be over soon. By the way, do you have any plans for the new year?

examples.japanese: 明日は日本語能力試験の日ですね。頑張ってください！ところで、来週の月曜日は空いてる。
examples.english: Tomorrow is the JLPT, right? Good luck! By the way, are you free next Monday?

examples.japanese: 俺は来年日本に留学する。ところで、君はどうするの？
examples.english: I will study abroad in Japan next year. By the way, what about you?

meaning: at the time; just as I was ~
structure: Expectation + ところが + result

examples.japanese: 今日は晴れだと思っている。ところが、雨だ。
examples.english: I thought today would be sunny. However, it is raining..

examples.japanese: 昨夜はコンサートに行くつもりだった。ところが病気で行けなくなった。
examples.english: I was planning to go to the concert last night. However, I couldn’t go because I got sick.

examples.japanese: 私はチームの勝利を信じていた。ところが、負けてしまった。
examples.english: I believed our team would win. However, they lost.

examples.japanese: 彼は非常に頭がいい。ところが大学に入れなかった。
examples.english: He’s very smart. Even so, he couldn’t get into college.

examples.japanese: 日本での生活は大変だと思った。ところが、すぐに慣れました。
examples.english: I thought life in Japan would be difficult, but I got used to it right away.

examples.japanese: 彼はお金持ちの人だと思った。ところがお金が全然なくて今まで見せた物は偽物だ。
examples.english: I thought he was rich, but it turns out he has no money and everything he showed off was fake.

meaning: as it is; current state; without changing
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + とおりに | Verb (casual past) | Noun + どおりにのとおりに

examples.japanese: 彼は言われたとおりにした。
examples.english: He did as he was told.

examples.japanese: 彼は時間どおりにやって来た。
examples.english: He arrived on time.

examples.japanese: すべてはスケジュールどおりに進んでいる。
examples.english: Everything is going according to schedule.

examples.japanese: じゃあ、先生が書くとおりに、一緒に漢字を書いてください。
examples.english: Let's get started, please write the kanji character together as the teacher draws it.

examples.japanese: 先生が言ったとおり、試験が難しかった。
examples.english: The exam was difficult, just as the teacher said it would be.

examples.japanese: 天気が晴れってきた。予報どおりだ。
examples.english: The weather started to clear up. The weather forecast was right.

meaning: to do something from beginning to end; completely, extremely ~
structure: Verb (ます stem) ます + 通すとおす

examples.japanese: やると決めたことは最後までやり通すべきだ。
examples.english: When you decide to do something, you should see it through to the end.

examples.japanese: 終電を出てしまったので、１時間かけて家まで歩き通した。
examples.english: The last train left, so I walked home for an hour.

examples.japanese: 50メートル以上前方を見通すことが難しかった。
examples.english: It was hard to see more than 50 meters ahead.

examples.japanese: ひと晩飲み通しに飲んだ。
examples.english: We kept drinking all night.

examples.japanese: こんな長い小説は一日で読み通せない。
examples.english: You can't read such a long novel in a day.

examples.japanese: 上司にバレないように、仕事のミスを隠し通した。
examples.english: In order to not have my boss find out, I covered up my mistake at work.

meaning: for; considering it’s (something or someone)
structure: Noun + として

examples.japanese: 彼は教師として働いている。
examples.english: He has been working as a teacher.

examples.japanese: 僕の友人としては君ばかりだ。
examples.english: You are the only friend I have.

examples.japanese: ナイフとして用いられている。
examples.english: It can be used as a knife.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、歌手として最近活躍しています。
examples.english: She is active as a singer lately.

examples.japanese: 私は留学生として日本に来ました。
examples.english: I came to Japan as a study abroad student.

examples.japanese: 同じ日本人として彼を応援して行きたいです。
examples.english: I want to support him as a fellow Japanese person.

meaning: not at all ~
structure: とても + Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: そんなこと、私にはとても出来ない。
examples.english: There's no way I could do something like that.

examples.japanese: この本の漢字は難しいので私にはとても読めない。
examples.english: The kanji in this book is difficult so I can barely read it.

examples.japanese: 20万円の携帯電話など、とても買えない。
examples.english: There's no way I can buy something like a 200,000 yen cellphone.

examples.japanese: 彼女がせっかく作ってくれたから、甘いものが嫌いなんて、とても言えない。
examples.english: Since she went through the trouble of making it for me, I couldn't possibly tell her I don't like sweets.

examples.japanese: 一度にこんなにたくさんの単語はとても覚えられません。
examples.english: I could not possibly memorize so much vocabulary at once.

examples.japanese: 歯が痛くてご飯はとても食べられなかった。
examples.english: My tooth hurt and so I could hardly eat anything.

meaning: is best; nothing is better than ~
structure: Verb (casual) + とは限らない | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 先生の答えがいつも正しいとは限りません。
examples.english: The teacher's answers are not always correct.

examples.japanese: こういう音楽は誰でも好きだとは限らない。
examples.english: This sort of music is not necessarily liked by everyone.

examples.japanese: お金持ちになれば、必ず幸せになるとは限りません。
examples.english: Becoming rich doesn't necessarily make you happy.

examples.japanese: いい大学を卒業したから、いい会社に入れるとは限らない。
examples.english: Just because you graduated from a good university doesn't mean you'll be able to get into a good company.

examples.japanese: 無料のほうがいいとは限らない。無料のものは質が低いものが多いです。
examples.english: The free option is not always necessary the best option. Often free items are of low quality.

examples.japanese: 学校にいかなければプロになれないとは限りません。自分で勉強してプロになる人もいます。
examples.english: It's not always true that if you don't go to school you can't become a professional. There are people who become professionals by studying on their own.

meaning: the moment [A], unintentionally / inadvertently caused something to happen
structure: つい + clause (often てしまう form)

examples.japanese: 料理がおいしくてつい食べ過ぎた。
examples.english: The food was so good that I ate too much.

examples.japanese: 彼女の前でつい他の女の子がかわいいって言ってしまった。
examples.english: Without thinking, I said some other girl was cute right in front of my girlfriend.

examples.japanese: 11時まで勉強すると決めたばかりのに、彼は30分後つい寝てしまった。
examples.english: Although he just decided to study until 11 o'clock, he fell asleep 30 minutes later.

examples.japanese: ゲームをつい夢中になってしまって、宿題ができなかった。
examples.english: I became so absorbed in the game that I couldn't do my homework.

examples.japanese: ダイエット中だが、ケーキを見てつい食べてしまった。
examples.english: Although I'm in the middle of a diet, I saw a cake and ended up eating it..

examples.japanese: 友達と約束したけど、つい秘密を漏らしてしまった。
examples.english: Although I made a promise with my friend, I revealed their secret without thinking..

meaning: at last; finally; beyond doubt
structure: ついに + phrase

examples.japanese: ついに着いたのだ！
examples.english: I finally arrived!

examples.japanese: 雨はついにやんだ。
examples.english: The rain stopped at last.

examples.japanese: 冬はついに終わった。
examples.english: At long last the winter was over.

examples.japanese: ついにオリンピックが始まる。
examples.english: The Olympics will finally begin.

examples.japanese: 二人はついに離婚した。
examples.english: They got divorced in the end.

examples.japanese: 私はついに仕事が決まりました。
examples.english: I finally got a job.

meaning: at the same time as; while; simultaneously ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ついでに | Verb (た form) | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 買い物のついでに、本屋に寄りました。
examples.english: I stopped by a book store while shopping.

examples.japanese: コンビニに行くなら、ついでにお茶も買ってきてくれない？
examples.english: If you're already going to the convenience store, could you please also buy me some tea?

examples.japanese: 仕事へ行くついでに駅まで送ってあげるよ。
examples.english: I'll give you a lift to the station on my way to work.

examples.japanese: 出かけるの？それならついでにゴミを出してくれる？
examples.english: Are you heading out? If so, could you please also take out the garbage when you go?

examples.japanese: 引っ越しのついでに、新しい家具を買いたいです。
examples.english: While I am moving, I want to buy some new furniture.

examples.japanese: 散歩のついでに、この手紙を出してくれませんか。
examples.english: Since you are going for a walk, could you please mail this letter for me?

meaning: in short; in a word; to sum up; to put it simply ~
structure: Clause + つまり + alternative explanation

examples.japanese: 彼は獣医、つまり、動物の医者です。
examples.english: He’s a veterinarian. In other words, he’s an animal doctor.

examples.japanese: 彼女は姉の娘だ。つまり、私にとっては姪です。
examples.english: She is my sister's daughter. In other words, my niece.

examples.japanese: 母の兄、つまり僕の伯父は、大学の先生です。
examples.english: My mother's older brother, in other words, my uncle, is a college professor.

examples.japanese: 彼女はその日の前日、つまり５月５日に彼に会った。
examples.english: She met him the day before, that is to say May fifth.

examples.japanese: 彼は今日から１週間後、つまり１２月１０日に帰ってくる。
examples.english: He will be back a week from today, that is, on December 10.

examples.japanese: つまり、うちの学校の生徒だということ？
examples.english: You mean you’re a student at my school?

meaning: have no intention to / didn't mean to ~
structure: Verb (ている form) + つもりだったつもりなのに | Verb (た form) | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 言ったつもりだった。
examples.english: I thought I said it.

examples.japanese: 私はそのメールを送ったつもりだった。
examples.english: I'm sure I sent that email.

examples.japanese: コーヒーを注文したつもりだった。
examples.english: I'm sure I ordered a coffee..

examples.japanese: それは予約したつもりだった。
examples.english: I thought I had made the reservation.

examples.japanese: 名前を書いたつもりだったが、書いていなかったようだ。
examples.english: I thought I wrote my name down, but apparently I did not.

examples.japanese: 返事をしたつもりだったが、送れていなかった。
examples.english: I thought I had responded, but I had not sent it.

meaning: have no intention to / didn't mean to ~
structure: Verb (た form) + つもりで | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 冗談のつもりで言ったのです。
examples.english: I meant it to be a joke.

examples.japanese: 私は死んだつもりで働いた。
examples.english: I worked as if there were no tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼はそれをどんなつもりで言ったのだと思いますか。
examples.english: What do you think he meant by that?

examples.japanese: 旅行に行ったつもりでお金をためている。
examples.english: I'm saving up money to go on a trip.

examples.japanese: 私たちは常にお客様の立場になったつもりで行動します。
examples.english: We always behave with the intent of taking the customer's point of view.

examples.japanese: 練習だと思うから真剣にできないんだ。練習だと思わないで、本番のつもりでやってみろ！
examples.english: You can't do it seriously because you're thinking of it as practice. Don't think of this as practice and give it a go as if it were the real deal!

meaning: not really; can't be regarded as ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + うちに | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 明るいうちに、帰りましょう。
examples.english: Let's head home while it's still light outside.

examples.japanese: 忘すれないうちに、メモをしておこう。
examples.english: Let's write a memo before you forget.

examples.japanese: これはまだ温かいうちに早く食べてください。
examples.english: Please eat this while it is still warm.

examples.japanese: 桜がきれいなうちにお花見に行きましょう。
examples.english: Let's go and watch the Sakura cherry blossoms while they are beautiful.

examples.japanese: 両親が元気なうちに旅行に連れていきたい。
examples.english: I want to take my parents on a trip while they are still energetic.

examples.japanese: 若いうちに一生懸命勉強しなさい。
examples.english: Study to your absolute best while you are young.

meaning: for the sake of; from the standpoint of; as a matter of; in terms of ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 上で | Verb (た form) | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 外国語を勉強する上で辞書はなくてはならないものだ。
examples.english: In order to study a foreign language, you need to have a dictionary.

examples.japanese: 仕事をする上で大切なのは、周りとのコミュニケーションです。
examples.english: In order to do one's job, what's important is communication with those around you.

examples.japanese: この薬は説明書をよく読んだ上で、ご使用ください。
examples.english: Please use this medicine after reading the instructions carefully.

examples.japanese: 実物を見た上で買うかどうか決めるつもりだ。
examples.english: Once I see the real thing in person, I will decide whether to buy or not.

examples.japanese: 留学の件は家族と相談した上でご返事いたします。
examples.english: Regarding the study abroad, once you consult with your family I will give my answer.

examples.japanese: 工事計画は、周辺住民との話し合いの上で決められるべきだ。
examples.english: The construction plan should be decided after discussing with the local residents.

meaning: let alone; not to mention; needless to say ~
structure: Verb (casual) + 上(に) | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 今日は曇っている上に風が強いので、とても寒く感じられる。
examples.english: Today in addition to being cloudy, the wind is strong and so it feels very cold.

examples.japanese: この店の料理はおいしい。その上、値段も安いのでいつもお客さんが多い。
examples.english: This restaurant's food is delicious. In addition, the prices are cheap so there are always a lot of customers.

examples.japanese: このパソコンは安い上に、機能も多いので、最近とても売れている。
examples.english: This computer is not only cheap, but it has a lot of functionality, so lately it has been selling very well.

examples.japanese: この手続きは、面倒な上に時間もかかるので、皆がいやがっている。
examples.english: This procedure is troublesome and time consuming so everyone hates it.

examples.japanese: この町は、地下鉄が通った上に、デパートもできて、便利になった。
examples.english: This town has become convenient now is connected by subway and in addition has built some department stores.

examples.japanese: この仕事は危険な上に、給料も低いし、最悪だ。
examples.english: This job is not only dangerous, but the salary is low, so it's pretty much the worst.

meaning: whether or not ~
structure: Noun + は別としてはべつとして | Verb (casual) + かどうか | な-adjective + かどうか | い-adjective + かどうか

examples.japanese: 彼女の料理は見た目は別として、味はとても美味しい。
examples.english: Apart from the appearance, her food tastes very good.

examples.japanese: 天気は別として、それは楽しいピクニックだった。
examples.english: Apart from the weather, it was a fun picnic.

examples.japanese: 大雨や大雪の日は別として、私は毎日ランニングをしている。
examples.english: Apart from days with heavy rain and heavy snow, I run every day.

examples.japanese: 野球は別として私はすべてのスポーツが好きだ。
examples.english: I like all sports, aside from baseball.

examples.japanese: 合格できるかどうかは別として、チャレンジしてみることは大切だ。
examples.english: Regardless of whether or not you can pass, it's important to challenge yourself.

examples.japanese: 彼は時々出張することは別としてあまり旅をしない。
examples.english: He doesn't travel much apart from occasional business trips.

meaning: anyhow; anyway; regardless; in any case; whether or not ~
structure: Noun + はもちろん + 2nd clause + も

examples.japanese: 彼女は、勉強はもちろん料理もよくできる。
examples.english: Not only is she a good student, but she is also good at cooking.

examples.japanese: おすしは日本ではもちろん、海外でも人気がある食べ物だ。
examples.english: Sushi is of course popular in Japan, but it is a popular food overseas as well.

examples.japanese: 私の彼は、顔はもちろん性格も完璧。
examples.english: My boyfriend has a nice face, not to mention a perfect personality.

examples.japanese: バニラケーキはもちろん、いちごのケーキも好きですよ。
examples.english: While I of course like vanilla cake, I also like strawberry cake.

examples.japanese: 日本語学校では、日本語はもちろん、日本の文化や習慣についても教えている。
examples.english: At Japanese language school, they of course teach Japanese, but also Japanese culture and customs.

examples.japanese: あのラーメン屋は、ラーメンはもちろん美味しいんですが、カレーライスも美味しいんですよ。
examples.english: That ramen shop also has some good curry rice in addition to great ramen.

meaning: thanks to; owing to; because of ~
structure: Topic + は + Verb (dictionary) + こと + で有名だ | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective + こと

examples.japanese: この学校はフットボールが強いことで有名です。
examples.english: This school is famous for being strong in football.

examples.japanese: 京都は古いお寺があることで有名だ。
examples.english: Kyoto is famous for its old temples.

examples.japanese: 日本は電子製品で有名です。
examples.english: Japan is famous for electric appliances.

examples.japanese: あのレストランは値段が安いことで有名です。
examples.english: That restaurant is famous for its low prices.

examples.japanese: 彼は珍しい動物をたくさん飼っていることで有名です。
examples.english: He is famous for raising many rare animals.

examples.japanese: この町は温泉で有名ですよ。時間があれば行ってみてください。
examples.english: This town is famous for its hot springs. Please go if you have time.

meaning: there is no way that; it is impossible to ~
structure: Verb (casual) + わけだわけです | Noun + である | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 毎日ギターを弾くから上手に弾けるわけだ。
examples.english: I'm good at playing guitar, because I play every day.

examples.japanese: 暑いわけだ。気温が36度もある。
examples.english: No wonder it feels so hot, it's 36 degrees (Celsius) out.

examples.japanese: 「って、知らないわけ？」
examples.english: "You mean to say you don't know?"

examples.japanese: あんなに食べたら太るわけだ。
examples.english: Eating like that it's no wonder they'd gain weight.

examples.japanese: 本当のことを言うと彼はその仕事には向かなかったわけだ。
examples.english: To tell you the truth, he simply was not fit for the job.

examples.japanese: 彼女は動物が嫌いだから犬を飼ったことがないわけだ。
examples.english: She doesn't like animals, so there's no way she's ever raised a dog.

meaning: for that reason; no wonder; as you’d expect; the fact is; so you mean ~
structure: Verb (casual) + わけではないわけじゃない | Noun + (だ)という | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 料理が作れないわけではないが、忙しいからあまり作らない。
examples.english: It's not that I can't cook. I'm just busy and don't do it that often.

examples.japanese: 先生は何でも知っているわけではありません。
examples.english: It's not like the teacher knows everything.

examples.japanese: そんなに遠いわけじゃないんですよ。
examples.english: It's not that far away..

examples.japanese: あの人のことが嫌いなわけではないが、一緒にいるとちょっと疲れる。
examples.english: It's not that I hate that person or anything like that. It's just a bit tiring being around them.

examples.japanese: 親の意見がいつも正しいわけではないが、色々アドバイスはして欲しい。
examples.english: Although it's not like the opinions of parents are always correct, I would like to hear various advice from them.

examples.japanese: お金をたくさん持てば幸せになるわけではない。
examples.english: Having a lot of money doesn't mean you will be happy.

meaning: for that reason; no wonder; as you’d expect; the fact is; so you mean ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past ) + わけがない | Noun + である | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼はお金がないですから、家を買えるわけがない。
examples.english: He has no money, there's no way he can buy a house.

examples.japanese: 私がそんなものを食べられるわけがない。
examples.english: There's no way I could eat anything like that..

examples.japanese: 彼がそんな早い時間に起きられるわけがない。いつも寝坊しているんだから。
examples.english: There's no way he can get up that early.. He is always sleeping in..

examples.japanese: こんな高いレストランで毎日、食事できるわけがない。
examples.english: There's no way I can eat at such an expensive restaurant every day.

examples.japanese: 全然勉強してないのに、君がJLPT N3に合格するわけがないよ。
examples.english: You haven't been studying at all, there's no way you'll pass the JLPT N3.

examples.japanese: 歌が下手な彼が歌手になれるわけがない。
examples.english: He's no good at singing and there's no way he'll become a singer.

meaning: for that reason; no wonder; as you’d expect; the fact is; so you mean ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + わけにはいかないわけにはいきません | Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 明日はテストがあるから、ゲームをするわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I have a test tomorrow, so there's no way I can play games right now.

examples.japanese: 日本の税金は、高くても払わないわけにはいかない。
examples.english: Even if Japanese taxes are high, they must be paid.

examples.japanese: あとで車を運転するので、今お酒を飲むわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I will be driving a car later, so I cannot drink any alcohol now.

examples.japanese: 行くと約束したから、行かないわけにはいきません。
examples.english: I promised that I’d go, so I have no choice but to go.

examples.japanese: あんなに面白そうな映画を、見に行かないわけにはいかない。
examples.english: That movie looks really interesting, I absolutely need to go and see it!

examples.japanese: 今日は彼女の誕生日だけど、システムトラブルでみんな頑張っているし、私だけ帰るわけにはいかない。
examples.english: Today is my girlfriend's birthday, but there is some system trouble at work and everyone is working hard to fix it so it's not like only I can go home..

meaning: instead of; replacing; on behalf of ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + 割に（は） | Noun + の | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼は年のわりに元気だ。
examples.english: He is in good shape for his age.

examples.japanese: このカメラは高いわりに、よく売れる。
examples.english: This camera sells unexpectedly well considering the high price.

examples.japanese: このコンピューター、中古のわりに高くない？
examples.english: Isn't this computer expensive for being used?

examples.japanese: 今日は休日のわりに人が少ないね。
examples.english: There are unusually few people today considering it's a holiday.

examples.japanese: 彼女は年の割には若く見える。
examples.english: She looks young for her age.

examples.japanese: この寿司は高い割にまずい。
examples.english: This sushi is bad for the price.

meaning: with the intention of doing ~
structure: わざと + action

examples.japanese: 彼はわざと間違えた。
examples.english: He made a mistake on purpose.

examples.japanese: 私は彼がわざとそうしたとは思いません。
examples.english: I don't think that he did that on purpose.

examples.japanese: それをわざと壊したのではありません。
examples.english: It's not like I broke that on purpose.

examples.japanese: わざとの可能性がある。
examples.english: There is the possibility that it was deliberate.

examples.japanese: 彼はわざとその質問に答えなかった。
examples.english: He didn't answer the question on purpose.

examples.japanese: 知っていながら、わざと知らないふりをする。
examples.english: To pretend not to know something even though one knows it.

meaning: on purpose; intentionally ~
structure: わざわざ + action

examples.japanese: 私が困っているとき、彼女はわざわざ助けてくれた。
examples.english: She went out of her way to help me when I was in trouble.

examples.japanese: あなたはわざわざ私の為にそれを買ってくれたのですか？
examples.english: Did you buy that just for me?

examples.japanese: わざわざ遠い所から会いにきてくれてありがとう。
examples.english: Thanks for going out of your way to see me from so far away.

examples.japanese: 彼は忙しいだが、わざわざ市内の観光を案内してくれた。
examples.english: He is very busy, but he took some time to show me around the tourist spots in the city.

examples.japanese: 友達は恋人に会いたいから、わざわざニューヨークへ行った。
examples.english: My friend really wanted to see his girlfriend, so he went all the way to New York.

examples.japanese: わざわざ駅まで送ってくれなくてもいいよ。
examples.english: You don't need to trouble yourself to see me off to the station.

meaning: than; rather than; more than ~
structure: Verb (casual) + よりも | Noun

examples.japanese: 兄は私よりも大きい。
examples.english: My older brother is bigger than I am.

examples.japanese: 量よりも質だ。
examples.english: Quality matters more than quantity.

examples.japanese: 私は親よりも早く寝ます。
examples.english: I go to sleep before my parents do.

examples.japanese: これまでよりも頑張ります。
examples.english: I'll work even harder than I have been until now.

examples.japanese: 私は海よりも山の方がいい。
examples.english: I like mountains more than the ocean.

examples.japanese: 誰よりも君のことを愛している。
examples.english: I love you more than anyone else in the world.

meaning: there is no way / means; cannot do ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + ようがないようもない

examples.japanese: どうにもしようがない。
examples.english: Nothing can be done about it.

examples.japanese: お礼の申し上げようもない。
examples.english: I cannot thank you enough.

examples.japanese: 台風で電車もバスも動かないので会社へ行きようがない。
examples.english: The trains and buses are not operating because of the typhoon so I have no way to get to work.

examples.japanese: 何とも言いようがないなあ。
examples.english: I just don't know what to say.

examples.japanese: 彼女の住所も電話番号も分からないので、連絡の取りようがない。
examples.english: I don’t have her address or phone number so I have no way to contact her.

examples.japanese: 携帯電話もお金も盗まれてしまって、連絡のしようがない。
examples.english: My cellphone and money was all stolen, so I have no way to contact anyone.

meaning: thinking of doing; planning to ~
structure: Verb (casual) + ような + 気がする | Noun + のような | な-adjective + な | い-adjective + ような

examples.japanese: それが本当のような気がする。
examples.english: I feel that it is true.

examples.japanese: 分かるような気がする。
examples.english: I think I understand.

examples.japanese: 今日は、宝くじが当るような気がする。
examples.english: I feel like I am going to win the lottery today.

examples.japanese: この食べ物を毎日食べると、太るような気がする。
examples.english: I feel like eating this food every day will make me gain weight.

examples.japanese: 卒業したのはつい昨日のような気がする。
examples.english: It seems as if I had graduated only yesterday.

examples.japanese: その答えは「no」のような気がした。
examples.english: I felt like the answer would have been "no".

meaning: really (seem, appear, etc.); truly; as if ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ように | Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: バスに乗り遅れないように早く出ました。
examples.english: I left early so I would not be late for the bus.

examples.japanese: 先生の話を忘れないように、メモしておきます。
examples.english: I will take some notes so as to not forget what the teacher said.

examples.japanese: 単語が覚えられるように、フラッシュカードを作りました。
examples.english: I made some flashcards to help me be able to memorize vocabulary.

examples.japanese: 皆さんに聞こえるようにもっと大きな声で話してください。
examples.english: Speak with a louder voice so everyone can hear.

examples.japanese: 大学に合格出来るように一生懸命勉強しています。
examples.english: I'm studying my absolute hardest so that I can be accepted to university.

examples.japanese: 私は日本の新聞を読めるように、漢字を勉強しています。
examples.english: I'm studying kanji so that I can read Japanese newspapers.

meaning: to look; to seem; to appear
structure: Verb (casual form) + ように見えるようにみえる | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼は元気なように見える。
examples.english: He looks very energetic.

examples.japanese: 彼は勉強が嫌いなように見える。
examples.english: He looks like he hates studying.

examples.japanese: 彼女は教師のようにみえる。
examples.english: She looks like a teacher.

examples.japanese: その子は怖いように見える。
examples.english: That child looks scared.

examples.japanese: 彼は馬のように見える。
examples.english: He looks like a horse.

examples.japanese: あなたは天使のように見える。
examples.english: You look like an angel.

meaning: if ~ (bad result)
structure: Verb (volitional form) + としない

examples.japanese: 彼は早く寝ようとしない。
examples.english: He doesn't try to go to bed early.

examples.japanese: その子供はどうしても野菜を食べようとしない。
examples.english: That kid will not even try to eat vegetables.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分が間違っていることを認めようとしない。
examples.english: He refuses to recognize that he's wrong.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分のことは何も言おうとしない。
examples.english: He doesn’t talk much about himself.

examples.japanese: うちの息子は夢をあきらめようとしない。
examples.english: My son isn’t giving up on his dream.

examples.japanese: 彼と話しても無駄だ。聞こうとしないから。
examples.english: It's useless to talk to him. He doesn't even attempt to listen.

meaning: to try to; to make sure that ~
structure: Verb (volitional form) + とするとしたとしたらとしていた

examples.japanese: ドアを開けようとしたが、鍵がかかっていました。
examples.english: I tried opening the door, but it was locked.

examples.japanese: お風呂に入ろうとしたら、電話が掛かってきた。
examples.english: Just as I was about to take a bath, the phone rang.

examples.japanese: 会社からまさに出ようとした時、雨が降ってきた。
examples.english: Right when I was trying to leave work, it started to rain.

examples.japanese: 電車に乗ろうとしたときにドアが閉まって乗れなかった。
examples.english: As I was about to get on the train, the doors suddenly shut and I wasn't able to get on..

examples.japanese: シャワーを浴びようとしたが、水が出なかった。
examples.english: I was about to take a shower, but no water would come out.

examples.japanese: 私は5時半に帰ろうとしたら、上司に呼ばれてしまいました。
examples.english: I was ready to head home at 5:30, but was suddenly called in by my boss.

meaning: can’t help but feel; can’t help but do; must do ~
structure: Verb ない (ない stem) + ず（に） | する changes to + せず（に）

examples.japanese: 勉強せずに試験に受かった。
examples.english: I passed the exam without studying.

examples.japanese: 今朝、私は朝ごはんを食べずに学校に来ました。
examples.english: This morning I went to school without eating breakfast.

examples.japanese: 私のことは気にせずに先に行ってください。
examples.english: Please go on ahead without worrying about me.

examples.japanese: 夕食を食べずに私を待っていてくれたんですか？
examples.english: Did you wait for me without eating dinner?

examples.japanese: 今日は、頭が痛かったから、学校に行かずに家で寝ていました。
examples.english: Today my head was hurting so without going to school I stayed home and slept.

examples.japanese: 今日は料理を作らずに、外食しに行こうよ。
examples.english: Today, let's go out to eat without cooking anything.

meaning: can't help but; dying to; extremely ~
structure: Verb ない (ない stem) + ずにはいられない

examples.japanese: あの本を読まずにはいられない。
examples.english: I can't help but to read that book.

examples.japanese: 彼女は彼のことを考えずにはいられなかった。
examples.english: She couldn’t stop thinking of him.

examples.japanese: 彼はテレビを見ずにはいられない人。
examples.english: He is a compulsive TV viewer.

examples.japanese: あの人はすごく面白いです。話を聞いたら、笑わずにはいられない。
examples.english: That person is very interesting. When you hear what they have to say you can't help but laugh.

examples.japanese: 明日のワールドカップの試合は、見ずにはいられない。
examples.english: I need to watch tomorrow's world cup match.

examples.japanese: この店のカレーはとても辛い。ちょっと食べても水を飲まずにはいられない。
examples.english: The curry at this shop is very spicy. Even just from eating a little bit you'll be reaching for water.

meaning: repeated at intervals, every ~
structure: Noun (measurable) + ずつ

examples.japanese: 私たちは一歩ずつ進みましょう。
examples.english: Let's move forward one step at a time.

examples.japanese: 彼女は少しずつ回復している。
examples.english: She is recovering little-by-little.

examples.japanese: 一日漢字を10個ずつ勉強しましょう！
examples.english: Let's study 10 kanji a day!

examples.japanese: 彼女はお客さんのメールを一個ずつ返事しています。
examples.english: She responds to the customer's email one by one.

examples.japanese: 私は毎日、単語を五つずつ覚えています。
examples.english: I learn 5 new words everyday.

examples.japanese: 私は英語が少しずつ上達してきた。
examples.english: I have come to improve my English little-by-little.

meaning: In ~ / At ~ / In terms of ~ (formal)
structure: Noun + において / における + Noun

examples.japanese: 現代社会において、インターネットは必要不可欠だ。
examples.english: In modern society, the internet is indispensable.

examples.japanese: 教育における問題は複雑だ。
examples.english: The problems in education are complex.

examples.japanese: このコンテストにおける審査基準を説明します。
examples.english: I will explain the judging criteria for this contest.

notes: Formal written equivalent of で (location/context). における attributively modifies nouns. Common in essays, news, and academic writing.

meaning: By ~ / Due to ~ / Depending on ~
structure: Noun + によって / により

examples.japanese: この絵はピカソによって描かれた。
examples.english: This painting was painted by Picasso.

examples.japanese: 努力によって夢が実現できる。
examples.english: Dreams can come true through effort.

examples.japanese: 人によって意見が違う。
examples.english: Opinions differ depending on the person.

notes: Three uses: (1) agent in passive sentences (by ~); (2) means/cause (by means of / due to); (3) variation by condition (depending on). により is the formal variant.

meaning: Over a period of ~ / Throughout ~
structure: Noun (time/range) + にわたって / にわたる + Noun

examples.japanese: 彼は10年にわたって研究を続けた。
examples.english: He continued his research for 10 years.

examples.japanese: 全国にわたる調査が行われた。
examples.english: A nationwide survey was conducted.

examples.japanese: 長期にわたる交渉の末、合意に達した。
examples.english: After prolonged negotiations, an agreement was reached.

notes: Indicates a span of time or range over which something extends. にわたる modifies nouns attributively; にわたって modifies verbs adverbially.

meaning: Starting with ~ / Including ~ / Such as ~
structure: Noun + をはじめ / をはじめとして / をはじめとする

examples.japanese: 東京をはじめ、日本の主要都市を訪れた。
examples.english: I visited the major cities of Japan, starting with Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 彼をはじめとするメンバーが参加した。
examples.english: The members, including him, participated.

examples.japanese: 野菜をはじめとして、果物も食べましょう。
examples.english: Let's eat vegetables and also fruits and so on.

notes: Introduces a representative example from a larger group. The noun before をはじめ is usually the most prominent example.

meaning: Although ~ / Even though ~ (contrast, formal)
structure: Plain form + ものの

examples.japanese: 試験に合格したものの、自信がない。
examples.english: Although I passed the exam, I don't have confidence.

examples.japanese: 努力したものの、うまくいかなかった。
examples.english: Even though I tried hard, it didn't go well.

examples.japanese: わかっているものの、なかなかできない。
examples.english: Even though I understand, I still can't manage to do it.

notes: A formal concessive conjunction. The second clause often describes a result that contradicts what might be expected from the first.

meaning: That's why ~ / It means that ~ / No wonder ~
structure: Plain form + わけだ

examples.japanese: 彼は10年間日本に住んでいた。日本語が上手なわけだ。
examples.english: He lived in Japan for 10 years. No wonder his Japanese is good.

examples.japanese: つまり、あなたが間違っているというわけだ。
examples.english: In other words, it means you are wrong.

examples.japanese: 結局、彼は来なかったわけだ。
examples.english: So in the end, the story is that he didn't come.

notes: Expresses a logical conclusion drawn from the preceding context. わけではない means 'it doesn't mean that ~' (partial negation).

meaning: Far from ~ / Not only ~ but also ~
structure: Noun / Plain form + どころか

examples.japanese: 謝るどころか、怒り始めた。
examples.english: Far from apologizing, he started to get angry.

examples.japanese: 上手になるどころか、もっと下手になった。
examples.english: Far from getting better, I got even worse.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語どころか、フランス語も話せる。
examples.english: She can speak not only English, but even French.

notes: Emphasizes that reality is the opposite of, or far exceeds, what was mentioned first. Often carries a surprised or frustrated tone.

meaning: For ~ / Considering ~ / Despite ~
structure: Plain form / Noun + の + わりに

examples.japanese: このレストランは値段のわりに味がいい。
examples.english: For the price, this restaurant has good food.

examples.japanese: 若いわりに落ち着いている。
examples.english: For someone young, he is quite calm.

examples.japanese: 勉強したわりに点数が低かった。
examples.english: Considering how much I studied, my score was low.

notes: Implies a gap or mismatch between expectation and reality. Can express pleasant surprise or disappointment.

meaning: After ~ / At the end of ~ (following a long process)
structure: Verb[た] / Noun + の + 末に

examples.japanese: 長い話し合いの末に、決定が下された。
examples.english: After lengthy discussions, a decision was made.

examples.japanese: 悩んだ末に、留学することにした。
examples.english: After much deliberation, I decided to study abroad.

examples.japanese: 努力の末に、夢が実現した。
examples.english: After a great deal of effort, my dream came true.

notes: Implies the culmination of a prolonged process. Contrast with 〜あげく(に), which usually has a negative or anticlimactic connotation.

meaning: While ~ / Even though ~ (written, formal)
structure: Verb[stem] + つつ / つつも

examples.japanese: 音楽を聞きつつ、仕事をした。
examples.english: I worked while listening to music.

examples.japanese: わかっているつつも、変えられない。
examples.english: Even though I understand, I can't change it.

examples.japanese: 会社の発展を願いつつ、退職しました。
examples.english: While wishing for the company's growth, I retired.

notes: Formal/literary equivalent of 〜ながら (simultaneous) and 〜ても (concessive). つつも adds a stronger concessive nuance.

meaning: Judging from ~ / From the standpoint of ~
structure: Noun + からすると / からすれば / からして

examples.japanese: 彼の態度からすると、知っているようだ。
examples.english: Judging from his attitude, he seems to know.

examples.japanese: 専門家からすれば、当然のことだ。
examples.english: From an expert's standpoint, it's obvious.

examples.japanese: その発言からして、彼は怒っている。
examples.english: Just from that remark, you can tell he's angry.

notes: Indicates a basis for a judgment or inference. からして adds 'even from just that one thing you can tell…' — an even stronger inference.

meaning: In addition to ~ / On top of ~
structure: Noun + に加えて / に加え

examples.japanese: 寒さに加えて、雪まで降ってきた。
examples.english: In addition to the cold, it even started snowing.

examples.japanese: 才能に加えて、努力も必要だ。
examples.english: In addition to talent, effort is also necessary.

examples.japanese: 語学力に加え、コミュニケーション能力も求められる。
examples.english: Communication skills are required in addition to language ability.

notes: Adds a cumulative element, often implying the second element compounds or worsens a situation. More formal than 〜だけでなく〜も.

meaning: Without doing ~ / Without ever ~
structure: Verb[dict] + ことなく

examples.japanese: 休むことなく働き続けた。
examples.english: He kept working without resting.

examples.japanese: 諦めることなく夢を追い続けた。
examples.english: She kept chasing her dream without giving up.

examples.japanese: 一度も失敗することなく完成した。
examples.english: It was completed without a single failure.

notes: Formal written expression. The plain-form equivalent is 〜ないで / 〜ずに. More emphatic and literary in feel.

meaning: Along with ~ / As ~ increases/changes
structure: Noun / Verb[dict] + に伴って / に伴い / に伴う + Noun

examples.japanese: 経済成長に伴って、生活水準が上がった。
examples.english: Along with economic growth, the standard of living rose.

examples.japanese: 年齢に伴う体力の低下は自然なことだ。
examples.english: A decline in physical strength accompanying age is natural.

examples.japanese: 気温の上昇に伴い、熱中症に注意が必要だ。
examples.english: With rising temperatures, care must be taken against heatstroke.

notes: Expresses a proportional or parallel change. に伴う attributively modifies the noun that follows it.

meaning: From the fact that ~ / Since ~ (as a basis for judgment)
structure: Plain form + ことから

examples.japanese: 彼が黙っていることから、知っていると判断した。
examples.english: From the fact that he was silent, I judged that he knew.

examples.japanese: その花が白いことから、「白雪姫」と名付けられた。
examples.english: From the fact that its flowers are white, it was named 'Snow White'.

examples.japanese: 人気があることから、予約が必要だ。
examples.english: Because it is popular, reservations are required.

notes: Presents evidence or a reason that leads to a conclusion or naming. Slightly formal; the conclusion often follows naturally from the evidence.

meaning: although (it is a certain time/condition); even though normally
structure: Verb (casual) + どころではないどころじゃない | Noun

examples.japanese: 彼はよく間違いをするが、バカどころではない。
examples.english: He often makes mistakes, but he is no fool.

examples.japanese: 宿題がたくさんあってテレビを見るどころではない。
examples.english: There's a bunch of homework to do, this is no time to be watching TV.

examples.japanese: 風邪がひどくて、遊びに行くどころじゃない。
examples.english: I have a bad cold and can't even think about going out right now.

examples.japanese: 彼女はケーキ屋で働いているから、毎年クリスマスは彼氏とデートどころではない。
examples.english: She works at a cake shop so every year on Christmas she has no time to go on a date with her boyfriend.

examples.japanese: 他人の仕事を手伝うどころではありません。自分の仕事も間に合わないんです。
examples.english: There is no time to be helping other people with their work. You'll end up being late with your own work.

examples.japanese: 年末から母の入院で、お正月どころではありません。
examples.english: My mother has been hospitalized since the end of the year, so I've been too preoccupied to even think about New Year's activities.

meaning: although (it is a certain time/condition); even though normally
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + どころか | Noun | な-adjective + (な) | い-adjective

examples.japanese: もっと勉強しないと、N2どころかN3も無理だ。
examples.english: If you do not study more, you will not be able to pass N2, let alone N3.

examples.japanese: そんな食べ物、健康になるどころか、病気になっちゃうよ。
examples.english: That food isn't going to make you healthy, on the contrary it will make you sick.

examples.japanese: 「夏休みは取れそう？」「忙しくて夏休みどころか日曜日も休めない。」
examples.english: "Does it look like you can take summer break off?""I'm so busy I won't be able to take a summer break, much less even a Sunday off."

examples.japanese: 医者に出された薬を飲んでいるのに、よくなるどころか、症状はひどくなる一方だよ。
examples.english: Even though I'm taking the medicine my doctor gave me, I am not getting better. On the contrary, my symptoms keep getting worse.

examples.japanese: 私は彼に役に立つどころか、迷惑もかけた。
examples.english: I was far from being of any help to him. Rather I got in his way.

examples.japanese: 忙しくて、休みをとるどころか、食事をする時間もない。
examples.english: I’m so busy that I don’t even have time to eat, let alone take a day off.

meaning: any kind of; every; whatsoever; whatever
structure: どうせ + phrase

examples.japanese: どうせやるなら上手にやれ。
examples.english: If you're going to do it no matter what, do it well!

examples.japanese: どうせ行くんでしょ。
examples.english: I daresay you are going to go no matter what.

examples.japanese: どうせ参加しないのなら、早めに伝えたほうがいい。
examples.english: If you're not going to participate after all, it's best to say so as quick as possible.

examples.japanese: どうせ、試合の前にまだ一週間があるのでもっと練習しょう。
examples.english: Anyway, we still have a week to go before the game so let's practice some more.

examples.japanese: 今から行ってもどうせ遅刻だから、行かないことにする。
examples.english: Even if I go now I will be late anyway, so I decided not to go.

examples.japanese: どうせ郵便局に行くのなら、切手を買ってくださいませんか？
examples.english: If you're going to go to the post office anyway, could you please buy me some stamps?

meaning: can’t help but; can’t refrain from ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 得ない

examples.japanese: あの人が結婚したって本当！？え～！あり得ないよ！
examples.english: Is it true that he got married? No way! It's not possible!

examples.japanese: あの真面目な彼が犯人？そんなことはあり得ない。
examples.english: You think someone as earnest as him is the culprit? That's unbelievable..

examples.japanese: 地震がいつ来るかなんて、予測し得ないことだ。
examples.english: It is unpredictable when an earthquake will occur.

examples.japanese: 無から有は生じ得ない。
examples.english: Nothing can come of nothing.

examples.japanese: 機械は完全には人力に代わり得ない。
examples.english: Machinery cannot completely take the place of human labor.

examples.japanese: このような困難な仕事は、我々の力だけでは処理し得ない。
examples.english: These difficult tasks cannot be handled by our own power alone.

meaning: unable to; cannot; it is not possible to ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 得る(える/うる)

examples.japanese: 君の話を信じるよ。だってこの世界ではどんなことでも起こり得るから。
examples.english: I believe in your story. I mean, anything is possible in this world.

examples.japanese: 事故はいつでも起こり得るので、気をつけてください。
examples.english: Accidents can happen at any time, so please be careful!

examples.japanese: タバコを吸いすぎや、お酒を飲み過ぎは病気の原因になり得ます。
examples.english: Excessive smoking and drinking too much alcohol can cause illness.

examples.japanese: 運動不足は病気の原因になり得るので、できるだけ体を動かすようにしてください。
examples.english: Lack of exercise can cause illness, so try to move as much as you can.

examples.japanese: この不況では大手企業の倒産もあり得る。
examples.english: In this recession, it's possible some major companies may go bankrupt.

examples.japanese: 1つのミスが、会社を倒産に導くこともあり得ることだ。気を抜かずに、頑張っていこう。
examples.english: One mistake can cause a company to go bankrupt. Let's do our best without fail.

meaning: furthermore; again; more and more ~
structure: 再びふたたび + phrase

examples.japanese: 来週の月曜日からレッスンを再び開始したいですか？
examples.english: Would you like to restart your lessons from next Monday?

examples.japanese: 今年の旅行は楽しかった。来年の冬再びここに来たい。
examples.english: This year's trip was fun. I want to come here again next winter.

examples.japanese: 10年後にようやく彼は、再び故郷の町を見た。
examples.english: He finally saw his hometown again after ten years.

examples.japanese: 昨日私は、図書館で１ヶ月前に出会った少女と再び会った。
examples.english: Yesterday I once again met the girl whom I met in the library a month ago.

examples.japanese: 本当に最悪の男だ。二度と再びあの男とは会いたくない。
examples.english: He really is the worst guy... I don't ever want to see him again.

examples.japanese: 彼女の両親が事故で亡くなってからピアノを弾かなかった。昨日は再び弾き始めた。
examples.english: She did not play the piano after her parents died in an accident. She started playing again yesterday.

meaning: style; manner; way​
structure: どんなあんなこんなどういう + ふうに + Verb | Verb (casual)

examples.japanese: こんなふうにやりなさい。
examples.english: Please do it like this.

examples.japanese: 私もあんなふうになりたいです。
examples.english: I also want to become that way.

examples.japanese: どういうふうに動くか見せてください。
examples.english: Please show me how it works.

examples.japanese: すみません、これはどんなふうにやればよいでしょうか。
examples.english: Excuse me, what is the correct way to do this?

examples.japanese: 勝手にそんなふうにしないでください。教えたどおりにやればいいです。
examples.english: Please don't do it your own way. Do it as you were taught to.

examples.japanese: 彼の日本語がペラペラですね。私もあんなふうになりたいです。
examples.english: His Japanese is very fluent. I also want to become like that.

pattern: がきっかけで / をきっかけに
meaning: thanks to; owing to; because of ~
structure: Verb (た form) + の/こと + がきっかけでをきっかけに | Noun

examples.japanese: 彼女は病気をきっかけにそのつまらない仕事を辞めた。
examples.english: She used her illness to quit that boring job.

examples.japanese: 昨年の事故をきっかけとして、安全対策が強化された。
examples.english: As a result of last year's accident, safety measures have been strengthened.

examples.japanese: 子供が生まれたのをきっかけとして、タバコを辞めた。
examples.english: As a result of my child being born, I quit smoking.

examples.japanese: パソコンを買ってもらったことがきっかけで、プログラミングの勉強を始めました。
examples.english: Taking advantage of the computer I received, I began studying programming.

examples.japanese: 失恋をきっかけに、海外に出て仕事をしようと決心した。
examples.english: After experiencing heartbreak, I decided to move and work abroad.

examples.japanese: 日本でのホームステイをきっかけに日本の文化にとても興味を持つようになった。
examples.english: As a result of my homestay in Japan, I became very interested in Japanese culture.

meaning: to seem to be; to appear; to behave as ~
structure: な-adjective な + げ | い-adjective + いIrregular: いい/よい => よさ | Verb ます (stem form) | Verb たい (tai form) | Noun (very limited)

examples.japanese: 何か、言いたげだね。
examples.english: They look like they want to say something.

examples.japanese: あの人は寂しげな目をしている。
examples.english: That person has a lonely look in their eyes

examples.japanese: 彼は眠たげな声でおはようと言った。
examples.english: He said good morning with a sleepy voice.

examples.japanese: ずいぶん、自信ありげだね。
examples.english: You seem very confident.

examples.japanese: 一人暮らしのために家を出る日、母は少し寂しげだった。
examples.english: My mother looked a little sad on the day I moved out to live by myself.

examples.japanese: そりゃあちょっとあやしげに見えますからね、そう思いませんか？
examples.english: It looks a little suspicious, don’t you think?

meaning: while, although; on the other hand~
structure: 逆に + phrase

examples.japanese: 娘はスポーツが好きだが、逆に息子はスポーツが嫌いだ。
examples.english: My daughter likes sports, but on the other hand my son hates them.

examples.japanese: 天気予報と逆に、雨が降り続いている。
examples.english: It’s been raining nonstop in contrast to the weather forecast.

examples.japanese: 彼はゲームが大好きだが、逆に弟さんは嫌いだ。
examples.english: He loves to play games, but contrarily his younger brother dislikes them.

examples.japanese: 逆に、嫌いな日本の料理はなんですか？
examples.english: On the other hand, what is a Japanese food that you hate?

examples.japanese: 私達の期待とは逆に、今年の売り上げは増えなかった。
examples.english: Contrary to our expectations, sales did not increase this year.

examples.japanese: 私はストレスがたまると食欲がなくなるではなく、逆に何か食べないと気が済まなくなる。
examples.english: I don't lose my appetite when I get stressed, rather I can't calm down unless I eat something.

meaning: conversely; on the contrary ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + 反面 | Noun + である | な-adjective + な/である | い-adjective | Phrase 1 + その反面 + Phrase 2

examples.japanese: この部屋は日当たりがいい反面、夏はかなり暑いです。
examples.english: This room has great light exposure, but on the other hand it is very hot in the summer.

examples.japanese: 子供の成長は嬉しい反面、どこか寂しい。
examples.english: I'm happy to see my children grow, but on the other hand I am a little bit sad.

examples.japanese: 彼氏ができたら、楽しい反面、一人の時間がすくなくなりました。
examples.english: I'm happy to have a boyfriend, but on the other hand my time for myself has considerably dropped.

examples.japanese: 一人暮らしは楽しい反面、一緒に話す相手がいないので寂しいこともあります。
examples.english: Living alone is enjoyable, but on the other hand it can sometimes be a little lonely not having someone to talk to.

examples.japanese: 子供にとって、インターネットは便利な反面、悪い影響を与えることもあります。
examples.english: For children, on one hand the inernet is very convenient, but there are also some negative effects as well.

examples.japanese: 転職をしたら、収入が増えた反面、ストレスも増えました。
examples.english: When changing jobs, although my salary increased, my stress also increased.

meaning: being the case; precisely because; as expected from ~
structure: 果たして + phrase

examples.japanese: 果たしてそうだろうか。
examples.english: Can it really be so?

examples.japanese: 果たして本当に足音が聞こえたのかどうかはわからない。
examples.english: I don’t know for sure if I really heard the footsteps or not.

examples.japanese: そのうわさは果たして本当だろうか。
examples.english: Can that rumor really be true?

examples.japanese: 私があの店にいるとき、彼らがそこにやってきたのは果たして偶然だろうか？
examples.english: Was it really a coincidence that they came to the store while I was there?

examples.japanese: この程度の金額で、果たして彼が承知するだろうか。
examples.english: Surely he will agree to this amount of money.

examples.japanese: 皆さんにも果たしていただく役割があります。
examples.english: Everyone surely has a role to carry out.

meaning: about; roughly; generally; approximately; completely​ ~
structure: 一応 + phrase

examples.japanese: 一応やりました。
examples.english: I did it (but it may still need some work).

examples.japanese: 一応やってみます。
examples.english: (I may not be able to do it well, but) I will give it a shot.

examples.japanese: 一応、付き合っている人がいるんだ。
examples.english: I am sort of seeing someone..

examples.japanese: 彼はもう寝たかもしれないけど、一応電話してみようかな。
examples.english: He may already be asleep, but I guess I should try to give him a call..

examples.japanese: 一応、明日までに返事をくれる？
examples.english: Can you at least give me an answer by tomorrow?

examples.japanese: 一応、連絡先を教えてくれる？
examples.english: Can you give me your contact information just in case?

meaning: except; with the exception of; excluding ~
structure: Noun + 以外 + (の、は、に）

examples.japanese: 食事以外には何ができる？
examples.english: Apart from eating, what else can we do?

examples.japanese: 彼女以外誰もいない。
examples.english: There's no one else but her.

examples.japanese: 水以外何も見えない。
examples.english: I don't see anything other than water.

examples.japanese: 彼は英語以外の言語は全く知らない。
examples.english: He knows no languages other than English.

examples.japanese: 私は彼女以外はみんな好きだ。
examples.english: I like everyone aside from her.

examples.japanese: 仕事以外のことも話せてよかったです。
examples.english: I was glad to be able to talk about something other than work.

meaning: more than…; above ~
structure: Verb (casual) + 以上に | Noun | な-adjective | 以上の + Noun

examples.japanese: 今まで以上に仕事を頑張ります。
examples.english: I will work even harder at work than I have until now.

examples.japanese: 必要以上にたくさんのお金を使わないでください。
examples.english: Please don’t use more money than you need.

examples.japanese: 私が予想していた以上に彼の様態はよくなかった。
examples.english: His condition was worse than I had expected.

examples.japanese: 今以上に日本語ができるようになりたいです。
examples.english: I want to get even better at Japanese than I am now.

examples.japanese: 私たちが泊まったホテルは、予想以上に豪華だった。
examples.english: The hotel that we stayed in was even more extravagant than we had imagined.

examples.japanese: 彼らは、わたしが考えた以上に強い反応を示した。
examples.english: They were taking the news worse than i had expected.

meaning: more than; not less than; beyond ~
structure: Verb (casual) + 以上（は） | Noun + である | な-adjective + である

examples.japanese: 約束した以上、きちんと守ってくださいね。
examples.english: You've made a promise, so be sure to keep it!

examples.japanese: 学生である以上、アルバイトではなく勉強が大事ですよ。
examples.english: Because you are a student, your studies are more important than your part-time job.

examples.japanese: 給料がこんなに安い以上は、転職を考える人がいるのも当然だ。
examples.english: With such low salaries, it's no wonder there are people who want to change jobs.

examples.japanese: お金を払って勉強する以上は、しっかり身につけたい。
examples.english: Since I am paying money to study, I really want to learn.

examples.japanese: 一度やると決めた以上は、最後まで責任を持ってやらないと。
examples.english: Once you decide to do something, you must stay responsible until the end.

examples.japanese: 出場が決まった以上、いい結果が出せるように頑張ろうと思う。
examples.english: Since my participation has been confirmed, I want to work hard to get a good result.

meaning: suddenly; accidentally; unexpectedly; unintentionally ~
structure: いきなり + action

examples.japanese: いきなり男の人に道を聞かれた。
examples.english: A man suddenly asked me for directions.

examples.japanese: いきなりあなたにメールを送ってしまい申し訳ありません。
examples.english: I'm sorry for sending you an email suddenly.

examples.japanese: 彼は彼女の手からいきなりハンドバッグを取った。
examples.english: He suddenly grabbed her purse from her hand.

examples.japanese: 彼女の兄弟は、いきなり結婚式に現れた。
examples.english: Her siblings showed up at the wedding out of the blue.

examples.japanese: 今日は会社に来るとき、私の前でタクシーがいきなり止まってびっくりした。
examples.english: Today on my way to work, I was surprised by a taxi suddenly stopping right in front of me.

examples.japanese: いつも厳しい社長はいきなり笑い出した。
examples.english: The always strict company president suddenly burst out laughing.

meaning: at once; right away; promptly
structure: 一気に + phrase

examples.japanese: お茶を一気に飲みました。
examples.english: I drank all of the tea at once.

examples.japanese: 私はこの本を一気に読みました。
examples.english: I read this book all in one go.

examples.japanese: 彼は一気に１０時間働いた。
examples.english: He worked for 10 hours without stopping.

examples.japanese: こういう仕事は一気にやった方がいいんだよ。
examples.english: This kind of work is best done all at once.

examples.japanese: 買ってきたお菓子は一気に食べないで、少しずつ食べましょうね。
examples.english: Don't eat all of the sweets you bought in one go, let's take our time eating them.

examples.japanese: その仕事を一気にやってしまいなさい。
examples.english: Please finish that job immediately.

meaning: while, although; on the other hand~
structure: Verb (casual) + 一方（で） | Noun + である | な-adjective + である | い-adjective

examples.japanese: お母さんは優しい一方で、お父さんはこわい。
examples.english: My mother is kind, but on the other hand my father is scary.

examples.japanese: 父は自分に厳しい一方で、他人には優しい。
examples.english: My father is very strict with himself but very kind to others.

examples.japanese: 彼女の仕事は夏は非常に忙しい一方、冬は暇になる。
examples.english: Her work is very busy in the summer, but on the other hand it is much more relaxed in the winter.

examples.japanese: 彼は俳優である一方で、歌手としても活躍している。
examples.english: He is an actor, and on the other hand is active as a singer.

examples.japanese: 海外旅行は非日常を体験できることから、楽しいと感じることが多い一方で、不安なこともある。
examples.english: Traveling abroad can be extraordinary, so it's often fun, but on the other hand can be uneasy.

examples.japanese: その仕事はあまり面白くなかったが、その一方で給与はよかった。
examples.english: That job was not very interesting, but on the other hand it paid well.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: いわゆる + Noun

examples.japanese: 彼はいわゆる語学の天才だ。
examples.english: He is what is called a genius in language.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいわゆる本の虫です。
examples.english: She is what we call a bookworm.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいわゆる「やり手」だ。
examples.english: She is what we call a“go‐getter."

examples.japanese: 彼は何でも知っているから、いわゆる生きる辞書だ。
examples.english: He knows everything, like a living dictionary.

examples.japanese: 彼女の考えは、いわゆる進歩的なものでした。
examples.english: Her ideas were progressive, so to speak.

examples.japanese: 兄はいわゆるポップミュージックに興味があります。
examples.english: My brother is interested in what you call pop music.

meaning: to end up; in the end; finally; after all ~
structure: いよいよ + phrase

examples.japanese: いよいよ大学の生活が始まります。初めて親に離れるからちょっと心配する。
examples.english: My university life has finally begun. Though it is my first time to be away from my parents so I am a little nervous.

examples.japanese: いよいよ来週の日曜日が母の日だ。母に何を買って上げたほうがいいかな。
examples.english: Mother's day is finally coming up next Sunday. I wonder what should I get for my mom..?

examples.japanese: いよいよスピーチが始まる。どうしよう！めちゃ緊張しているよ。
examples.english: The speech is about to start! I'm very nervous!

examples.japanese: いよいよ彼女の出番だ。頑張って練習したからうまく行けるといいね！
examples.english: Finally it's time for her entrance! She worked hard with her practice, so I hope it goes well!

examples.japanese: いよいよ結婚式が目前に迫ってなんとなく落ち着かない。
examples.english: Now that our wedding ceremony is just around the corner, we can't seem to calm down.

examples.japanese: 昨晩から胃が痛くなった。今朝に痛みがいよいよ酷くなった。
examples.english: My stomach has been hurting since last night and this morning the pain has without a doubt gotten worse.

meaning: no sooner than; as soon as ~
structure: Verb (た form) + かと思ったらかと思うとかと思えば

examples.japanese: 空が急に暗くなってきたかと思うと、雨が降ってきた。
examples.english: No sooner had the sky turned dark, when it started to rain.

examples.japanese: 娘が帰って来たかと思うと、すぐに家を出ていった。
examples.english: Just as my daughter returned home, she was out the door again.

examples.japanese: うちの近くの公園の花が咲いたかと思ったら、もう散ってしまった。
examples.english: No sooner than the flowers were starting to bloom at our nearby park, the pedals had fallen.

examples.japanese: 息子が勉強を始めたかと思ったら、リビングでドラマを見ている。
examples.english: No sooner than my son had started studying, he was already in the living room watching TV.

examples.japanese: 彼は食事を始めたかと思ったら寝てしまった。
examples.english: Just when he thought he would start eating he fell asleep.

examples.japanese: 日曜日なのに、お父さんは忙しそうだね。さっき戻ったかと思うと、また出かけて行った。
examples.english: Even though it is Sunday, father seems very busy. No sooner than he returned a moment ago, he was already out the door again.

meaning: as soon as; the moment ~
structure: Verb + か(dictionary form) + Verb ない + か + のうちに

examples.japanese: 授業が終わるか終わらないかのうちに彼は教室を出た。
examples.english: He left the classrom as soon as class ended.

examples.japanese: 彼が電車が止まるか止まらないかのうちにホームに飛び降りた。
examples.english: He jumped onto the platform just as the train stopped.

examples.japanese: 会社に着くか着かないかのうちに雨が降り出しました。
examples.english: It started raining just as I arrived at the company.

examples.japanese: とても疲れていたのだろう。ソファーに横になるかならないかのうちに眠ってしまった。
examples.english: I must have been really tired. I passed out right away after sitting on my sofa.

examples.japanese: 信号が赤から青に変わるか変わらないかのうちに、先頭のバイクが飛び出していった。
examples.english: Just as the light changed from red to green, the bike in the front darted off.

examples.japanese: とてもお腹が空いていたのだろう。テーブルに座るか座らないかのうちに食べ始めた。
examples.english: I must have been really hungry. I started eating immediately as I sat down at the table.

meaning: conversely; on the contrary ~
structure: Phrase 1 + かえって + phrase 2

examples.japanese: 彼は手助けどころかかえって邪魔になった。
examples.english: He was in no position to help, on the contrary he got in the way.

examples.japanese: それはかえって言わずにおく方がよい。
examples.english: That had rather better be left unsaid.

examples.japanese: 彼女は痩せるどころかかえって体重が増えた。
examples.english: Her weight went up instead of down.

examples.japanese: タクシーに乗ったら電車よりかえって時間が掛かった。
examples.english: Surprisingly, taking a taxi took longer than the train.

examples.japanese: 親切で言ったつもりだが、かえって怒らせてしまったようだ。
examples.english: I planned on saying it kindly, but I've instead seemed to have angered them.

examples.japanese: 不幸がかえって幸福となる。
examples.english: One's misfortune can turn into a blessing.

meaning: not necessarily so; is not always true
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + 限り | Noun + である
