examples.japanese: 明日は、雨が降らない限り、10時に学校で会いましょう。
examples.english: As long as it doesn't rain tomorrow, let's meet at the school at 10 am.

examples.japanese: この仕事は、私が生きている限り、ずっと続けていきたい。
examples.english: I want to continue doing this job as long as I am alive.

examples.japanese: 私の知っている限りでは、彼女はまだ結婚していません。
examples.english: As far as I know she's still not married.

examples.japanese: 日本にいる限り、日本語が必要だよ。
examples.english: While you are in Japan, you need to know Japanese (language).

examples.japanese: 今のやり方を変えない限り、悪い状況は続くでしょう。
examples.english: As long the current way of doing things doesn't change, these bad conditions will likely continue.

examples.japanese: お店の中にお客様がいる限り、お店は閉めません。
examples.english: While there are still customers inside, this shop will not close.

meaning: should do, but don't; absolutely not; there's no way ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + かねるかねます

examples.japanese: すぐにお返事はできかねます。
examples.english: I can not give you an immediate answer.

examples.japanese: 私はそれに賛同しかねます。
examples.english: I am not able to agree with that.

examples.japanese: 残念ながら、そのご提案はお受けいたしかねます。
examples.english: Unfortunately I cannot accept that proposal.

examples.japanese: 私は担当者ではございませんので、その質問にはお答えしかねます。
examples.english: I am not in charge of this, so I cannot answer your questions.

examples.japanese: 飛行機で行くか、新幹線で行くか、まだ決めかねている。
examples.english: I still cannot decide weather to go by plane or shinkansen.

examples.japanese: 彼女の考えには賛成しかねるところが多いです。
examples.english: There are many points with her thinking that I cannot agree with.

meaning: from the point of view of; by the look of; judging from ~
structure: Noun + から言うとから言えばから言って

examples.japanese: 僕の成績から言えば、国立大学は無理だと思う。
examples.english: With these grades, I don’t think I'm going to be able to get into a national university

examples.japanese: 能力から言って、彼がこの仕事に一番適切だと思います。
examples.english: In terms of ability, I think he’s the best candidate for the job.

examples.japanese: 現状から言って、直ちにその計画を実行するのは無理だ。
examples.english: With our current condition, it would be impossible for us to execute the plan right away.

examples.japanese: この作文は、日本語能力から言えば、まだまだだが、内容はいい。
examples.english: This essay is not great in terms of Japanese ability, but the content itself is good.

examples.japanese: 僕の経験から言うと、留学をする前に基本的な文法や単語は復習しておいた方がいい。
examples.english: From my experience, before studying abroad it's best to review fundamental grammar and vocabulary.

examples.japanese: 客の立場から言うと、この店は入口が狭くて入りにくい。しかし、店の側から言えば管理やすい。
examples.english: From the perspective of the customer, this shop's entrance is narrow and hard to enter. However, from the perspective of the shop it is easy to manage.

meaning: judging from; based on; since; from; even ~
structure: Verb (casual) + からこそ | Noun + だ | だからこそ + phrase

examples.japanese: 早く起きたからこそ私は始発電車に間に合った。
examples.english: I was able to catch the first train because I woke up early.

examples.japanese: 毎日一生懸命に練習したからこそ、優勝できたのです。
examples.english: I was able to win because I trained every day to the best of my ability.

examples.japanese: 子どもの将来を考えたからこそ一流の大学に入れたいのです。
examples.english: Because I am thinking of my child's future, I want them to go to a first-class university.

examples.japanese: どうしてもかなえたい夢があるからこそ、辛くても頑張ります。
examples.english: Because I have a dream that I want to make come true no matter what is exactly why I can keep pushing through even when things are tough.

examples.japanese: 成功したからこそ、いろいろな失敗や辛い体験を笑いながら話せる。
examples.english: Because I succeeded, I can now talk about various failures and tough experiences while laughing.

examples.japanese: そういう態度で仕事をするからこそ、私は彼が嫌いだ。
examples.english: That attitude of his during work is exactly why I dislike him.

meaning: in terms of; from the point of view of ~
structure: Noun + から見るとから見ればから見て

examples.japanese: 虫嫌いな私から見ると、ゴキブリを手でつかむなんてありえない。
examples.english: For someone who hates bugs like me, catching cockroaches by hand is unthinkable.

examples.japanese: 緊張している様子から見て、彼らは新入社員だろう。
examples.english: Judjing from their nervious appearance, they must be new to the company.

examples.japanese: 専門家から見れば、間違ったダイエットをしている人が多いようだ。
examples.english: From the point of view of a specialist, many people have a flawed diet.

examples.japanese: 日本の習慣には、外国人から見ると妙なものもあるだろう。
examples.english: There may be some Japanese customs that seem strange from a foreigner’s perspective.

examples.japanese: 昔の人から見ると、現代人の生活のリズムは速すぎるかもしれない。
examples.english: From the point of view of people from the past, the rhythm of life for people nowadays may be too fast.

examples.japanese: あの様子から見て、彼は昨晩飲みすぎたようだ。
examples.english: By the looks of him, it seems that he drank a bit too much last night.

meaning: judging from; based on; since; from; even ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + からには | Verb (casual, past)

examples.japanese: 約束したからにはその約束を守らなければならない。
examples.english: Since you’ve made a promise, you must keep it.

examples.japanese: 私はJLPT N2 試験を受けるからには、合格したいです。
examples.english: Now that I will be taking the JLPT N2, I want to pass!

examples.japanese: 自分で決めたからには、大変でも頑張ります。
examples.english: Since this is something I decided, even if things get rough I will push through it.

examples.japanese: 北海道に来たからには、カニやイクラなど、海の幸を食べたい。
examples.english: Since I've come to Hokkaido, I want to eat various seafood like crab and squid.

examples.japanese: 大学に行くからには、毎日まじめに勉強するつもりだ。
examples.english: Since I will go to university, I plan to study earnestly everyday.

examples.japanese: 海外で生活するからには、色々と困ることが起こるのはしかたがない。
examples.english: When living abroad, it is inevitable that various problems will occur.

pattern: からすると / からすれば
meaning: judging from; based on; since; from; even ~
structure: Noun + からすると | からすれば

examples.japanese: 彼の症状からすると、心臓の病気かもしれません。
examples.english: Judging from his condition, it might be a heart illness.

examples.japanese: 今度のJLPTですが、今の皆さんの実力からすると問題なく合格できるでしょう。
examples.english: As for this upcoming JLPT exam, considering everyone's ability level you all should be able to pass without any problems.

examples.japanese: ラーメンを食べる時に音を出す習慣は外国人からすると、考えられないことだそうです。
examples.english: The custom of making sounds while eating ramen seems to be a bit strange for foreigners.

examples.japanese: この1年間の成績からすると、希望の大学を合格の可能性は十分になる。
examples.english: Judging from this year's results, there is a good chance you'll be accepted into your university of choice.

examples.japanese: 子供の能力からすると、どんなに頑張っても親の要求水準に答えることはできません。
examples.english: Judging from the children’s abilities, no matter how hard they work they will not be able to live up to their parents expectations.

examples.japanese: 周りの態度からすると、あの人が有名人ではないでしょうか。
examples.english: Judging from the attitudes of the people around him, he is probably a celebrity

meaning: difficult to do; is unreasonable / unrealistic / impossible
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + っこない | Verb (potential stem form)

examples.japanese: 車なんて買えっこないよ、自転車を買うお金もないんだから。
examples.english: There's no way I can buy a car! I don't even have enough money to buy a bicycle..

examples.japanese: 3歳の子供にそんな難しいことを言っても分かりっこないよ。
examples.english: If you say something that difficult to a 3-year-old, there's no way they are going to be able to understand you..

examples.japanese: もう新宿駅には100回以上行ったんだから、迷いっこないよ。
examples.english: I've been to Shinjuku station over 100 times, so there's no way I'd get lost there.

examples.japanese: 今日中に漢字を100字覚えるなんて無理だ。できっこない。
examples.english: It's impossible to memorize 100 kanji today.. There's no way I could do it..

examples.japanese: あの大学には合格しっこない僕はそんなに頭がよくないから。
examples.english: There's no way I could get into that university, I'm not that smart..

examples.japanese: こんなに弱い選手ばかりでは、次の試合に勝てっこない。
examples.english: With a team full of weak players like this, they won’t stand a chance in the next match.

meaning: how…!; what…!
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことだ | Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 風邪ぎみなら、早く寝ることですよ。
examples.english: If you feel like you're catching a cold, you should go to bed early.

examples.japanese: 無理をしないことだよ。
examples.english: You shouldn't push yourself too hard

examples.japanese: N2に合格したかったら、とにかく漢字を覚えることだよ。
examples.english: If you want to pass the N2, you should memorize kanji.

examples.japanese: 日本語がうまくなりたかったら、日本人の恋人をつくることですよ。
examples.english: If you want to improve your Japanese, you should get a Japanese boyfriend/girlfriend.

examples.japanese: 一度に全部は無理です。毎日少しずつ勉強することです。
examples.english: It is impossible to do it all at once. It is best to study a little bit everyday.

examples.japanese: いやなことを忘れるにはとにかく笑うことですよ。
examples.english: In order to help forget something negative, you should start by smiling.

meaning: so; therefore; the reason for something
structure: Usage style #1 | Noun + の + ことだから | Usage style #2 | Verb + ことだからことだし | Noun + である | な-adjective + な/である | い-adjective

examples.japanese: それは、私にとって重要なことだから答えて。
examples.english: It is very important for me, so please answer it.

examples.japanese: あなたのことだから上々でしょう。
examples.english: I'm sure you did an excellent (since it's you we're talking about).

examples.japanese: 明るい彼女のことだから、どこへ行ってもすぐ友達ができるでしょう。
examples.english: Since she has a bright personality, she is able to make friends no matter where she goes.

examples.japanese: 急を要することだから急いでください。
examples.english: Please hurry, it's urgent.

examples.japanese: ケチで有名な彼のことだから百円だって貸してくれないだろうな。
examples.english: He's got a reputation of being stingy with money, so it's doubtful he'd lend even just 100 yen.

examples.japanese: もう誰も来ないことだし、店を閉めよう。
examples.english: Since no one else will come, let's go ahead and close up shop.

meaning: how; in what way; how much; to what extent
structure: Verb (casual) + ことか | Noun + である | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 何度注意したことか？
examples.english: How many times have I warned you?

examples.japanese: この景色はなんときれいなことか。
examples.english: This scenery is incredibly beautiful!

examples.japanese: 僕は合格できたら、どんなに嬉しいことか。
examples.english: If I am able to pass, I will be immeasurably happy!

examples.japanese: 今まで何度酒をやめようと思ったことか。
examples.english: Until now how many times have I thought about quitting drinking?

examples.japanese: 学生時代、奨学金がもらえてどれほど助かったことか。
examples.english: Getting a scholarship when I was a student really saved me..

examples.japanese: 大好きな人に好きって伝えられることがどんなに幸せなことか。
examples.english: It is such a happy feeling being able to tell the person you love that you love them.

meaning: cannot do without ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことなく

examples.japanese: お父さんは10年間休むことなく会社に通った。
examples.english: My father worked for 10 years without taking a break.

examples.japanese: 彼らは試合に勝つために、1日も休むことなく練習に励んだ。
examples.english: In order to win the match, they practiced continually without any days off.

examples.japanese: 彼は緊張することなく、最後まで落ち着いて発表した。
examples.english: Without getting nervous, he gave his speech calmly until the end.

examples.japanese: 彼は何度失敗してもあきらめることなく、研究を続けた。
examples.english: No matter how many times he failed, he never gave up and continued his research.

examples.japanese: 同僚は同期にも相談することなく会社を辞めてしまった。
examples.english: My coworker quit in the same year he entered the company without consulting anyone.

examples.japanese: 夫は毎年忘れることなく、結婚記念日に花を贈ってくれる。
examples.english: My husband gives me flowers every year without forgetting our wedding anniversary.

meaning: have to do; must; should ~
structure: Verb (casual, past) + (という) + ことにはならない | な-adjective + だという | い-adjective + という

examples.japanese: でも、どうやらそんなことにはならないようです。
examples.english: But this did not seem likely to happen.

examples.japanese: 彼が絵が好きだからといって絵がうまいということにはならない。
examples.english: Just because he likes painting does not mean that he paints well.

examples.japanese: 彼女は貧しいからといって不幸だということにはならない。
examples.english: Just because she’s poor does not mean that she is unhappy.

examples.japanese: 他人が悪い事をしているからといって自分もそうしてよいということにはならない。
examples.english: Just because someone else is doing something bad does not mean it's OK for you to do it too.

examples.japanese: 本やインターネットの資料を写しただけではレポートを書いたことにはならない。
examples.english: Just because you copied text from the internet or books doesn’t mean that you’ve written a report.

examples.japanese: 彼女が貧しいからと言って不正直だと言うことにはならない。
examples.english: Just because she is poor, it does not mean that she is dishonest.

meaning: if only; I wish; I'm sorry it's not actually (regret)
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + くせして | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 大学生のくせして、そんなことも知らないの。
examples.english: Even though you are a university student, you don't know that?

examples.japanese: 彼は歌が下手なくせして、いつもカラオケに行きたがる。
examples.english: Despite being bad at singing, he always wants to go to do karaoke.

examples.japanese: 彼は大きな体のくせして、本当に力がないんだね。
examples.english: Despite having a large body, he doesn't really have any power.

examples.japanese: 何も知らないくせして、知っているようなことを言う。
examples.english: Even though you don't know anything, you talk as though you do.

examples.japanese: 彼女はおかしいだね。好きなくせして、嫌いだと言っている。
examples.english: She is a bit strange. Even though she likes him she says that she hates him.

examples.japanese: 他人の悪い口ばかりを言うもんじゃないよ、自分は何も出来ないくせして。
examples.english: You shouldn't be just saying bad things about others, especially when you can't do anything yourself.

meaning: if; in the case that ~
structure: Noun + なら + まだしも | Noun + は

examples.japanese: 一度だけならまだしも、二度も失敗してしまった。
examples.english: It would be alright if I only messed up once, but I failed twice..

examples.japanese: あの人、wordやexcelが使えないのはまだしも、メールもできないらしいよ。
examples.english: It's one thing that they don't know how to use word and excel, but apparently they don't even know how to use email.

examples.japanese: 僕の英語力では、旅行はまだしも、留学なんて無理です。
examples.english: With my English ability, I can handle a bit of traveling, but studying abroad is out of the question.

examples.japanese: 数分ならまだしも、30分も待ってません。
examples.english: I'm alright waiting a few minutes, but 30 minutes is unacceptable.

examples.japanese: 50年前ならまだしも、今そんなことを信じてる人はいません。
examples.english: If it were 50 years ago, someone may believe you, but no one is going to believe that story now.

examples.japanese: 数日ならまだしも、10日間も滞納しています。
examples.english: It would be alright if it were just a few days, but you are currently 10 days behind on your payment.

meaning: so as not to; to not ~
structure: U-verb (dictionary form) + まい | Ru-verb ます (stem form) | Exception: する => すまい | Exception: くる => こまい

examples.japanese: あんなところは二度と行くまい。
examples.english: I'll never go to such a place again.

examples.japanese: 彼はそう簡単に態度を変えるまい。
examples.english: He won't be able to change his behavior that easily.

examples.japanese: すべてが終わった。あの二人は二度と会うことはあるまい。
examples.english: Everything is over. Those 2 will probably never meet again.

examples.japanese: 信用していた親友が僕の秘密をもらした。絶対に許すまい。
examples.english: My good friend whom I trusted let my secret out. There's no way I can forgive them..

examples.japanese: その時私がどれほど苦しかったかは、誰にも分るまい。
examples.english: Nobody could possibly understand how much I was suffering at that time.

examples.japanese: 自分の目で確かめない限り、そんな恐ろしいことは誰も信じまい。
examples.english: Without seeing it with one's own eyes, there's no way anyone will believe such a thing.

meaning: continue to (go in negative direction)
structure: Verb (dictionary form) +（が） + まま（に） | Verb (られる form) +（が） | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 今のままにしておこう。
examples.english: Let's leave this as is.

examples.japanese: 思うままにどうぞ意見を言ってください。
examples.english: Please tell me your honest opinion.

examples.japanese: 上司に命令されるままに行動していただけだ。
examples.english: I just acted as directed by my boss.

examples.japanese: 感想を思うままにアンケートに書いてください。
examples.english: Please fill in the questionnaire as you like.

examples.japanese: 一日一日を、思うがままに生きたい。
examples.english: I want to live each and everyday to my heart's content.

examples.japanese: セールスマンに言われるまま、契約書にサインをしてしまった。
examples.english: I signed the contract as I was told by the salesman.

meaning: not … by any means; no matter how hard one tries, cannot ~
structure: まったく + Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 全く漢字が書けない。
examples.english: I cannot write kanji at all.

examples.japanese: 今日は全く風がない。
examples.english: There is no wind today.

examples.japanese: 私は彼の言うことがまったく理解できない。
examples.english: I can't understand what he says at all.

examples.japanese: 彼が怒っている理由は、私にはまったくわからない。
examples.english: I have no idea why he is angry.

examples.japanese: もしかしたら彼とはまったく関係がないかもしれない。
examples.english: Maybe this hasn’t got anything to do with him at all.

examples.japanese: 私の彼氏は、野球にはまったく興味がない。
examples.english: My boyfriend is not interested in baseball at all.

meaning: as it is bound to (happen); following the natural course
structure: Verb (casual) + の + も当然だ | Verb (て form)

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人で優しい人だから、みんなが好きになるのも当然だ。
examples.english: She is beautiful and kind, so it's only natural that everyone likes her.

examples.japanese: 相手のチームが弱いだから、試合を勝つのも当然だ。
examples.english: The other team is weak so of course we will win the match.

examples.japanese: このパソコンの機能がよいから高い値段で売られるのも当然だ。
examples.english: This computer has good functionality, so it's no wonder why it is sold at a high price.

examples.japanese: 彼はあんなひどいことを言ったから、彼女が怒るのも当然だ。
examples.english: It's only natural that she would be upset after he said such a horrible thing.

examples.japanese: 彼の息子は全国大会で優勝したから、自慢するのも当然だ。
examples.english: His son won the national competition, so it's only natural for him to brag about it.

examples.japanese: 彼が、お父さんのことを誇りにしているのも当然だ。
examples.english: It's only natural for him to be proud of his father.

meaning: because; for that reason
structure: Verb (casual) +（んだ） + ものもん | Noun + なんだ | な-adjective + なんだ | い-adjective +（んだ）

examples.japanese: 今日は早く帰ってきたんです。体調がよくないんだもの。
examples.english: I came home early today because I don't feel well

examples.japanese: 「またN2不合格だった．．．」「しょうがないよ、難しいもんね。」
examples.english: "I failed the N2 again...""It can't be helped, it's really tough to pass."

examples.japanese: 「どうして食べないの？」「だって、全然美味しくないんだもん。」
examples.english: "Why don't you eat it?""Because it doesn't taste good at all."

examples.japanese: 高いんですもの、買えません。
examples.english: It's too expensive, so I cannot buy it.

examples.japanese: 今日の試験はダメだった。勉強しなかったんだもん、仕方がない。
examples.english: Today's test was no good. I didn't study for it though, so it can't be helped.

examples.japanese: 私何も話すことなんかありませんよ。だって何も知らないんですもの。
examples.english: I have nothing to say. I mean, I don't even know anything..

meaning: because; for that reason
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ものだもんだものじゃない | Verb (ない form) | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 人は誰でも間違いをするものだ。
examples.english: Everybody makes mistakes.

examples.japanese: 人は見かけでは分からないものだ。
examples.english: People cannot be understood by just their outward appearance.

examples.japanese: 人は誰でも失敗するものです。
examples.english: Everybody experiences failure.

examples.japanese: たくさん運動したら疲れるものです。
examples.english: Working out a lot will naturally make one tired.

examples.japanese: 子供は早く寝るもんだよ。
examples.english: Children must go to bed early.

examples.japanese: 人の悪口は言うものじゃない。
examples.english: One should not say bad things of others.

meaning: because; for that reason
structure: Verb (casual) + ものだからものですからもんだから (spoken) | Noun + な | な-Adjective + な | い-Adjective

examples.japanese: 目覚まし時計が壊れたものだから、遅刻してしまった。
examples.english: My alarm clock broke, so I was late.

examples.japanese: すみません、風邪を引いてしまったものですから、今日は欠席です。
examples.english: Sorry, I caught a cold and so I will be absent today.

examples.japanese: 上着を着たままですみません。寒いものだから。
examples.english: I'm sorry for wearing my jacket, but I'm a bit cold..

examples.japanese: すみません。お酒は苦手なものですから。
examples.english: My apologies, I am not very good with alcohol.

examples.japanese: 一人っ子なものだからわがままに育ててしまいました。
examples.english: I'm an only child so I grew up a little bit selfish

examples.japanese: 遅くなってごめんなさい。道路が混んでいたものだから。
examples.english: I'm sorry for being late. Traffic was really bad..

meaning: difficult to do; is unreasonable / unrealistic / impossible
structure: Verb (casual, past) + ものではない

examples.japanese: 何が起こるかわかったものではない。
examples.english: There is no knowing what will happen.

examples.japanese: 目上の人にそんな言い方をするものではない。
examples.english: You should't talk that way to your superiors/seniors.

examples.japanese: 口の中に物を入れたまましゃべるものではない。
examples.english: You shouldn’t speak with your mouth full.

examples.japanese: 小さい子を一人で遠くに遊びに行かせるものではない。
examples.english: We shouldn’t let little kids play far from home.

examples.japanese: こんな料理、お客さんに出せたものではないよ。もっと練習しなさい。
examples.english: Food like this should not have been served to customers. Make sure to practice more!

examples.japanese: 借りた本に書き込むをするものではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't write inside a borrowed book.

meaning: shouldn’t do something; it’s impossible to ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ものがある | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼の話にはどこか納得できないものがある。
examples.english: There’s something unconvincing about his story.

examples.japanese: 社長の言葉には、こころに響くものがある。この会社を成長させるために、もっと頑張りたい。
examples.english: There's something that resounds from the company president's words and that makes me want to work harder to help the company's growth.

examples.japanese: 確かに、一人で受付と司会をやるのは厳しいものがある。
examples.english: Certainly it is quite difficult to both lead the meeting and run reception all alone.

examples.japanese: こんなに古いパソコンで仕事をするのは、かなりきついものがある。新しいパソコンにしてもらいたい。
examples.english: It feels quite difficult to be working on an old computer like this. I wish they'd upgrade it to a new computer.

examples.japanese: こんなに悪いことが続くと、何かこわいものがある。今年は運が悪いのかも。
examples.english: There is something dreadful about bad things happening continually like this. My luck might be not so good this year..

examples.japanese: 自分の子供が、今年もう20歳になるのか。感慨深いものがあるな。
examples.english: My child is already turning 20 this year? There's something really emotional about this..

meaning: but; although; even though ~
structure: Verb (potential form れる) + ものなら | もんなら (spoken)

examples.japanese: やれるもんなら、やってみろ。
examples.english: If you can do it, let's see you try.

examples.japanese: 止められるものなら止めてみるがよい。
examples.english: Try and stop me if you can.

examples.japanese: やり直せるものならやり直したい。
examples.english: I wish I could start over.

examples.japanese: 忘れられるものなら、忘れたいよ。
examples.english: I wish I could forget it.

examples.japanese: 彼らがやれるものならやらせてみろ。
examples.english: Let them try it if they dare.

examples.japanese: 生まれ変われるものなら、鳥になりたい。だって、空を飛びたいんだもん。
examples.english: If I could be reborn, I'd want to be a bird. Then I could fly through the sky.

meaning: but then; although; though ~
structure: Verb (casual) + ものの | Noun + である | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 秋であるものの、まだ暑い。
examples.english: Although it's fall, it is still hot.

examples.japanese: 申し込みはしたものの、試験を受けるかどうか未定です。
examples.english: Although I applied to take the test, I'm not sure if I'll take it or not.

examples.japanese: 車の免許は持っているものの、ほとんど運転したことがありません。
examples.english: Although I have my driver's license, I have rarely ever driven.

examples.japanese: 買ったものの、使い方が分からない。
examples.english: Although I bought it, I don't know how to use it..

examples.japanese: 金欠ではあるものの、毎日美味しい食事を楽しんでいる。
examples.english: Although it's true I'm broke, every day I enjoy a delicious meal.

examples.japanese: 私のアパートは駅からはちょっと遠いものの、静かできれいな住宅街にある。
examples.english: My apartment may be far from the station, but it is in a very quiet and beautiful neighborhood.

meaning: at least ~
structure: もう少しで + Verb (ます stem) +そうだった/そうになった | Verb (dictionary form) +ところだった"

examples.japanese: もう少しであの川でおぼれるところでした.
examples.english: I almost drowned in that river.

examples.japanese: もう少しで、私は、終電に乗り遅れそうでした。
examples.english: If I were just a little later then I would have missed the last train.

examples.japanese: 彼は、バナナの皮で滑り、もう少しで転ぶところだった。
examples.english: He slipped on a banana peel and nearly fell.

examples.japanese: 君はもう少しで私の目を鉛筆で突き刺すところだったよ。
examples.english: You nearly poked me in the eye with your pencil.

examples.japanese: その話を聞いて、もう少しで泣くところだった。
examples.english: I was on the verge of tears when I heard that story.

examples.japanese: もう少しで大切な卒業論文をタクシーの中に忘れるところだった。
examples.english: I almost left my precious graduation thesis in the taxi.

meaning: as long as; while… is the case; as far as; while ~
structure: Verb (ない form) + ことには + Verb(ない form) | Noun + でない | な-adjective + でない | い-adjective + いくない

examples.japanese: 彼が来ないことには、会議を始めることができない。
examples.english: Unless he comes, we cannot start the meeting.

examples.japanese: 一口食べてみないことには、美味しいかどうかわかりません。
examples.english: Unless you try a bite, you won't know if it tastes good or not.

examples.japanese: 病院へ見舞いに行かないことには、彼の病状は分からない。
examples.english: I won’t know his current condition unless I go to the hospital to visit him.

examples.japanese: 両方の話を聞いてみないことには、ケンかの原因が分からないでしょう。
examples.english: You won’t know the reason why they fought unless you hear both sides of the story.

examples.japanese: 実際に読まないことには、この小説のおもしろさはわからないだろう。
examples.english: You won’t understand why this novel is interesting unless you read it.

examples.japanese: 日本語がある程度できないことには、日本でアルバイトをするのは出来ない。
examples.english: You won't be able to work a part-time job in Japan unless you can understand some amount of Japanese.

meaning: focused on; centered on
structure: Verb (casual form) + 中を中では | Noun + の | Adjective

examples.japanese: 私はお店の中をうろうろしていた。
examples.english: I wandered around in the store.

examples.japanese: 雨が降っているから彼女は部屋の中を走った。
examples.english: Since it was raining outside, she ran inside.

examples.japanese: 彼らは雨の中を歩き続けました。
examples.english: They continued to walk in the rain.

examples.japanese: 教会の中では帽子を脱ぎなさい。
examples.english: Please remove your hat inside the church.

examples.japanese: 携帯電話は電車の中では使わない方がいい。
examples.english: You had best not use your cellphone on the train.

examples.japanese: お忙しい中を手伝っていただき、本当にありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you very much for helping me while you are busy.

pattern: なくはない / なくもない
meaning: is not entirely impossible
structure: Verb ない + くはないくもない | Noun + がな | な-adjective + じゃな | い-adjective + いくな

examples.japanese: 自信がなくはないが、ただちょっと緊張している。
examples.english: It’s not that I have no confidence, I’m just a little nervous.

examples.japanese: 息子は野菜を食べなくはないが、あまり好きではない。
examples.english: It’s not that my son doesn’t eat vegetables, he just doesn’t like them very much.

examples.japanese: あなたの気持ちは分からなくはないが、ただその行為には賛成できない。
examples.english: It’s not that I don’t understand how you feel, I just can’t agree with that kind of action.

examples.japanese: 仕事に不満はないけど、給料は安いし、時には転職を考えなくもない。
examples.english: I don't have any dissatisfaction with this job, but the salary is low and I may eventually consider changing jobs.

examples.japanese: 食欲がなくはないが、もう少し後で私は食事をしたいです。
examples.english: It’s not that I do not have an appetite but I would like to eat a little bit later.

examples.japanese: 結婚するつもりはなくもないが、仕事が安定してからのほうがいいだろう。
examples.english: It’s not that I don’t want to get married, I just think it's better to wait until I have a stable job.

meaning: get by without doing ~
structure: Verb (ない root) + なくて済むないで済む

examples.japanese: 母が車で迎えに来てくれたので、歩かなくて済みました。
examples.english: My mother came to pick me up and so I didn't have to walk.

examples.japanese: amazonさえあれば外出しなくて済む。
examples.english: As long as there is Amazon, we can get by without going outside.

examples.japanese: 予約しておいたおかげで、待たなくて済みました。
examples.english: I didn't have to wait thanks to making a reservation.

examples.japanese: 友達がおごってくれたのでお金を払わないで済みました。
examples.english: My friend treated me, so I didn't have to pay any money.

examples.japanese: 私の友達が自分のアパートに泊めてくれたのでホテルに泊まらなくて済んだ。
examples.english: My friend let me stay at their apartment, so I got by without having to stay at a hotel.

examples.japanese: 今年は涼しかったので、エアコンを使わなくて済みました。
examples.english: This year was cool and I got by without using my air conditioner.

meaning: only; can only be; there is no alternative, only ~
structure: なにも + Verb/Noun/Adj (ない form)

examples.japanese: 私達はなにもいらない。
examples.english: We don't need anything.

examples.japanese: 彼女はなにも言わなかった。
examples.english: She did not say anything.

examples.japanese: どのみち、何も聞こえなかった。
examples.english: In any case, I couldn't hear anything.

examples.japanese: 彼はただ新聞を読むだけでなにもしなかった。
examples.english: He did nothing but read newspapers.

examples.japanese: そのお店は混雑していたので、私はなにも買えなかった。
examples.english: That store was crowded so I couldn't buy anything.

examples.japanese: それは冗談だけなんだから、なにもそんなに怒ることはない。
examples.english: It's just a joke, there’s no need to get so angry.

meaning: moreover; furthermore; and yet; what’s more ~
structure: なお + phrase

examples.japanese: かなり多くの人々が今なおそれを信じている。
examples.english: Many people still believe that.

examples.japanese: とても寒く、なお悪いことに、雨が降り始めた。
examples.english: It was very cold, and what was worse, it began to rain.

examples.japanese: 今度の打ち合わせは土曜日です。なお、時間は後ほどお伝えします。
examples.english: The meeting next time will be on Saturday. I’ll let you know about the exact time later.

examples.japanese: あとで起こったことはなお悪かった。
examples.english: What followed was worse.

examples.japanese: この件の説明は以上です。なお、詳細についてプリントをご覧ください。
examples.english: I’m finished explaining this matter. Please look at the handout for details.

examples.japanese: この試合に申し込むとき、履歴書を提出してください。なお参加費も提出してください。
examples.english: When you apply for the match, please submit your resume. In addition, please submit the participation fee.

meaning: should; appropriate; it is natural to do ~
structure: Verb ない + ねばならない

examples.japanese: 歯医者に行かねばならない。
examples.english: I must go to the dentist.

examples.japanese: 9時までに戻らねばならない。
examples.english: I'm supposed to be back by nine.

examples.japanese: ビザが切れたので、国に帰らねばならない。
examples.english: My visa expired so I have to go back to my home country.

examples.japanese: 来月から、転勤で北海道へ行かねばならない。
examples.english: From next month, I will be changing jobs and have to go to Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: 地球を守るために、プラスチック製品を減らさねばならない。
examples.english: In order to help save the earth, we have to reduce the amount of plastic products.

examples.japanese: どんなに辛いことがあっても、家族のためにしばらくは耐えねばならない。
examples.english: No matter how tough things get, we have to endure it for the family.

meaning: when; at the time; on the occasion ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + にあたって(は)にあたり | Noun

examples.japanese: 皆さん、JLPTを受けるにあたって、大切なことを伝えておきます。
examples.english: Everyone, I will tell you an important thing for when you take the JLPT exam.

examples.japanese: アルバイトをするにあたっては、学業や体に無理のないようにすること。
examples.english: If you are going to work part-time, make sure that it does not interfere with your studies or health.

examples.japanese: 結婚するにあたって、たくさんのお金を準備しなければならない。
examples.english: When you get married, you need to prepare a lot of money.

examples.japanese: 日本に留学するにあたって、行く前にしておくべきことは先輩に聞いた。
examples.english: I asked my senior for things I should do before studying abroad in Japan.

examples.japanese: 試験を始めるにあたり、まずは注意事項を読んでおいてください。
examples.english: When starting the test, first read the important points.

examples.japanese: マンションを買うにあたって、妻と色んな調査をしました。
examples.english: When I bought an apartment, I did a lot of research with my wife.

meaning: there is no way / means; cannot do ~
structure: Noun + にほかならない

examples.japanese: 合格したのは、彼の努力の結果にほかならない。
examples.english: Him being able to pass is nothing else but the result of his hard effort.

examples.japanese: 緊急時に一番大切なことは、まず落ち着くことにほかならない。
examples.english: In an emergency, the most important thing is nothing other than to first calm down.

examples.japanese: 自分からやると言ったのに、途中でやめてしまうのは無責任にほかならない。
examples.english: Despite saying you would do it yourself, to stop halfway through is nothing short of irresponsible.

examples.japanese: 事故が発生した原因は、運転手の前方不注意にほかならない。
examples.english: The only reason why the accident occurred is because the driver didn’t pay attention.

examples.japanese: 親が子供を叱るのは子供を愛してるからにほかならない。
examples.english: The only reason why a parent scolds their child is because they love them.

examples.japanese: 彼らが日本へ行くのは、お金を稼ぎたいからにほかならない。
examples.english: They will come to Japan because they want to save money, and nothing else.

meaning: not limited to; not only… but also ~
structure: Noun + に限らず

examples.japanese: 最近は、女性に限らず男性も化粧をする。
examples.english: Lately, not only women but also men have been wearing makeup.

examples.japanese: この映画は子供に限らず、大人も楽しめます。
examples.english: With this movie, not only children but also adults can enjoy it.

examples.japanese: この番組は若者に限らず老人も関心します。
examples.english: This program is interesting to not only young people, but to elderly people as well.

examples.japanese: ディズニー映画は子供に限らず、大人にも人気がある。
examples.english: Diseney movies are popular with not only children, but with adults as well.

examples.japanese: これから、科学に限らず文学もちゃんと勉強します。
examples.english: From now on I will study not only science, but literature as well.

examples.japanese: 女の子に限らず男の子も掃除や洗濯をしなければならないよ。
examples.english: Not just the girls, but the boys as well must help clean and wash.

meaning: not necessarily so; is not always true
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + に限る | Noun

examples.japanese: 寒い日は、熱いラーメンに限る。
examples.english: On a cold day, nothing beats a hot bowl of ramen.

examples.japanese: 風邪には寝ているに限る。
examples.english: Staying in bed is the best remedy for a cold.

examples.japanese: 何といっても我が家に限る。
examples.english: After all, there's no place like home.

examples.japanese: 夏は冷たいビールに限る。
examples.english: In summer, nothing beats a cold beer..

examples.japanese: 語学は若い時に限る。
examples.english: Languages are best learned in one's youth.

examples.japanese: たこ焼きはやっぱり大阪に限るね。
examples.english: Takoyaki is best in Osaka.

meaning: not necessarily so; is not always true
structure: Noun + に限って

examples.japanese: うちの娘に限って、人をいじめるようなことはしません。
examples.english: Our daughter would be the last person to do something like bully another person.

examples.japanese: 私は学校に休んだ日に限って、テストがある。
examples.english: There was a test on the one day I missed school..

examples.japanese: 仕事が忙しい日に限って、なぜかシステムトラブルが発生する。
examples.english: The system errors always occur only on the busy days at work.

examples.japanese: ここから富士山が見えるそうだけど、今日に限って雲が多いね。
examples.english: You can apparently see Mt. Fuji from here, but today there are a lot of clouds.

examples.japanese: 彼は、いつも家にいるのに、今日に限って留守でした。
examples.english: Although he is always home, today of all days he was not.

examples.japanese: 見たいドラマがある日に限って残業で帰りが遅くなってしまう。
examples.english: Of course on the day with the TV show I want to watch I have overtime and will get home late.

meaning: despite; in spite of; nevertheless; although ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に関わらずにかかわらず | Noun | Adjective

examples.japanese: このバスは距離にかかわらず、どこまで行っても200円だ。
examples.english: This bus costs 200 yen regardless of the distance you go.

examples.japanese: 値段にかかわらず、新しいiPhoneが発売したら買うつもりだ。
examples.english: I plan to buy the new iPhone once it is released, regardless of the price,

examples.japanese: 明日の国際交流イベントに来る来ないにかかわらず、連絡してください。
examples.english: Regardless of if you come to tomorrow's international exchange event or not, please contact me.

examples.japanese: お酒を飲む飲まないに関わらず、飲み会の参加費は3,000円です。
examples.english: Regardless of if you drink or not, the fee for the drinking party is 3,000 yen.

examples.japanese: 好き嫌いに関わらず、家族のためにこの仕事は必ずしなければならない。
examples.english: Regardless of whether I like it or not, I must do this job to support my family.

examples.japanese: テストの点数に関わらず、間違えたところは復習するようにしてください。
examples.english: Regardless of your test score, please review the mistakes you made.

meaning: depending on; in accordance with ~
structure: Noun + 関わるにかかわるにかかわってにかかわり

examples.japanese: 息子はマスコミに関わる仕事をしている。
examples.english: My son works in a job related to mass communications.

examples.japanese: 命に関わる病気ではないので、安心してください。
examples.english: This is not a life-threatening illness so please relax.

examples.japanese: 政治に関わる仕事をしているのでコメントできない。
examples.english: I work in relation with the government and therefore cannot comment.

examples.japanese: 彼は汚職事件に関って逮捕された。
examples.english: He was arrested in relation to a corruption case.

examples.japanese: こんな質が低い商品を売ったら店の評判に関わる。
examples.english: The reputation of this shop will be affected if it sells products of this low quality.

examples.japanese: 睡眠剤は飲みすぎると、命に関わることもある。
examples.english: Taking too much sleeping medicine could become life-threatening.

meaning: the most of all; the best; nothing is more ... than ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + に越したことはない | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: そうするに越したことはない。
examples.english: That is the best thing to do.

examples.japanese: 何が起こるかわからないから、試験のときは、早く行くに越したことはない。
examples.english: You never know what might happen, so it's best to go early on the test day.

examples.japanese: 値段に関係なくいい質のものを買いたいが、安く買えるに越したことはない。
examples.english: I want to buy an item of good quality regardless of price, but nothing beats getting it at a cheaper price.

examples.japanese: 同じ業種をするなら、給料が高いに越したことはない。
examples.english: If you're going to work in the same industry, it would be best to go for a higher salary.

examples.japanese: 当日はレストランに行っても大丈夫だと思うけど、念のために予約しておくに越したことはない。
examples.english: I think it would be fine if you went to a restaurant on that day, but just to be safe it would be best to make a reservation.

examples.japanese: 地震がいつ起こるかわからないから、とにかく避難の物を準備しておくに越したことはない。
examples.english: You never know when an earthquake might suddenly occur, so it's best to prepare evacuation items.

meaning: still; yet​; furthermore; in addition ~
structure: Noun + に加えて

examples.japanese: のどの痛みに加えて、熱も出てきたので学校を休むしかない。
examples.english: In addition to throat pain, I've started getting a fever and have no choice but to miss school.

examples.japanese: 彼女は週末にアルバイトに加えて、ボランティア活動もしている。
examples.english: In addition to working a part-time job on weekends, she also works as a volunteer.

examples.japanese: 今学期から初級クラスに加えて、中級クラスでも教えるようになった。
examples.english: From this semester, in addition to teaching the beginner class I will also be teaching the intermediate class.

examples.japanese: 母は高血圧に加えて、心臓もあまり良くないので心配だ。
examples.english: My mother has high blood pressure in addition to a weak heart so I am worried.

examples.japanese: 彼女は看護師の資格に加えて、保育士の資格も持っている。
examples.english: In addition to having her nurse qualification, she also is certified as a childcare worker.

examples.japanese: 今年から家のローンに加えて、子供の学費も払わなければならないので大変だ。
examples.english: From this year, in addition to the house loan we need to pay for the kid's school fees so things are a bit tough.

meaning: according to; in keeping with; to be based on ~
structure: Noun + に基づいてに基づき

examples.japanese: この小説は実際にあったことに基づいて書かれたそうです。
examples.english: This novel is apparently written based on things that actually happened.

examples.japanese: このテストの結果に基づいて君たちのクラスを分けるので、頑張ってください。
examples.english: We will split your class based on the results of this test, so good luck!

examples.japanese: 集めた資料に基づいて、卒業の論文を書きました。
examples.english: I wrote my graduation thesis based on the collected materials.

examples.japanese: 私は長年の経験に基づき新入社員を教育する。
examples.english: I educate new employees based on years of experience.

examples.japanese: 公務員の給与は、法律に基づいて決められています。
examples.english: The salaries of civil servants are determined by law.

examples.japanese: アンケート結果に基づいて、新商品の方向性を決めるつもりだ。
examples.english: Based on the results of the questionnaire, we will decide the direction of the new product.

meaning: suitable for ~
structure: Noun + に向かってに向けて

examples.japanese: 先生に向かって失礼なことを言わないでください。
examples.english: Please don’t say rude things to your teacher.

examples.japanese: 彼女は今どこに向かっていますか？
examples.english: Where is she heading to?

examples.japanese: 私は今新幹線に乗って東京に向かっています。
examples.english: I am currently on a bullet train heading towards Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 学生たちは黒板に向かって座っている。
examples.english: The students are sitting facing the blackboard.

examples.japanese: 選手はゴールに向かって全速力で走っている。
examples.english: The players are running toward the goal at full speed.

examples.japanese: 私は夢に向かって頑張って努力をしたいです。
examples.english: I'd like to do my best and work hard towards my dream.

meaning: based on; according to; in accordance with ~
structure: Noun + に応じてに応じた

examples.japanese: この学校は生徒の日本語のレベルに応じて、クラスを分けます。
examples.english: At this school students are divided up based on their Japanese ability level.

examples.japanese: 家具は部屋の広さに応じて決めたほうがいい。
examples.english: You had best pick furniture based on the space of the room.

examples.japanese: この店は季節に応じてメニューが異なるからおもしろい。
examples.english: This restaurant is interesting because the menu varies according to the season.

examples.japanese: このテーブルは、人数に応じて、大きさを変えることもできるんです。
examples.english: This table can change sizes according to the number of people to fit.

examples.japanese: 大学では、学生の興味に応じて、好きな授業を受けることができる。
examples.english: At university, students can take classes according to what they are interested in.

examples.japanese: 地震が起きたら、その時にいる場所に応じて、避難の仕方は変わる。
examples.english: When an earthquake occurs, the evacuation method changes depending where you are at that time.

meaning: when; at the time; on the occasion ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に際して（は） | Noun

examples.japanese: 車を買うに際しては、保険に入らなければならない。
examples.english: When you buy a new car, you must buy insurance.

examples.japanese: 試験に際して、携帯電話の電源を切ってください。
examples.english: Please turn off your cell phones during the test.

examples.japanese: お申し込みに際しては、履歴書が必要となります。
examples.english: When applying, a resume is required.

examples.japanese: 図書館のご利用に際しては、以下の点にご注意ください。
examples.english: Please follow the below rules when using the library.

examples.japanese: 仕事選びに際してはベネフィッツも重要だ。
examples.english: Benefits are important when choosing a job.

examples.japanese: 出発に際して彼はいろいろ世話をしてくれた。
examples.english: He helped me out with various things during my departure.

meaning: prior to; to be the first (pioneer); being ahead of ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に先立ちに先立ってに先立つ | Noun

examples.japanese: 会議に先立って、資料を集めておかなければならない。
examples.english: Before the meeting, we must gather the resources.

examples.japanese: 日本への留学に先立ち、パスポートの申請をしました。
examples.english: Before studying abroad in Japan, I applied for my passport.

examples.japanese: 新製品の発売に先立って、テレビやネットで連日宣伝しています。
examples.english: Prior to launching new products, we promote them on TV and online every day.

examples.japanese: オリンピックの開催に先立ち、応援グッズやチケットなどの販売が開始された。
examples.english: Prior to the Olympics, sales of support items and tickets began.

examples.japanese: 手術をするに先立って、医師は患者とその家族に考えうる全てのリスクを説明した。
examples.english: Prior to surgery, the doctor explained all possible risks to the patient and their family.

examples.japanese: 家の購入に先立って、先輩や友達にいろいろなアドバイスをもらいました。
examples.english: Prior to buying the house, I got some advice from my seniors and friends.

meaning: no matter what; at any cost; after all ~
structure: Verb (casual) + にせよにしろ | Noun + (である) | な-adjective + (である) | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 熱が下がったにせよ、しばらく安静が必要です。
examples.english: Even if your fever has gone down, you still need to rest.

examples.japanese: 欠席するにせよ連絡はしてください。
examples.english: Even if you will be absent, please contact us.

examples.japanese: 事故で自転車がめちゃくちゃになったが、何にしろ、誰もけがをしなくてよかった。
examples.english: My bike got pretty messed up in an accident, but at any rate, I'm just glad nobody was hurt.

examples.japanese: ここは不便でどの駅に行くにせよ、徒歩で30分以上かかる。
examples.english: This place is really inconvenient, no matter which station you go to will take at least 30 minutes by foot.

examples.japanese: 来るにせよ来ないにせよ、必ず連絡を入れてください。
examples.english: Whether you will come or not, please make sure to inform us.

meaning: even if; regardless; whether... or ~
structure: Verb(dict. form) + にしろにせよ + Verbない form + にしろにせよ | Noun + Noun | な-adj + な-adj | い-adj + い-adj

examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーに行くにしろ行かないにしろ、連絡してくださいね。
examples.english: Whether you go to the party tomorrow or not, please contact me.

examples.japanese: 就職するにしろ進学するにしろ、自分でよく考えてください。
examples.english: Think carefully by yourself whether you’ll start working or pursue higher education.

examples.japanese: 犬にしろ猫にしろ、このマンションではペットを飼ってはいけない決まりです。
examples.english: Whether it be dogs or cats, pets are not allowed in this apartment.

examples.japanese: 給料が上がるにしろ上がらないにしろ、私はこの仕事を辞めます。
examples.english: I will quit this job regardless of whether my salary goes up or not.

examples.japanese: 使うにしろ使わないにしろ、それをもらったことにはお礼を言った方がいいですよ。
examples.english: Whether you will use it or not, you should say thanks for receiving it.

examples.japanese: 親にしろともだちにしろ、みんなが彼と結婚することを反対した。
examples.english: Whether it be her parents or her friends, everyone was opposed to her getting married to him.

pattern: にしたら / にすれば
meaning: in the case of~; assuming~; if A then B
structure: Noun + にしたらにすれば

examples.japanese: あなたにすれば小さなことかもしれないけど、ほかの人にはそうでもないんですよ。
examples.english: To you, this may be just a small issue, but that's not the same for other people.

examples.japanese: 大きすぎる親の期待は、子供にしたら苦痛だ。
examples.english: Too big of expectations from parents are painful for children to bear.

examples.japanese: 犬や猫は可愛いが、飼っていない人にすれば迷惑なこともある。
examples.english: Dogs and cats are cute, but they can be a nuisance to people who don’t have them.

examples.japanese: 彼にすれば冗談のつもりでも、彼女はすごく傷ついている。
examples.english: To him it was just a joke, but she is extremely hurt.

examples.japanese: 日本人にすれば簡単な漢字でも、外国人にはとても難しいことかもしれない。
examples.english: From a Japanese person's perspective, even a simple kanji character might be very difficult for foreigners.

examples.japanese: 両親にすれば、一人の娘を海外に留学させるのは、かなり心配だったと思います。
examples.english: I think that for her parents, having their only daughter study abroad was very worrying.

meaning: if (you) continue... you'll end up / I don't care about it
structure: Verb(dict. form) + にしてもにしろ + Verb(dict. form) + にしてもにしろ | Noun + Noun | な-adj + な-adj | い-adj + い-adj

examples.japanese: 行くにしても行かないにしても、早く決めてください。
examples.english: Hurry up and decide whether you will go or not.

examples.japanese: 高いにしろ安いにしろ、この教科書は買わないといけません。
examples.english: Regardless of cost, I need to buy this textbook.

examples.japanese: 飲み会に参加するにしても、しないにしても明日までに参加可否を連絡ください。
examples.english: Let me know whether you will participate or not in the drinking party by tomorrow.

examples.japanese: JLPTを受けるにしても、受けないにしてもしっかりと勉強する必要がある。
examples.english: Whether you take the JLPT or not, you will still need to study hard.

examples.japanese: 英語を学ぶにしても中国語を学ぶにしても目的や目標をはっきりしないと続かないよ。
examples.english: Whether you learn English or Chinese, you won't be able to continue on without clearly defining your objectives and goals.

examples.japanese: 犬にしても猫にしてもこのマンションではペットを飼ってはいけないことになっている。
examples.english: Whether it is a dog or cat, pets are not allowed in this apartment building.

meaning: as; therefore; in accordance with; according to; consequently ~
structure: Noun + に沿ってに沿いに沿うに沿った

examples.japanese: この坂道に沿って自転車で行けば、1時間半ぐらいで頂上に着きます。
examples.english: If you go along this mountain road by bicycle, you will reach the peak in about an hour and a half.

examples.japanese: 週末は、川の道に沿って二時間ほど仲間とサイクリングしました。
examples.english: On the weekend, I went cycling for about 2 hours with my friends along the river path.

examples.japanese: この道を線路に沿って真っすぐ行くと、左側に美味しいケーキ屋があります。
examples.english: If you go straight along this road parallel to the railroad tracks, on the left side there is a delicious cake shop.

examples.japanese: 今日はお配りしている資料の内容に沿って、発表いたします。
examples.english: Today I will make an announcement in accordance with the documents being handed out.

examples.japanese: 祖父の遺産は、遺言に沿って分配しました。
examples.english: My grandfather's inheritance was divided up in accordance with his will.

examples.japanese: 計画に沿って実施されているので、問題がないと思います。
examples.english: Since we followed the plan, I don’t think there should be any problems.

meaning: certainly; I’m sure/certain that; it must be the case that ~
structure: Verb (casual) + に相違ない | Noun + （である） | な-adjective + （である） | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 冷蔵庫に入れていたアイスクリームを食べたのは、娘に相違ない。
examples.english: I'm certain it was my daughter who ate the ice cream I put in the freezer.

examples.japanese: その情報を漏らしたのは彼女に相違ない。
examples.english: The one who leaked that information must be her.

examples.japanese: この日本語学校は色々な国の学生がいる、楽しいに相違ない。
examples.english: This Japanese language school has students from various countries, it will certainly be enjoyable.

examples.japanese: これだけの証拠があるなら、犯人はあの男に相違ない。
examples.english: With this much evidence, without a doubt that man is the criminal.

examples.japanese: この地域の水汚染の問題を解決するのは難しいに相違ない。
examples.english: "Solving this area’s water pollution problem is certainly going to be difficult. "

examples.japanese: この絵の描き方を見ると父親が描いたものに相違ない。
examples.english: Looking at the way this was drawn, this is without a doubt my father's work.

meaning: nothing but; none other than ~
structure: Verb (casual) + に過ぎないに過ぎません | Noun + (である) | な-adjective + (である) | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 単に幸運だったにすぎない。
examples.english: That was just pure luck.

examples.japanese: これはまだ始まりにすぎない。
examples.english: This is only the beginning.

examples.japanese: そんなのは言い訳に過ぎない。
examples.english: That's just an excuse.

examples.japanese: それはただの道具にすぎない。その道具をどう使うかが大切だ。
examples.english: That is merely a tool. What is important is how you use it.

examples.japanese: 病気で病院へ行ったといっても、ただの風邪に過ぎない。
examples.english: Although i said that i went to the hospital because i was sick, it was just a normal cold.

examples.japanese: 私はこの会社の一社員にすぎませんから、決定権はありません。
examples.english: I am nothing more than an employee of this customer and have no decision making power.

meaning: according to; in view of; in light of ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に伴ってに伴いに伴う | Noun

examples.japanese: それに伴って私たちの予定は再度変わるかもしれません。
examples.english: Accordingly, our plans may change again.

examples.japanese: 人口が増えるに伴って、いろいろな問題が起こってきた。
examples.english: As the population increased, various problems began to occur.

examples.japanese: 彼は昨日のパーティーに婚約者に伴って来た。
examples.english: He came to yesterday's party with his fiance.

examples.japanese: 会社を倒産に伴って、多くの社員が失業した。
examples.english: Following the company's bankruptcy, many employees lost their jobs.

examples.japanese: インターネットの普及に伴って、ネットで買い物をする人が増えた。
examples.english: With the spread of the internet, more and more people are shopping online.

examples.japanese: これに伴ってタイムスケジュールの変更をお願いします。
examples.english: Please modify the time schedule according to this.

meaning: due to the fact that; because of ~
structure: Noun + につき

examples.japanese: 昼休みにつき、事務所は2時まで休みです。
examples.english: The office will be closed until 2 o’clock due to the lunch break.

examples.japanese: 現在、工事中につき、このエリアは通行ができません。
examples.english: Due to this area being currently under construction, you cannot pass through.

examples.japanese: 店内改装につき、しばらく休業いたします。
examples.english: Due to store interior remodeling, this shop will be closed for a while.

examples.japanese: 冷房中につき、部屋に入る時はドアを閉めてください。
examples.english: Because the AC is running, please close the door when you enter the room.

examples.japanese: 会議中につき中に入ってはいけない。ここでお待ちください。
examples.english: Because there is a meeting going on, you cannot enter inside. Please wait here.

examples.japanese: 現在、この商品は製造中止につき、販売しておりません。
examples.english: Because production of this product has been stopped, it is currently not being sold.

meaning: through; by way of; after; via ~
structure: Noun + にわたって

examples.japanese: 道路は数マイルにわたってまっすぐ続いていた。
examples.english: The road ran straight for several miles.

examples.japanese: 広い地域にわたって大雪が降った。
examples.english: There was heavy snow over a large area.

examples.japanese: 雨が１週間にわたって降り続いた。
examples.english: The rain continued throughout the entire week.

examples.japanese: この会社は2世紀にわたって、おもちゃを作っている。
examples.english: This company has been making toys for 2 centuries.

examples.japanese: 彼の知識は広範囲にわたっている。
examples.english: His knowledge is very extensive.

examples.japanese: 長年にわたる戦争のため、あの美しかった街はすっかり変わってしまった。
examples.english: Due to the war that lasted many years, the once beautiful village had completely changed.

meaning: in spite of; regardless of ~
structure: Verb (casual) + にも関わらずにもかかわらず | Noun + （である） | な-adjective + （である） | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 大学生にも関わらず、基本的な漢字が書けない人もいる。
examples.english: Despite being university students, there are some people who cannot write basic kanji.

examples.japanese: 問題が易しかったにも関わらず、不注意でミスをしてしまった。
examples.english: Even though the problem was easy, I made a careless mistake.

examples.japanese: 一生懸命勉強したにも関わらず、入りたかった大学の試験に落ちてしまった。
examples.english: Despite studying to the best of my ability, I failed the entrance exam for my target university.

examples.japanese: 彼は全く日本語が話せないにも関わらず、日本で生活したいと言っている。
examples.english: He says he wants to live in Japan, despite not being able to speak Japanese at all.

examples.japanese: 校則で禁止されているにも関わらず、授業中にスマホを使う学生が多い。
examples.english: Despite being banned by school regulations, many students use smartphones during class.

examples.japanese: 彼女は日本語が上手であるにも関わらず、日本人と会話する時はいつも英語を使う。
examples.english: Although she is good at Japanese, she always uses English when speaking to Japanese people.

meaning: for the sake of; from the standpoint of; as a matter of; in terms of ~
structure: Noun + の上で（は） | 上の

examples.japanese: 規則の上では彼はまだ学生だ。
examples.english: According to the rules, he is still a student.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事の上では私の先輩だ。
examples.english: He has more experience on the job than I do.

examples.japanese: 彼女は健康上の理由で学校をやめた。
examples.english: She quit school for health reasons.

examples.japanese: 法律上、日本人は二十歳にならないとタバコを吸ったり、お酒を飲んだりできない。
examples.english: According to the law, Japanese people cannot smoke or drink until they turn 20 years old.

examples.japanese: ニュースの上では、市役所の前で大変な事故が起こった。
examples.english: According to the news, a terrible accident occurred in front of the city hall.

examples.japanese: この図の上では、去年と比べたら今年の売上が下がっています。
examples.english: According to this figure, compared to last year, profits this year are decreasing.

meaning: let alone; not to mention; needless to say ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + のみならず | Noun | な-adjective + である | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼は英語のみならず、スペイン語も話せる。
examples.english: Not only does he speak English, he speaks Spanish as well.

examples.japanese: 彼のアニメは国内のみならず、海外でも人気がある。
examples.english: His anime is popular not only in Japan, but internationally as well.

examples.japanese: 健康のためには、食事のみならず、生活リズムも重要になってくる。
examples.english: For your health, not only is diet important, but so is the rhythm of your lifestyle.

examples.japanese: 学生のみならず、教師もスポーツ大会に参加することになっている。
examples.english: Not only the students, but the teachers as well will be participating in the sports festival.

examples.japanese: こちらの製品は日本国内のみならず、海外でも広くご利用いただいています。
examples.english: This product is not only being widely used in Japan, but internationally as well.

examples.japanese: この不景気では中小企業のみならず、大企業でも経費の削減をしている。
examples.english: In this recession, not only small and medium-sized companies but also large companies are cutting costs.

meaning: unable to; cannot; it is not possible to ~
structure: Verb (ない form) ない + ぬ

examples.japanese: 知らぬが仏。
examples.english: Ignorance is bliss.

examples.japanese: 彼は何にも知らぬ。
examples.english: He knows nothing.

examples.japanese: どの本も気に入らぬ。
examples.english: None of these books interest me.

examples.japanese: 人は働かねばならぬ。
examples.english: Man must work.

examples.japanese: 是非そうでなければならぬ
examples.english: It must be so.

examples.japanese: いらぬお世話だ。
examples.english: It is none of your business.

pattern: 抜きにして / 抜きで
meaning: cannot do without ~
structure: Noun + 抜きにして（は） | 抜きで（は） | 抜きに（は）

examples.japanese: ハンバーガーはマスタード抜きでお願いします。
examples.english: No mustard on the hamburger please!

examples.japanese: 冗談抜きで真面目に考えってください。
examples.english: Stop joking around and think about it seriously.

examples.japanese: 今夜、仕事の話は抜きにして楽しく飲みましょう！
examples.english: Tonight, let's not talk about work and just enjoy ourselves!

examples.japanese: すみません、チーズ抜きでお願いできますか。
examples.english: Excuse me, can I please have mine without cheese?

examples.japanese: 毎回遅刻してくるし、今度のパーティーはトムさん抜きでやろうか。
examples.english: Since he always comes late, let's have the next party without Tom.

examples.japanese: 彼女抜きでは、このプロジェクトは成功しなかっただろう。
examples.english: Without her, this project would likely not have succeeded.

meaning: as an opportunity/chance to ~
structure: Noun + を契機にを契機として

examples.japanese: 入院を契機に、今後はできるだけ毎日運動しようと思った。
examples.english: As a result of my hospitalization, I am thinking to work out as much as possible every day from now on.

examples.japanese: 入社試験に落ちたのを契機に英会話の勉強を始めた。
examples.english: I made the best of failing the company entrance exam and started studying English conversation.

examples.japanese: 父は病気を契機にお酒を辞めました。
examples.english: My father's illness helped him to quit drinking alcohol.

examples.japanese: 昨年の事故を契機として、安全対策を強化された。
examples.english: Safety measures have been strengthened as a result of last year's accident.

examples.japanese: もうすぐタバコの値上がりになるので、これを契機に辞めることにしました。
examples.english: Soon the prices of cigarettes will go up, so I decided to take this as an opportunity to quit.

examples.japanese: 夫は病気を契機に食生活を見直したり、運動したりするようになった。
examples.english: As a result of my husband's illness, he started improving his diet and working out.

meaning: to be related to; to concern; associated with ~
structure: Noun + をめぐってをめぐる

examples.japanese: 父の残した土地をめぐって、兄弟喧嘩が続いていく。
examples.english: Concerning the father's leftover land, the fight among siblings continues.

examples.japanese: 昨日の会議では、新しい計画をめぐって、様々な意見が出された。
examples.english: At yesterday's meeting, many opinions were given regarding the new plan.

examples.japanese: オリンピックの代表をめぐって、最後のレースが行われます。
examples.english: The final race with the Olympic representatives will take place.

examples.japanese: そのドラマは、一人の女性をめぐって、三人の男性が戦う話です。
examples.english: That drama is about three men fighting over one woman.

examples.japanese: 環境の問題をめぐって多くの意見が出された。
examples.english: Many opinions were proposed regarding the environmental issues.

examples.japanese: その問題をめぐって、みんなが方策を考えようとして、少し間があった。
examples.english: There was a pause while everyone tried to think of a way around the problem.

meaning: according to; in keeping with; to be based on ~
structure: Noun + をもとにをもとにして

examples.japanese: 試験の結果をもとにしてクラス分けを行います。
examples.english: We’ll divide the class based on the test results.

examples.japanese: この映画は実際にあった話をもとに作られた。
examples.english: This movie was made based on things that actually happened.

examples.japanese: 友だちのアドバイスをもとに、新しいビジネスを始めた。
examples.english: Based on advice from my friend, I've started a new business.

examples.japanese: 人の噂だけをもとにして人の判断するのは良くないだと思います。
examples.english: I don't think it's good to judge people based only on rumors.

examples.japanese: 調査団からの報告をもとに救援物資の調達が行われた。
examples.english: Relief supplies were procured based on reports from the inspection team.

examples.japanese: 実際にあった事件をもとに映画化して大ヒットした作品です。
examples.english: This is a hugely successful movie that’s based on a case that actually happened.

meaning: with the exception of; excepting ~
structure: Noun + を除いて(は)を除けば

examples.japanese: 彼は日曜日を除いて毎日働いている。
examples.english: He works every day except Sundays.

examples.japanese: この本は２,３の間違いを除いて、とてもよい本です。
examples.english: This book is very good except for a few mistakes.

examples.japanese: うちの娘は食事の時を除いてずっと自分の部屋にいる。
examples.english: Our daughter spends all of her time with the exception of meals inside her room.

examples.japanese: 私は火曜日を除いてはいつでも空いています。
examples.english: I’m free the whole week except Tuesday.

examples.japanese: 私を除いて、この部屋には誰もいませんでした。
examples.english: Other than me, there was no one in this room.

examples.japanese: 今回の試験はいちばん難しいものを除いてすべての問題に答えた。
examples.english: On this exam I was able to answer every question other than the most difficult one.

meaning: in spite of; regardless of ~
structure: Noun + を問わず

examples.japanese: この公園では季節を問わず美しい花が見られます。
examples.english: You can see beautiful flowers in this park regardless of the season.

examples.japanese: このスポーツクラブは年齢を問わず誰でも入れます。
examples.english: Anyone can join this sports club, regardless of age.

examples.japanese: 高い安いの値段を問わず、私はいいものを買いたいです。
examples.english: Regardless of if the price is high or low, I want to buy good items.

examples.japanese: 学歴、経験を問わず、やる気がある社員を募集します。
examples.english: Regardless of education and experience, we are looking for employees with motivation.

examples.japanese: この島には、季節を問わず、多くの観光客が訪れる。
examples.english: Regardless of the season, this island is always visited by many tourists.

examples.japanese: インターネットが発達したことで、場所を問わずどこでも仕事ができるようになった。
examples.english: With the development of the internet, we've become able to do work from anywhere, regardless of location.

meaning: do~; order somebody to do something
structure: お + Verb ます (stem form) + 願います願えますか | お/ご + Noun (action)

examples.japanese: しばらくお待ち願います。
examples.english: Please wait a moment.

examples.japanese: 図書館では小さな声でお話し願います。
examples.english: Please speak in a small voice in the library.

examples.japanese: ご提案の詳細についてお聞かせ願えますか？
examples.english: Would you please share the details of your proposal?

examples.japanese: ご自分のシートベルトが安全にかかっているかお確かめ願います。
examples.english: Please make sure that your seat-belt is securely fastened.

examples.japanese: 私は明日休みますと、安田課長にお伝え願えますか。
examples.english: Could you please inform section manager Yasuda that I will be absent tomorrow.

examples.japanese: その書類を作成したのでご確認願います。
examples.english: I have made the document, so please confirm it.

meaning: while; besides; at the same time; in addition
structure: Phrase + おまけに

examples.japanese: 寒くておまけに風も強かった。
examples.english: It was cold, and to make matters worse, the wind was strong.

examples.japanese: この部屋は私には大きすぎる。おまけに家賃が高すぎる。
examples.english: This room is too big for me, and what's more, the rent is too expensive.

examples.japanese: 明日から３連休だ。おまけに宿題もない、最高だ。
examples.english: There are three consecutive holidays from tomorrow. To make things even better, there is no homework, this is great!

examples.japanese: その辞書は役に立つし、おまけに高くない。
examples.english: That dictionary is useful and in addition it is not expensive.

examples.japanese: お腹がすいたが冷蔵庫は空だ。おまけにインスタントラーメンもない。
examples.english: I'm hungry but the refrigerator is empty. To make things even worse, I don't even have any instant noodles.

examples.japanese: 朝寝坊して家を出るのが遅くなった。おまけに雨が降ってきた。
examples.english: I slept in the morning and left home late. To make things worse, it started raining.

meaning: dare to; daringly; deliberately; purposely ~
structure: おそらく + phrase

examples.japanese: これは恐らく間違いです。
examples.english: This is likely a mistake.

examples.japanese: 彼は恐らくパーティーには来ないだろう。
examples.english: He probably won't come to the party.

examples.japanese: 明日は恐らく雨が降るでしょう。
examples.english: It will rain perhaps tomorrow.

examples.japanese: それはおそらく可能です。
examples.english: There might be a possibility.

examples.japanese: 恐らく彼は承知しないでしょう。
examples.english: I'm afraid he won't agree.

examples.japanese: その事は恐らく君のいうとおりでしょう。
examples.english: I dare say you're right about that.

meaning: dare to; daringly; deliberately; purposely ~
structure: Verb (casual) + 恐れがあるおそれがある | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 梅雨に入ってからほとんど雨が降っていない。このまま降らないと、水不足になる恐れがある。
examples.english: It has barely rained since entering the rainy season. If things continue like this, there is worry of a water shortage.

examples.japanese: 大きい地震が来たら、この建物は倒れる恐れがある。
examples.english: If a big earthquake comes, this building may collapse.

examples.japanese: この番組は子供に悪い影響を与える恐れがある。
examples.english: This show is worried to have a negative effect on children.

examples.japanese: 台風がこのまま北上すると、日本に上陸する恐れがある。
examples.english: If the typhoon continues north, it may land in Japan.

examples.japanese: このまま手術をしなければ、眼が見えなくなる恐れがあると医者に言われた。
examples.english: The doctor told me that if I didn't do the surgery, I could go blind.

examples.japanese: こんなに赤字が続くと、この会社は倒産の恐れがある。
examples.english: If the deficit continues, the company is at risk of bankruptcy.

meaning: there is no need to; unnecessary; no match for ~
structure: Noun + および + Noun

examples.japanese: 鉛筆及び紙を持ってきてください。
examples.english: Please bring a Pencil and a Paper.

examples.japanese: 教室内での飲食及び喫煙はご遠慮ください。
examples.english: Please restrain from eating, drinking, and smoking within the classrooms.

examples.japanese: 安全のために観光する時、地図及びホテルの情報を持っていたほうがいい。
examples.english: To be safe when you are traveling, you should bring a map and your hotel information.

examples.japanese: 私は兄と外見及び性格が大きく異なる。
examples.english: There is a big difference in appearance and personality between me and my older brother.

examples.japanese: 試験中は携帯電話および他の電子機器が使用禁止です。
examples.english: Mobile phones and other electronic devices are prohibited during the test.

examples.japanese: 図書館の中では携帯電話及びゲーム機械を使ってはいけません。
examples.english: Do not use mobile phones or play games in the library.

meaning: (not) at all; (not) in the least ~
structure: ろくに + Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 昨夜はろくに寝なかった。
examples.english: I did not sleep well last night.

examples.japanese: 彼とはろくに話をしたことも無い。
examples.english: I scarcely ever talked with him.

examples.japanese: 彼の字は汚くて、ろくに読めない。
examples.english: His handwriting is messy and I'm not able to read it properly.

examples.japanese: 彼女は昨日からろくに何も食べなかった。
examples.english: She hasn't properly eaten since yesterday.

examples.japanese: 若い頃、日本語をたくさん学んだが、今はろくに覚えない。
examples.english: When I was young, I learned a lot of Japanese, but now I don't remember much.

examples.japanese: 彼はろくに働かないくせに給料のことに文句を言っています。
examples.english: He is complaining about the salary even though he doesn’t properly work.

meaning: emphasize speaker's feelings; to my (surprise/etc)
structure: 幸いなことに幸い + phrase

examples.japanese: 幸い彼は気づかなかった。
examples.english: Luckily, he did not notice.

examples.japanese: 幸い私は締切に間に合った。
examples.english: Fortunately, I was able to meet the deadline.

examples.japanese: 幸いなことに、母の心臓の手術はうまくいった。
examples.english: Fortunately, my mother's heart surgery went well.

examples.japanese: 幸いなことに、息子は新しい学校での生活にすぐに慣れた。
examples.english: Fortunately, my son quickly adjusted to life in his new school.

examples.japanese: 幸いなことに私たちは事故を避けることができた。
examples.english: Fortunately, we were able to avoid an accident.

examples.japanese: 近所で火事が起きたが、その家の人たちは幸い無事だった。
examples.english: A fire broke out in the neighborhood, but luckily the people in that house were fine.

meaning: perhaps; likely; probably; I dare say ~
structure: Verb (casual) + せいか | Noun + の | な-adjective + な/だった | い-adjective

examples.japanese: たくさん仕事をしたせいか、病気になってしまった。
examples.english: I got sick perhaps because I worked too much

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んだせいか頭痛が治った。
examples.english: My headache has gone away, likely from the medicine I took.

examples.japanese: 今日はお天気がよいせいか、とても眠たいです。
examples.english: I'm very sleepy, perhaps because of the nice weather today.

examples.japanese: 年のせいか、最近は色んなことをよく忘れた。
examples.english: I forget many things recently, probably because I am aging.

examples.japanese: 睡眠不足のせいか、目まいがした。
examples.english: I felt dizzy, probably because of my lack of sleep.

examples.japanese: ストレスがいっぱいあるせいか、胃が痛いです。
examples.english: My stomach hurts, probably because I have a lot of stress.

meaning: especially; above all ~
structure: せっかく + clause (+ conjunction)

examples.japanese: せっかく勉強したのに合格できなかった。
examples.english: Even though I went through the effort of studying, I couldn't pass (the test).

examples.japanese: せっかくレポートを書いたのに提出しなくてもよくなった。
examples.english: Even though I went through the effort of writing my report, I ended up not having to turn it in.

examples.japanese: せっかく母がお弁当を作ってくれたのに家に忘れてしまった。
examples.english: Although my mother went through the effort of making my lunch box for me, I forgot it at home.

examples.japanese: せっかくのお志ですがお断り致します。
examples.english: I am sorry, but I must decline your kind offer.

examples.japanese: せっかく来たのだから楽しまなきゃ。
examples.english: Since I've come all the way here I may as well enjoy myself.

examples.japanese: せっかく日本にいるのですから、色んな所に旅行に行ってみたいです。
examples.english: Since I am in Japan, I want to take advantage and travel to many places.

meaning: at least; even just a little (adverbial particle)
structure: せめて + phrase

examples.japanese: せめてあと十分待ってくれませんか。
examples.english: Can't you wait just ten more minutes?

examples.japanese: 一日にせめて二回は歯を磨くべきだ。
examples.english: You should brush your teeth at least twice a day.

examples.japanese: じゃ、せめてテーブルの準備でもしましょう。
examples.english: Well, at least let me set up the table.

examples.japanese: 優勝するのは無理だとしても、せめて入賞はしたい。
examples.english: Even if winning is out of the question, I would like to at least place near the top.

examples.japanese: せめて日曜だけも遊ぶがよい。
examples.english: You ought to enjoy yourself on Sunday at least.

examples.japanese: せめて百円なら売るけれども。
examples.english: I would sell it for at least 100 yen..

meaning: no sooner than; as soon as ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 次第

examples.japanese: 部屋の準備ができ次第、会議を始めます。
examples.english: Once the room preparations are complete, we will begin the meeting.

examples.japanese: 雨がやみ次第、出発することにしましょう。
examples.english: Let's depart once the rain stops.

examples.japanese: 詳しいことは情報が入り次第、お伝えします。
examples.english: I will inform you with more specific details once I get more information.

examples.japanese: 式が終了次第、ロビーに集合してください。
examples.english: As soon as the ceremony is over, please gather in the lobby.

examples.japanese: 来週のスケジュールが決まり次第、連絡してください。
examples.english: Please contact me as soon as next week’s schedule is decided.

examples.japanese: 参加者の情報がわかり次第、教えていただけませんか。
examples.english: Once you know the data for the participants, would you please let me know?

meaning: depending on the way; depending on how; according to how ~
structure: Noun + 次第で（は）次第だ

examples.japanese: 我々が成功できるかどうかは君次第だ。
examples.english: It is up to you whether we can succeed or not.

examples.japanese: 花火大会は天気次第で中止になる場合もあります。
examples.english: The fireworks festival may be cancelled depending on the weather.

examples.japanese: 結婚した相手次第で人生が決まってしまうこともある。
examples.english: Sometimes the person you married will decide your future.

examples.japanese: ビアガーデンに客がたくさんいるかどうかは天気次第だ。
examples.english: The number of customers in the beer garden is at the mercy of the weather.

examples.japanese: 仕事は紹介するが、うまくいくかどうかは本人次第だ。
examples.english: I can introduce some work, but whether it goes well or not is dependent on the person interviewing.

examples.japanese: 言葉の使い方次第で、相手を喜ばせるもあるし、怒らせることもある。
examples.english: Depending on how you choose your words, you may either please or anger your partner.

meaning: as soon as, dependent upon
structure: 次第に + phrase

examples.japanese: 風は次第におさまった。
examples.english: The wind gradually died down.

examples.japanese: それは次第に消えた。
examples.english: That gradually disappeared.

examples.japanese: 彼らは次第に仲良くなっていった。
examples.english: They gradually became closer.

examples.japanese: 今朝は雨でしたが、午後から次第に天気は回復してきました。
examples.english: It rained this mornin, but the weather gradually got better from the afternoon.

examples.japanese: 練習を続ければ、次第に結果が出るようになりますよ。
examples.english: If you keep practicing, you will gradually be able to get results.

examples.japanese: 戦争によってその国は資源を次第に失った。
examples.english: The war gradually drained the country of its resources.

meaning: still; yet​; furthermore; in addition ~
structure: しかも + phrase

examples.japanese: この教科書の説明はわかりやすくて、しかも詳しい 。
examples.english: This textbook’s explanations are easy to understand and what’s more, they’re very detailed.

examples.japanese: 今日はとても暑い。しかも、湿度も高いので何もしたくないだ。
examples.english: It's very hot today, and furthermore it's very humid so I don't feel like doing anything.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事がとても早い。しかも、正確で丁寧だから安心して任せられる。
examples.english: He is very fast with his work, and furthermore he is very accurate and careful so you can rest assured and depend on him.

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人で頭がいい。しかも性格もいいですから皆さんは彼女のことが好きになる。
examples.english: She is beautiful and smart. Furthermore, she has a good personality and so everyone falls in love with her.

examples.japanese: 外食は高くて。しかも、栄養がかたよるので、なるべく自炊しようと思っている。
examples.english: Eating out is expensive and bad for our health, so I think we should do our own cooking as much as possible.

examples.japanese: 漢字の読み方は一つだけではなく。しかも、似たようなものがたくさんあるので覚えるのが大変だ。
examples.english: Kanji do not only have one reading and to top things off there are many similar characters so it can be hard memorizing them.

meaning: according to; from the viewpoint of ~
structure: その上 + phrase

examples.japanese: その上、そのレストランは私たちのホテルからとても近い。
examples.english: In addition, the restaurant is very near to our hotel.

examples.japanese: この靴の値段は高い、その上デザインも良くない。
examples.english: These shoes are expensive and furthermore the design is not good.

examples.japanese: 今日は暑いです。その上湿度も高い。
examples.english: It's hot today, and in addition, it is also very humid.

examples.japanese: この仕事は面白いし、その上給料がいいのです。
examples.english: This job is interesting, and in addition the pay is good.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語を出来るし、その上日本語も上手だ。
examples.english: She speaks English and in addition is good at Japanese.

examples.japanese: その上、あなたは英語の授業も受ける必要があるよ。
examples.english: Besides, it is necessary that you take the English class.

meaning: although (it is a certain time/condition); even though normally
structure: それなのに + phrase

examples.japanese: 毎日残業しているし、休日も出勤した。それなのに給料がまだ少ない。
examples.english: I work overtime everyday and even work on holidays. Despite that, my salary is still low.

examples.japanese: この間に買った時計は高かった。それなのにすぐに壊れた。
examples.english: The watch I bought recently was really expensive, but despite that it broke right away.

examples.japanese: 彼の家は誰よりも学校に近い。それなのにいつも遅刻する。
examples.english: His house is closer to school than anyone else, but despite that he is always late.

examples.japanese: 私は一生懸命勉強している。それなのに成績はよくならない。
examples.english: I’ve been studying very hard, yet my grades have not improved.

examples.japanese: 毎日節約している。それなのに、お金がちっともたまらない。
examples.english: I’m saving money every day, yet I have no money in my savings.

examples.japanese: こんな暑い時に自転車で図書館へ行った。それなのに休館日だった。調べてから行けばよかった。
examples.english: On this hot day I went to the library by my bicycle, but despite my efforts it was closed. I should have looked up the open hours beforehand.

meaning: if I/we could; if [A] is possible, then [B]; if one can do something, then ~
structure: それなら + phrase

examples.japanese: 「朝から、調子が悪いです。」「それなら、早く帰って病院へ行ったほうがいいですよ。」
examples.english: "I've not been feeling well since this morning.""If that's the case, then you should head home early and go to the hospital."

examples.japanese: 「道がすごく渋滞しているようだよ。」「それなら、電車で行きましょう。」
examples.english: “There seems to be some bad traffic jams on the roads.”“In that case then let’s go by train.”

examples.japanese: 「何か甘いものを食べたい。」「それなら、冷凍庫にアイスクリームがあるから食べる？」
examples.english: "I want to eat something sweet.""In that case, we have some ice cream in the freezer. Do you want some?"

examples.japanese: 「どこか旅行に行こうと思うんだけど。」「それなら、京都がいいよ。」
examples.english: "I want to go travelling somewhere.""In that case, I recommend Kyoto!"

examples.japanese: 「新しいスマホが欲しいんだけど、買ってくれない？」「それなら、アルバイトをして自分で買いなさい。」"
examples.english: "I want a new smartphone, will you buy me one?""In that case, get a job and buy it yourself."

examples.japanese: 「このままだと、希望の大学に合格できないと思う。」「それなら、ゲームばかりせず、もっと勉強しなさい。」
examples.english: "At this rate, I won't be able to get into my target university.""In that case, you should stop playing games all the time and study more."

meaning: even; even if/though ~
structure: それにしても + phrase

examples.japanese: それにしてもあなたは絵が上手ですね。
examples.english: At any rate, I think you are great at drawing.

examples.japanese: それにしても私はあなたが優秀だと思います。
examples.english: At any rate, I think you are exceptional.

examples.japanese: 今日は早く帰ると言ったが、それにしても8時半まで残業した。
examples.english: He said he would return home early today, but even so he worked overtime until 8:30.

examples.japanese: それにしてもあなたは遅くまで働くつもりですか。
examples.english: Even so, do you still plan to work until late?

examples.japanese: 彼女がちょっと遅刻すると言ったが、それにしても遅くない？
examples.english: She said she would be a little late, but even so, isn't she too late?

examples.japanese: 日本の夏はいつも蒸し暑いですよ。それにしても今年はずいぶん蒸し暑いですね。
examples.english: The Japanese summer is always muggy. Even so, this year is especially muggy.

meaning: if you ask; if one may say ~
structure: そういえば + phrase

examples.japanese: そういえば、子供のころ、両親と一緒にここに来たことを覚えている。
examples.english: Come to think of it, I remember coming here together with my parents during my childhood.

examples.japanese: いい家ですね。そういえば、お兄さんは建築家さんでしたよね。
examples.english: It’s a very nice house. Come to think of it, isn’t your big brother an architect?

examples.japanese: そういえば、昨日のテストはどうでしたか？ よくできましたか？
examples.english: Come to think of it, how was yesterday's test? Did you do well?

examples.japanese: あれ、雨？そういえば、天気予報で午後から雨が降るって言ってたね。
examples.english: Is that rain? Come to think of it, the weather report said it would rain in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: 売り場が混んでいると思ったら、チョコレートか。ああ、そういえば、明日はバレンタインデーだった。
examples.english: The shops are full of people who want to buy chocolate. Come to think about it, tomorrow is Valentine’s Day.

examples.japanese: 今度、美味しいスイーツを食べに行きたいですね。そう言えば、あそこに新しいケーキ屋ができていましたよ。
examples.english: I'd like to go and eat some delicious sweets next time. Come to think of it, there's a new cake shop over there.

meaning: judging from; considering; by the look of ~
structure: そうすると + phrase

examples.japanese: まだ出発しないの？そうすると、約束の時間に間に合わないよ。
examples.english: You haven't left yet? You're not going to make it on time now.

examples.japanese: 私は大学を早く卒業したいです。そうすると、仕事をやって親に返報できます。
examples.english: I want to hurry and graduate university. Once that is done I can start working and pay back my parents.

examples.japanese: テニスの練習は土曜日の朝にしよう。そうすると、土曜日の午後は、時間ができる。
examples.english: Let's have tennis practice on Saturday morning. That way we can have time in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: 帰る前に社内を回ってみた。そうすると、トイレの電気がまだついて、気づいた。
examples.english: Before heading home, I walked around the inside of the company. By doing so, I noticed that the bathroom light was still on.

examples.japanese: そうすると彼は、目の前にあったペンを手にとってなにやらメモし始めた。
examples.english: Having done that, he grabbed the pen in front of him and started writing something.

examples.japanese: 東京へ新幹線で行くの？そうすると、電車よりお金が3倍にかかるよ。
examples.english: You're going to Tokyo by bullet train? That way the fee is 3 times higher than the normal train.

meaning: end up; in the end; as a result (negative)
structure: Verb (た form) + 末（に） | Noun + の

examples.japanese: いろいろ迷った末に、留学することにした。
examples.english: After worrying about various things, I decided to study abroad.

examples.japanese: 3時間にわたる激しい議論の末、ようやく意見がまとまった。
examples.english: After 3 hours of intense debate, we finally unified everyone's opinions.

examples.japanese: 彼は3年間の闘病生活の末に、亡くなった。
examples.english: After fighting the illness for 3 years, he passed away.

examples.japanese: 考えた末に、会社を辞めて独立することにしました。
examples.english: After giving it a lot of thought, i decided to quit my job to start my own business.

examples.japanese: 住民と話し合いの末、その建物の建設は中止となった。
examples.english: After the discussion with the residents, the construction of the building was suspended.

examples.japanese: ８時間にわたる話し合いの末に、やっと契約を結んだ。
examples.english: After discussing for 8 hours, we finally closed the deal.

meaning: (not) at all; (not) in the least ~
structure: 少しも + Verb (ない form) | Noun + ではない | な-adjective + ではない | い-adjective + いくない

examples.japanese: こんな暑い天気でピクニックするなんて、少しも楽しくないよ。
examples.english: Having a picnic in such hot weather isn't fun at all.

examples.japanese: この町は10年前と少しも変わらない。
examples.english: This town hasn't changed much from 10 years ago.

examples.japanese: あなたは少しも日本語が読めないのですか。
examples.english: You can't read Japanese even a little?

examples.japanese: 私は彼の言うことは少しも理解できなかった。
examples.english: I could not make any sense of what he said.

examples.japanese: そんな冗談は僕には少しも面白くないよ。
