examples.english: That kind of joke isn't one bit funny to me.

examples.japanese: その薬は私には少しも効かなかった。
examples.english: The medicine had no effect on me.

meaning: even if; no matter (who, what, when, where, why, how); though ~
structure: 少なくとも + phrase

examples.japanese: 彼女は少なくとも３０歳だ。
examples.english: She is not less than thirty.

examples.japanese: 彼は少なくとも1日に10時間働いた。
examples.english: He worked for at least 10 hours a day.

examples.japanese: 人数が足りませんね。少なくともあと3人は必要です。
examples.english: We are short on people. We need at least 3 more people.

examples.japanese: あなたは少なくとも10時には寝るべきだ。
examples.english: You should go to bed at 10 o'clock at the very least.

examples.japanese: 少なくとも週に１度は自分の部屋を掃除しなさい。
examples.english: Clean your room at least once a week.

examples.japanese: その肉は少なくとも１時間は火にかける必要がある。
examples.english: The meat needs to cook for at least an hour.

meaning: in one go; without stopping; all at once; immediately; instantly; right away ~
structure: 直ちに + phrase

examples.japanese: 彼らは直ちに彼女に手術をしなければならないだろう。
examples.english: They will have to operate on the woman immediately.

examples.japanese: 私はこの仕事を直ちにしなければならない。
examples.english: I must do this work immediately.

examples.japanese: 万一間違いを見つけたら、直ちに知らせてください。
examples.english: If you should find any mistakes, please let me know at once.

examples.japanese: 彼女は仕事が終わって直ちに事務所を出た。
examples.english: She left the office immediately after work.

examples.japanese: 直ちに出発しないと、私は約束に遅れるだろう。
examples.english: Unless I leave right away, I'll be late for my appointment.

examples.japanese: 彼の様子はよくないから、直ちに病院に連れていこう！
examples.english: He doesn't look good, so let's take him to the hospital right away.

meaning: please do; could you please…; I ask of you to ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + たまえ

examples.japanese: 入りたまえ。
examples.english: Come in.

examples.japanese: 分からない事があったら何でも聞きたまえ。
examples.english: Ask anything if you don't understand.

examples.japanese: この金は君の好きなように使いたまえ。
examples.english: Use this money as you like.

examples.japanese: ご飯を食べる前に手を洗いたまえ。
examples.english: Wash your hands before eating.

examples.japanese: 静かに！ちゃんと上司の説明を聞きたまえ。
examples.english: Be quiet! Make sure to listen to the boss's explanation.

examples.japanese: もう8時だよ。早く起きたまえ。
examples.english: It's already 8 o'clock! Hurry up and get up!

meaning: having done that; if that is done; if it is done in that way
structure: Verb (て form) + いては

examples.japanese: そんなに甘いものばかり食べていては、太りますよ。
examples.english: If you only eat sweets, you will gain weight.

examples.japanese: そんな暗いところで本を読んでいては目が悪くなってしまうよ。
examples.english: If you keep reading books in such a dark place, your eyes will go bad.

examples.japanese: いつも親に頼っていては、成長が出来ないよ。
examples.english: If you keep always relying on your parents, you will never be able to grow as a person.

examples.japanese: 毎日そんなに遅くまで残業をしていては体を壊しますよ。
examples.english: If you keep working overtime late like that you're going to destroy your body.

examples.japanese: そんなに毎日甘いものばかり食べていては虫歯になりますよ。
examples.english: If you keep eating nothing but sweets every day, you're going to get some cavities.

examples.japanese: あの男の金を返すのを待っていてはきりが無い。
examples.english: If you wait for him to pay, you will have to wait for ever.

meaning: far from; anything but; let alone; not to mention; much less ~
structure: Verb（て form) + まで | Noun + までしてまでする

examples.japanese: 頭を下げてまで金を借りたくない。
examples.english: I wouldn't lower myself to borrow money.

examples.japanese: 私は借金をしてまで、家を買うつもりはない。
examples.english: I don't intend to buy a house if it means taking on debt.

examples.japanese: なぜそうまでして嘘をつくのだろうか。
examples.english: Why do they go so far to lie?

examples.japanese: どれだけ欲しくても、借金までして買いたいとは思わない。
examples.english: Regardless of how much I may want it, I don't want to buy it if it means going in debt.

examples.japanese: 俺は父に反対してまで彼女の味方になった。
examples.english: I supported her, even though it meant defying my father.

examples.japanese: カンニングまでしてテストでいい点を取りたいとは思わない。
examples.english: I would not go so far as to cheat in order to get a good test score.

meaning: extremely; very; nothing more ... than this; as ... as it could possibly be
structure: Verb (て form) + ならない | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: うちの息子が大学に合格して、うれしくてならない。
examples.english: I’m so glad that my son passed the university entrance exam.

examples.japanese: 外国で生活した時、不安でならなかった。
examples.english: I was very nervous when I lived abroad.

examples.japanese: あの二人はどうして離婚したのか、知りたくてならない。
examples.english: I really want to know why those got divorced.

examples.japanese: 親友の結婚式に出席できないのが残念でならない。
examples.english: I'm extremely disappointed that I cannot attend my best friend's wedding.

examples.japanese: この駅の近くは、悪い人が多いから、危なくてならない。
examples.english: There are a lot of bad people near this station so it is very dangerous.

examples.japanese: 今日受けたテストで、何点を取れたか、気になってならない。
examples.english: I'm very curious about what score I will get on the test I took today.

meaning: to be forced to do something because one has no other choice
structure: Verb (たくて form) + たまらない | な-adjective + なで | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: あなたに会いたくてたまらない。
examples.english: I want to see you so bad...

examples.japanese: 日本の夏は暑すぎてたまらない。
examples.english: I can't stand Japan's hot summer.

examples.japanese: 私は外国へ行きたくてたまらない。
examples.english: I am aching to go abroad.

examples.japanese: 子どものことが心配でたまらない。
examples.english: I'm overwhelmed with worry about my children.

examples.japanese: 私は目が痛くてたまらない。
examples.english: My eyes hurt so much I can't stand it.

examples.japanese: 彼女が出来て嬉しくてたまらない。
examples.english: I'm so glad that I was able to get a girlfriend!

meaning: just like; same as ~
structure: Verb (て form) + 当然だ当たり前だ | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: 毎日遅くまで残業しているから、疲れて当然だ。
examples.english: You're working overtime late everyday, so it's only natural to be tired.

examples.japanese: 人間だから間違いがあって当然です。そんなに落ち込まないでください。
examples.english: You're only human, so it's natural to make mistakes. Don't let it get you down.

examples.japanese: マンションの近くに電車が走っているから、うるさくて当たり前だ。
examples.english: There are trains going by nearby the apartment, so it's of course going to be loud.

examples.japanese: 今回のテストはとても簡単なので満点が取れて当然です。
examples.english: The test this time was very easy, so it's only natural to be able to get a full score.

examples.japanese: 女性だから料理ができて当たり前だと思わないでください。
examples.english: Please don't think that just because someone is a girl it's natural for them to be able to cook.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいつも人の悪口ばかり言っているので、みんなに嫌われて当然だ。
examples.english: She is always saying bad things about people, so it's only natural that she is disliked by everyone.

meaning: can't bear to; unable to; troublesome to; can’t stand to ~
structure: Verb (て form) + はいられない | Noun + で | な-adjective + で

examples.japanese: ぐずぐずしてはいられない。
examples.english: We have no time to lose.

examples.japanese: 泣かないではいられない。
examples.english: I can't help crying.

examples.japanese: 彼の言うことを信じないではいられない。
examples.english: I cannot help believing what he says.

examples.japanese: もうすぐ試験だから遊んではいられない。勉強に集中しなきゃ。
examples.english: My exams are near so I can't afford to slack off. I need to focus on my studies.

examples.japanese: 今年から大学生になるから、いつまでも親に頼ってはいられない。
examples.english: I'll be a college student this year, so I can't rely on my parents forever.

examples.japanese: 明日は早く起きるので、いつものように遅くまで本を読んではいられない。
examples.english: I will get up early tomorrow, so I can't stay up and read late as usual.

meaning: must not; should not; do not ~
structure: Verb (て form) + はならない

examples.japanese: 過去を忘れてはならない。
examples.english: We must never forget the past.

examples.japanese: 教師はいじめを見逃してはならない。
examples.english: Teachers must not overlook bullying.

examples.japanese: 水は生きるためになくてはならない。
examples.english: Water is necessary for life.

examples.japanese: どんなことでも失敗したら、人のせいにしてはなりません。
examples.english: No matter the failure, you must not place the blame on others.

examples.japanese: 友達と約束したから、秘密を漏らしてはならない。
examples.english: I promised my friend, so their secret must not be leaked out.

examples.japanese: 自分の利益のために法律を違反することがあってはならない。
examples.english: You must never break the law for your own benefit.

meaning: and ~ (indicates two contrasting actions)
structure: V1ては + V2て + V1ては + V2て | V2ます + V2ます

examples.japanese: 立っては座り、座っては立ち、気分が落ち着かない。
examples.english: I keep standing and sitting down again, and can't seem to settle down.

examples.japanese: 食べては寝て、寝ては食べの生活は必ず太る。
examples.english: If you do nothing but sleep and eat, you will definitely gain weight.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ってはやんで降ってはやんでの日が続いている。
examples.english: It keeps raining on and off every day.

examples.japanese: 学んだことを覚えては忘れ、覚えては忘れを繰り返している。
examples.english: I keep repeating the cycle of memorizing and forgetting what I've studied.

examples.japanese: 結婚しては離婚して、離婚しては結婚している彼は信用できない。
examples.english: He keeps getting married and divorced, so I don't trust him.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに山登りをした。歩いては休み、していたので、頂上までたどり着くのはずいぶん長い時間かかってしまった。
examples.english: It had been a while since I climbed a mountain. I kept resting after only walking for a bit and it ended up taking a long time before I reached the peak.

meaning: just like; same as ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + と同時に | Noun | な-adj + である

examples.japanese: 彼らは笑うと同時に泣いた。
examples.english: They laughed and cried at the same time.

examples.japanese: 大学に入学すると同時に、私はアルバイトを始めました。
examples.english: I started a part-time job at the same time that I entered university.

examples.japanese: その店は開店と同時に満席になった。
examples.english: That restaurant became full at the same time that it opened.

examples.japanese: 私が乗り込むと同時に電車のドアが閉まった。
examples.english: The door closed at the same time as I walked onto the train.

examples.japanese: 昨日のニュースは大阪で地震と同時に火事が起こった。
examples.english: According to yesterday's news, a fire coincided with the earthquake in Osaka.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けると同時に私の電話のベルがなりました。
examples.english: My phone rang just as I was opening the door.

meaning: this way; that way; in such a way; how
structure: Noun + といった

examples.japanese: バスケットボール、サッカーといったスポーツは大学生に人気がある。
examples.english: Sports such as basketball and soccer are popular with college students.

examples.japanese: とんかつや天ぷらといった揚げ物の料理が好きです。
examples.english: I love fried foods like "tonkatsu" and "tempura".

examples.japanese: 彼女はアイスクリームやチョコレートといった甘い物が好きだ。
examples.english: She likes sweets such as ice cream and chocolate.

examples.japanese: トヨタやホンダといった車の会社は世界で有名だ。
examples.english: Car companies such as Toyota and Honda are famous in the world.

examples.japanese: この日本語学校にはタイ、ベトナムといった東南アジアからの留学生が多い。
examples.english: This Japanese language school has many students from Southeast Asia such as Thailand and Vietnam.

examples.japanese: 私は、「こんにちは」「さようなら」といった簡単な言葉を話せます。
examples.english: I can say simple words like "hello" and "goodbye".

meaning: this way; that way; in such a way; how
structure: Phrase + という風にというふうに

examples.japanese: 彼女は信じられないというふうに頭を振った。
examples.english: She shook her head in disbelief.

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも自分が天才だというふうに思い込んでいた。
examples.english: He always fancied himself as a genius.

examples.japanese: これは非常に大事なことだという風に思っております。
examples.english: I believe that this is extremely important.

examples.japanese: 日本にはどういう影響があるというふうに見ていますか。
examples.english: How do you see this affecting Japan?

examples.japanese: 彼はどうしようもないという風に首を振った。
examples.english: He shook his head as if to say it's hopeless.

examples.japanese: ぜひ皆様のご協力、ご指導も頂きたいというふうに思っています。
examples.english: I would appreciate everyone's cooperation and advice.

meaning: called; named; that ~
structure: Clause 1 + ということは + clause 2

examples.japanese: あなたが会社を辞めるということは本当ですか。
examples.english: Is it true that you are quitting the company?

examples.japanese: 彼は、まだ来ませんね。ということは、今日は欠席ですね。
examples.english: He still hasn't come, so he will be marked as absent for today.

examples.japanese: 30％割引きということは、２万円なら６千円安くなるんですね。
examples.english: A 30% discount, in other words 20,000 yen will become 6,000 yen cheaper.

examples.japanese: あの家を売ったということは、おそらく事業に失敗したのだろう。
examples.english: Since they are selling that house, I wonder if their business failed?

examples.japanese: 一日8時間月曜日から土曜日まで働くということは、一週間で48時間の労働だ。
examples.english: Working 8 hours everyday from Monday to Saturday means 48 hours of work in one week.

examples.japanese: 自転車が二台しかないということは、俺たちは誰かが歩かなければならないということだ。
examples.english: We only have two bicycles, so that means one of us has to walk.

meaning: during; for; since; over a period of time
structure: Verb (casual form) + というものだというものがある | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: これがいわゆる「天ぷら」というものです。
examples.english: This is what we call "tempura".

examples.japanese: 辛い時に助けてくれるのが、親友というものだ。
examples.english: Those who help you in rough times are called true friends.

examples.japanese: それがまさに愛というものだ。
examples.english: That is what love is all about.

examples.japanese: 人はみんな平等ではない。それが人生というものだ。
examples.english: Not all people are equal. That's just part of life.

examples.japanese: 私は山田ケンというものです。
examples.english: My name is Ken Yamada.

examples.japanese: それは無理押しというものだ。
examples.english: That is forcing things too much.

meaning: during; for; since; over a period of time
structure: Verb (casual form) + というものではないというものでもない | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: お金があれば幸せだというものでもない。
examples.english: Having money is no guarantee that you will be happy.

examples.japanese: 私の仕事は誰でもできるというものではない！
examples.english: My work is not something that just anybody can do!

examples.japanese: 日本に留学すれば、日本語が上手になるというものでもない。
examples.english: If you study abroad in Japan, that does not necessarily mean you will get good at speaking Japanese.

examples.japanese: 情報が多ければ判断が楽というものではない。
examples.english: Having more information does not always necessarily make a decision easier.

examples.japanese: 外国語はただ文法を覚えれば話せるというものではない。
examples.english: With foreign languages, just memorizing grammar does not necessarily mean you will be able to speak the language.

examples.japanese: 値段が高ければ良い品物だというものでもない。
examples.english: Just because the price is high doesn't mean that it is a good quality item.

meaning: among other things; such as; like ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + とか（で） | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: アメリカで育ったとかで。
examples.english: I heard they were raised in America.

examples.japanese: 今度の試験はかなり難しいとかで。
examples.english: I heard the next test is going to be really hard.

examples.japanese: 事故があったとかで、今、電車が止まっています。
examples.english: I heard there was an accident and so the train is stopped now.

examples.japanese: 安田さんは忙しいとかで今夜の飲み会に来れないそう。
examples.english: I heard Mr. Yasuda is quite busy and I don't think she'll be able to make it to drinks tonight.

examples.japanese: 今夜の花火大会は、雨で中止だとか。
examples.english: I heard that tonight's fireworks were cancelled due to rain.

examples.japanese: さっき聞いたんだけど、田中さんは来年、会社を辞めるとか。本当に辞めるんだろう。
examples.english: I just heard that Mr. Tanaka will be quitting next year. I wonder if he really is quitting..

meaning: already; now; no longer; not anymore
structure: とっくに + Verb

examples.japanese: 彼はとっくに帰りました。
examples.english: He came home a long while ago.

examples.japanese: もうとっくに学校へ出かけている時間じゃないの。
examples.english: It's high time you left for school, isn't it?

examples.japanese: 寝る時間はとっくに過ぎているよ。
examples.english: It's way past your bedtime.

examples.japanese: そのお菓子はとっくに賞味期限を過ぎていた。
examples.english: Those sweets are long past their expiration date.

examples.japanese: 子供が出来たから、彼はタバコをとっくに辞めた。
examples.english: He quit smoking back when he had kids.

examples.japanese: そうしていなかったら、僕はとっくに死んでいたよ。
examples.english: If I had not done this, I would already be dead.

meaning: if... (counterfactual condition), then would be ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ところだった

examples.japanese: 危ないところだった。
examples.english: That was a close call.

examples.japanese: ちょうど寝るところだった。
examples.english: I was just about to head to bed.

examples.japanese: ああ, もう少しで忘れるところだった。
examples.english: Oh, I almost forgot!

examples.japanese: 太陽がまさに沈むところだった。
examples.english: The sun was just about to set.

examples.japanese: 僕はもう少しで出かけるところだった、ちょうどよいところだった。
examples.english: I was just about to head out, you came at just the right time.

examples.japanese: もう少しで電車に乗り遅れるところだった。
examples.english: I almost missed the train.

meaning: even so; however; even though ~
structure: Verb (た / ている / ていた) + ところにところへところを | Noun + の | Adjective

examples.japanese: 私はちょうど家を出ようと思っているところに、小雨が降り始めた。
examples.english: I was just about to leave home when a light rain started to fall.

examples.japanese: 駅に着いたところに財布を忘れたことに気づいた。
examples.english: When I arrived at the station I realized I forgot my wallet.

examples.japanese: 家を出ているところに、電話がかかってきた。
examples.english: My phone rang just as I was leaving my house.

examples.japanese: 授業中に居眠りしているところを先生に見つかってしまった。
examples.english: My teacher caught me sleeping in the middle of class.

examples.japanese: 道に迷って困っていたところへ、警察が通りかかった。
examples.english: A policeman passed by just when I was getting lost.

examples.japanese: 電話しようと思っていたところに、ちょうどその相手から電話がかかってきた。
examples.english: Just when I was about to call him, he called me.

meaning: from the point of view of; by the look of; judging from ~
structure: Verb (casual) + ところを見ると

examples.japanese: 彼女はラーメンを食べているところを見ると、ダイエットはやめたんだね。
examples.english: Judjing from the fact that she's eating ramen, she must have quit her diet.

examples.japanese: 顔が赤くなっているところを見ると、私が言ったことは本当だ。
examples.english: Seeing their face turn red means that what I said must have been true.

examples.japanese: 嬉しい顔をしているところを見ると、彼女はN2を合格しただろう。
examples.english: Judging from her happy face, she likely passed the N2.

examples.japanese: 怖がることなく近づいていくところを見ると、彼女は犬好きかもしれない。
examples.english: Seeing her approach without fear, she might like dogs.

examples.japanese: 大勢の客が行列しているところを見ると、ケーキ屋はとても美味しいようだ。
examples.english: Judging from the large crowd, the cake shop seems to be very delicious.

examples.japanese: その会社、いつも社員を募集しているところを見ると、人がすぐに辞めてしまうのかなあ。
examples.english: Seeing as how that company is always hiring, I wonder if everyone quits right away.

meaning: unable to draw a conclusion; unable to judge
structure: Verb ないく + とも | い-adjective + いく | phrase

examples.japanese: え、そうですとも。
examples.english: Yes, that is most certainly so.

examples.japanese: 辛くとも、頑張る！
examples.english: Even if things get rough, I'll do my best!

examples.japanese: 言わなくとも分かるはず。
examples.english: Even if it wasn't said, you should understand.

examples.japanese: 遅くとも一週間以内に終わらせます。
examples.english: Even if I'm running late, I'll make sure to finish within the week.

examples.japanese: 彼がいなくともけっこう間に合う。
examples.english: We can do very well without him.

examples.japanese: 竹田は君の助けがなくとも自分の面倒ぐらいみれるよ。
examples.english: Takeda can look after himself without your assistance.

meaning: (not) at all; (not) in the least ~
structure: 1 + [counter] + として + ... + + Verb (ない form)

examples.japanese: 僕は一日として学校を休んだことがない。
examples.english: I have never missed school for even a single day.

examples.japanese: 彼女は一度として宿題を忘れたことがない。
examples.english: She has never once forgotten her homework.

examples.japanese: 彼の提案に誰一人として反対できませんでした。
examples.english: Not a single person could oppose his proposal.

examples.japanese: 津波により家が流されてしまい、何１つとして残っていない。
examples.english: The house was washed away by the tsunami, and nothing remains.

examples.japanese: この人形は全て手作りなので、一つとして同じものがありません。
examples.english: All of these dolls are handmade, so no one is the same as another.

examples.japanese: 私が仕事を辞めることは同僚の誰一人として知らなかった。
examples.english: Not a single one of my colleagues knew I would quit my job.

meaning: even if; even supposing that ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + としても | Noun + だ | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 今回の試験で不合格になったとしても、諦めずに次回も受験するつもりです。
examples.english: Even if I were to fail the exam this time, I plan to not give up and take the exam again.

examples.japanese: たとえ買えるとしても，そんな家は買わないだろう。
examples.english: I wouldn't buy such a house even if I could.

examples.japanese: 学校を卒業後、国に帰ったとしても、日本語の勉強は続けるつもりです。
examples.english: After I graduate school, even if I head to my home country, I plan to continue studying Japanese.

examples.japanese: 私はお金持ちになったとしても、今と変わらない生活をするでしょう。
examples.english: Even if I were to become rich, my life likely wouldn't change much from what it is like now.

examples.japanese: 彼を説得しようとしても無駄だ。
examples.english: It's pointless to try to persuade him.

examples.japanese: ジョギングに行くと決めていた日に、たとえ雨が降ったとしても、決行するのだ。
examples.english: On the day you decided to go jogging, even if it's raining, make sure you do it.

meaning: but then; although; though ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + つつ (も)

examples.japanese: 彼は時々車を運転しつつ、電話をする。
examples.english: He sometimes talks on the phone while driving.

examples.japanese: 彼は忙しいと言いつつ、長電話をしている。
examples.english: Although he says he is busy, he has been talking on the phone for a long time.

examples.japanese: 健康に良くないとは知りつつ、タバコがやめられない。
examples.english: Even while knowing tobacco is bad for one's health, they still cannot quit.

examples.japanese: ダイエットしようと思いつつ、甘いものを見ると食べてしまう。
examples.english: Even though I'm thinking to go on a diet, every time I see something sweet I end up eating it..

examples.japanese: 先生と相談しつつ、進路を決めたいと思う。
examples.english: While consulting with my teacher, I want to decide my future path.

examples.japanese: いけないと知りつつも、ゴミを分別せずに捨ててしまう。
examples.english: Even though I know it is wrong, I throw away my garbage without separating it.

meaning: while; during; without change; performed in this condition
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + つつある

examples.japanese: スマホの登場で、デジタルカメラの人気がなくなりつつある。
examples.english: Since the release of the smartphone, digital camera's have been losing popularity.

examples.japanese: 最近はゴルフをしていないので、下手になりつつあります。
examples.english: Lately I haven't been playing golf, so I am losing my touch.

examples.japanese: 日本は高齢化が進みつつある。
examples.english: Japan's population continues to age.

examples.japanese: 事故から一週間が経ち、原因などが明らかになりつつある。
examples.english: It's been one week since the accident and the cause of the accident is becoming clear.

examples.japanese: 最近、買い物をしすぎてお金がなくなりつつあります。
examples.english: Lately I've been shopping too much and am losing money.

examples.japanese: コスプレ文化が世界に広まりつつあるようだ。
examples.english: Cosplay culture is spreading around the world.

meaning: besides; in addition; furthermore ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 上は | Verb (た form)

examples.japanese: 約束した上は、どんなことがあっても守ります。
examples.english: Since I’ve made a promise, I will keep it no matter what happens.

examples.japanese: プロ選手になると決めた上は、苦しくても頑張らなければならない。
examples.english: Since you've decided to become a professional athlete, even if things get tough you have to always do your best.

examples.japanese: N2を受験する上は、高得点で合格したいです。
examples.english: Since I will be taking the N2, I want to pass with a high score.

examples.japanese: 家族を離れて日本で働く上は、十分な覚悟が必要である。
examples.english: Since you will be moving away from your family to work in Japan, you will need to properly prepare yourself.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事を引き受けた上はいつも全力を尽くします。
examples.english: He always does his best after taking a job.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは失敗した。こうなった上は言い訳をしても無駄だ。
examples.english: This project failed. Since it's come to this, there is no point in making excuses.

meaning: let alone; not to mention; needless to say ~
structure: Noun + は + もとより + ~も

examples.japanese: 私は車はもとより自転車もないんです。
examples.english: I don't have a bicycle, let alone a car.

examples.japanese: 私が生まれた村は、電車はもとより、バスも全然ない。
examples.english: There are no trains, let alone buses in the village I was born in.

examples.japanese: キャベツはサラダで食べるのはもとより、炒めても美味しい。
examples.english: Cabbage is of course good in salad, but it is also good in stir-fry.

examples.japanese: 見た目はもとより味も最高ですよ！
examples.english: Not only does it look good, but the taste is also great!

examples.japanese: イギリスでは土曜日はもとより金曜の午後まで休みにしている会社もある。
examples.english: There are companies in England that not only take Saturday's off, but Friday afternoons off as well.

examples.japanese: 僕はもとより知っていた。
examples.english: I knew from the very beginning.

meaning: I don't know about ... but; it may be possible for ... but ~
structure: Noun + はともかく（として）

examples.japanese: 行くか行かないかはともかく、レストランの予約だけはしておこう。
examples.english: Whether or not we are going, let's at least make the restaurant reservation.

examples.japanese: この店の品物は、質はともかく種類は多い。
examples.english: Regardless of the quality of the goods at this store, they have a lot of variety.

examples.japanese: 奥さんの料理は見た目はともかく味は美味しい。
examples.english: Regardless of weather it looks good or not, my wife's cooking tastes pretty good.

examples.japanese: 漢字を読むことはともかく、書くことは苦手だ。
examples.english: I can't even write kanji, let alone read it.

examples.japanese: あの俳優は、顔はともかくとして演技が素晴らしい。
examples.english: Whether or not he/she has a nice face, they are a great actor.

examples.japanese: ともかく無事でよかった。
examples.english: In any case, I'm glad you're OK.

meaning: not only... but also; as well as ~
structure: わずかに + Phrase

examples.japanese: 電車がわずかに遅れている。
examples.english: The train is running slightly late.

examples.japanese: 道はここでわずかに右に曲がっている。
examples.english: The road bends slightly to the right here.

examples.japanese: 財布の中に残っていたお金はわずかに500円だった。
examples.english: The money remaining in the wallet was only 500 yen.

examples.japanese: 私は学校へわずかに二ヶ月しか行っていません。
examples.english: I only went to school for barely 2 months.

examples.japanese: わずかに4日間でそんなにたくさんの仕事をしたとは驚きだ。
examples.english: I'm surprised you did all that work in just four days.

examples.japanese: バスの中にはわずかに５人しか居なかった。
examples.english: There were no more than five passengers on the bus.

meaning: to end up; in the end; finally; after all ~
structure: やがて + phrase

examples.japanese: やがて真っ暗になった。
examples.english: It soon became completely dark.

examples.japanese: やがて考えがまとまってきた。
examples.english: My ideas finally began to take shape.

examples.japanese: 空は曇ってきた。やがて雨になるかもしれない。
examples.english: The sky is starting to get cloudy. It might start raining soon.

examples.japanese: やがてうちの近くの公園は桜が咲きます。
examples.english: Before long, the cherry blossoms will be blooming in the park near our house.

examples.japanese: 彼が親と喧嘩して家を出てからやがて三年になる。
examples.english: It will soon be 3 years since he left home after fighting with his parents.

examples.japanese: やがて、彼らは厳しい現実を受け入れるようになった。
examples.english: In time they came to accept the harsh reality.

meaning: pattern to give two representative examples (usually negative)
structure: Verb (dictionary) + やら + [B]やら | Noun | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 大学生は宿題やらアルバイトやらで忙しい。
examples.english: University students are quite busy with things like homework and part time jobs.

examples.japanese: さっきコンビニでおにぎりやらお茶やらを買った。
examples.english: A short while ago I bought some rice balls and tea from the convenience store.

examples.japanese: 疲れやら空腹やらで、彼は死んだように倒れた。
examples.english: With fatigue and hunger, he fell down as if he were dead.

examples.japanese: サイクリングをする時は嬉しいやら楽しいやら、とてもいい気分だ。
examples.english: When I go cycling I feel very happy and have a lot of fun. It really is a great feeling!

examples.japanese: カバンにはパソコンやらノートやら教科書やらが入っている。
examples.english: In my backpack, I have things like my laptop, my notebook, textbook, etc..

examples.japanese: 両親からの仕送りは、家賃やら食費やらでほとんどなくなってしまった。
examples.english: All of the money I got from my parents disappeared from things like my rent and food expenses.

meaning: it's not worth; no need to ~
structure: よほどよっぽど + explanation

examples.japanese: よほど前にあった事です。
examples.english: It happened a long time ago.

examples.japanese: そこはここからよほど離れている。
examples.english: That place is quite far from here.

examples.japanese: 彼はこれまでよりよほどよく働いております。
examples.english: He is working much harder than before.

examples.japanese: 彼はよほどのことがなければ気持ちを変えないだろう。
examples.english: It'll take a lot to make him change his mind.

examples.japanese: よほど本当のことを言ってやろうかと思った。
examples.english: I had a good mind to tell him the truth.

examples.japanese: 仕事があまりにもきついから、よっぽど会社を辞めようかと思っている。
examples.english: My work is really tough and I'm strongly thinking about quitting.

meaning: also; let alone; from the beginning
structure: time, place or person + より

examples.japanese: 今日より、毎日日本語を勉強します。
examples.english: From today, I will study Japanese everyday.

examples.japanese: 昨日、山田さんよりお電話を頂きました。
examples.english: I received a call from Mr. Yamada yesterday.

examples.japanese: 心より感謝します。
examples.english: I truly appreciate it (from my heart)

examples.japanese: 授業は9月1日より開始です。
examples.english: Classes start from the 1st of September.

examples.japanese: 来週の水曜日より、大阪に出張します。
examples.english: From next Wednesday I will be going on a business trip to Osaka.

examples.japanese: 四月一日より試験を行います。
examples.english: The exam will be held from April 1st.

meaning: to be forced to do something because one has no other choice
structure: Verb (dictionary) + （より）ほか（は）ない（より）ほか（しかたが）ない

examples.japanese: この仕事は君に信頼するよりほかはない。
examples.english: I have no choice but to trust you with this job.

examples.japanese: バスがないので、歩いていくよりほか仕方がない。
examples.english: Since there are no buses, i have no choice but to go on foot.

examples.japanese: 頼れる人はいないから、自分がやるよりほか仕方がない。
examples.english: I have no one to depend on, so the only option is to do it myself.

examples.japanese: 僕は学力が足りないから勉強で補うよりほかはない。
examples.english: I don't have great academic ability, so I need to make up for it by studying.

examples.japanese: 自転車が壊れてしまった。学校へバスで行くよりほか仕方がない。
examples.english: My bicycle broke. Now I have no choice but to go to school by bus.

examples.japanese: 台風が来るので、残念だが明日の大会は延期するよりほかない。
examples.english: A typhoon is coming, so although it is unfortunate the only option is to delay the event.

meaning: having done that; if that is done; if it is done in that way
structure: Verb (casual form) + ようでは + bad result

examples.japanese: この問題が分からないようではN２には合格できないよ。
examples.english: If you don't understand this problem, then you won't be able to pass the N2.

examples.japanese: 試験の前の日に勉強を始めるようでは、合格はできない。
examples.english: If you start studying the day before the exam, you will not be able to pass.

examples.japanese: この問題が解決できないようでは困るよ。
examples.english: If we can't resolve this problem, there's going to be trouble.

examples.japanese: 最初の日から、仕事に遅刻するようでは悪い印象になるよ。
examples.english: If you are late to work from the first day, it will leave a bad impression.

examples.japanese: 報告書にこんなにミスがあるようでは、君に仕事を任せられない。
examples.english: If there are this many errors in your written report, then I will not be able to entrust any work with you.

examples.japanese: 自分の管理もできないようでは、人の上に立つこともできない。
examples.english: If you cannot control yourself, you will not be able to be in a position above others.

meaning: right? isn't it? let's~; confirmation
structure: Verb (volitional form) + ではないかじゃないか

examples.japanese: 困った時はお互いに助け合っていこうではありませんか。
examples.english: Let's help each other when we are in trouble.

examples.japanese: 日本語を身につけるために頑張ろうではないか。
examples.english: Let’s do our best to master Japanese.

examples.japanese: 今日はお祝いだ。みんなで飲もうではないか。
examples.english: Today is a for celebration! Why don't we all go out for drinks together?

examples.japanese: 誰もやらないなら、僕がやってみようじゃないか。
examples.english: If no one is going to do it, why don't I give it a try?

examples.japanese: この問題については、もっと話し合おうではないか。
examples.english: Regarding this problem, why don't we discuss it a bit more?

examples.japanese: この町を人気になる方法について、一緒に考えようではありませんか。
examples.english: Why don't we brainstorm together about how to get more popular in this town?

meaning: simply because; on account of~ (negative result)
structure: 要するに + phrase

examples.japanese: 要するに時と金の問題だ。
examples.english: In short, it is a question of time and money.

examples.japanese: 要するに、彼女は行きたくないって言ったでしょう。
examples.english: To sum up, she said she doesn't want to go, right?

examples.japanese: その会合は勉強にならない。要するに時間の無駄だった。
examples.english: That gathering did not help with my studies, in short it was a waste of time.

examples.japanese: 終電が出てしまった。要するに、今日は電車で帰れないということだ。
examples.english: The last train left.. In short, I won't be able to return home by train today.

examples.japanese: 合格点に10点足りず、不合格でした。要するに、まだまだ努力が足りなかった。
examples.english: I was short 10 points of a passing score and failed. In short, I did not put in enough effort..

examples.japanese: 彼は一度も入賞しなかった。要するに才能がなかったということだ。
examples.english: He's never even once placed in a contest. To put it simply, lacked talent.

meaning: can’t help but; can’t refrain from ~
structure: Verb (ない root) ない + ざるを得ない | Exception: しない -> せ

examples.japanese: 私はそうせざるを得ない。
examples.english: I have no choice but to do that.

examples.japanese: いやな仕事でも、生活のためには続けざるを得ない。
examples.english: Even if it's work you don't like, you must continue working in order to maintain your livelihood.

examples.japanese: 彼は受験のため、サークル活動を休まざるを得なかった。
examples.english: In order to prepare for exams, he had no choice but to quit his club activities.

examples.japanese: 彼女は進学したいが、家族が学費を払える状況でもないので、諦めざるを得ない。
examples.english: She wants to go to university, but her family is not in a position to help support her so she has no choice but to give up.

examples.japanese: 今回の旅行を楽しみにしていたが、母が急に入院したので、行くのをキャンセルせざるを得ない。
examples.english: I was looking forward to this trip, but my mother was suddenly hospitalized so we had to cancel it.

examples.japanese: 留学したい気持ちは分かるが、この病状では、延期せざるを得ないだろう。
examples.english: I understand you want to study abroad, but with your medical condition there is no choice but to postpone.

meaning: get by without doing ~
structure: Verb ない (ない stem) + ずに済む | Exception: する => せずに済む

examples.japanese: 今年は涼しかったので、エアコンを使わずに済みました。
examples.english: This year was cool and I got by without using my air conditioner.

examples.japanese: ここでは1日中雨が降らずに済むことはほとんどない。
examples.english: Hardly a day passes here without rain.

examples.japanese: 損をせずに済んだ。
examples.english: I got off without any loss.

examples.japanese: 私の友達が自分のアパートに泊めてくれたのでホテルに泊まらずに済んだ。
examples.english: My friend let me stay at their apartment, so I got by without having to stay at a hotel.

examples.japanese: 死なずに済んだのはまったくの幸運だった。
examples.english: I escaped death by pure luck.

examples.japanese: 金を借りずに済むなら借りはしません。
examples.english: I would not borrow money if I could help it.

meaning: Starting with ~ / Beginning with ~ (as the first in a series)
structure: Noun + を皮切りに / を皮切りとして

examples.japanese: 東京公演を皮切りに、全国ツアーが始まった。
examples.english: Starting with the Tokyo performance, the national tour began.

examples.japanese: この発言を皮切りに、議論が激化した。
examples.english: Starting from this remark, the debate intensified.

examples.japanese: 彼の参加を皮切りに、多くの人が集まってきた。
examples.english: Beginning with his participation, many people gathered.

notes: 皮切り literally means 'first cut of the skin' (from a surgical origin). Describes the triggering start of a chain of events or a series.

meaning: Simply because ~ / Just because ~ (leading to a bad outcome)
structure: Plain form + ばかりに

examples.japanese: 正直に言ったばかりに、嫌われてしまった。
examples.english: Simply because I spoke honestly, I ended up being disliked.

examples.japanese: 急いでいたばかりに、財布を忘れた。
examples.english: Just because I was in a hurry, I forgot my wallet.

examples.japanese: 夢中になっていたばかりに、時間を忘れた。
examples.english: Simply because I was absorbed in it, I forgot the time.

notes: Expresses regret — a single cause leading to a negative consequence. Unlike 〜から or 〜ので, this strongly implies that one thing alone caused the trouble.

meaning: Other than ~ / Besides ~ / No one/nothing else but ~
structure: Noun + をおいて + [negative expression]

examples.japanese: この仕事は彼をおいて他にできる人はいない。
examples.english: There is no one other than him who can do this job.

examples.japanese: 今をおいて、チャンスはない。
examples.english: There is no chance other than now.

examples.japanese: あなたをおいて、誰に相談できますか。
examples.english: Besides you, who can I consult?

notes: Always used with a negative clause. Strongly asserts exclusivity — there is only this one option.

meaning: If that's the case ~ / If it means ~
structure: Noun / Plain form + とあれば

examples.japanese: 君のためとあれば、何でもする。
examples.english: If it's for you, I'll do anything.

examples.japanese: 緊急事態とあれば、すぐ行きます。
examples.english: If it's an emergency, I'll go right away.

examples.japanese: 必要とあれば、徹夜してでもやり遂げる。
examples.english: If it's necessary, I'll pull an all-nighter to finish it.

notes: Expresses a willingness to act given a specific condition. The condition is treated as an accepted fact that justifies the response.

meaning: Once ~ (there's no going back)
structure: Verb[た] + が最後

examples.japanese: 彼に捕まったが最後、逃げられない。
examples.english: Once he catches you, there's no escaping.

examples.japanese: あのゲームを始めたが最後、止められない。
examples.english: Once you start that game, you can't stop.

examples.japanese: 約束したが最後、守らなければならない。
examples.english: Once you've made a promise, you must keep it.

notes: Dramatic or literary expression. Implies that crossing a certain threshold makes retreat or reversal impossible.

meaning: While ~ / In addition to one's main activity ~
structure: Verb[dict] / Noun + の + かたわら

examples.japanese: 彼は会社員をするかたわら、小説を書いている。
examples.english: While working as a company employee, he writes novels.

examples.japanese: 子育てのかたわら、資格の勉強をしている。
examples.english: While raising children, she is studying for a qualification.

examples.japanese: 研究のかたわら、後進の指導もしている。
examples.english: Alongside his research, he is also mentoring the next generation.

notes: Describes a secondary activity done alongside a primary one. More formal than 〜ながら. The main activity is typically a job, role, or major commitment.

meaning: In accordance with ~ / Based on ~
structure: Noun + に即して / に即した + Noun

examples.japanese: 規則に即して行動してください。
examples.english: Please act in accordance with the rules.

examples.japanese: 現実に即した計画が必要だ。
examples.english: A plan based on reality is necessary.

examples.japanese: 法律に即して判断する。
examples.english: I will make a judgment in accordance with the law.

notes: Formal expression indicating conformity with established standards, reality, or rules. Similar to 〜に基づいて but に即して carries more of a 'fitting/appropriate to' nuance.

meaning: While ~ / Despite the situation of ~ (caught/seen in the act)
structure: Verb[plain] + ところを

examples.japanese: 休んでいるところをすみません。
examples.english: I'm sorry to disturb you while you're resting.

examples.japanese: 逃げようとしているところを捕まえた。
examples.english: I caught him in the act of trying to escape.

examples.japanese: お忙しいところをお越しいただき、ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for coming despite being so busy.

notes: Describes catching someone in a particular state or interrupting them. The polite phrases すみません/ありがとう often follow it.

meaning: If only ~ / I wish ~ (regret)
structure: Plain form + ものを

examples.japanese: 早く言ってくれればよかったものを。
examples.english: If only you had told me sooner.

examples.japanese: 素直に謝れば済んだものを。
examples.english: If only he had just apologized honestly.

examples.japanese: もっと注意すればよかったものを。
examples.english: I wish I had been more careful.

notes: Expresses regret that things didn't turn out as hoped. The speaker implies that a better outcome was possible but not taken. Often ends a sentence.

meaning: Even if not ~ / At least ~
structure: Verb[ない] + までも

examples.japanese: 毎日でないまでも、週に一度は運動する。
examples.english: Even if not every day, I exercise at least once a week.

examples.japanese: 完璧でないまでも、ある程度の品質は必要だ。
examples.english: Even if not perfect, a certain level of quality is necessary.

examples.japanese: 専門家でないまでも、基礎知識は持っている。
examples.english: Even if not an expert, I do have basic knowledge.

notes: Acknowledges a lower standard is acceptable — 'even if we can't achieve X, at least Y'. The standard in the main clause is always below the one in the ないまでも clause.

pattern: 〜いかんによらず / 〜いかんにかかわらず
meaning: Regardless of ~ / No matter what ~
structure: Noun + いかんによらず / いかんにかかわらず

examples.japanese: 理由のいかんによらず、遅刻は許されない。
examples.english: Regardless of the reason, tardiness is not permitted.

examples.japanese: 結果のいかんにかかわらず、全力を尽くす。
examples.english: Regardless of the outcome, I will give my all.

examples.japanese: 天候のいかんにかかわらず、試合は行われる。
examples.english: The match will be held regardless of the weather.

notes: Very formal. いかん means 'how/what it is'. Used in official contexts, rules, or written language. Interchangeable with 〜にかかわらず in many cases.

meaning: Cannot help but ~ / Cannot refrain from ~
structure: Verb[ない-stem] + ずにはいられない

examples.japanese: そのニュースを聞いて、泣かずにはいられなかった。
examples.english: Hearing that news, I couldn't help but cry.

examples.japanese: おかしくて、笑わずにはいられない。
examples.english: It's so funny I can't help but laugh.

examples.japanese: 不正を見て、言わずにはいられない。
examples.english: Seeing the injustice, I cannot refrain from speaking out.

notes: Expresses an irresistible compulsion. する → せずにはいられない (する is irregular). The casual form is 〜ないではいられない.

meaning: Nothing but ~ / Is precisely ~
structure: Noun / Plain form + にほかならない

examples.japanese: これは努力の結果にほかならない。
examples.english: This is nothing other than the result of hard work.

examples.japanese: 彼の行動は裏切りにほかならない。
examples.english: His actions are nothing short of betrayal.

examples.japanese: それは愛情にほかならないと思う。
examples.english: I believe that is nothing but love.

notes: Formal, emphatic assertion. States that something is exclusively and precisely what is named — no other interpretation is possible. Stronger than 〜にすぎない (merely).

meaning: Without any particular intention to ~ / Absently ~
structure: Verb[dict] + ともなく / ともなしに

examples.japanese: 見るともなくテレビを見ていた。
examples.english: I was watching TV without really watching it.

examples.japanese: 聞くともなしに、隣の会話が聞こえてきた。
examples.english: Without intending to listen, I overheard the conversation nearby.

examples.japanese: どこへ行くともなく歩いた。
examples.english: I walked without going anywhere in particular.

notes: Describes an action done absentmindedly or without conscious intent. The same verb is often repeated in both clauses: 見るともなく見る.

meaning: Even if ~ / Even though ~ (concessive, formal)
structure: Noun / Plain form + といえども

examples.japanese: プロといえども、失敗することがある。
examples.english: Even professionals make mistakes sometimes.

examples.japanese: 法律といえども、すべてが正しいわけではない。
examples.english: Even the law is not always right.

examples.japanese: 親友といえども、秘密は話せない。
examples.english: Even to a close friend, I cannot reveal this secret.

notes: Classical/formal concessive. Grants a premise and then contradicts or qualifies it. Stronger and more literary than 〜でも or 〜ても.

meaning: pattern to give two representative examples (usually negative)
structure: Pattern | [A] + だの + [B] + だの | Conjugations | Verb + だの | Noun (だった） | な-adjective （だった） | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 父は酒だの、タバコだのが好きで、健康が心配です。
examples.english: My father really likes things like alcohol and cigarettes, so I really worry for his health.

examples.japanese: お菓子だの、アイスだの甘いものばかり食べてるから虫歯になるんだよ。
examples.english: Because you only eat sweets and ice cream you are going to get some cavities.

examples.japanese: 僕の毎月の小遣いは、飲み会だのカラオケだので消えていく。
examples.english: My monthly allowance usually disappears from drinking parties and karaoke.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、風邪を引いただの、頭が痛いだのと言って、よく授業を休む。
examples.english: She often skips class by saying things like I've caught a cold or I've got a headache..

examples.japanese: 一生結婚しないだの、海外で暮らすだの、うちの娘は本当に自分勝手だ。
examples.english: She will never get married and lives abroad, my daughter is truly a selfish person.

examples.japanese: 彼女は部屋が狭いだの、寒いだのといつも文句を言っている。
examples.english: She is always complaining about things like the room being too small or it being cold, etc..

meaning: surely; certainly; no doubt; indeed​ ~
structure: Sentence (casual) + だろうに

examples.japanese: 私があなたの立場だったら、辞めているだろうに。
examples.english: Were I in your position, I would have quit.

examples.japanese: 子育てで疲れているだろうに、妻は家事も頑張ってくれている。
examples.english: My wife is doing her best with the housework, even though she may be tired from raising our children.

examples.japanese: 子供を激しく叱るなんてよくないだろうに、叱らないと子供が自立できない。
examples.english: Although harsly scolding children is surely not good, if we don't scold them at all, our kids won’t become independent.

examples.japanese: 万一彼があなたに会えば、彼は驚くだろうに。
examples.english: Should he be able to see you, he would surely be surprised.

examples.japanese: リスクがあるだろうに、なぜ続けているのか話を聞いてみたい。
examples.english: I'd like to hear why you're continuing this, even though there clearly are risks.

examples.japanese: 時間なんてたくさんあるだろうに、有効に使わない人こそ少ないと嘆く。
examples.english: Although there is a lot of time, it is tragic that only few people use it effectively.

pattern: であれ / であろうと
meaning: whether [A] or [B]
structure: Noun + であれであろうと

examples.japanese: 若い時はどんな仕事であれ、一生懸命取り組みました。
examples.english: When I was young, no matter what the work was I always gave it my best effort.

examples.japanese: 嘘をつくとは、どんな理由であれ、許されないことだ。
examples.english: Whatever the reason, lying is an unforgivable act.

examples.japanese: 彼女が誰であれ、特別扱いするのはダメでしょう。
examples.english: Regardless of whoever she may be, preferential treatment is surely not acceptable.

examples.japanese: 彼の話が真実であろうと無かろうと違いは無い。
examples.english: It makes no difference whether his story is true or not.

examples.japanese: 故意であろうとなかろうと人を傷つけたことには変わりはありません。
examples.english: Whatever the intent may be, that doesn't change the fact that someone was hurt.

examples.japanese: 犯人が誰であれ、どこにいようと、必ず私が捕まえる。
examples.english: Whoever the criminal may be, wherever they may be, I absolutely will catch them.

meaning: whoever; whatever; however; even ~
structure: Noun + であれであろうと + Noun + であれであろうと

examples.japanese: 彼がお金持ちであれ貧乏であれ、私の気持ちが変わることはない。
examples.english: It doesn't matter whether he is rich or poor, my feelings will not change.

examples.japanese: 先生であれ学生であれ、規則には従わなければなりません。
examples.english: Whether you are a teacher or a student, everyone must follow the rules.

examples.japanese: オクラであれ納豆であれ、ネバネバしたものはとにかく嫌いだ。
examples.english: Whether it be okra or natto, I hate these kinds of sticky foods.

examples.japanese: たとえ雨であろうと雪であろうと、明日の試合は予定通り行います。
examples.english: Even if it rains or snows, tomorrows match will continue as scheduled.

examples.japanese: 正社員であろうと、パートであろうと、仕事に対する責任は変わりません。
examples.english: Whether you are a full-timer or part timer, one's responsibility towards work does not change.

examples.japanese: 車であれ電車であれこの天候では無理だろう。
examples.english: Whether it be by car or train, it's impossible in this weather.

meaning: negative connection/comparison (like father like son)
structure: Noun + で + もあり + Noun + で + もある | な-adj + で + な-adj + で | い-adj + いく + い-adj + いく

examples.japanese: 明日の試合は興奮でもあり、緊張でもある。
examples.english: I'm both excited and nervous for tomorrow's match.

examples.japanese: 高校に卒業したら喜ばしくもあり悲しくもある。
examples.english: Graduating from high school is both happy and sad.

examples.japanese: 考えすぎてしまうのは、長所でもあり、短所でもある。
examples.english: Thinking too much is both a strength and a weakness.

examples.japanese: 彼は教師でもあり小説家でもある。
examples.english: He is both a teacher and a novelist.

examples.japanese: この本は面白くもあり有益でもある。
examples.english: This book is both interesting and informative.

examples.japanese: 彼女はこの組織の創業者でもあり、経営者でもある。
examples.english: She is both the founder and the operator of this organization.

pattern: でも何でもない / くも何ともない
meaning: one may well say so, but~; not only... but also ~
structure: Noun + でも何でもない | な-adjective | い-adjective い + くも何ともない

examples.japanese: 誕生日でもなんでもないのにプレゼントをもらった。
examples.english: I got a present even though it wasn't my birthday or anything like that.

examples.japanese: 彼の冗談は面白くもなんともない。
examples.english: His joke is not interesting at all.

examples.japanese: 彼は僕の親戚でもなんでもない。
examples.english: I am not related to him at all.

examples.japanese: 彼のこと、好きでもなんでもないけれど、なぜか気にかかる。
examples.english: I don't really like him at all but there is something interesting about him.

examples.japanese: 今回の結果は不思議でもなんでもないし、当然だと思う。
examples.english: The result this time is nothing strange and I think was to be expected.

examples.japanese: 苦労でもなんでもないよ。君に手伝えれば僕が嬉しいです。
examples.english: It's not hard work or anything. I would be very happy if I could help you.

meaning: isn't it; I wonder if it’s not ~
structure: Noun + でなくてなんだろう

examples.japanese: 彼女に対するこの気持ちは、愛でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: The feeling of mine for her must be love.

examples.japanese: 子供のために病気になるまで働くとは、親の愛でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: Working to the point of sickness for the sake of one's child is nothing other than parental love.

examples.japanese: 彼は裁判で無罪を主張しているが、彼のやったことは殺人ででなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: He is claiming to be innocent in court, but what he did was clearly murder.

examples.japanese: あの政治家のやったことは汚職でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: What that politician did was definitely corrupt.

examples.japanese: 友達は飛行機で隣に座った人と結婚したそうだ。これが運命でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: My friend married the person he was sitting next to on the plane. This must be fate.

examples.japanese: 写真ではイケメンだったのに、実物は全然違うなんて、詐欺でなくてなんだろうか。
examples.english: In the picture, he looks handsome, but the reality is completely different, isn't that a scam?

meaning: must be; is definitely ~
structure: Verb (casual) + の + ではあるまいか | Noun + (なの) | な-adjective + (なの) | い-adjective + の

examples.japanese: この調子なら、今年の売り上げ目標を達成できるのではあるまいか。
examples.english: If this is the case, I wonder if we can reach our sales target this year.

examples.japanese: 天気予報で今日は天気が悪いと言っていたが、雨は降らないのではあるまいか。
examples.english: The weather forecast said that the weather would be bad today, but I wonder if it's not going to rain.

examples.japanese: 道がすごい渋滞だね。約束の時間に間に合わないのではあるまいか。
examples.english: The road is very congested. I wonder if we won't make it in time (to the promised time).

examples.japanese: 100万円宝くじが当たるなんて夢ではあるまいか。
examples.english: Isn't it a dream to win a 1 million yen lottery?

examples.japanese: 上司は僕のチームの意見に反対するのではあるまいか。
examples.english: I wonder if my boss disagrees with my team's opinion.

examples.japanese: 私がノーベル賞をもらえるなんて、夢ではあるまいか。
examples.english: Isn't it a dream that I received the Nobel Prize?

meaning: isn't it; I wonder if it’s not ~
structure: Noun + ではあるまいしでもあるまいしじゃあるまいし

examples.japanese: 子供ではあるまいし、泣くのはやめなさい。
examples.english: Stop crying! You are not a child.

examples.japanese: 新入社員ではあるまいし、基本的なことは説明する必要ないと思います。
examples.english: You're not a new employee, so I don't think I need to explain the basics.

examples.japanese: お金持ちじゃあるまいし、そんな高価なものは買えません。
examples.english: It's not like I'm rich, so I can't buy such an expensive item.

examples.japanese: 一生会えなくなるわけじゃあるまいし、そんなに悲しまないでよ。
examples.english: It's not like you won't be able to meet for the rest of your life, so don't be so sad.

examples.japanese: 面接試験は初めてではあるまいし、どうしてそんなに緊張するの？
examples.english: It’s not like you are having your first interview, so why are you so nervous?

examples.japanese: 夏じゃあるまいし、この冬にTシャツ1枚で外出するなんて、頭がどうかしているよ。
examples.english: You must be crazy going out in the middle of winter in a T-shirt. It's not summer, you know.

meaning: ~ is not enough to solve the problem; cannot be resolved by ~
structure: Verb (casual) + (の) + ではすまないではすまされない | Noun

examples.japanese: このストーリーはただの笑い話では済まされないと思うところがある。
examples.english: I don't think this story is just a funny story.

examples.japanese: どんな言語を学ぶにしても辞書なしでは済まない。
examples.english: Whatever language you study, you cannot do without dictionary.

examples.japanese: あなたが彼女に言ったことは、冗談では済まされない。
examples.english: What you said to her isn’t acceptable as "just a joke".

examples.japanese: 自分にとっては冗談のつもりでも、相手にとっては冗談では済まされない場合もある。
examples.english: There are times where it may just be a joke for you, but it's not a joke for the other person.

examples.japanese: インフルエンザが流行してるこの時期、私たちも他人事では済まされない。
examples.english: At this time of the flu epidemic, we can't ignore it and leave it alone.

examples.japanese: 会社の情報を売ろうとした社員は、処分なしでは済まないでしょう。
examples.english: Employees who intend to sell company information will certainly not get away without being punished.

meaning: it's no use; can't do anything
structure: どうにも + Verb (ない form) | Noun + がない

examples.japanese: こんな蒸し暑い天気は、どうにも我慢できない。
examples.english: I can't stand this humid weather.

examples.japanese: 私はこの場所ではどうにも勉強に集中できない。
examples.english: I cannot concentrate on my studies at all in this place.

examples.japanese: 彼女が亡くなったことをどうにも信じられない。
examples.english: I just can't believe that she passed away.

examples.japanese: 彼の怠惰な性格は、どうにも直しようがない。
examples.english: Nothing can be done to fix his lazy personality.

examples.japanese: その携帯電話はどうにも直しようがないほどに壊れてしまった。
examples.english: The cell phone broke to the point that it couldn't be fixed.

examples.japanese: 彼はどうにも身の置き場がないような様子だ。
examples.english: He seems to have no place for himself.

meaning: as soon as; the moment ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + が早いか

examples.japanese: その人は、信号の色が変わるが早いか、走り出した。
examples.english: That guy ran off as soon as the crosswalk light changed.

examples.japanese: うちの子はいつも学校から帰ってきて、かばんを放り出すが早いか、遊びに行ってしまう。
examples.english: As soon as my child gets home from school, they immediately drop their bag and go off to play.

examples.japanese: 隣席のクラスメイトは、授業の終わりのベルが鳴るが早いか、教室を出て行った。
examples.english: My classmate who sits next to me rushed out of the classroom the instant the bell rang.

examples.japanese: 先生が地震だと叫ぶが早いか、子供たちは机の下に潜り込んだ。
examples.english: The kids crawled under the table as soon as the teacher shouted “Earthquake.”

examples.japanese: 警察に気がつくが早いか、その男はどこかへ向かって走り出した。
examples.english: As soon as he noticed the police, the man started running off somewhere.

examples.japanese: デパートが開店するが早いか、主婦たちが特売場に押し寄せた。
examples.english: As soon as the new department store opened, all of the housewives rushed in for the bargain sales.

meaning: and; and the like; and so forth ~
structure: Noun-1＋が/も＋Noun-1＋なら、Noun-2＋も＋Noun-2＋だ

examples.japanese: 先生が先生なら、学生も学生だ。
examples.english: Like teacher like student. (with a bad teacher like this of course the students are also bad)

examples.japanese: 味が味なら、サービスもサービスだ。
examples.english: With bad taste like this, of course the service is also bad.

examples.japanese: 子供が子供なら、親も親だ。
examples.english: With the kid like this, of course the parents are also bad.

examples.japanese: あのカフェは、味も味なら、サービスもサービスだ。
examples.english: That cafe's food and service are both bad.

examples.japanese: この会社の社員は常識がない。上司が上司なら、部下も部下ですね。
examples.english: The employees at this company have no common sense. If the managers are bad, then the general staff will be too.

examples.japanese: このレストランは店員の態度が悪いし、料理も美味しくない。店員が店員なら、味も味ですね。
examples.english: This restaurant's staff has a poor attitude and the food is not good. With staff like this, of course the food is also no good.

meaning: style; manner; way​
structure: Noun + がましい

examples.japanese: 差し出がましい男だ。
examples.english: He is too forward.

examples.japanese: 彼女は言い訳がましい事は一切言わなかった。
examples.english: She didn't say anything sounding like an excuse.

examples.japanese: 彼は他人がましい振る舞いをする。
examples.english: He behaves like others.

examples.japanese: 言い訳がましいことは言わないほうがカッコいい。
examples.english: It's cooler to not to make excuses.

examples.japanese: 彼女は恩着せがましい態度で僕と踊ってくれた。
examples.english: She danced with me in a gracious manner.

examples.japanese: 彼のこの差し出がましい言葉に僕は気を悪くした。
examples.english: I was offended by his ill-mannered words.

meaning: when; at the time; on the occasion ~
structure: Verb ます (sterm form) + がてら | Noun

examples.japanese: 散歩がてら、コンビニに行ってくるよ。
examples.english: I'm going for a walk and will stop by a convenience store.

examples.japanese: 友達を駅まで送りがてらDVDを返してきた。
examples.english: While I was dropping my friend off at the station, I returned the DVD.

examples.japanese: 遊びがてらお立ち寄りください。
examples.english: Please stop by when you are free

examples.japanese: ちょっと買い物がてら、銀行に寄って記帳してきます。
examples.english: After a little shopping, I will stop by the bank and update my bank book.

examples.japanese: 紅葉を見がてら隣の町まで歩いた。
examples.english: While looking at the autumn leaves, I ended up walking to the next town.

examples.japanese: 今朝にランニングがてら公園の桜を見に行ったが、まだ早かった。
examples.english: I went to see the cherry blossoms in the park while I was running this morning, but it was still too early.

pattern: ごとき / ごとく / ごとし
meaning: altogether; entirely; completely ~
structure: Verb （＋が／かの）(dictionary / た form) + ごとき + nounごとく～（文の途中）ごとし（文の終わり） | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 彼は風のごとく走っています。
examples.english: He is running like the wind.

examples.japanese: 誰も見ていないかのごとく自由に踊りましょう。
examples.english: Let's dance freely as if no one is watching.

examples.japanese: 彼女は水のごとくお金を使う。
examples.english: She spends money like water.

examples.japanese: 彼は何でも知っているかのごとく、いつも自信を持って話す。
examples.english: He always speaks with confidence, as if he knew everything.

examples.japanese: すでに述べたがごとく、この調査方法にはいくつかの問題点がある。
examples.english: As I pointed out earlier, there are a few problems with the method used to conduct this survey.

examples.japanese: 今回のごとき事件は二度と起こしてはいけない。
examples.english: An incident like this one should never happen again.

meaning: completely; entirely; nothing but ~
structure: Noun + ぐるみ

examples.japanese: 私たちは家族ぐるみで仲良くしている。
examples.english: We are close with everyone in our family.

examples.japanese: 町ぐるみで自然環境の保全に努めている。
examples.english: The entire town is striving together to protect its natural environment.

examples.japanese: 彼女とは長年家族ぐるみの付き合いをしている。
examples.english: She and I have been good friends for a long time and so have our families.

examples.japanese: その企業が会社ぐるみで脱税をしてたのが発覚した。
examples.english: That company was caught for doing company-wide tax evasion.

examples.japanese: 子供たちの非行を減らすために、町ぐるみで活動している。
examples.english: We are working throughout the town to reduce children's delinquency.

examples.japanese: 先週にクラスぐるみで京都へ旅行に行った。
examples.english: Last week I went on a trip to Kyoto with my class.

meaning: end up; in the end; as a result (negative)
structure: Verb (dictionary) + 羽目になるハメになる

examples.japanese: 私は歩く時に転んで、入院する羽目になった。
examples.english: I fell while walking and ended up being hospitalized.

examples.japanese: 授業をサボりすぎたので、試験前は徹夜する羽目になりそうだ。
examples.english: Because I skipped class too much, It looks like I will end up staying up all night the day before the exam.

examples.japanese: 急いで家を飛び出して、傘を忘れたので、結局戻る羽目になった。
examples.english: I hurried out of the house and forgot my umbrella, so I ended up having to go back to get it.

examples.japanese: 冬に暖かい格好をしないと,ひどい風邪をひく羽目になる。
examples.english: If you don't dress warmly in winter, you will end up catching a bad cold.

examples.japanese: うっかりしてデータを消してしまったので、もう一度入力する羽目になった。
examples.english: I accidentally deleted the data so I had to input it all in again.

examples.japanese: もしこんなことを続けていたら、彼は刑務所に入る羽目になるぞ。
examples.english: If he keeps continuing like this, he's going to end up in jail.

meaning: rather than (do ...)​
structure: Verb (casual form) + ほうがましだ | Noun + の

examples.japanese: あなたと結婚するくらいなら、独身のほうがましだ。
examples.english: It's better to be single than to marry you.

examples.japanese: ギャンブルに金を浪費するなら捨てたほうがましだ。
examples.english: I would rather throw my money away than waste it on gambling.

examples.japanese: 途中でやめるぐらいなら始めからやらないほうがましだ。
examples.english: If you're going to give up halfway, it's better to not start at all.

examples.japanese: そんな雑誌を読むくらいなら、昼寝をするほうがましだよ。
examples.english: It's better to take a nap than to read such a magazine.

examples.japanese: こんな天気の中を出かけるよりは、家にいるほうがましだ。
examples.english: It's better to stay at home than to go out in this weather.

examples.japanese: これを彼にあげるなら捨ててしまったほうがましだ。
examples.english: I'd rather throw it away than give it to him.

pattern: いかんだ / いかんでは / いかんによっては
meaning: regardless of; whether or not; doesn't matter whether ~
structure: Noun +（の） + いかんだいかんで（は）いかんによっては

examples.japanese: 検査の結果いかんでは、入院もあり得ます。
examples.english: Depending on the result of the test, you may be hospitalized.

examples.japanese: 来月の業績いかんによっては、閉店することも考えている。
examples.english: We are considering closing the store depending on the performance of next month.

examples.japanese: 父は体調いかんでは会社を辞めるかもしれない。
examples.english: My father may quit the company depending on his physical condition.

examples.japanese: 試験に合格できるかどうかは、あなたの努力いかんだよ。
examples.english: Whether you can pass the exam depends on your efforts.

examples.japanese: 台風の状況いかんでは、旅行をキャンセルかもしれません。
examples.english: Depending on the typhoon situation, the trip may be cancelled.

examples.japanese: 試験の結果いかんでは、卒業できない可能性もある。
examples.english: Depending on the test results , you may not be able to graduate。

meaning: any kind of; every; whatsoever; whatever
structure: いかに + Verb | Noun | Adjective

examples.japanese: これがいかに難しいかわかり始めている。
examples.english: I'm starting to see how difficult this is.

examples.japanese: この会合がいかに重要かを彼は全然わかっていない。
examples.english: He has no idea how important this meeting is.

examples.japanese: 彼女の顔を見れば彼女がいかに幸せかがわかった。
examples.english: Looking at her face showed how happy she was.

examples.japanese: 彼は法を守ることはいかに大切かを指摘した。
examples.english: He pointed out how important it is to uphold the law.

examples.japanese: あの人は君の目にいかに映じたか。
examples.english: How has he impressed you?

examples.japanese: 私は教育がいかに重要であるかを痛感しました。
examples.english: I fully realized just how important education is.

meaning: how; in what way; how much; to what extent
structure: いかにも + sentence

examples.japanese: 彼女はいかにも女優です。
examples.english: She is indeed an actress.

examples.japanese: 新しい冷蔵庫はいろいろな機能がついていかにも便利そうだ。
examples.english: The new refrigerator comes with many functions and indeed looks very convenient.

examples.japanese: 彼の質問の仕方は、いかにも報道記者らしかった。
examples.english: His way of asking questions was just like a news reporter.

examples.japanese: 彼はいかにも青年らしく熱心に仕事をする。
examples.english: He devotes himself to his work with all the passion of youth.

examples.japanese: そのゲームはいかにも楽しそうだが、実はとてもつまらないよ。
examples.english: The game indeed sounds fun, but it's actually very boring.

examples.japanese: この大事の場合に彼が怪我をしたのはいかにも残念だ。
examples.english: It's a shame he was injured in this important situation.

pattern: いずれにしても / いずれにしろ / いずれにせよ
meaning: whoever; whatever; however; even ~
structure: いずれにしても + sentence | いずれにしろ | いずれにせよ

examples.japanese: いずれにしてもスケジュールは変更できない。
examples.english: At any rate, we can't change the schedule.

examples.japanese: リスクは低いが、いずれにしても気を付けるに越したことはない。
examples.english: The risk is low, but anyway it's best to be careful.

examples.japanese: いずれにしても、支店長とよく話し合って進めてください。
examples.english: In any case, please discuss it with the branch manager and proceed.

examples.japanese: いずれにしろ、明日は列車に乗りなさい。
examples.english: In any case, please take the train tomorrow.

examples.japanese: いずれにせよ彼が来たら、あなたにお知らせします。
examples.english: Anyway, I'll let you know when he comes.

examples.japanese: このまま続行するかどうか、いずれにせよ今日中に決めなければならない。
examples.english: In any case, we have to decide by the end of today whether or not to continue as is.

meaning: to seem to be; to appear; to behave as ~
structure: Noun + じみた + Noun | じみるじみている

examples.japanese: その男は子供じみたことをしてよく妻を困らせた。
examples.english: The man often annoyed his wife by doing childish things.

examples.japanese: 以前、子供じみた悪ふざけをして友達を泣かせました。
examples.english: I used to make my friends cry by playing childish pranks.

examples.japanese: 先輩は誰かにアドバイスするとき、いつも説教じみている。
examples.english: My senior always sound like they are preaching when they are giving advice.

examples.japanese: 彼はこれらの狂気じみた計画に夢中になりすぎている。
examples.english: He is too absorbed in these crazy-like plans.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分の息子の子供じみた行動に、かなり寛大に対処する。
examples.english: He deals fairly generously with his son's childish behavior.

examples.japanese: あの子はまだ若いのに、どうしてそんな年寄りじみた言い方をするの。
examples.english: That child is still young, so why do they speak in such an old-fashioned way?

meaning: whether [A] or [B]
structure: Verb (casual) + か否か | Noun + である | な-adjective + である | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 私にはそれが真実か否かが分からない。
examples.english: I don't know whether that is true or not.

examples.japanese: 彼が成功するか否かは、彼の努力次第だ。
examples.english: Whether he succeeds or not depends on his efforts.

examples.japanese: 自分の日本語が皆さんに理解されるか否か不安だ。
examples.english: I'm worried whether or not my Japanese will be understood by everyone.

examples.japanese: ダイエット中だけどケーキを食べるか否か迷っている。
examples.english: I'm on a diet now and am struggling with whether or not I should eat cake.

examples.japanese: 私たちは彼が必要であるか否か判断します。
examples.english: We will decide whether he is necessary or not.

examples.japanese: 僕たちは大学へ行くべきか否かを決めかねている。
examples.english: We cannot decide whether we should go to college or not.

meaning: as soon as; the moment ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + （か）と思いきや | Noun + (だ) | な-adjective + (だ) | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: 今日は一日中晴れると思いきや、午後からざあざあ降りになった。
examples.english: I thought it would be sunny all day today, but it started to rain in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: この映画はホラーかと思いきや、実はコメディ映画だった。
examples.english: I thought this movie was a horror movie, but it was actually a comedy movie.

examples.japanese: 宝くじに当たったかと思いきや、番号を見間違えてしまった。
examples.english: I thought I won the lottery, but I had read the number wrong..

examples.japanese: やっと富士山の頂上に着いたと思いきや、まだ8合目だった。
examples.english: I thought I had finally reached the peak of Mt. Fuji, but then realized I was still only at the 8th aid station.

examples.japanese: やっと道路工事が終ったので、これからは静かになるだろうと思いきや、別の工事が始まった。
examples.english: Finally the road construction ended and I thought it would be quiet from now on, but another construction started.

examples.japanese: やっと試験が終わって休めるかと思いきや、宿題をたくさん出されました。
examples.english: I finished my exam and thought I could finally relax, but then got assigned a bunch of homework.

meaning: to think; to feel ~
structure: な-adjective + な + 限りだ | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: 妹の結婚式に出られないとは、残念な限りだ。
examples.english: I feel really bad that I can't attend my younger sister's wedding ceremony..

examples.japanese: 心配していた試験に合格して嬉しい限りだ。
examples.english: I'm so glad that I was able to pass that exam I was so worried about.

examples.japanese: 宝くじに当たったなんて、何とも羨ましい限りだ。
examples.english: I can't believe they hit the lottery... I'm so jealous..

examples.japanese: 年を取って、お金もなく、家族もいないのは、心細い限りです。
examples.english: I feel pretty helpless as I am now old with no family and no money.

examples.japanese: 近所においしいお弁当屋さんができて、一人暮らしの身として嬉しい限りだ。
examples.english: There is a delicious lunch box shop in the neighborhood. For those living alone, they must be very happy.

examples.japanese: この計画を中止しなければならないとは残念な限りだ。
examples.english: If this plan had to be stopped then it would be such a pity.

meaning: although; even though ~
structure: Verb (casual, past)Verb (ます stem) + かいもなく | Noun + の(must be する verb noun)

examples.japanese: 待ったかいもなく、彼はとうとう帰ってこなかった。
examples.english: Even though I waited, he didn’t return.

examples.japanese: 毎日運動したかいもなく、あまり痩せなかった。
examples.english: Even though I’ve been exercising everyday, I didn’t lose much weight.

examples.japanese: 高い薬を飲んだかいもなく病気は治らなかった。
examples.english: Even though I took expensive medicine, my illness did not go away.

examples.japanese: 手術のかいもなく、愛犬が死んでしまった。
examples.english: Even though we tried the surgery, my beloved dog passed away.

examples.japanese: 努力のかいもなく、JLPT N1に合格することができなかった。
examples.english: Despite my best efforts, I could not pass the JLPT N1 exam.

examples.japanese: 予選で落ちてしまい、一生懸命練習したかいもなかった。
examples.english: Failing in the audition round, it was a waste of hard work.

meaning: is not entirely impossible
structure: verb (casual) + 可能性がある | Noun + の

examples.japanese: これをいっぱい食べたら、病気の可能性があるよ。
examples.english: If you eat a lot of this, you may get sick.

examples.japanese: その犬は暴れる可能性がある。
examples.english: There is a possibility that the dog will be violent.

examples.japanese: それは今後増える可能性があります。
examples.english: There's a possibility that will increase from now on.

examples.japanese: このニュースレターを受け取った可能性があるのは誰ですか。
examples.english: Who might have received this news letter?

examples.japanese: 私はあなたにもその可能性があると思います。
examples.english: I think that you have that potential in you too.

examples.japanese: あの行動が無駄になる可能性がある。
examples.english: There is a possibility that action will go to waste.

meaning: both ... and; not only ... also; whether it be ... or ~
structure: い-adjective い + かれ + い-adjective い + かれ

examples.japanese: この番組も、遅かれ早かれ視聴者に飽きられるだろう。
examples.english: People will sooner or later become tired of this program, too.

examples.japanese: 人は多かれ少なかれ、悩みをもっているものだ。
examples.english: More or less, everyone has something they are worried about.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事で遅かれ早かれ成功する見込みがある。
examples.english: He is likely to succeed at work sooner or later.

examples.japanese: 子どもは良かれ悪しかれ親から影響を受けて育ちます。
examples.english: Children, for better or for worse, are influenced by their parents.

examples.japanese: 緊張して失敗した経験は多かれ少なかれ誰にでもあるのではないだろうか。
examples.english: Perhaps everyone has more or less experienced the feeling of failing from being nervous.

examples.japanese: 若い女性なら、多かれ少なかれセクハラを経験したことがあるだろう。
examples.english: Every young women has experienced sexual harassment of some sort.

meaning: beforehand; in advance; previously​
structure: かつて + sentence

examples.japanese: 彼女はフランスにかつて住んでいた。
examples.english: She once lived in France.

examples.japanese: ロンドンはかつて霧で有名だった。
examples.english: London was once famous for its fog.

examples.japanese: 京都はかつて日本の首都でした。
examples.english: Kyoto was once the capital of Japan.

examples.japanese: かつて彼はそこで父に会った。
examples.english: Once he met his father there.

examples.japanese: 彼はかつて事故を起こしそうになった。
examples.english: He was once about to have an accident.

examples.japanese: 私はかつてある手術をうけたことがあった。
examples.english: I have had surgery before.

meaning: there is a limit to what is acceptable; to go too far
structure: Verb (casual form) + 嫌いがある | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 彼は物事を少しすぎる嫌いがある。
examples.english: He tends to take things too seriously.

examples.japanese: 彼女は面接の時に緊張する嫌いがある。
examples.english: She has a bad habit of getting nervous during an interview.

examples.japanese: この頃の若者は協調性に欠ける嫌いがある。
examples.english: Young people these days tend to lack the ability to work well with others.

examples.japanese: 最近の子供はスマホやゲームの影響で夜遅くまで起きる嫌いがある。
examples.english: Children these days tend to stay up late into the night due to the effects of playing games or using smartphones.

examples.japanese: うちの部長は自分と違う考え方を認めようとしない嫌いがある。
examples.english: My manager tends to refuse to accept opinions different from their own.

examples.japanese: 話をおもしろくするためだろうか、彼はものごとを大げさに言う嫌いがある。
examples.english: Perhaps to make the story interesting, he tends to exaggerate.

meaning: one after another; starting with ~
structure: Verb (ば conditional) + きりがない | Verb (たら conditionarl) | Verb (dictionary) + と

examples.japanese: 彼女との思い出は語り出したら切りがない。
examples.english: My memories with her are endless.

examples.japanese: 彼の欠点を数えれば切りがない。
examples.english: There is no end to his shortcomings.

examples.japanese: 日本戦争に関する本は数え上げたら切りがない。
examples.english: There are countless books on Japanese wars.

examples.japanese: 彼がいったん不平を言い始めると切りがない。
examples.english: Once he starts complaining, there is no end to it.

examples.japanese: 欲を言えば切りがないから、このマンションに決めよう。
examples.english: There is no end to what we want, so let's just decide on this condominium.

examples.japanese: 悩み出したら切りがないので、途中で吹っ切れることも重要だ。
examples.english: If you start to worry, there is no end to it, so it is important to overcome it on the way.

meaning: utmost; extremely ~
structure: Noun + きっての + Noun

examples.japanese: 彼はうちの大学きっての秀才だ。
examples.english: He is the most talented person in our university.

examples.japanese: 彼女はこの会社きっての美人です。
examples.english: She is the most beautiful woman in this company.

examples.japanese: そのグループきっての人気アイドルは田中さんです。
examples.english: The most popular idol in that group is Tanaka.

examples.japanese: 清水寺は京都きっての観光名所だ。
examples.english: Kiyomizu temple is one of the best tourist attractions in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: あのレストランは現在にも大阪きっての名料亭である。
examples.english: Still today, that restaurant is one of the best restaurants in Osaka.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本の芸能界きっての高い給料を貰った人です。
examples.english: He is the highest paid person in the Japanese entertainment industry.

meaning: although; even though ~
structure: Noun + こそ + ～が… | ～けれど…

examples.japanese: この生徒は字こそ汚いが、いい文章を書く。
examples.english: This student's handwriting is difficult to read, but their story is good.

examples.japanese: あの男は有名な大学こそ通学するが、実は何も知らないよ。
examples.english: That guy goes to a famous university, but he doesn't really know anything.

examples.japanese: この携帯電話は形こそいいですが、値段がちょっと高いです。
examples.english: This cell phone has a nice shape, but it's a little expensive.

examples.japanese: この本は表紙こそ目立つだが、大した内容でもなくてつまらないんだ。
examples.english: This book has an eye-catching cover, but the content is nothing special and rather boring.

examples.japanese: 彼女は指導者でこそあるが、責任はまったくない。
examples.english: She is a leader, but she has absolutely no responsibility.

examples.japanese: そのキノコは色と形こそ奇麗だが、毒があって食べると病気になりますよ。
examples.english: The color and shape of that mushroom is beautiful, but it is poisonous and you will get sick if you eat it.

meaning: like; as if; the same as ~
structure: ことごとく + VerbAdjective (limited)

examples.japanese: 生徒はことごとく知っている。
examples.english: I know each and every student.

examples.japanese: 本の内容はことごとく新しい。
examples.english: The contents of the book are entirely new.

examples.japanese: 私達の計画はことごとく失敗した。
examples.english: All our plans have completely failed.

examples.japanese: 彼は彼女の要求にはことごとく応じる。
examples.english: He responds to all her requests.

examples.japanese: 彼女はスーパースターの特徴をことごとく備えている。
examples.english: She has all the characteristics of a superstar.

examples.japanese: 彼は文法をことごとく無視している。
examples.english: He ignores all grammar.

pattern: ことこの上ない / この上ない / この上なく
meaning: the most / greatest … of all
structure: この上ない + Noun | この上なく + な-adjectiveい-adjective | な-adjective + な/である + ことこの上ない | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: この上なく幸せだ。
examples.english: I have never been happier.

examples.japanese: 私はそれがこの上なく好きです。
examples.english: I like that the most.

examples.japanese: 子猫は可愛いことこの上ないものだ。
examples.english: There's nothing cuter than a kitten.

examples.japanese: N１の文法は複雑なことこの上ない。
examples.english: The grammar of N1 is the most complicated.

examples.japanese: おばあちゃんが亡くなって、この上ない悲しさを味わった。
examples.english: My grandmother passed away and I felt the utmost sadness.

examples.japanese: 外国に住んでいるときに、家族を懐かしんで、寂しいことこの上ないものだ。
examples.english: There is nothing more lonely than missing family while living abroad.

meaning: to be forced to do something because one has no other choice
structure: Verb (casual) + こともあって | Noun + という | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 今日は天気がいいこともあって、公園にたくさん人が来ている。
examples.english: Many people are coming to the park today, partly because of the good weather.

examples.japanese: ちょうど受験前ということもあって、息子はピリピリしている。
examples.english: Partly because the exam is coming up, my son is very nervous.

examples.japanese: 昨日は初めて会議の司会ということもあって、とても緊張した。
examples.english: I was very nervous yesterday, partly because I was the host of the meeting for the first time.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語ができることもあって、外国人の友達も多い。
examples.english: She can speak English among other things and has many foreign friends.

examples.japanese: 脚本があまりよくなかったこともあって、このドラマの視聴率は低かった。
examples.english: The audience rating of this drama was low, partly because the script was not very good.

examples.japanese: 母が病気になったこともあって, 今年は外国へ行かないことにした。
examples.english: I decided not to go abroad this year, partly because my mother got sick.

meaning: there's no need to; it’s not necessary to ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことのないよう（に）ことがないよう（に）

examples.japanese: 道に迷うことのないように、グーグルマップで場所を確かめておいた。
examples.english: In order to not get lost, I checked the location on Google Maps.

examples.japanese: 読書で目を使い過ぎることのないようにしなさい。
examples.english: Make sure you don't overwork your eyes by reading too much.

examples.japanese: 思い残すことのないように、今を全力で生きる。
examples.english: In order to not have any regrets, I live now to the fullest.

examples.japanese: 災害が来ても慌てることのないよう、日頃から準備しておこう。
examples.english: We should be more generally prepared for a disaster so that we do not panic when it happens.

examples.japanese: 二度とこのような事故が起きることのないよう、安全対策を講じます。
examples.english: We will come up with a safety strategy to ensure that this kind of accident never happens again.

examples.japanese: 今後、二度と同じことが起きることがないよう、努力いたします。
examples.english: I will work hard to ensure something like this doesn't happen again.

meaning: rather than (do ...)​
structure: Noun + くらいぐらい + のものだなものだ

examples.japanese: 息子が電話をよこすのは、お金に困った時ぐらいのものだ。
examples.english: My son only calls me when he needs money.

examples.japanese: そんな事をするのは君くらいのものだ。
examples.english: No one but you would do such a thing.

examples.japanese: 仕事が忙しくて、ゆっくりできるのは週末ぐらいのものだ。
examples.english: I'm busy with work and can only relax on weekends.

examples.japanese: あの学校は生徒が四五百くらいのものだ。
examples.english: The school has not more than four or five hundred students.

examples.japanese: 彼女が仕事を辞めないように説得できるのは、君ぐらいのものだ。
examples.english: You're the only one who can convince her to not quit her job.

examples.japanese: 私たちが買える家は、これぐらいのものだ。
examples.english: The only house we can buy is one like this.

pattern: までだ / までのことだ
meaning: not to say; although it does not reach the level of ~
structure: Verb (casual) + まで（のこと）だ | それ + までだ | これ

examples.japanese: ちょっと聞いてみたまでだ。
examples.english: I just wanted to ask (there's nothing else to it)

examples.japanese: この値段まで安くしてくれないなら、今回の契約をキャンセルするまでのことだ。
examples.english: If you won't lower the price, then I will just cancel the next contract.

examples.japanese: 誰も手伝ってくれないのなら、自分一人でやるまでのことです。
examples.english: If no one is willing to help you, then you can just do it by yourself.

examples.japanese: 給料が下がるなら、会社を辞めるまでです。
examples.english: If my salary is just going to get lower, I have no choice but to quit.

examples.japanese: 妻が反対だと言えば、諦めるまでです。
examples.english: If my wife is going to disagree, then I'll have no choice but to give up.

examples.japanese: 風邪をひいたら、すべての予定を取りやめて寝るまでだ。
examples.english: If you catch a cold, you just have to cancel all your appointments and get some rest.

meaning: must not; should not; do not ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + まじき | Noun + にある/としてある

examples.japanese: 生徒に暴力を振るなんて、先生としてあるまじき行為だ。
examples.english: Violence against students is something a teacher absolutely should not do

examples.japanese: 他の人の案を盗むなんて許すまじきことだ。
examples.english: Stealing someone else's ideas is an unforgivable behavior.

examples.japanese: 彼のやったことは、人としてあるまじき残酷な行為だ。
examples.english: What he did was a cruel and unacceptable action for a human being.

examples.japanese: 試験中にカンニングのような許すまじき行為をする人は０点にします。
examples.english: Those who do unforgivable acts such as cheating during the exam will be given 0 points.

examples.japanese: 学生を恐喝するとは、教師にあるまじき行為だ。
examples.english: It is totally unacceptable for a teacher to blackmail students.

examples.japanese: 弱い者をだましてお金を取るなど、人間にあるまじき行為だ。
examples.english: Things like deceiving the weak and taking their money is not something humans should do.

meaning: should do, but don't; absolutely not; there's no way ~
structure: まるっきり + Verb | Noun

examples.japanese: これは私の欲しいものとまるっきり反対だ。
examples.english: This is exactly the opposite of what I want.

examples.japanese: 彼はオペラについてまるっきり知らない。
examples.english: He doesn't know anything about opera.

examples.japanese: 翻訳の仕事はまるっきり初めてなので、いろいろ教えてください。
examples.english: This is my very first time working as a translator, so please teach me various things.

examples.japanese: 私は英語がまるっきり話せませんが、秘書は大丈夫です。
examples.english: I can't speak English at all, but my secretary is fine.

examples.japanese: あなたは私の言うことなんかまるっきり信じてないんでしょう?
examples.english: You don't really believe what I say, right?

examples.japanese: JLPTの試験が終わると、日本語の勉強する気がまるっきりなくなってしまった。
examples.english: After the JLPT exam, I completely lost the desire to study Japanese.
