meaning: at the same time as; while; simultaneously ~
structure: Verb (た / ない) +も + 同然 + だ/の | Noun+ (も)

examples.japanese: 友達ですが、子供の頃からずっとそばにいるので兄弟も同然です。
examples.english: He is my friend, but we have always been together since our childhood so he is just like my brother.

examples.japanese: この車は中古車といっても新品も同然だ。
examples.english: Although this is a used car, it is almost as good as a new one.

examples.japanese: 目標がないなら死んだも同然だ。
examples.english: Having no goals is just like being dead.

examples.japanese: 社会人になったけど、毎日試験の勉強をしているので、学生同然の生活だ。
examples.english: I became a working adult, but every day I am studying for exams so my life is just like a student's.

examples.japanese: 彼女は料理が上手で、プロ同然といっても過言ではない。
examples.english: She's good at cooking, and it's no exaggeration to say she's at a professional level.

examples.japanese: 彼女と2年間一緒に住んでいたから、これは結婚生活も同然だ。
examples.english: I lived together with my girlfriend for 2 years, so it's just like married life.

meaning: not in the least; nothing like that
structure: Noun + もさることながら

examples.japanese: 彼女は外見もさることながら性格もとてもいいです。
examples.english: Of course she looks very nice, but her personality is also very good.

examples.japanese: 試合に勝つには選手の実力もさることながら、運も必要なのだ。
examples.english: Winning the match is not only based on the ability of the players, but luck is also essential.

examples.japanese: このカメラは、価格もさることながら、デザインもよいので人気がある。
examples.english: This camera is popular because of it's price, but it's design is also very good.

examples.japanese: 最近は忙しすぎて、疲労もさることながら、ストレスもピークに達している。
examples.english: Recently, I've been so busy that I'm not only tired but also very stressed.

examples.japanese: この映画は話の内容もさることながら映像の美しさも評判がいい。
examples.english: This movie has a good reputation not only for the content of the story but also for the beauty of the footage.

examples.japanese: あの男はビジネスの知識もさることながら、プレゼンのスキルも非常に高い。
examples.english: Not only does that man have general business knowledge, but his presentation skill is extremely high.

meaning: ended up not doing ~
structure: Verb (stem form) ます + もしないで

examples.japanese: 彼女は、いつもやりもしないで、できないと言う。
examples.english: She always gives up before she even tries.

examples.japanese: 食べもしないで、まずいかどうかなんてわからないでしょ。
examples.english: You can't know if it's bad or not without eating it first, right?

examples.japanese: 食事もしないでゲームばかりしていると、病気になるよ。
examples.english: If you just play games without eating anything, you will get sick.

examples.japanese: 知りもしないで偉そうなことを言うな。
examples.english: Don't act like you're an expert when you don't know much about it.

examples.japanese: 彼は授業に遅れてきたのに謝りもしないで席に着いた。
examples.english: Although he was late for class, he took his seat without apologizing.

examples.japanese: 気持ちを相手に伝えもしないで、自分のことを解ってほしいって無理でしょ。
examples.english: You can't expect people to understand you without telling them how you feel.

meaning: long ago; already; a long time ago
structure: もはや + sentence

examples.japanese: もはや意味はありません。
examples.english: It's meaningless now.

examples.japanese: 彼はもはやここでは働いていません。
examples.english: He is no longer working here.

examples.japanese: 彼らにはもはや時間がない。
examples.english: They no longer have time.

examples.japanese: その規則はもはや効力がない。
examples.english: That rule is no longer in effect.

examples.japanese: もはや彼の言うことを信じない。
examples.english: I don't believe him anymore.

examples.japanese: もはやそれに関して私にできることは何もない。
examples.english: There is nothing I can do about it anymore.

meaning: speaking of; I told you already; come on (annoyance / dissatisfaction)
structure: Verb (casual) + ものを | な-adjective | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: お金が無いなら、言ってくれたらよかったものを。
examples.english: I wish you had told me you didn't have any money.

examples.japanese: ちょっと知らせてくれたらいいものを。
examples.english: I wish you had notified me.

examples.japanese: 黙っていればいいものを、つい余計なことを言ってしまった。
examples.english: I ended up saying something unnecessary and regret not keeping my mouth shut.

examples.japanese: もう少し頑張れば合格するものを、惜しかったね。
examples.english: If only you worked a little harder, you would've passed. You were really close.

examples.japanese: やればできるものを、なんでやらないの？
examples.english: If only you tried you could do it, so why don't you?

examples.japanese: 黙っていればバレなかったものを、どうして言っちゃうかなあ。
examples.english: If only they had kept their mouth shut, no one would have found out. I wonder why they talked about it?

pattern: ものと思われる / ものと見られる
meaning: as soon as one realizes ..., then ~
structure: Verb (casual) + （もの）と思われる（もの）と見られる | Noun +（だ） | な-adjective | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: この店のパスタは冷凍したものと思われる。
examples.english: The pasta in this shop is supposedly frozen.

examples.japanese: 日本の少子化問題はさらに進むと見られている。
examples.english: The problem of Japan's declining birthrate is expected to go further.

examples.japanese: 彼は、今一番人気のあるアイドルだと見られている。
examples.english: He is believed to be the most popular idol right now.

examples.japanese: 兄の普段の成績から、合格は間違いないと見られている。
examples.english: From his brother's usual grades, it is believed that he will pass.

examples.japanese: 愛知県では、今後も大きいな地震が来ると思われている。
examples.english: It is expected that a large earthquake will occur in Aichi Prefecture.

examples.japanese: あの事件は事故ではなく、殺人である可能性が高いと見られている。
examples.english: It is believed that the incident was likely a murder, not an accident.

meaning: to assume; to suppose; on the presumption that ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + ものとする

examples.japanese: 第５条議長は全会議を主宰するものとする。
examples.english: Article 5. The president shall preside at all meetings.

examples.japanese: 科料は2万円を超えないものとする。
examples.english: The fine shall not exceed 20,000 yen.

examples.japanese: 契約の延長は、双方の同意によるものとする。
examples.english: The contract extension must be agreed by both parties.

examples.japanese: 住所変更の通知は、その到達によって効力が発生するものとする 。
examples.english: Notice of a change of address shall be effective only upon receipt of concerned parties.

examples.japanese: 委員会の決定は，その委員の過半数によるものとする。
examples.english: The board shall take its decisions by majority.

examples.japanese: 商標は，登録した後に公告するものとする。
examples.english: The trade mark shall be published after registration.

meaning: shall; to assume; understood as ~
structure: Verb (casual form) + ものとして

examples.japanese: スミスさんはもう来ないものとして、始めましょう。
examples.english: Let's assume Mr. Smith is not coming and get started.

examples.japanese: 何も知らないものとして説明してください。
examples.english: Please explain it to me as though I know nothing.

examples.japanese: 予算はそれしかないものとして準備してくれ。
examples.english: Please make preparations under the assumption that this is all the budget we have.

examples.japanese: 私はいないものとして、授業を続いてください。
examples.english: Please continue the lesson as though I were not here.

examples.japanese: 初級漢字は出来るものとして、中級漢字のクラスを取った。
examples.english: I took the mid-level kanji class assuming I understood basic kanji.

examples.japanese: たぶん行けないと思うので、私はいないものとして、話を進めてください。
examples.english: I don't think I will be able to go, so please continue the talk assuming I will not be there.

meaning: otherwise; or else; if not ~
structure: Noun + もしくは + Noun

examples.japanese: 遅刻するの場合は先生もしくは僕に連絡してください。
examples.english: If you are late, please contact your teacher or me.

examples.japanese: お問い合わせは、電話もしくはファックスでお願いします。
examples.english: For inquiries, please contact us by phone or fax.

examples.japanese: あの男は弁護士もしくは裁判官ですか。
examples.english: Is that man a lawyer or a judge?

examples.japanese: 参加費はクレジットカードもしくは現金で払うことができます。
examples.english: The participation fee can be paid by credit card or by cash.

examples.japanese: この施設は、会員もしくはその家族に限り使用できる。
examples.english: This facility can only be used by members or their families.

examples.japanese: 明日は社長もしくは部長が新計画を発表なさります。
examples.english: Tomorrow, the president or general manager will announce a new plan.

meaning: as if to say; as though~
structure: Verb (ない root) ない + んばかり（に）んばかりの + Noun | Exception : しない -> せん

examples.japanese: 川の水が溢れんばかりになっている。
examples.english: The river is about to flood.

examples.japanese: 彼女は泣き出さんばかりの顔をして、私に助けを求めてきた。
examples.english: She came to me for help looking as though she was about to cry.

examples.japanese: 行きたかった大学に合格した息子は、飛び上がらんばかりに喜んでいた。
examples.english: My son passed the entrance exam to his target university. He was as happy as if he could fly.

examples.japanese: 絶対に許さないと言わんばかりの顔で睨んでいる。
examples.english: He glared with an expression as if to say that he would absolutely not forgive them.

examples.japanese: 彼女のスピーチが終わると、割れんばかりの拍手が沸き起こった。
examples.english: After her speech ended, the sound of the applause sounded like it was about to break the entire hall.

examples.japanese: ずっと夜勤で、三日間何も食べずに寝んばかりのしんどい顔をしていた。
examples.english: I've constantly been working night shifts and so my face looked as though I hadn't slept or ate for 3 days.

meaning: as if; as though ~
structure: Verb (ない root) ない + んがため（に）んがための + Noun | Exception : しない -> せん

examples.japanese: 一人の青年がおぼれている子供を救わんがために、川に飛び込んだ。
examples.english: A young man jumped into a river in order to save a drowning child.

examples.japanese: 来年、自分のレストランを開店せんがために、今一生懸命お金をためている。
examples.english: I'm doing my best to save money now in order to open my own restaurant next year.

examples.japanese: 選手達は金メダルを取らんがために、寝る時間も惜しんで練習に励む。
examples.english: The athletes spare no time to sleep and practice hard in order to win the gold medal.

examples.japanese: 彼はお金をもうけんがために、ずいぶん酷いことをやってきた。
examples.english: He has done a lot of terrible things in order to make money.

examples.japanese: 自分の利益を得んがための発言では、人の心を動かせない。
examples.english: Words that are only for one's personal benefit cannot move people's hearts.

examples.japanese: お母さんの手術を払わんがために、私は同時にいろいろな仕事をします。
examples.english: I juggle a lot of different work at the same time in order to pay for my mom's surgery.

meaning: only; just; nothing else
structure: Verb (ない form) + までも

examples.japanese: 暑いと言わないまでも、暖かい。
examples.english: It's not enough to say it's hot, but it is warm.

examples.japanese: 彼女はけちとは言わないまでも、とてもつましい。
examples.english: She is very frugal, not to say stingy.

examples.japanese: 電話をしないまでもメッセージぐらいをしてください。
examples.english: You don't need to call, but at least send a message.

examples.japanese: プロになれないまでも、サイクリングのレースに出るつもりだ。
examples.english: Although I cannot become a pro, I plan to enter more cycling races.

examples.japanese: 毎月帰ってこいとは言わないまでも、たまには顔を見せて欲しい。
examples.english: I'm not telling you to come home every month, but at least I would like to see your face every once in a while.

examples.japanese: 毎日はしないまでも、週に１回くらいは部屋の掃除をしましょう。
examples.english: Not to say I clean my room every day, but I try to do it at least once a week.

meaning: only (emphasis)
structure: Verb (ない form) + （もの）でもない

examples.japanese: あなたが本気で勉強すれば、半年でN1合格をできないものでもない。
examples.english: If you study hard, it's not impossible to pass N1 in half a year.

examples.japanese: 今すぐに家を出れば、コンサートに間に合わないものでもない。
examples.english: You may be able to make it in time for the concert if you leave the house right now.

examples.japanese: 今から皆で頑張れば、この提案は成立しないものでもない。
examples.english: If we all do our best from now on, this proposal may not be unsuccessful.

examples.japanese: 条件によってはその仕事を引き受けないものでもない。
examples.english: I may be willing to take the work on depending on the conditions.

examples.japanese: 私はそのシステムを作れないものでもないですが、お金と時間がかかります。
examples.english: It's not that I can't make that system, but it costs money and time.

examples.japanese: ここからタクシーに乗れば、フライトの時間に間に合わないものでもない。
examples.english: If you take a taxi from here, it may not be too late to make your flight on time.

pattern: ないものか / ないものだろうか
meaning: to think; to suppose; it is believed/expected that ~
structure: Verb (ない form) + ものかものだろうか

examples.japanese: あなたがもう少し分かりやすく話せないものか。
examples.english: Can't you make it a little easier to understand?

examples.japanese: この橋は早く完成しないものか。
examples.english: Can't this bridge be finished soon?

examples.japanese: この匂いはなんとかならないものか。
examples.english: Can't we do anything about this smell?

examples.japanese: デジカメが壊れた。何とか直らないものだろうか。
examples.english: The digital camera is broken. Can anything be done to fix it?

examples.japanese: 子どもに野菜を食べてもらう良い方法がないものだろうか。
examples.english: Isn't there a good way to get kids to eat vegetables?

examples.japanese: 簡単にお金が手に入る方法がないものか、といつも思っています。
examples.english: I'm always wondering about "isn't there an easier way to get money".

meaning: (1) surely..., but ~; although... is likely, ~ (2) should have (regret); might / must have been ~
structure: Verb (ない form) + とも限らない

examples.japanese: 間違えないとも限らないので、もう一度確認した方がいい。
examples.english: It's possible that there may be a mistake, so you should double check.

examples.japanese: 日本の電車がいくら時間に正確だと言っても、遅れないとも限りませんよ。
examples.english: No matter how punctual a Japanese train may be, it doesn't mean that it will never be late.

examples.japanese: 今日は雨が降らないとも限らない、傘を持って行ったほうがいい。
examples.english: I can't say for sure that it won't rain today, so you had best bring an umbrella.

examples.japanese: しっかり鍵をかけないと、泥棒に入られないとも限らない。
examples.english: If you don’t lock the door properly, a thief might get in.

examples.japanese: 練習ではいつも完璧だったとしても、試験では失敗しないとも限らない。
examples.english: Even if you practice flawlessly, that doesn't guarantee you won't fail the exam.

examples.japanese: いつ何が起こらないとも限らないので、保険にはちゃんと入っておこう。
examples.english: There is a chance that something may happen at any time, so let's be sure to buy insurance.

meaning: somehow; without knowing; without thinking; unconsciously​ ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + こと + なくして（は） | Noun

examples.japanese: 努力なくしては成功などあり得ない。
examples.english: Success is not possible without effort.

examples.japanese: 私は辞書なくしては、この本が読めません。
examples.english: I can't read this book without a dictionary.

examples.japanese: 私は彼女なくしては生きていけない。
examples.english: I cannot go on living without her.

examples.japanese: パスポートなくしては、海外へ行くことはできません。
examples.english: Without a passport, one cannot travel abroad.

examples.japanese: この問題の解決なくして、我が社の未来はない。
examples.english: Without an answer to this problem, there is no future for our company.

examples.japanese: 健康な体なくしてどんなにお金があっても幸せとは言えない。
examples.english: It doesn't matter how much money one has, they cannot be happy without a healthy body.

meaning: completely; entirely; nothing but ~
structure: Usage 1 + Noun + 並み（に） | Usage 2 + 並みの + Noun

examples.japanese: 君の料理はプロ並みだ。
examples.english: Your cooking is like a professional.

examples.japanese: 彼女の歌はプロ並みに上手だ。
examples.english: Her songs are as good as a professional.

examples.japanese: 彼女は日本人並みに日本語が上手だ。
examples.english: She speaks Japanese as good as a Japanese person does.

examples.japanese: あの子は大人並みに漢字をよく知っている。
examples.english: That kid knows as much kanji as an adult does.

examples.japanese: 英語の先生としては世間並みだ。
examples.english: As an English teacher, they are average.

examples.japanese: 僕も人間並みに風邪を引いた。
examples.english: I guess I am human after all since I caught a cold.

pattern: なんという / なんと / なんて
meaning: not in the least; nothing like that
structure: なんという + Noun + だ / か / だろうなのだろうなんだろう | な-adj | なんとなんて + Noun + なん/の + だろう | な-adj + なん/の | い-adj + の

examples.japanese: ここからの景色、なんて綺麗なんだろう。
examples.english: What a beautiful view from here!

examples.japanese: 彼女は軽く触られても大きく叫んだ。なんという敏感な人だ。
examples.english: She shouted loudly when touched lightly. What a sensitive person.

examples.japanese: あいつは雷の音でも怖がっている。なんという臆病な人だ。
examples.english: He is scared even by the sound of thunder. What a timid person he is!

examples.japanese: 彼は一人で冷蔵庫を運んでしまって。なんという凄い力だ。
examples.english: He carried the refrigerator all by himself. What a great power he has!

examples.japanese: こんな安い給料で真面目に働く彼はなんてバカらしい。
examples.english: How stupid he is to work seriously with such a low salary.

examples.japanese: 津波が来て、彼は妻と子供を残して自分が先逃げ。なんという悲劇だろうか。
examples.english: When the tsunami came, he left his wife and children and escaped first. What a tragedy!

meaning: [A] or [B] or something; for instance ~
structure: 何しろ + sentence

examples.japanese: 僕はお腹がすいたよ。何しろ朝からご飯を食べていないからね。
examples.english: I'm hungry. After all, I haven't eaten anything since morning.

examples.japanese: 彼女はうまくできなかったが、何しろ初めてのことだったからね。
examples.english: She didn't do well, but anyway that's because that was her first time.

examples.japanese: 何しろ僕たちには不思議に似たところがある。
examples.english: At any rate, there are strange similarities between us.

examples.japanese: 部屋の掃除が大変だ。何しろとても広いからね。
examples.english: It’s hard to clean up this room since as you know it’s very spacious.

examples.japanese: どこにも異常はないかもしれないが、何しろ大至急検査をしてみる必要がある。
examples.english: There may not be any abnormalities anywhere, but in any case it is necessary to carry out an inspection as soon as possible.

examples.japanese: 私たちの部は今とても忙しいんですよ。何しろオリンピックの準備がたくさんあります。
examples.english: Our department is very busy right now. After all, there is a lot of preparation for the Olympics.

meaning: at least; even just a little (adverbial particle)
structure: Noun + ならでは

examples.japanese: 納豆は日本ならではの食べ物だ。
examples.english: Natto is a food distinctive of Japan.

examples.japanese: それはあなたならではの発想です。
examples.english: That is something only you would be able to think of.

examples.japanese: 彼ならではとてもこの仕事は扱えない。
examples.english: There is no one who I can entrust this job to other than you.

examples.japanese: これは当店ならではの特別価格です。
examples.english: This is a special price that is only offered in this store.

examples.japanese: このような習慣があるのは、この地方ならではです。
examples.english: This kind of custom is unique to this region.

examples.japanese: 桜の木の下で酒を飲んで歌を歌う。日本ならではのお花見の風景だ。
examples.english: Drinking alcohol under the cherry blossom trees. This "cherry blossom viewing" is unique to Japanese culture.

pattern: ならいざしらず / はいざしらず
meaning: anyhow; anyway; regardless; in any case; whether or not ~
structure: Noun + ならいざしらずはいざしらず

examples.japanese: 10年前ならいざ知らず、今時、テレビを持っていない人は珍しい
examples.english: I didn't know about 10 years ago, but today people without a TV are rare.

examples.japanese: 他の人ならいざ知らず、私はそんなことができない。
examples.english: I don't know about others, but I can't do it.

examples.japanese: 外国はいざ知らず、それは我が国では法律で禁止されている。
examples.english: I don't know about other countries, but it is prohibited by law in our country.

examples.japanese: 一週間の旅行はいざ知らず、日帰り旅行にはそんな大きなかばんは要らない。
examples.english: I don't know about a week's travel, but for a day trip, you don't need such a big bag.

examples.japanese: 初めてとか２回目ならいざ知らず、経験者が失敗するのは許されない。
examples.english: If it's the first time or the second time that's different, but it's unforgivable for an experienced person to fail.

examples.japanese: 6歳の子供ならいざ知らず、大人がこんなことをしらないなんておかしい。
examples.english: It's one thing for a 6-year-old child, but it's strange for an adult to not know this.

meaning: at least; even just a little (adverbial particle)
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + なり

examples.japanese: 家を出るなり、雨が降りだした。
examples.english: It started raining as soon as I left the house.

examples.japanese: 窓を開けるなり、変な虫が入ってきた。
examples.english: As soon as I opened the window, some strange bug entered the room.

examples.japanese: 赤ん坊は、私の顔を見るなり、大声で泣き出した。
examples.english: Once the baby saw my face, it started crying.

examples.japanese: 入ってくるなり、彼は倒れた。
examples.english: The instant he came in, he fell down.

examples.japanese: うちの息子は学校から帰るなり、パソコンばっかり。
examples.english: Once our son returns from school, all he does is use the computer.

examples.japanese: 彼の姿を見るなり私は恐怖で震えた。
examples.english: I trembled with fear from the moment I saw him.

meaning: as soon as; right after ~
structure: Verb + なりになりの + Noun | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 初心者なりによくやった。
examples.english: He did well for a beginner.

examples.japanese: 私なりに頑張ったつもりだったが、結果はダメだった。
examples.english: I planned to give it my best in my own way, but the result was not good.

examples.japanese: 自分なりの魅力を出したい。
examples.english: I want to show my own appeal in my own way.

examples.japanese: 彼は足が遅いが、遅いなりに全力で走った。
examples.english: Although he is slow, he ran giving his best effort.

examples.japanese: 山田は彼なりに良いやつだ。
examples.english: In his own way, Yamada is a pretty good guy.

examples.japanese: 先輩が会社を辞めた理由は私なりに理解しています。
examples.english: I think I understand why my senior quit his job.

meaning: as soon as; right after ~
structure: NounAdverb + なりとも

examples.japanese: 誰なりとも連れて来い。
examples.english: Bring anyone you'd like.

examples.japanese: ちょっとなりとも会いたい。
examples.english: I would like to see him, even if just for a while.

examples.japanese: 写真なりとも見たい。
examples.english: I would like to see at least a photo of him.

examples.japanese: 何なりともご遠慮無く召し上がれ。
examples.english: Please help yourself to anything you like.

examples.japanese: わずかなりともお役に立てるのであれば、喜んでお手伝いいたします。
examples.english: I would be glad to help, even though I may only be of little use..

examples.japanese: チャンスがあるなら、一目なりとも会ってみたい。
examples.english: If there's a chance to see them, then I'd love to! Even if it's just a glance.

meaning: pattern to give two representative examples (usually negative)
structure: Noun-1 + なり + Noun-2 + なり | Verb-1(dictionary form) + Verb-2(dictionary form)

examples.japanese: どうせ暇なら、掃除なり洗濯なりしてくれない？
examples.english: Since you have nothing to do, could you please help with the cleaning or laundry?

examples.japanese: メールなり電話なりで、彼女に連絡してください。
examples.english: Please get in touch with her by e-mail or phone.

examples.japanese: 顔色が悪いですよ。座るなり横になるなり、楽にしてください。
examples.english: You're face is pretty pale. Please sit down or lay down, whatever makes you comfortable.

examples.japanese: 休みで仕事がないなら、掃除するなり洗濯するなり、家事を手伝ったらどう？
examples.english: Since you're off of work, why don't you help out with the housework like cleaning or laundry?

examples.japanese: この魚は生では食べられないから、煮るなり焼くなりしてください。
examples.english: This fish can't be eaten raw, so please boil or fry it somehow.

examples.japanese: もう使わないなら、人にあげるなり捨てるなりしたほうがいいと思います。
examples.english: If you're not going to use it anymore, I think it's best you either give it to someone else or throw it away.

meaning: while; besides; at the same time; in addition
structure: Noun + に

examples.japanese: 日本の朝食と言えば、ご飯にお味噌汁でしょう。
examples.english: When speaking of Japanese breakfast, rice and miso soup should come to mind.

examples.japanese: 彼はスーツにネクタイを締めてとてもかっこよく見えた。
examples.english: He looked quite handsome in his suit and tie.

examples.japanese: ジーンズにワイシャツが主流。
examples.english: The "jeans and dress shirt" style is the mainstream.

examples.japanese: このサンダルはショートパンツにもよく似合います。
examples.english: These sandals go really well with shorts too.

examples.japanese: パスタに合うのはどちらのワインですか？
examples.english: Which wine goes better with pasta?

examples.japanese: 私は、家では大抵ジーンズにＴシャツを着ています。
examples.english: I wear mostly jeans and a T-shirt when I am at home.

meaning: cannot; not worthy; not worth doing ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + に値する | Noun

examples.japanese: 彼女の行為は尊敬に値する。
examples.english: Her deeds deserve respect.

examples.japanese: 彼は我々の称賛に値する。
examples.english: He is worthy of our praise.

examples.japanese: あいつはその罰を受けるに値する。
examples.english: He deserves that punishment.

examples.japanese: 他の誰よりも彼女がその賞に値すると思う。
examples.english: I think she deserves the award more than anyone else.

examples.japanese: その会社は投資に値する価値を持っている。
examples.english: That company is worth the investment.

examples.japanese: 私はその役職に値する人物ではありません。
examples.english: I'm not someone who deserves that (managerial) position.

meaning: due to the fact that; because of ~
structure: Noun + にあって（は / も）

examples.japanese: 彼は事故にあって足を折った。
examples.english: He had an accident and broke his leg.

examples.japanese: 彼は危険にあって勇敢だった。
examples.english: He showed bravery in the face of danger.

examples.japanese: 彼は落雷にあって死んだ。
examples.english: The lightning struck him dead.

examples.japanese: 母は大学講師だが、家庭にあっては普通の母親だ。
examples.english: My mother is a university lecturer, but she is an ordinary mother at home.

examples.japanese: 困難な状況にあっても彼は絶対にあきらめない。
examples.english: No matter how complicated of a situation it may become, he will never give up.

examples.japanese: 田中部長は、普段めちゃくちゃ怖いけど、家庭にあって私たちが想像できないほど優しいパパだそうだよ。
examples.english: Our manager Mr. Tanaka is normally really scary, but apparently at home he is an unbelievably kind father.

meaning: and ~ (indicates two contrasting actions)
structure: Verb (dictionary) + の + にひきかえにひきかえて | Noun + （である） | な-adjective + な/である | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 去年のJLPTにひきかえ、今年のはとても難しかった。
examples.english: This year was very difficult, as opposed to last year's JLPT.

examples.japanese: 隣の立派な家にひきかえ、うちの家は古くてみすぼらしい。
examples.english: In contrast to the magnificent house next door, our house is old and shabby.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事でとても真面目なのにひきかえ、個人生活には超だらしない。
examples.english: He is very serious at work, unlike his personal life where he is super sloppy.

examples.japanese: 昨日までは暑いのにひきかえ、今日はずいぶん涼しくなった。
examples.english: It was hot until yesterday, but it's getting cooler today.

examples.japanese: 彼女はたくさん友達がいるのにひきかえ、私は友達と呼べる人は全然いない。
examples.english: In contrast to her abundance of friends, I have absolutely no one to call a friend.

examples.japanese: 大人しく引っ込み思案な姉にひきかえ、妹のほうは社交的で友達も多い。
examples.english: In contrast to her quiet and thoughtful older sister, her younger sister is more social and has many friends.

meaning: when it comes to; as for ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に至って(も) | Noun

examples.japanese: 株価がここまで下落するに至っても彼はまだ売りたくないらしい。
examples.english: Even though the stock price has dropped to this low, he doesn't seem to want to sell.

examples.japanese: 大学を卒業するに至ってもなお、自分のやりたいことが見つかっていない人も多い。
examples.english: Even after graduating from university, many people still haven't found what they want to do.

examples.japanese: ひどい症状が出るに至っても彼は病院に行こうとしなかった。
examples.english: Even though he was showing serious symptoms, he still didn't plan to go to the hospital.

examples.japanese: あの男は結婚に至ってもまだ浮気をしています。
examples.english: That man is still having an affair even though he is married.

examples.japanese: 昼から始まった緊急の会議は、深夜に至ってもまだ続いている。
examples.english: The urgent meeting that started at noon is still going on even though it is late at night.

examples.japanese: 数々の証拠が出るに至っても、あの政治家は罪を認めようとしない。
examples.english: Even with all the evidence, the politician refuses to admit the crime.

meaning: even if; even though; although something reached the point ~
structure: Noun + に至っては

examples.japanese: いつも賛成するの母に至っては今度、僕の計画に反対した。
examples.english: Even my mother, who always agrees with me, is opposing my plan this time.

examples.japanese: これは特に学校の重要な問題です。校長先生に至っては勝手に決められない。
examples.english: This is a particularly important issue for the school. Even the school principal cannot decide this on their own.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は信じられないほど暑く、地元に至っては40度まで気温が上昇した。
examples.english: This summer was unbelievably hot, with temperatures rising to even 40 degrees Celsius in the local area.

examples.japanese: 今年は不景気で、どの会社も募集が少ない。当社に至っては次の2年に人事を採用しないそうだ。
examples.english: The economy is in a recession this year, and most all companies are barely hiring. It seems that even our company will not hire any new staff over the next two years.

examples.japanese: 彼の成績が落ちてきている。今回の試験に至ってはクラスの上位30位にも入れていない。
examples.english: His grades are going down. He didn't even get in the top 30 of the class for this exam.

examples.japanese: 高校の友達は私以外皆結婚した。友人に至っては来年3回目の結婚するそうだ。
examples.english: All my high school friends got married except me. It seems that one of my friends will even get married for the third time next year.

meaning: both ... and; not only ... also; whether it be ... or ~
structure: Noun (person only) + に言わせれば

examples.japanese: 私に言わせれば、日本の一番美味しい料理はやっぱりラーメンだ。
examples.english: If you ask me, I would say that the best Japanese food is ramen.

examples.japanese: 私に言わせれば、彼女は少し変わっている。
examples.english: If you ask me, she's a little strange.

examples.japanese: ４０歳なんて、私に言わせればまだまだ若いですよ。
examples.english: If you ask me, 40 is still young!

examples.japanese: 父は天才と言われているが、私に言わせれば、単なる努力家だ。
examples.english: People often say my dad is a genius, but if you ask me, he's simply a hard worker.

examples.japanese: 我々の世代の人間に言わせれば、あの人の行動は普通ではない。
examples.english: If you ask anyone from our generation, they'll agree that that person's actions are not normal.

examples.japanese: 私に言わせれば、タバコを止められないやつは意志が弱いだけだと思う。
examples.english: If you ask me, I think people who can't quit smoking are just weak-willed.

pattern: に限ったことではない
meaning: to feel strongly
structure: Noun + に限ったことではないに限ったことでもない

examples.japanese: 若者のマナーが悪いのは、この国に限ったことではない。
examples.english: It is not only this country where young people have bad manners.

examples.japanese: 漢字が書けなくなったのは、最近に限ったことではなく、スマートフォンを使うようになってからずっとだ。
examples.english: It's not only recently that I became unable to write kanji, I've been like this way back since I started using a smartphone.

examples.japanese: 今学期にインフルエンザがはやったのは、今年に限ったことではなく、昨年も同様だった。
examples.english: The flu that spread around this semester was not only big this year, but also last year as well.

meaning: when handled by (N), becomes a completely different result
structure: Noun + にかかっている | Phrase

examples.japanese: 合格できるかどうかは、これから１ヶ月のがんばりにかかっている。
examples.english: Whether or not you can pass depends on your hard work for the next month.

examples.japanese: 俺たちのチームが勝つかどうかは、君にかかっているよ。
examples.english: Whether our team wins or not is up to you.

examples.japanese: 私たちの会社の運命は、新しい社長の手腕にかかっている。
examples.english: The fate of our company depends on the skill of the new president.

examples.japanese: 契約の成否は、取引先がこの条件をどう考えるかにかかっている。
examples.english: Whether to sign the contract or not depends on how the client thinks about the conditions.

examples.japanese: 新しい自転車を買ってもらえるかどうかは、来月のテストの結果にかかっている。
examples.english: Whether or not we will buy you a new bicycle depends on your results of next month's tests.

examples.japanese: この国が将来、繁栄するかどうかは、現在の若者にかかっている。
examples.english: Whether the country will prosper in the future depends on the youth of today.

meaning: all we can do is; can do nothing but; only ~
structure: Noun + にかまけて

examples.japanese: 彼はゲームにかまけて全然勉強しなかった。
examples.english: He was absorbed in the game and didn't study at all.

examples.japanese: スポーツにかまけて学業を怠る学生もいる。
examples.english: Some students are obsessed with sports and neglect to study.

examples.japanese: 子供にかまけて本を読む暇もないのよ。
examples.english: I don't even have time to read a book because I'm busy taking care of my baby.

examples.japanese: 夫はスマホゲームにかまけて、家事を手伝おうとしない。
examples.english: My husband is obsessed with smartphone games and doesn't try at all to help out with the housework.

examples.japanese: 忙しさにかまけて、彼女と会う約束だったのに忘れてしまった。
examples.english: I was so busy that I forgot I had promised to meet her.

examples.japanese: 彼女はバイトにかまけて、全然日本語の勉強をしていません。
examples.english: She is busy with her part-time job and hasn't studied Japanese at all.

meaning: easy to; likely to; prone to; have a tendency to ~
structure: verb (dictionary) + にかたくない | Noun

examples.japanese: 彼らが離婚したことは想像に難くない。
examples.english: It's not hard to imagine that they got divorced.

examples.japanese: １点足りず合格できなかった彼の悔しさは、想像に難くない。
examples.english: It is not difficult to imagine his regret for not being able to pass the exam because of missing 1 point.

examples.japanese: この作品を作るのに、どんなに時間がかかったかは察するに難くない。
examples.english: It's not hard to imagine how much time they spent making this work of art.

examples.japanese: 5年前の自分を思い出せば、新入社員の苦労を理解するに難くない。
examples.english: Thinking back of myself 5 years ago, it's not hard to understand the hardships of new employees.

examples.japanese: 外国に滞在するとき、彼女はどんなに苦労したか想像に難くない。
examples.english: It’s not hard to imagine how tough her situation was when she lived abroad.

examples.japanese: 状況から判断して、彼が犯人であることは想像に難くない。
examples.english: Judging from the situation, it is not hard to imagine that he is the culprit.

meaning: when it comes to; concerning ~
structure: Noun + にまつわる

examples.japanese: 私はファッションにまつわる事柄が好きです。
examples.english: I like things related to fashion.

examples.japanese: お金にまつわる漢字は「貝」がつくものが多いです。
examples.english: Many kanji related to money use the kanji character for "shellfish".

examples.japanese: これはお酒にまつわる話を集めた本である。
examples.english: This is a book that collects stories about alcohol.

examples.japanese: 彼はこの城にまつわる不思議な話を始めた。
examples.english: He began to tell a mysterious story about this castle.

examples.japanese: 僕の父は家族にまつわる問題専門の弁護士だ。
examples.english: My dad is a lawyer specializing in family issues.

examples.japanese: 小さい頃アメリカにいた彼は英語にまつわる豆知識をたくさん知っている。
examples.english: He was in the United States when he was little and knows a lot of trivia about English.

meaning: with the intention to; on the condition / assumption ~
structure: Noun + に則って

examples.japanese: 私はその契約に則って支払います。
examples.english: I will pay according to the contract.

examples.japanese: 日本に住んでいるのだから、日本のルールに則って生活する必要がある。
examples.english: Since I live in Japan, I need to live according to Japanese rules.

examples.japanese: 会社の規則に則って、不正を行った同僚は解雇された。
examples.english: According to company rules, a colleague who committed fraud was dismissed.

examples.japanese: 家庭のゴミは自治体のルールに則って捨ててください。
examples.english: Please dispose of household waste according to the rules of the local government.

examples.japanese: その犯罪者は法律に則って、厳しく処罰されるだろう。
examples.english: The criminal will be severely punished according to the law.

examples.japanese: 試験中の不正行為は校則に則って処理する。
examples.english: Cheating during the exam will be handled in accordance with the school rules.

meaning: to be soon; the time has come to; nearby; ahead of ~
structure: Noun + に先駆けて

examples.japanese: その映画は、世界に先駆けて、日本での上映を決まった。
examples.english: It's been decided that the world premiere for the movie will be in Japan.

examples.japanese: その会社は、他社に先駆けて、低燃費の車を開発した。
examples.english: This company developed fuel-efficient cars before other companies.

examples.japanese: 世界に先駆けて、紙は古代の中国において発明されました。
examples.english: The world's first writing paper was invented in ancient China.

examples.japanese: その記者は新しい学校の開始に先駆けて校長をインタビューした。
examples.english: The reporter interviewed the school principal prior to the opening of the new school.

examples.japanese: 来月の大学入試に先駆けて、神社へ合格祈願しに行く人が増えている。
examples.english: An increasing number of people are going to pray for success at the shrine ahead of the university entrance exam next month.

examples.japanese: CDの発売に先駆けて、そのアーチストのコンサートが開かれた。
examples.english: The artist's concert was held prior to the release of their CD.

meaning: worth doing; can do; cannot bear doing ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + に忍びない

examples.japanese: 熱でつらそうな子供を見るに忍びない。
examples.english: It pains my heart to see a child suffering with a fever.

examples.japanese: お父さんが仕事で疲れて寝ているので、起こすに忍びない。
examples.english: My dad is tired from work and sleeping, so I can't bear to wake him up.

examples.japanese: 元主人がこれまでにしてきたひどい行為の数々は語るに忍びない。
examples.english: I can't stand to talk about the terrible acts that my ex-husband has done so far.

examples.japanese: うちの子が病気で弱っていく姿を見るに忍びない。
examples.english: I can't stand to see my child weakening due to illness.

examples.japanese: この財布はもうボロボロだけど、彼氏がくれたプレゼントなので、捨てるに忍びない。
examples.english: This wallet is already worn out, but it's a gift my boyfriend gave me, so I can't bring myself to throw it away.

examples.japanese: 気に入っていないが、校長先生からもらったお土産なので、捨てるに忍びない。
examples.english: I don't like it, but it's a souvenir I got from the principal, so I can't bring myself to throw it away.

pattern: にしたところで / としたところで
meaning: even; even if/though ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + にしたところでとしたところでにしたってとしたって | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: いくらおいしいにしたって、その見た目じゃ食べる気にならない。
examples.english: No matter how delicious it may be, with that appearance I don't feel like eating it.

examples.japanese: 走ったとしたって間に合わないだろうから、次の電車にしよう。
examples.english: Even if I ran, I wouldn't be in time, so let's take the next train.

examples.japanese: どちらにしたって状況が悪いことには変わりない。
examples.english: Either way, the situation is still bad.

examples.japanese: 今から急いだとしたって間に合わないだろう。
examples.english: Even if you hurry from now on, you won't make it in time.

examples.japanese: これから毎日勉強するにしたところで、3ヶ月じゃ合格できないだろう。
examples.english: Even if you studied every day from now on, you won't be able to pass in just 3 months.

examples.japanese: 手元には１円もない。通帳にしたって同じだ。
examples.english: I don't have a single yen at hand. It's the same for my bankbook.

meaning: even ~ (with emphasis)
structure: Noun + にして

examples.japanese: ３回目にして、やっとN１に合格することができた。
examples.english: I finally passed the JLPT N1 on my 3rd try!

examples.japanese: 田中さんは18歳にして、社長になった。
examples.english: Mr. Tanaka became a company president when he was only 18.

examples.japanese: 頼んでいた仕事を彼は一日にして全て終わらせてしまった。
examples.english: He finished all of the requested work in just one day.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、４５歳にして孫が生まれたらしいよ！
examples.english: I heard that she had a grandchild at just 45!

examples.japanese: 天才の彼にして間違えるのだから、できないのは当然である。
examples.english: If that genius couldn't solve it then it's only natural that you couldn't either.

examples.japanese: あの時部長が言っていた言葉の意味が、今にして初めて理解できました。
examples.english: I now understand the meaning of the words my manager said that time.

meaning: to be based on; to take into account ~
structure: Noun + に即しに即してに即した

examples.japanese: 学校の規則に即して、学生の髪の毛は黒色にしなければならない。
examples.english: According to school rules, student hair must be black.

examples.japanese: 会社の現状に即して物事を考えよう。
examples.english: Think about things in line with the current state of the company.

examples.japanese: 銀行も、時代に即した新しいサービスを提供しなければならない。
examples.english: Banks also have to offer new services that are in line with the times.

examples.japanese: 最近は事実に即した報道をしていないマスメディアが増えてきたように思う。
examples.english: Recently, I think that the number of mass media that do not report according to the facts has increased.

examples.japanese: 昨日、社長は販売目標を実態に即して下げると公表した。
examples.english: Yesterday, the company president announced that he would lower the sales target in line with the actual situation.

examples.japanese: コーチは試合の流れに即して選手の交代を指示した。
examples.english: The coach instructed the change of players according to the flow of the game.

pattern: に耐える / に耐えない
meaning: can do; worthy; worth doing
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に耐える / に堪えるに堪える / に堪えないにたえる / にたえない | Noun

examples.japanese: この展示は鑑賞に耐える作品が少ない。
examples.english: There are not many works of art which are worth looking at in this exhibition.

examples.japanese: 今年は鑑賞に堪える日本の映画が多くて、とてもよかった。
examples.english: It was great that there were many Japanese movies this year that were worthy of appreciation.

examples.japanese: この写真はアマチュアカメラマンが撮ったものだが、十分評価に耐える作品だ。
examples.english: This photo was taken by an amateur photographer, but it is a work that is worthy of recognition.

examples.japanese: このアニメは子供向けに作られていますが、大人でも見るに堪える内容です。
examples.english: This anime is made for children, but it's content that even adults can watch.

examples.japanese: これは20年間の使用に耐える丈夫な製品です。
examples.english: This is a very durable product which will last for 20 years.

examples.japanese: このシャツは毎日の洗濯に耐える素材で作られています。
examples.english: This shirt is made of a material that can withstand daily washing.

pattern: に足らない / に足りない
meaning: can do; worthy; worth doing
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に足らないに足りない | Noun※ must be suru verb.

examples.japanese: それは取るに足らない話だ。
examples.english: That's not a story worth mentioning.

examples.japanese: 彼は頼むに足りない人だ。
examples.english: He is an unreliable person.

examples.japanese: 4人いれば何事も恐れるに足らない。
examples.english: If we have 4 people, there's no need to be afraid.

examples.japanese: あなたの実力をもってすれば、大学入試など恐れるに足りない。
examples.english: With your ability, you don’t need to worry about the university entrance exam.

examples.japanese: 彼らの言葉は一つとして信じるに足りない。
examples.english: Not a single of their words are believable.

examples.japanese: 就職難など、能力がある学生にとっては、恐れるに足りない。
examples.english: Capable students need not worry about the job shortage.

meaning: cannot; not worthy; not worth doing ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + に足るに足りる | Noun※ must be suru verb.

examples.japanese: 彼はその仕事を任せるに足る人です。
examples.english: He's a worthy man to give the job to.

examples.japanese: あの方は皆さんに尊敬するに足るお母様です。
examples.english: She is a mother who deserves the respect of everyone.

examples.japanese: ナイフについた彼の指紋は信頼するに足る証拠です。
examples.english: His fingerprint on the knife is credible evidence.

examples.japanese: インターネットで得た情報は信用に足るものではない。
examples.english: The information obtained on the Internet is not credible.

examples.japanese: 学生生活のいい思い出は信頼するに足る教師に出会えたということだ。
examples.english: A good memory of my student life is that I met a teacher I could trust.

examples.japanese: パスポートはあなたがだれであるかを証明するに足る書類です。
examples.english: A passport is a sufficient document to prove who you are.

meaning: according to; in keeping with; to be based on ~
structure: Noun + に照らして

examples.japanese: 彼は社則に照らして処分された。
examples.english: He was punished according to company rules.

examples.japanese: 犯罪は全て法に照らして裁かれる。
examples.english: All crimes are judged in the light of the law.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分の経験に照らして後輩にアドバイスした。
examples.english: He advised his juniors according from his experience.

examples.japanese: その事実に照らして彼に罪がないことは明らかだ。
examples.english: In light of that fact, it is clear that he is innocent.

examples.japanese: 赤の服は現地の文化規範に照らして着用しないほうがいい。
examples.english: According to local cultural norms, you should not wear red clothing.

examples.japanese: 彼がこの会社のためにやってきたことに照らして昇進すべきだ。
examples.english: In light of what he has done for the company, he should be promoted.

meaning: not limited to only ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + にとどまらず（～も） | Noun +（である） | な-adjective + である | い-adjective + だけ

examples.japanese: 母のケーキ作りは単なる趣味にとどまらず、自分の店を開くまでになった。
examples.english: Making cakes for my mother was more than just a hobby, I even opened my own shop.

examples.japanese: アニメや漫画は日本にとどまらず、海外でも多くのファンを増やしている。
examples.english: Anime and manga are gaining a lot of fans not only in Japan but also overseas.

examples.japanese: この小説は、女性にとどまらず、若い男性にも人気そうだ。
examples.english: This novel seems to be popular not only with women but also with young men.

examples.japanese: 彼はそのレストランで、文句を言うにとどまらず、テーブルをひっくり返してしまった。
examples.english: He not only complained to the restaurant, he flipped the table over.

examples.japanese: 彼女の研究は科学にとどまらず、医療分野にも広がっている。
examples.english: Her research is not limited to science and extends to the medical field as well.

examples.japanese: 最近は、週末にとどまらず、平日もバーベーキューをする人が増えているそうだ。
examples.english: Recently, it seems that more and more people are barbecuing not only on weekends but also on weekdays.

meaning: is not entirely impossible
structure: Verb (dictionary) + には無理がある | Noun

examples.japanese: こんなにたくさんの料理を一人で食べるには無理がある。
examples.english: It is impossible to eat this much food by oneself.

examples.japanese: 私の個人的な経験から見ると、このプロジェクトには無理があると思います。
examples.english: From my personal experience, I think this project unrealistic.

examples.japanese: やはりこの予定には無理があると思いました。
examples.english: As I thought that, this schedule was impossible after all.

examples.japanese: 課長の計画には無理があると思います。３ヶ月では到底終わりません。
examples.english: I think the manager's plan is unreasonable. It definitely will not finish in just 3 months.

examples.japanese: この予算でシステムを作るには無理がありますよ。
examples.english: It is impossible to make a system with this budget.

examples.japanese: 二泊三日のスケジュールで、これらの場所を全部まわるには無理がありますよ。
examples.english: With a schedule of two nights and three days, it is impossible to go around to all of these places.

meaning: whether or not; regardless
structure: Noun + によらず

examples.japanese: 性別、年齢によらず、条件に当てはまる方であれば誰でもいいです。
examples.english: Anyone who meets the conditions is welcome, regardless of gender or age.

examples.japanese: この学習書はレベルによらず役に立つので買ったほうがいいでしょう。
examples.english: This study book is useful regardless of level, so you should buy it.

examples.japanese: 君は見かけによらずよく食べるね。
examples.english: You eat a lot regardless of how it looks.

examples.japanese: このクラブは年齢によらずサッカーが好きなら参加できます。
examples.english: This club is open to anyone who likes soccer, regardless of their age.

examples.japanese: うちの会社は学歴によらず、実力がある人材を求めている。
examples.english: Our company is looking for talented people regardless of their educational background.

examples.japanese: 職種によらず、賃金によらず、仕事があれば何でもやります。
examples.english: I will do anything if I have a job, regardless of job type or wage.

meaning: by means of; with; on / at / as of (time)​
structure: Noun + に + Noun + を重ねて

examples.japanese: 苦労に苦労を重ねて、僕はここまで成長できた。
examples.english: After a lot of hard work, I was able to grow up to this point.

examples.japanese: 勉強に勉強を重ねて、ようやくN1に合格できた。
examples.english: After continuously studying hard, I finally passed N1.

examples.japanese: 失敗に失敗を重ねて、ついに新しいカメラのモデルが完成した。
examples.english: After many failures, a new camera model was finally completed.

examples.japanese: 改良に改良を重ねて、皆様に満足していただける最高の商品となりました。
examples.english: We have made continuous improvements to make it the best product that will satisfy everyone.

examples.japanese: 彼は努力に努力を重ねて、ここまでの地位を築いてきた。
examples.english: He has continuously worked hard to build his social status to this point.

examples.japanese: 僕はよく天才と言われるが、努力に努力を重ねてここまできたんだ。
examples.english: I'm often referred to as a genius, but I've worked very hard to get here.

meaning: not limited to; not only… but also ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + にも程があるにもほどがある | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 冗談にもほどがある。
examples.english: Your joke has gone too far.

examples.japanese: 今回のテストは難しいにもほどがあるレベルだった。
examples.english: This test was beyond difficult.

examples.japanese: 彼の態度は失礼にもほどがある。
examples.english: His rude attitude is beyond acceptable.

examples.japanese: 君の部屋が汚いにも程がある！早く掃除しなさいよ。
examples.english: Your room is beyond dirty! Clean it up quickly!

examples.japanese: 情けないにも程があるぞ。
examples.english: There’s a limit to how pathetic you can get.

examples.japanese: 途中で仕事を投げ出すなんて、無責任にも程がある。
examples.english: You can’t just give up on a job halfway through. There’s a limit to how irresponsible you can be.

meaning: even if I wanted to… I couldn’t ~
structure: Noun + にもまして

examples.japanese: 昨日のテストはいつにも増して難しかった気がする。
examples.english: I felt that yesterday's test was more difficult than usual.

examples.japanese: 今年の文化祭りは、去年にも増して、たくさんの人に来てもらえた。
examples.english: This year's cultural festival attracted many more people than last year.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに会った友達は、以前にも増して美しかった。
examples.english: My friend who I had not seen in a while was even more beautiful than before.

examples.japanese: お母さんは誰にも増して、お父さんのことを心配しているよ。
examples.english: Mom is more worried about Dad than anyone else.

examples.japanese: 今日はいつもにも増して寒いし早く帰りたいです。
examples.english: It's colder than usual today and I want to go home early.

examples.japanese: こうして友人と一緒に食事を楽しむことは何にも増して幸せなことである。
examples.english: Enjoying a meal and having fun with friends in this way is happier than anything else.

meaning: there is no need to; unnecessary; no match for ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + に(は)あたらない | Noun (must be する verb)

examples.japanese: 彼女の実力を知っていたので、N1合格も驚くに当たらない。
examples.english: Knowing her ability, passing N1 is not surprising.

examples.japanese: 多少ミスしたくらいでは心配には当たらない。
examples.english: A few mistakes is not worth worrying about.

examples.japanese: 私の考えでは、彼女の行為は非難するには当たりません。
examples.english: In my opinion, there is no need to criticize her actions.

examples.japanese: 天気は変わりやすいので、予報が外れても責めるには当たらない。
examples.english: The weather is volatile, so it's not worth blaming the weather forecast if it is wrong.

examples.japanese: あの野球選手が引退したことは驚くに当たらない。
examples.english: It's no surprise that baseball player has retired.

examples.japanese: 試験に落ちたからと言って、嘆くには当たらない。
examples.english: Just because you failed the exam doesn't mean you should stress over it.

meaning: it’s not worth; there’s no need to; does not correspond to ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + に(は)及ばない | Noun

examples.japanese: タクシーで帰るので、ご心配には及びません。
examples.english: I will return by taxi, so there is no need for you to worry.

examples.japanese: ファックスを使えばいい。郵便で送るには及ばない。
examples.english: If you can use a fax machine, you don't need to bother sending it by post.

examples.japanese: 電話で済むことだから、わざわざ行くには及ばない。
examples.english: You don't need to trouble yourself to go since you can do it over the phone.

examples.japanese: これは初級の文法ですから、説明するには及びませんね。
examples.english: This is a beginner level grammar, so there's no need to explain, right?

examples.japanese: 面接の結果は電話で連絡しますので、こちらに来るには及びません。
examples.english: Interview results will be announced by phone so you don't need to come here.

examples.japanese: どんなに頑張っても、彼の成績には及ばない。
examples.english: No matter how hard I study, I can't compete with his grades.

meaning: utmost; extremely ~
structure: Noun + の至り

examples.japanese: こんな素晴らしい賞をいただいて、光栄の至りです。
examples.english: It is an honor to receive such a wonderful award.

examples.japanese: 憧れのアーティストからサインをもらえるなんて、感激の至りだ。
examples.english: I was deeply moved because I got a signature from the artist I admired.

examples.japanese: そんなことをするのは愚の至りだ。
examples.english: Doing something like that is the height of foolishness.

examples.japanese: 日本の首相にお目にかかって、私は光栄の至りです。
examples.english: It is such an honor for me to meet the Prime Minister of Japan.

examples.japanese: 今日はお客様の名前を間違えてしまい、汗顔の至りだ。
examples.english: Today, I made a mistake with a customer's name, and so my face is covered in sweat.

examples.japanese: 自分の書いた物語が本になるなど想像していませんでした。光栄の至りです。
examples.english: I never imagined that the story I wrote would become a book. It's such an honor.

meaning: extremely; very ~
structure: Noun + の極み

examples.japanese: 優勝できて、感激の極みです。
examples.english: I am beyond excited that we've won the championship.

examples.japanese: 長時間の試合で、選手たちは疲労の極みに達していた。
examples.english: The players were completely exhausted during the long-lasting game.

examples.japanese: 交通事故で多くの人が亡くなり、痛恨の極みだ。
examples.english: Many people lose their lives in traffic accidents, it is very tragic.

examples.japanese: 家を建てたばかりなのに、地震で壊れてしまい、痛恨の極みだ。
examples.english: Our house was destroyed in the earthquake immediately after we finished building it. It is such a horrible feeling.

examples.japanese: 私のような者がこのような名誉ある賞を頂けるとは、感激の極みだ。
examples.english: I'm deeply honored that someone like me to receive such an honorable award.

examples.japanese: あなたにとっては日常的なことかもしれませんが、私にとってはそれは贅沢の極みです。
examples.english: It may be everyday for you, but for me it's the height of luxury.

meaning: utmost; extremely ~
structure: Verb (casual) + のなんの（って） | Adjective

examples.japanese: このカレーは辛いのなんのって、全然食べられなかった。
examples.english: The curry was incredibly spicy, I couldn't eat it all.

examples.japanese: この映画は怖いのなんのって。昨夜私は眠れなくなったほどだ。
examples.english: This movie is very scary. So scary that I couldn’t sleep last night.

examples.japanese: このスマホは使いにくいのなんのって、前の機種に変更したいよ。
examples.english: This smartphone is extremely difficult to use, so I'd like to change to the previous model.

examples.japanese: 昨日の試験が難しかったのなんのって。僕は合格できるなんか全然思わないよ。
examples.english: Yesterday's exam was extremely difficult. I have no idea if I'll be able to pass or not.

examples.japanese: 自分が作った料理がまずいのなんのって、もう料理は作らないことに決めました。
examples.english: The food I cook is so bad I decided to never cook again.

examples.japanese: そのアニメのサントラがカッコイイのなんのって。君のCDを借りてもいいか。
examples.english: What a super cool anime soundtrack. Can I borrow your CD?

pattern: のやら / ものやら / ことやら
meaning: or ~ (I don't know)
structure: Verb (casual form) + のやらものやらことやら | Noun + な | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 今の不景気はいつまで続くのやら？
examples.english: I wonder how long this current economic slump will continue.

examples.japanese: 息子は大学を卒業したのに、仕事もせずに何をやっているのやら。
examples.english: Even though my son has graduated from university, he isn't working. I wonder what he is doing.

examples.japanese: 言葉も話せないのに、来年半年間ベトナムに行くことにした。どうなることやら。
examples.english: Even though I don't speak the language, I decided to go to Vietnam for half a year next year. I wonder what will happen...

examples.japanese: もうすぐ大学入試なのに、田中さんは勉強せずにゲームばかりして、何を考えているのやら。
examples.english: Even though university entrance exams are right around the corner, Tanaka doesn't study and spends all his time playing games. Really, what is he thinking?

examples.japanese: 奥さんをガンで亡くした彼に、どう声をかけたらいいものやら。
examples.english: He recently lost his wife to cancer and so I'm not sure how I should approach him.

examples.japanese: マンションの近くの公園で遊ぶ子どもの声がうるさくて仕方がないが、どこに苦情を言っていいものやら分からない。
examples.english: The kids at the park by my apartment are really loud. Although it can't be helped, is there no place for me to vent my frustration?

meaning: such things as A and B; A and B and so on ~
structure: [A]のやら + [B]のやら | Verb (casual form) + のやら | な-adjective + な | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 彼はバスに間に合ったのやら間に合わなかったのやら．．．
examples.english: I wonder if he made it in time or not for the bus...

examples.japanese: このカレーは辛すぎて、美味しいのやら美味しくないのやら分からない。
examples.english: This curry is too spicy I can't tell whether it tastes good or not.

examples.japanese: 嘘なのやら本当なのやら、彼氏が｢愛してる｣と言ってくれた。
examples.english: I'm not sure if it was a lie or the truth, but my boyfriend told me that he loves me!

examples.japanese: 彼女はパーティーに行くのやら行かないのやらはっきりしない。
examples.english: She won't say clearly whether or not she will go to the party.

examples.japanese: 田中さんは授業内容が分かっているのやら分かっていないのやら、無表情なので分からない。
examples.english: I'm not sure whether or not Tanaka understands the class content since his face lacks any expression.

examples.japanese: 仕事がないので毎日友達と遊んでいる。暇なのやら忙しいのやら。
examples.english: Since I'm out of work, I've just been hanging out with my friends everyday. I'm not sure if I'm "full of free time" or busy.

meaning: based on; according to; in accordance with ~
structure: Noun + を踏まえて

examples.japanese: 集めたデータを踏まえてレポートを作成します。
examples.english: I will create a report based on the collected data.

examples.japanese: あなたはそれを踏まえて何か良い提案がありますか。
examples.english: Do you have any good suggestions based on that?

examples.japanese: アンケート結果を踏まえて業務を改善したいと思います。
examples.english: I would like to improve our business performance based on the results of the survey.

examples.japanese: 消費者の意見を踏まえて商品開発をしましょう。
examples.english: Let's develop products based on the opinions of consumers.

examples.japanese: あなたはこの状況を踏まえて再度ご検討ください。
examples.english: Please re-examine this based on this situation.

examples.japanese: デザイナーは社員の意見を踏まえて、その会社の制服を一新した。
examples.english: The designer renewed the company's uniform based on the opinions of employees.

meaning: during; for; since; over a period of time
structure: Noun + を経て

examples.japanese: さまざまな海外での経験を経て、彼は成長した。
examples.english: Through various overseas experiences, he grew up.

examples.japanese: 20年の時を経て、伝説のバンドが復活する。
examples.english: After 20 years, the legendary band is making a comeback.

examples.japanese: 日本からの直行便がないので、イギリスを経てスペインへ行く。
examples.english: Since there is no direct flight from Japan, I will go to Spain via England.

examples.japanese: その選手はオリンピックを経て、急激に力をつけてきった。
examples.english: That athlete has rapidly gained strength after the Olympics.

examples.japanese: 多くの書類審査や面接を経て、やっとビザがもらえた。
examples.english: After many document reviews and interviews, I finally got a visa.

examples.japanese: 当社では、新入社員は３ヶ月の研修を経て、各部署へ配属となります。
examples.english: At our company, new employees will be assigned to each department after three months of training.

meaning: prior to; to be the first (pioneer); being ahead of ~
structure: Noun + を控えて | Noun + を/が + Noun + に控えて

examples.japanese: 私の帰国を控えて、友人たちが送別会を開いてくれた。
examples.english: Before returning to my home country, my friends held a farewell party for me.

examples.japanese: 新店舗の開店を控え、店内は準備で慌ただしい。
examples.english: With the opening of the new store ahead, the store is busy with preparations.

examples.japanese: 私の次女は来年の春に高校受験を控えています。
examples.english: My second daughter is preparing to take the high school exam next spring.

examples.japanese: 妹は結婚を明後日に控えて、不安で眠れない様子だ。
examples.english: My sister seems to be anxious and unable to sleep as she is about to get married the day after tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 試合を十日後に控えて選手たちは練習に余念がない。
examples.english: With only 10 days left until the competition, the players wholeheartedly focus on practice.

examples.japanese: 卒業を来年に控えている学生に、進学先のアンケートを実施した。
examples.english: We conducted a questionnaire on what schools students graduating next year will be going to.

meaning: as an opportunity/chance to ~
structure: Verb (casual, non-past) + の + をいいことに | Noun + (であるの) | な-adjective + なの | い-adjective + の

examples.japanese: 私は夏休みであるのをいいことに外国を旅行する。
examples.english: I took advantage of summer vacation to travel abroad.

examples.japanese: 先生がいないのをいいことに朝の授業をサボった。
examples.english: Taking advantage of the teacher's absence, I skipped morning class.

examples.japanese: 私が知らないのをいいことに彼は私をだました。
examples.english: He took advantage of my ignorance and deceived me.

examples.japanese: 彼はお金持ちであるのをいいことに、毎日違う女の人とデートする。
examples.english: He takes advantage of his wealth and dates different women every day.

examples.japanese: 先生が優しいのをいいことに、学生たちは授業中にふざけた。
examples.english: Taking advantage of the teacher's gentleness, the students played during class.

examples.japanese: 相手の無知なのをいいことに、お金をだまし、取るなんて、ひどい人だ。
examples.english: Taking advantage of the other person's ignorance and defrauding them of their money, what a terrible person.

pattern: を顧みず / も顧みず
meaning: in defiance of; not losing to / afraid / worrying about ~
structure: Noun + を顧みずも顧みず

examples.japanese: 危険も顧みず彼は彼女を救うために川へ飛び込んだ。
examples.english: He jumped into the river to save her, without any regard of danger.

examples.japanese: 彼女は費用を顧みず家を飾った。
examples.english: She decorated the house without paying attention to the cost.

examples.japanese: 彼は医者の忠告を顧みず、お酒を飲む。
examples.english: He drinks without regard to the advice of the doctor.

examples.japanese: あの人は相手の気持ちも顧みず、思ったことは何でも言う。
examples.english: He doesn't care about other people's feelings and says whatever he thinks.

examples.japanese: 父は家庭を顧みず、ギャンブルばかりしている。
examples.english: My father only cares about gambling without any regard for his family.

examples.japanese: 政府は国民の権利を顧みず勝手にふるまっている。
examples.english: The government behaves without regard to the rights of the people.

meaning: while; at the same time; incidentally; for the purpose of ~
structure: Noun + を兼ねても兼ねて

examples.japanese: 私は興味と実益を兼ねて、イラストを描いています。
examples.english: I draw illustrations for both interest and profit.

examples.japanese: 日本語の勉強を兼ねて、スーパーでアルバイトをしています。
examples.english: I study Japanese and also work part-time at a supermarket.

examples.japanese: 今回の帰国するのは両親に会う事を兼ねて、結婚の報告をします。
examples.english: When I return to Japan this time, I will meet my parents as well as announce my marriage.

examples.japanese: 冷蔵庫の整理を兼ねて残っていた野菜を使い切った。
examples.english: I used up the remaining vegetables while also organizing the refrigerator.

examples.japanese: 本日はご挨拶を兼ねて、当社の新商品のご紹介に参りました。
examples.english: Today, I came to greet you and also introduce this company's new products.

examples.japanese: 運動と気分転換を兼ねて、毎日1時間散歩する習慣を続けています。
examples.english: I maintain a habit of walking for 1 hour daily, both to move my body and to get a change of pace.

meaning: starting from; the last time (ending a continued action)
structure: Noun + を皮切りに（して） | を皮切りとして

examples.japanese: 今日の会議では、田中さんの発言を皮切りにして反対意見が次々と出た。
examples.english: At today's meeting, starting with Mr. Tanaka's statement, a lot of contrary opinions were raised.

examples.japanese: 好きなアイドルは、東京を皮切りに、全国10ヵ所でライブを開く。
examples.english: The idol group I like will be performing in 10 places across Japan, starting in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 彼女の店は名古屋で成功したのを皮切りに、各地に次々と出店していずれも成功を収めた。
examples.english: Her store first succeeded in Nagoya, and then continued to expand and succeed in other areas.

examples.japanese: 今度イタリア出店を皮切りに彼はヨーロッパに進出しようとしている。
examples.english: Starting with the opening of a store in Italy, he is about to expand into Europe.

examples.japanese: 新しいゲームソフトは、日本での発売を皮切りに、順次世界で発売を予定している。
examples.english: The new game software is scheduled to be released worldwide, starting with the release in Japan.

examples.japanese: その日を皮切りとして日本の詩や文学が好きになりました。
examples.english: Starting from that day, I became fond of Japanese poetry and literature.

meaning: since ~ (indicates a large change before & after)
structure: Verb (casual) + の + を機に | Noun

examples.japanese: 会社を辞めたのを機に、サイクリングを始めた。
examples.english: Quitting my job provided me with the opportunity to start cycling.

examples.japanese: 妻が妊娠を機に、私はたばこを辞めることにした。
examples.english: As a result of my wife getting pregnant, I decided to take the opportunity to quit smoking.

examples.japanese: 私はこれを機に貴社製品がもっと売れることを期待しています。
examples.english: I hope this will be an opportunity to sell more of the company's products.

examples.japanese: 日本では車検を機に、車を売る人は多いです。
examples.english: In Japan, there are many people who take the opportunity to sell their cars when it is time for the annual vehicle inspection.

examples.japanese: 転職を機に、もっと広い部屋に引っ越したいと思う。
examples.english: To make the most of changing jobs, I want to take the opportunity to move to a larger room.

examples.japanese: パソコンが壊れたが、修理すると逆に高いので、これを機に新しいのを買うつもりだ。
examples.english: My computer broke, but it's expensive to repair, so I'll take this opportunity to buy a new one.

meaning: always; never stop; can’t help but ~
structure: Noun + を禁じ得ない

examples.japanese: 彼の不幸な人生には、同情を禁じえない。
examples.english: I can't help but feel sympathy for his unfortunate circumstances.

examples.japanese: 彼女の身の上話を聞いて、涙を禁じえない。
examples.english: I can't help crying when hearing her story.

examples.japanese: 先生の変顔に笑いを禁じえなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't help but laugh at the teacher's funny face.

examples.japanese: 大手企業が相次いで倒産すると聞いて、驚きを禁じえない。
examples.english: I can't help but be surprised to hear that major companies are going bankrupt one after another.

examples.japanese: この映画のラストシーンでは、誰も涙を禁じえないでしょう。
examples.english: In the last scene of this movie, no one will be able to stop themselves from crying.

examples.japanese: 政治家の汚職を見るにつけ怒りを禁じえない。
examples.english: I can't help but get angry when I see the corruption of politicians.

pattern: をもって / をもちまして
meaning: success after continuous (effort, work, adjustments, etc.)
structure: Noun + をもってをもちまして

examples.japanese: 彼女の実力をもってすれば、成功するだろう。
examples.english: With her abilities, she will likely succeed.

examples.japanese: 最新技術をもってすればその開発も難しくないだろう。
examples.english: With the latest technology, its development will not be difficult.

examples.japanese: あの先生は私が何を尋ねても、いつも誠意をもって答えてくれる。
examples.english: That teacher always answers in good faith no matter what I ask.

examples.japanese: 今の医療技術をもってしても治せない病も多い。
examples.english: There are many diseases that cannot be cured even with the current medical technology.

examples.japanese: 本日をもって、セールは終了となります。
examples.english: The sale ends today.

examples.japanese: １８時をもってタイムセールは終了します。
examples.english: The time-sale will end at 6pm.

pattern: を押して / を押し切って
meaning: in defiance of; not losing to / afraid / worrying about ~
structure: Noun + を押してを押し切って

examples.japanese: コーチの反対を押して怪我をしているのに試合に出た。
examples.english: Even though my coach protested because of my injury, I still entered the match.

examples.japanese: 障害を押し切って目的のことをしてください。
examples.english: Overcome obstacles and focus on your goals.

examples.japanese: 大事な決勝戦だったので、怪我を押して彼は出場した。
examples.english: It was an important final, so overcame his injury to play in the match.

examples.japanese: 両親の反対を押し切って、あの二人は結婚しました。
examples.english: Overcoming the opposition of their parents, the two married.

examples.japanese: 風邪を引いたけど休めないから、無理を押して出社した。
examples.english: I caught a cold, but I couldn't take the day off, so I forced myself to push through and go to work.

examples.japanese: 今日は大事な試験だったので、病気の体を押して受けにいった。
examples.english: It was an important exam today, so I pushed my sick body and went to take it.

meaning: end up; in the end; as a result (negative)
structure: Noun + を境に（して）

examples.japanese: 大学の卒業を境に、同じクラスの友達とも会わなくなった。
examples.english: Since graduating from college, I stopped seeing friends from the same class.

examples.japanese: 僕は妻の妊娠を境に、タバコとお酒を辞めました。
examples.english: After my wife got pregnant, I quit smoking and drinking.

examples.japanese: 我が国はオリンピックを境に急速に発展した。
examples.english: Our country (Japan) has developed rapidly since the Olympics.

examples.japanese: あの事件を境にして、彼女は誰とも一緒に住みたくなくなったそうだ。
examples.english: Since that incident, she doesn't seem to want to live with anyone anymore.

examples.japanese: あの両親の事故を境に、彼女は一度も笑わなくなった。
examples.english: After her parents' accident, she never laughed again.

examples.japanese: 彼は退職を境に、東京を離れて田舎でのんびり暮らしている。
examples.english: After his retirement, he left Tokyo to live leisurely in the countryside.

meaning: partly because; also because of; plus the reason for ~
structure: Noun + を余儀なくされるを余儀なくされたを余儀なくされている

examples.japanese: その試合は雨のため、延期を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: Due to the rain, the game had to be postponed.

examples.japanese: 大きなミスをしたため、彼は辞職を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: He was forced to resign because he made a big mistake.

examples.japanese: 火事で住まいが焼けたため、家探しを余儀なくされた。
examples.english: The fire burned my house, forcing me to find a new home.

examples.japanese: 試合中の怪我は彼に26歳で引退を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: Injuries during the match forced him to retire at the age of 26.

examples.japanese: 災害のため、多くの住民が避難所での生活を余儀なくされている。
examples.english: Many people have been forced to live in shelters because of the disaster.

examples.japanese: 台風が来たため登山計画の変更を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: Due to the typhoon, we had to change the mountain climbing plan.

meaning: even if; even though; despite ~
structure: Noun + をよそに

examples.japanese: 親の心配をよそに、彼女は一人旅に出かけた。
examples.english: She went on a trip alone despite her parents worrying.

examples.japanese: 彼は周囲の反対をよそに、危険な仕事を続けた。
examples.english: He continued his dangerous work, despite the opposition from his surroundings.

examples.japanese: 両親の反対をよそに、医者の仕事を辞めてしまった。
examples.english: Despite my parents' opposition, I quit my job as a doctor.

examples.japanese: 教師の警告をよそに、あの学生は遅刻を繰り返している。
examples.english: Despite the teacher's warning, that student is repeatedly late.

examples.japanese: 住民たちの抗議行動をよそに、ダムの建設の計画が進められている。
examples.english: Despite the protests of the residents, plans are underway to build a dam.

examples.japanese: 親の心配をよそに、彼は早朝からサーフィンに出かけて行った。
examples.english: Despite his parents' worries, he went surfing early in the morning.

meaning: to be based on; to take into account ~
structure: Noun + を前提としてを前提に（して）前提で

examples.japanese: 私たちは結婚を前提として交際しています。
examples.english: We are dating with intent of marriage.

examples.japanese: 私の企画は君の協力を前提としている。
examples.english: My plan depends on the condition of your cooperation.

examples.japanese: 彼は氏名を明かさないことを前提に記者にその話を言った。
examples.english: He spoke to the journalist on the condition that his name is not disclosed.

examples.japanese: あなたの提案は我々のあり金以上の金を前提にしている。
examples.english: Your proposal supposes more money than we actually have.

examples.japanese: いつでも事故を起こることを前提として、慎重に運転する。
examples.english: Drive carefully with the assumption that an accident can occur at any time.

examples.japanese: 君の言ったことは、真実であることを前提にして、とても大変な状況になってしまいそうだ。
examples.english: Assuming what you said is true, then this seems like this will turn into a very serious situation.

meaning: while; on the same occasion; at the same time; coincidentally ~
structure: Verb (casual) + 折に（は） | Noun + の

examples.japanese: お暇の折にはぜひ遊びに来てください。
examples.english: Please come and visit us when you are free.

examples.japanese: 来日の折には、私がご案内します。
examples.english: I will guide you when you come to Japan.

examples.japanese: 来週に君の家にお伺いする折に、本をお返しします。
examples.english: I will return the book when I visit your house next week.

examples.japanese: 今度、東京に来る折にはお立ち寄りください。
examples.english: Please drop in when you come to Tokyo next time.

examples.japanese: その折にはご助力をいただき誠にありがとうございました。
examples.english: Thank you very much for your assistance on that occasion.

examples.japanese: 次回、お目にかかった折に、旅行の話を聞かせてくださいね。
examples.english: Please tell us about your trip the next time we meet.

meaning: at the most; no more than​; at best; roughly; about ~
structure: およそ + something to be approximated

examples.japanese: 私はおよそ100冊の本を持っています。
examples.english: I have about 100 books.

examples.japanese: 私たちの職場にはおよそ80名の社員がいます。
examples.english: Our workplace has about 80 employees.

examples.japanese: およそこの花瓶はどれくらいの価値がありますか。
examples.english: Approximately how much is this vase worth?

examples.japanese: 私の家の最寄り駅からおよそ2時間かかります。
examples.english: It takes about 2 hours from the nearest station to my house.

examples.japanese: およそ三分の一のメンバーが出席しました。
examples.english: Roughly one third of the members attended.

examples.japanese: およそ10年ぶりに私は先生と友達に会いました。
examples.english: For the first time in about 10 years, I met my teacher and friends.

meaning: ending particle; adds force or indicates command
structure: phrase + さ

examples.japanese: やってみるさ！
examples.english: Give it a try!

examples.japanese: よくあることさ。
examples.english: It happens.

examples.japanese: そういうものさ。
examples.english: That's the way it is.

examples.japanese: そういうことさ。
examples.english: That's that.

examples.japanese: 世間とはこうしたものさ。
examples.english: That's the way things are.

examples.japanese: 気にすることはないさ。
examples.english: You don't need to worry about it.

meaning: to seem to be; to appear; to behave as ~
structure: さも + sentence + (そうに/そうな)sentence + (ように/ような)

examples.japanese: 彼はさもおいしそうにビールを飲みほした。
examples.english: He drank up beer deliciously.

examples.japanese: 子供はさも眠そうな様子で、大きなあくびをした。
examples.english: With a seemingly sleepy appearance, the baby let out a big yawn

examples.japanese: 彼はさも満足そうに微笑した。
examples.english: He smiled, appearing to be satisfied.

examples.japanese: その少年はさもおいしそうに食べ始めた。
examples.english: The boy started eating as if the food was truly delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼はさも満足そうにでき上がった作を眺めいた。
examples.english: He looked at the finished work with apparent satisfaction.

examples.japanese: あの老人はさもがっかりの様子で立ち去った。
examples.english: The old man left, looking disappointed.

meaning: or; otherwise
structure: Sentence 1 + さもないとさもなければ + Sentence 2

examples.japanese: 急ぎなさい！さもないとあなたは学校に遅れるでしょう。
examples.english: Hurry up! Otherwise you will be late for school.

examples.japanese: スノースーツを着なさい、さもないとと風邪を引きますよ。
examples.english: Put on your snowsuit, or you'll get cold.

examples.japanese: 肉を冷蔵庫に入れなさい。さもないと腐るよ。
examples.english: Put the meat in the fridge. Otherwise it will rot.

examples.japanese: 一生懸命勉強しなさい、さもないと試験に落ちるぞ。
examples.english: Study hard, otherwise you will fail the exam.

examples.japanese: すぐ起きなさい、さもないと７時のバスに乗り遅れますよ。
examples.english: Get up right away, or you'll miss the 7 o'clock bus.

examples.japanese: すぐに医者を呼びに言ってくれ、さもないと患者はもっと悪化するだろう。
examples.english: Call the doctor right away, or the patient will get worse.

meaning: (1) surely..., but ~; although... is likely, ~ (2) should have (regret); might / must have been ~
structure: さぞ（かし） + phrase

examples.japanese: お父さんが病気になって、さぞご心配だろう。
examples.english: Thair father got sick and they surely must be worried.

examples.japanese: あなたはそんな狭い家で住んでいて、さぞ大変でしょうね。
examples.english: It must be hard for you living in such a small house.

examples.japanese: 君の成功を聞けばご両親はさぞお喜びになるでしょう。
examples.english: Your parents will surely be delighted to hear about your success.

examples.japanese: そんな大きな量で食べられるとは、さぞかし彼はお腹がすいていたんでしょう。
examples.english: He must have been hungry to be able to eat such a large amount.

examples.japanese: こんなにすばらしい本を書くとは、著者はさぞかしりっぱな学者だろう。
examples.english: To write such a wonderful book, the author must be a splendid scholar.

examples.japanese: あんなにかわいがっていた子供を失って、さぞ悲しいことだろう。
examples.english: It must be truly sad to lose such a beloved child.

meaning: to get stuck with; to end up with (something unpleasant)
structure: Verb (dictionary form) + （という） + 始末だ | この / その / あの

examples.japanese: うちの娘は、ダイエットのしすぎで病気になり、入院する始末だ。
examples.english: My daughter got sick from dieting too much and as a result she ended up in the hospital.

examples.japanese: 昔はお金がなくて、電気や水道も止められる始末だった。
examples.english: In the past I had so little money that my electricity and water were cut off.

examples.japanese: 試験の前に何も復習しなくて、ゲームばかりして、赤点をもらう始末だ。
examples.english: Before the exam I didn’t study anything and only played games. As a result, I got a bad score.

examples.japanese: 彼女はちゃんと勉強せず、バイトするばかりで、留年する始末だ。
examples.english: She did not study properly and only focused on part-time work. As a result, she had to repeat a year of school.

examples.japanese: 人を信じすぎた私、何度も騙される始末で、もう目が覚めた。
examples.english: After believing in people too much and being deceived countless times, I finally came to my senses.

examples.japanese: 彼は遅刻してきたくせに早退したいと言い出す始末でやる気があるのか疑問である。
examples.english: Considering he arrived late and said he wants to leave early, I am in doubt of his motivation.

meaning: as soon as; the moment ~
structure: Verb (dictionary form)Verb (た form) + そばから

examples.japanese: 名前を聞いたそばから忘れてしまう。
examples.english: I forget names almost instantly after I hear them.

examples.japanese: 田中さん、注意したそばから間違えてるよ。
examples.english: Tanaka makes the mistakes right after I warn him.

examples.japanese: お給料はもらったそばから、なくなっていく。どこに消えるんだろう．．．
examples.english: As soon as I receive my salary, it all disappears. I wonder where it all goes...?

examples.japanese: 彼女は「今日からダイエットする」と言ったそばから、カフェでアイスを食べていた。
examples.english: Right after she said "I'm going on a diet from today", she was eating ice cream at a cafe.

examples.japanese: うちの子は、片付けているそばから部屋を散らかしてしまう。
examples.english: Our child messes up the room as soon as we finish cleaning it.

examples.japanese: 教わったそばから忘れないようにちゃんとメモを取ろう。
examples.english: Make sure to take some notes so you don't forget what you learn right after I teach you.

meaning: as an opportunity/chance to ~
structure: Verb (stem form) ます + そびれる

examples.japanese: 遅刻して飛行機に乗りそびれた。
examples.english: I was late and missed the plane.

examples.japanese: 今朝は忙しくて、朝食を食べそびれてしまった。
examples.english: I was so busy this morning that I missed breakfast.

examples.japanese: 質問しようと思ったけど、緊張で言いそびれてしまった。
examples.english: I was going to ask a question, but I was so nervous that I missed the opportunity to say it.

examples.japanese: バスが混んでて降りそびれてしまった。
examples.english: The bus was so crowded that I missed the opportunity to get off the bus.

examples.japanese: ラジオで彼らの音楽がかかってたんだけど、バンド名を聞きそびれてしまった。
examples.english: Their music is playing on the radio, but I missed the chance to hear the band's name.

examples.japanese: 彼女に謝るつもりだったが, 言いそびれてしまった.
examples.english: I was going to apologize to her, but I missed the chance.

pattern: 損なう / 損ねる / 損じる
meaning: to miss a chance; to fail to do ~
structure: Verb (ます stem) ます + 損なう（そこなう）損ねる（そこねる）損じる（そんじる）

examples.japanese: 逃げた飼い犬を捕まえ損ねた。
examples.english: I failed to catch my pet dog that ran away.

examples.japanese: 昨日は大好きなアイドルのライブを聞き損なった。
examples.english: I missed the live performance of my favorite idol yesterday.

examples.japanese: 事故で入院したから、友人の結婚式を出損じた。
examples.english: I missed my friend's wedding because I was hospitalized in an accident.

examples.japanese: バスのスケジュールが間違えたから、最後のバスに乗り損ねてしまった。
examples.english: I missed the last bus because I messed up the bus schedule.

examples.japanese: 注意しなくては駄目だよ、さもないとまたやり損なうよ。
examples.english: You have to be careful, otherwise you'll make a mistake again.

examples.japanese: 突然パソコンが動かなくなって、ファイルを保存し損ねた。
examples.english: Suddenly my computer stopped working and I failed to save the file.

meaning: nothing but; none other than ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + 術がない

examples.japanese: こんなに壊れては、もう直す術がない。
examples.english: If it breaks like this, there is no way to fix it.

examples.japanese: 彼の電話番号を知らないので、連絡する術がない。
examples.english: I don't know his phone number, so I have no way of contacting him.

examples.japanese: 彼の言った事は全部噓だと知っているが、証明する術がない。
examples.english: I know everything he said is a lie, but there is no way to prove it.

examples.japanese: 地震や津波などの自然災害に、人類は成す術がない。
examples.english: There is no way for humankind to deal with natural disasters such as earthquakes and tsunamis.

examples.japanese: もう癌は全身に転移しているので、治す術がありません。
examples.english: The cancer has spread throughout the body and there is no cure.

examples.japanese: いつ地震が起こるか、誰にも予測できる術がない。
examples.english: No one can predict when an earthquake will occur.

meaning: even; even if/though ~
structure: Noun + （で）すら（に）すら

examples.japanese: こんな問題、小学生すらわかるよ。
examples.english: Even an elementary school kid would know this kind of problem.

examples.japanese: 喉が痛くて、水すら飲めない。
examples.english: My throat hurts so much I can't even drink water.

examples.japanese: この悩みは家族にすら言えない。
examples.english: I can't talk about this problem to anyone, even my family.

examples.japanese: 盗みが悪いことであるのは、小さい子供ですら知っている。
examples.english: Even small children know that stealing is something bad.

examples.japanese: 結婚なんてとんでもない。私は男の人と話したことすらないのです。
examples.english: Getting married is out of the question. I've never even talked to a man before.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、大学教授ですら気が付かなかった問題点を指摘しました。
examples.english: She pointed out problems that even university professors had not noticed.

pattern: た弾みに / た拍子に
meaning: because; since ~
structure: Verb (た form) + 弾みに（はずみに）拍子に（ひょうしに）

examples.japanese: くしゃみをした拍子にメガネが落ちた。
examples.english: The moment they sneezed, their glasses fell off.

examples.japanese: 持ち上げた弾みに、買い物袋が破れた。
examples.english: The moment I lifted it up, the shopping bag ripped apart.

examples.japanese: ぶつかった弾みに、棚に置いた本が落ちてしまった。
examples.english: When I accidentaly bumped into the shelf, the book sitting on top of it fell over.

examples.japanese: よろけた拍子に、隣の人の足を踏んでしまった。
examples.english: When I stumbled, I accidentally stepped on the foot of the person next to me.

examples.japanese: 人とぶつかった拍子に、持っていたスマホを落としてしまった。
examples.english: I dropped my smartphone when I bumped into someone.

examples.japanese: 後ろから誰かに押された弾みに、靴が脱げてしまった。
examples.english: Being pushed from behind by someone caused my shoes to come off.

pattern: たことにする / たことになる
meaning: to pretend; to act as if ~
structure: Verb (た form) + （という）ことにする（という）ことになる | Noun +（だ） | な-adjective +（だ） | い-adjective (た form)

examples.japanese: それは無かったことにして下さい。
examples.english: Please just pretend that didn't happen.

examples.japanese: この話は聞かなかったことにしてください。
examples.english: Please pretend as if you did not hear anything.

examples.japanese: 夫の不倫を見なかったことにする。
examples.english: I decided that I will pretend I did not see my husband's affair.

examples.japanese: 風邪だということにして学校を休んだ。
examples.english: I pretended to have a cold and took a break from school.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、大学を卒業したことになっているけれど、実際は中退したらしい。
examples.english: She is supposed to have graduated from college, but she seems to have dropped out.

examples.japanese: 友達が書いたレポートを、自分が書いたことにして提出した。
examples.english: I submitted a report written by a friend as if I had written it.

meaning: even if; even though; despite ~
structure: Verb (た form) + ところで

examples.japanese: どんなに走ったところで、絶対に間に合わないだろう。
examples.english: Even if I run, there's no way I'd make it in time.

examples.japanese: 何回読んだところで、意味は全く理解できない。
examples.english: Even if I read it numerous times, I wouldn't be able to understand anything.

examples.japanese: その学校は、卒業したところで、いい就職先はないだろう。
examples.english: Even if I graduate from that school, it's doubtful there are any good work opportunities after that.

examples.japanese: 怒ったところで、何も解決しないし、まずは落ち着いて話をきこう。
examples.english: Being upset won't help resolve anything. First calm down and then let's hear what you have to say.

examples.japanese: そんな多額の借金は、家を売ったところで、到底返せない。
examples.english: With such a large amount of debt, even if I sold my house, I wouldn't be able to pay it off.

examples.japanese: 試験はもう終わったんだし、後悔したところで結果は何も変わらないよ。
examples.english: The test is already over. Even if you have regrets now, that won't change the results at all.

meaning: always; never stop; can’t help but ~
structure: Verb (た form) + ためしがない

examples.japanese: そんな事は今までに聞いたためしがない。
examples.english: I've never heard of such a thing.
