examples.japanese: 彼女は約束の時間を守ったためしがない。
examples.english: She has never kept her promised time.

examples.japanese: 宝くじをたくさん買ってきたが、今まで当たったためしがない。
examples.english: I bought a lot of lottery tickets, but I have never won.

examples.japanese: 彼はこの会社で10年間働いたけど、休暇を取ったためしがない。
examples.english: He worked for this company for 10 years and has never taken a vacation.

examples.japanese: 彼とはよく食事をするが、おごってくれたためしがない。
examples.english: I often go out to eat with him, but he has never paid for me.

examples.japanese: 毎月、寄付金を貰っているが、寄付の人に会ったためしがない。
examples.english: I get donations every month, but I have never met a donor.

meaning: if you do... negative result
structure: Verb (た) + ら + Verb (た) + で | Noun + なら + Noun + で | な-adj + なら + な-adj + で | い-adj + いかったら + い-adj + いかったで

examples.japanese: 失敗したらしたで、もう一度チャレンジすればいい。
examples.english: If you make a mistake, you can try again.

examples.japanese: 試験に落ちたら落ちたで、また来年受けるだけだ。
examples.english: If I fail the exam, I fail, and I'll just take it again next year.

examples.japanese: 大学に入ったら入ったで、お金がかかって大変だ。
examples.english: If you get into university, it costs money and is tough.

examples.japanese: もちろん、安く買えるほうがいいが、安かったら安かったで少し不安になる。
examples.english: Of course, it's better to buy it cheaper but if it's too cheap I'm a little worried.

examples.japanese: 便箋がなかったらないで、コピー用紙でも構わない。
examples.english: If there's no writing paper, then copy paper will work.

examples.japanese: 会社の飲み会は面倒だけど、行ったら、行ったで楽しい。
examples.english: The company drinking parties are a hassle, but when I go, it's fun.

meaning: at the most; no more than​; at best; roughly; about ~
structure: たらばなら + sentence + verb (casual) + ところだ

examples.japanese: もし遅刻しなければ、今頃ゆっくりお昼ご飯でも食べてるところだ。
examples.english: If I hadn't been late, I would probably be taking my time eating lunch right about now.

examples.japanese: パソコン修理してくれなかったら今頃買い替えていたところだ。
examples.english: If you hadn't fixed my computer, I would be buying a new one right about now.

examples.japanese: 友達が注意していただかなければ、間違えていたところだ。
examples.english: If it hadn't been for my friend warning me, I would have made a mistake.

examples.japanese: 先生がこのことを知ったら怒っているところだ。
examples.english: If my teacher knew about this, they would be angry.

examples.japanese: あの時に面接を合格したら、今は日本で留学しているところだ。
examples.english: If I had passed the interview at that time, I would be currently studying abroad in Japan.

examples.japanese: パスポートを落とさなかったら、今頃に東京の空港にいたところだ。
examples.english: If I hadn't dropped my passport, I would have been at the airport in Tokyo by this time.

meaning: even if I wanted to… I couldn’t ~
structure: 1 + classifier(日, 分, 秒, 瞬, 円, 匹, etc) + たりとも～ない

examples.japanese: 彼は１日たりとも、学校を休んだことがない。
examples.english: He has never missed even a day of school.

examples.japanese: １分たりとも遅刻は許しません。
examples.english: I will not allow you to be late for even a minute.

examples.japanese: 試験では一秒たりとも時間を無駄に使ってはいけません。
examples.english: You shouldn't waste even one second during the exam.

examples.japanese: 一日たりとも、日記を欠かしたことはない。
examples.english: I've never missed writing a single day in my diary.

examples.japanese: その店は、一円たりともまけてくれないよ。
examples.english: That shop is strict on their prices, and won't even drop a single yen.

examples.japanese: 試験まであと１週間。今は１日たりとも無駄にできない。
examples.english: There's one week left until the exam. I can't waste even a day now.

meaning: of all people (expression showing surprise at a high standing person's misbehavior)
structure: Noun + たるものたる

examples.japanese: 医者たるもの、患者の命を優先に考えるべきだ。
examples.english: As a doctor, you should give priority to the life of the patient.

examples.japanese: 教師たるもの、学生の見本となるような行動すべきだ。
examples.english: As a teacher, you should act as a model for students.

examples.japanese: 警察官たるもの、市民の安全を守るべきだ。
examples.english: As a police officer, you should protect the safety of the citizens.

examples.japanese: 親たるもの、子どもが悪いことをしたときに、きちんと叱るべきだ。
examples.english: As a parent, one should properly discipline their children when they misbehave.

examples.japanese: 大学生たるものが、パソコンを使えないのは恥ずかしい。
examples.english: It's embarrassing for college students to not be able to use a computer.

examples.japanese: 一国の大統領たるものが、このような発言をしてはいけない。
examples.english: The president of a country must not make such a statement.

meaning: cannot bring oneself (to do); unable to bear ~
structure: Verb (て form) + （は）かなわない | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + い + くて

examples.japanese: 隣の工事がうるさくて敵わない。
examples.english: I can't stand the noise of the construction site next door.

examples.japanese: N1の問題は難しくて敵わない。でも、勉強するしかない。
examples.english: The questions in N1 are difficult beyond my ability. But I have no choice but to study.

examples.japanese: 私の家は駅から遠くて不便で敵わない。
examples.english: My house is far from the station and unbearably inconvenient.

examples.japanese: ダイエットをしているのに、美味しいケーキを見たら我慢されては敵わない。
examples.english: Even though I'm on a diet, I can't stand it when I see a delicious looking cake.

examples.japanese: 夏休みは旅行に行きたかったけど、チケットが高くてはかなわない。
examples.english: I wanted to go on a trip during the summer vacation, but the tickets are too expensive.

examples.japanese: この席はドアが開く度に冷たい風が入ってくるので、寒くて敵わない。
examples.english: This seat has a cold breeze every time the door opens, so it's cold but it can't be helped.

meaning: sufficient by; no problem to; resolve by ~
structure: Verb (て form) + みせる

examples.japanese: 今度の試験には、絶対合格してみせるよ。
examples.english: I will definitely pass the next exam.

examples.japanese: 将来必ず有名なピアニストになってみせる。
examples.english: I will definitely become a famous pianist in the future.

examples.japanese: 僕は小説を書いて賞をを取ってみせる。
examples.english: I’ll write a novel and definitely win an award.

examples.japanese: 今年の旧正月前に絶対、新しい仕事ゲットしてみせる。
examples.english: I will definitely get a new job before this year's Lunar New Year.

examples.japanese: 彼は、一か月以内に結婚相手を見つけてみせると宣言した。
examples.english: He declared that he would definitely find a marriage partner within a month.

examples.japanese: やり方がわからないので、一度やってみせてくれませんか。
examples.english: I don't know how to do it, so can you please show me?

meaning: must not; should not; do not ~
structure: Verb (て form) + しかるべきだ

examples.japanese: 後輩なら先輩に敬語を使ってしかるべきだ。
examples.english: If you are a junior, you should use honorifics towards your seniors.

examples.japanese: 退学する前に、親と相談してしかるべきだ。
examples.english: You should consult with your parents before leaving school.

examples.japanese: この小説はもっと評価されてしかるべきだ。こんなに面白い本は読んだことがない。
examples.english: This novel should be acknowledged more. I've never read such an interesting book.

examples.japanese: この道には車がたくさん通っているのだから、信号があってしかるべきだ。
examples.english: There are a lot of cars passing through this road, so it's only natural there should be a traffic light.

examples.japanese: 優秀な学生には奨学金が与えられてしかるべきだ。
examples.english: Excellent students should be given scholarships.

examples.japanese: 老人のための国立の病院がもっとあってしかるべきだ。
examples.english: There should be more national hospitals for the elderly.

meaning: it doesn’t end with just ~; it will take more than ~
structure: Verb (て form) + 済むことではない済む問題ではない | Noun + で

examples.japanese: 人のカメラを壊して、弁償で済むことではないよ。君はちゃんと謝らないと。
examples.english: After breaking someone's camera, you can't just resolve it by paying compensation. You also have to properly apologize.

examples.japanese: それは謝罪と賠償だけで済む問題ではないと思う。
examples.english: I don't think that can be resolved with just an apology and compensation.

examples.japanese: 大事な書類をなくしてしまうなんて、謝って済むことではない。
examples.english: After losing important documents, apologizing isn't going to resolve anything.

examples.japanese: この問題は補償金で済むことではない。心からの謝罪が必要だ。
examples.english: This problem cannot be solved with just compensation. It is necessary to sincerely apologize from the heart.

examples.japanese: その事件は一人が責任を取って辞めて済むことではない。
examples.english: This case cannot be resolved simply by one person accepting responsibility and quitting their job.

examples.japanese: 被害者にお金を返して済むことではない。彼のやったことは逮捕されると思う。
examples.english: Just returning the money to the victim will not resolve this case. I think they will be arrested for what they did.

meaning: can't bear to; unable to; troublesome to; can’t stand to ~
structure: Verb (て form) + やまない

examples.japanese: 僕は君たちの合格を願ってやまない。
examples.english: I'm always wishing for your success.

examples.japanese: 親は子供の将来を期待してやまないものだ。
examples.english: Parents always have high expectation for their kids’ future.

examples.japanese: 地震で全員が無事を祈ってやまない。
examples.english: I always wish for everyone's safety during an earthquake.

examples.japanese: ご結婚おめでとうございます。お二人の幸せを願ってやまない。
examples.english: Congratulations on your wedding. I wish you both happiness.

examples.japanese: 息子が外国に住むと親は心配してやまない。
examples.english: When one's son lives abroad, their parent will always be worried.

examples.japanese: 事故にあった方々の一日でも早い回復を祈ってやまない。
examples.english: I never stop praying for the quick recovery of those who have had an accident.

meaning: of all people (expression showing surprise at a high standing person's misbehavior)
structure: Verb (casual) + 手前 | Noun + の

examples.japanese: 自分が一番若い手前、皆のお茶を入れるのは当然だ。
examples.english: Since I am the youngest, it is only natural that I am the one who prepare's everyone's tea.

examples.japanese: 熱があるから学校を休むと言ってしまった手前、外に出て誰かに見られてはまずい。
examples.english: Considering I said I couldn't go to school because I have a fever, it would be bad if someone spotted me going outside.

examples.japanese: お任せしますと言った手前、友達が買ってきた弁当が嫌とは言えなかった。
examples.english: Since I left it up to my friend's judgement, I can't say that I don't like the bento lunch box he bought for me.

examples.japanese: この仕事は先生に紹介してもらった手前、すぐにはやめることはできない。
examples.english: Considering my teacher introduced this job to me, there's now way I can quit right away.

examples.japanese: 約束した手前、たとえ雪が降っても行かないわけにはいかない。
examples.english: Considering you made a promise, even if it for example it snows, you must still go.

examples.japanese: 子供たちの手前、この事を知らないとは言えない。
examples.english: For the children, they can't say they don't know about this.

meaning: to also be; both… and ~
structure: Verb (て form) + も差し支えないもさしつかえない | Noun + で | な-adjective + で | い-adjective + いくて

examples.japanese: お返事は明日でも差し支えない。
examples.english: You can reply tomorrow.

examples.japanese: その書類は印鑑がなくても差し支えない。
examples.english: That document does not have an official stamp (inkan).

examples.japanese: この内容なら、そのまま放送しても差し支えない。
examples.english: With this content, you can broadcast it as it is.

examples.japanese: 途中で参加でも差し支えない。
examples.english: It doesn't matter if you join in the middle (of the event).

examples.japanese: お支払いは、商品が届いた後でも差し支えない。
examples.english: You can pay after the goods arrive.

examples.japanese: 申込用紙はコピーでも差し支えない。
examples.english: A copy of the application form is also acceptable.

meaning: because; since ~
structure: Noun + と/が/も + 相まってあいまって

examples.japanese: 空の青と相まって、紅葉がより美しく見える。
examples.english: The fall colours look more beautiful with the blue sky.

examples.japanese: 努力と運が相まって、合格することができた。
examples.english: Combining effort and luck, I was able to pass the exam.

examples.japanese: この冷蔵庫はデザインのよさも相まってよく売れている。
examples.english: This refrigerator is selling well due to its good design.

examples.japanese: 青い空と湖が相まって、富士山がとても美しいです。
examples.english: The blue sky and the lake together make Mt. Fuji even more beautiful.

examples.japanese: このエビチリはエビの甘さとソースの辛さが相まって、とても美味しいです。
examples.english: This chili shrimp dish is very delicious due to the sweetness of the shrimp and the spiciness of the sauce.

examples.japanese: 昨日は休日と久しぶりの晴天が相まって、遊園地はとても混んでいた。
examples.english: The amusement park was very crowded yesterday due to the combination of it being a holiday and the first sunny day in a long time.

meaning: if you ask; if one may say ~
structure: Verb (casual) + と言えなくもない | Noun +（だ/である） | な-adjective +（だ/である） | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: ８時起床は早起きと言えなくもない。
examples.english: Getting up at 8 o'clock can be said to be an early riser.

examples.japanese: 彼女は遠目から見ると、あのアイドルに似ていると言えなくもない。
examples.english: From a distance, she can be said to resemble that idol.

examples.japanese: このテストで人の知能指数を分かると言えなくもない。
examples.english: It can be said that this test shows a person's IQ.

examples.japanese: 道に迷うのは旅の楽しみの一つと言えなくもない。
examples.english: It could be said that getting lost is one of the pleasures of traveling.

examples.japanese: 今朝のはこの冬一番の積雪と言えなくもない。
examples.english: It can be said that this morning is the most snowfall this winter.

examples.japanese: 月収から見ると、私の彼氏の給料はまあまあ高いと言えなくもない。
examples.english: From looking at the monthly income, my boyfriend's salary can be said to be reasonably high.

meaning: completely; entirely; nothing but ~
structure: Noun + という + (same) noun

examples.japanese: 津波によって家という家が全て流されてしまった。
examples.english: The tsunami washed away all the houses (leaving none behind).

examples.japanese: 大雪で東京に行くの電車という電車が中止されている。
examples.english: All trains heading towards Tokyo have been canceled due to heavy snow.

examples.japanese: 家に変な匂いがこもったので、窓という窓を全部開けた。
examples.english: I had a strange smell in my house, so I opened every single window.

examples.japanese: 息子の部屋は壁という壁に車のポスターが貼ってある。
examples.english: The walls of my son's room are covered with car posters.

examples.japanese: チラシをこの地域の家という家に配って歩いた。
examples.english: I delivered flyers to every single house in this area.

examples.japanese: 今日という今日は、この仕事をやり遂げなければならない。
examples.english: I must finish this work today!

meaning: at the most; no more than​; at best; roughly; about ~
structure: Verb (casual) + というか + Verb (casual) + というか | Noun + Noun | な-adj + な-adj | い-adj + い-adj

examples.japanese: 気温が低すぎて、寒いというか痛い。
examples.english: The temperature is too low. It's more painful than cold.

examples.japanese: あんこが好きというか、ないと生きていけない。
examples.english: I really like "anko" (sweet red bean paste), or rather I should say I can't live without it.

examples.japanese: それは、面白いというか、珍しいというか、とにかく変わったものだ。
examples.english: That's interesting, or rather it's rare. In any case, it's strange.

examples.japanese: たぶん行かないと思う。というか、お金がないから、行けない。
examples.english: I don't think I will go. Or rather I should say I don't have any money and so I can't go.

examples.japanese: 私は合格したが、親友は不合格だった。嬉しいというか、残念というか、複雑な気持ちだ。
examples.english: I passed the exam, but my best friend did not. I'm happy, or perhaps I should say I'm sad. It's a complicated feeling.

examples.japanese: あんなところに一人で行くなんて、無茶というか、無知というか、彼女のすることは理解できません。
examples.english: To go somewhere like that alone, she is either crazy or ignorant. I can't understand her actions.

meaning: through; by way of; after; via ~
structure: Noun (time unit) + というもの

examples.japanese: この一週間というもの、そればっかりです。
examples.english: We've had nothing else this past week

examples.japanese: 引っ越ししてからのこの１週間というもの、ずっと荷物の整理をしている。
examples.english: I've been organizing my luggage for the past week since I moved.

examples.japanese: 彼女は3年間というもの、完全に自分の小説を書くことに没頭した。
examples.english: For three years she was completely absorbed in writing her novel.

examples.japanese: この１週間というもの、納期が近いので残業が続いている。
examples.english: Overtime has continued for the past week because the delivery date is near.

examples.japanese: この一ヶ月間というもの、仕事が忙しくて朝ごはんをろくに食べていない。
examples.english: I haven't properly eaten breakfast for the past month because I've been busy with work.

examples.japanese: この４０年というもの、私は家族のために、会社のために毎日一生懸命働いてきた。
examples.english: For the last 40 years, I have worked hard every day for my family and for my company.

pattern: というところだ / といったところだ
meaning: about; roughly; generally; approximately; completely​ ~
structure: Noun + というところだといったところだってところだ

examples.japanese: 彼女は多く見ても２０歳というところだ。
examples.english: She is 20 years old at most.

examples.japanese: ジムに行くのは週2、3回というところだ。
examples.english: I go to the gym at best 2 to 3 times a week.

examples.japanese: 日本語の勉強時間は2、3時間というところだ。
examples.english: The time I spend studying Japanese is no more than 2 to 3 hours each day.

examples.japanese: 時給は850円から1,000円というところだ。
examples.english: The hourly wage is from 850 to no more than 1,000 yen.

examples.japanese: 明日の気温は２０度から３０度といったところです。
examples.english: Tomorrow's temperature will be around 20 to 30 degrees Celsius.

examples.japanese: 毎日の勉強時間は1～2時間というところなんですが、もう少し増やすべきでしょうか。
examples.english: I spend roughly 1~2 hours studying every day, but perhaps I should increase it a little more?

meaning: it’s not that; it doesn’t mean that ~
structure: Phrase + というわけだというわけです

examples.japanese: それが私たちの目的というわけです。
examples.english: That is our goal.

examples.japanese: じゃあ、あと１時間ぐらいはいられるというわけですね。
examples.english: So this means you will still be around for another hour or so?

examples.japanese: あの男と結婚するというわけだね。
examples.english: In other words you plan to marry that man?

examples.japanese: 結局は損をせずにすんだというわけだ。
examples.english: The fortuante part of this was that I got off without any loss.

examples.japanese: それで君は全ての役割をはたして、私が感謝するというわけだ。
examples.english: Then you will have played your part and earned my gratitude completely.

examples.japanese: A：来年度から始業時間が３０分早くなるらしいよ。B：じゃあ、今９時だから、８時半になるというわけですね。
examples.english: A: It seems that the start time will be 30 minutes earlier from next year.B: It's 9 o'clock now, so that means it will be 8:30, right?.

meaning: that's why; no wonder; this means; it is the case that ~
structure: Verb (casual) + というわけではないというわけでもない | Noun | な-adjective + だ | い-adjective

examples.japanese: それは全くウソというわけではない。
examples.english: That's not entirely false.

examples.japanese: 私はこのプラン全体に反対というわけではない。
examples.english: I'm not entirely against this plan..

examples.japanese: 彼はお金がないというわけではない。ただケチなだけだ。
examples.english: He is not without money. He's just stingy.

examples.japanese: 両方とも好きというわけではない。
examples.english: I don't like either of them.

examples.japanese: 彼女は金があってもそれだけ幸福というわけではない。
examples.english: She's none the happier for her wealth.

examples.japanese: どんな場合にもこの規則が適用できるというわけではない。
examples.english: This rule does not necessarily apply to every case.

meaning: all; every single ~ (no exceptions)
structure: Noun-1 + といわず + Noun-2 + といわず

examples.japanese: 顔といわず、手といわず泥まみれだ。
examples.english: Their face and hands and everything are covered in mud.

examples.japanese: 晴れといわず雨といわずジョギングをしている。
examples.english: Rain or sunshine or whatever the weather may be, I always go jogging.

examples.japanese: 社長は平日といわず週末といわず仕事をしている。
examples.english: The company president is always working, both on weekdays and on weekends.

examples.japanese: 僕は、鶏肉といわず、牛肉といわず、肉は食べません。
examples.english: I don't eat meat of any kind, be it chicken, beef, or whatever.

examples.japanese: 日本人は、子どもといわず、大人といわず、漫画をよく読みます。
examples.english: Japanese people, both children and adults, love to read comics.

examples.japanese: お隣の赤ちゃんは、昼といわず、夜といわず、一日中よく泣いている。
examples.english: The baby next door is always crying all day long, both day and night.

meaning: at the sight of; upon seeing; after confirming ~
structure: Verb (casual) + とみると | Noun +（だ） | な-adjective | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: 彼女は、店員が中国人だとみると、中国語で話しかける。
examples.english: After realizing the shop staff is Chinese, she speaks to them in Chinese.

examples.japanese: 本格的なイタリア料理屋ではないとみると、彼女はガッカリしていて、少ししか食べなかった。
examples.english: After realizing that it wasn't a full-fledged Italian restaurant, she was disappointed and only ate a little.

examples.japanese: 妹は、男の人にお金げないとみると、急にその人に興味がなくなるようだ。
examples.english: As soon as she notices that a man has no money, she loses interest.

examples.japanese: 困難になっている人とみると、必ず助けてあげたくなる。
examples.english: After realizing someone is in trouble, I definitely want to help them right away.

examples.japanese: 同僚は問題がちょっと難しいとみると、自分で考えないで人に聞く。
examples.english: As soon as my colleague finds a question a little difficult, he ask others for help without thinking for himself.

examples.japanese: 私はただ建前のことしか言わない人とみると、相手と付き合いたくなくなるタイプだ。
examples.english: I'm the type of person who doesn't want to hang out with other people after realizing they never share their private thoughts with me and only show me their public face (tatemae).

pattern: となると / となれば
meaning: at / on / under certain conditions (time, position, age, number of times)
structure: Verb (casual) + と（も）なるとと（も）なればとなったら | Noun | な-adjective | い-adjective

examples.japanese: いざ出発となると、不安になってきた。
examples.english: When it came time to leave, I became anxious.

examples.japanese: 彼はとてもいいひとですが結婚となると、ちょっと頼りない気がする。
examples.english: He is a very nice person, but when it comes to marriage, he feels a little unreliable.

examples.japanese: あのような一流レストランともなると、男性はネクタイが必要です。
examples.english: When it comes to such a top-notch restaurant, men need to wear a tie.

examples.japanese: 銀行でお金を借りるとなれば、手続きが大変です。
examples.english: When it comes to borrowing money at a bank, the procedure is difficult.

examples.japanese: 今年、JLPT N1を受けるとなると、今の２倍は勉強しなければならないだろう。
examples.english: If you will take JLPT N1 this year, you will have to study twice as much as you do now.

examples.japanese: これ以上、消費税率が上がるとなると、国民の生活はますます厳しくなるだろう。
examples.english: If the consumption tax rate rises any further, people's lives will become more difficult.

meaning: (those) who are; (that) which is; in the capacity of ... should ~
structure: Noun + ともあろう（ものが）ともあろう（人が）

examples.japanese: 弁護士ともあろうものが、犯罪に関わっていたなんて。
examples.english: Of all people, for a lawyer to be connected with a crime...

examples.japanese: 社長ともあろう者が、遅刻なんてありえないよ。
examples.english: For the company president, tardiness is unimaginable.

examples.japanese: 教師ともあろうものが、教え子に手を出すとは。
examples.english: Of all people, for a teacher to strike their student...

examples.japanese: 公務員ともあろう者が、副業だなんて許されません。
examples.english: For a public official of all people to have a side business is unforgivable.

examples.japanese: 親ともあろう者が、子供に暴力を振るうなんてどういうことですか。
examples.english: As a parent, what are you thinking by resorting to violence with your children?

examples.japanese: 数学の教師ともあろう者が、こんな問題も解けないなんて恥ずかしいよ。
examples.english: It's embarrassing that even a math teacher can't solve such a problem.

pattern: ともなく / ともなしに
meaning: have no intention to / didn't mean to ~
structure: 1) + Verb (dictionary) + ともなくともなしに | 2) + interrogative word + (particle)疑問詞 ＋ (助詞)

examples.japanese: 休みの日にはどこへ行くともなしにドライブすることが多い。
examples.english: On my days off, I often drive without any destination in mind.

examples.japanese: チラシを見るともなく見ていたら、友達が映っていた。
examples.english: Without looking intentionally, I somehow noticed a flyer that my friend appeared on.

examples.japanese: 何を買うともなく、デパートの中をブラブラしていたら、友人に会った。
examples.english: I met a friend when I was wandering around the department store without any particular intention of buying anything.

examples.japanese: テレビを見るともなしに見ていたら、知り合いがテレビに出ていて驚いた。
examples.english: Without any intention to watch TV, I noticed an acquaintance of mine appear on the TV and was surprised!

examples.japanese: どこからともなく彼が現れた。
examples.english: He suddenly appeared out of nowhere.

examples.japanese: 鳥の鳴き声がどこからともなく聞こえてくる。
examples.english: I started hearing a bird singing, not knowing where it was singing from.

meaning: bad habit; to have a tendency to ~
structure: ともすれば + clause

examples.japanese: 彼はともすれば子どもに甘かった。
examples.english: He tended to be lenient toward the children.

examples.japanese: 僕は冬にともすればインフルエンザになりがちである。
examples.english: I tend to get the flu in winter.

examples.japanese: 政府はともすればマスメディアを統制したがる。
examples.english: The government tends to control the media.

examples.japanese: 休みの日はとても長く感じ、ともすればお酒ばかり飲んでしまいがちだ。
examples.english: Holidays feel very long, and I tend to drink only alcohol.

examples.japanese: 何やら外では雪が降っている。ともすれば明日の運動会は中止になりそうだ。
examples.english: Somehow it's snowing outside. It looks like tomorrow's athletic meet may be canceled.

examples.japanese: 私たちは解決策を出さないと、ともすれば大きなトラブルに発展する可能性があります。
examples.english: If we don't come up with a solution, it can lead to major troubles.

meaning: as soon as one realizes ..., then ~
structure: とっさに + action

examples.japanese: 地震が起きた時にとっさにテーブルの下に逃げた。
examples.english: When the earthquake struck, I quickly ran under the table.

examples.japanese: 石が落ちてきたので、とっさに頭をかばった。
examples.english: As the stones fell, I immediately covered my head.

examples.japanese: その犬を避けようと彼はとっさに車の進路を変えた。
examples.english: He quickly changed the course of his car to avoid the dog.

examples.japanese: 彼はとっさにハンドルを左に切って衝突を免れた。
examples.english: He quickly turned the steering wheel to the left and escaped the collision.

examples.japanese: 秘密の計画が彼女にばれそうになり、とっさにうそをついてしまった。
examples.english: She was about to find out about my secret plan, so I quickly told a lie.

examples.japanese: トラックが急に曲がって来たのでとっさに右に曲がった。
examples.english: The truck suddenly turned, so I immediately turned to the right.

pattern: とは比べものにならない
meaning: unlike; totally different; very different from ~
structure: Noun + とは比べものにならない

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人で英語もぺらぺらだし、とても私とは比べものにならないです。
examples.english: She is beautiful and fluent in English, so I can't even compare to her.

examples.japanese: 私の料理はお母さんとは比べものにならない。
examples.english: My cooking skill cannot compare with my mother's.

examples.japanese: 今の車の性能は、昔とは比べものにならない。
examples.english: Cars these days are much more fuel efficient than they were in the past.

examples.japanese: 彼はとても優秀で、お前とは比べものにならないよ。
examples.english: He is so outstanding, how can he be compared to you.

examples.japanese: 例年とは比べものにならないほど楽しい夏休みを過ごした。
examples.english: I had a summer vacation that was incomparably more enjoyable than usual.

examples.japanese: 彼の練習の時間は、他の選手とは比べものにならない。
examples.english: His practice time is incomparable to other players.

pattern: とは打って変わって / とは打って変わり
meaning: I didn't know; I was surprised that; the fact that ~
structure: Noun + とはうってかわってとはうってかわり

examples.japanese: 昔とは打って変わり、今の僕の村は大きいな家がたくさんあります。
examples.english: Unlike the old days, my village now has a lot of big houses.

examples.japanese: 父は若い時とは打って変わって、とても優しくなった。
examples.english: Unlike when my father was young, now he is very kind.

examples.japanese: 行きとは打って変わり、帰りは新幹線で快適だ。
examples.english: We went back by shinkansen, which was completely different and very comfortable.

examples.japanese: 今日の株価は、昨日とは打って変わって上昇傾向にある。
examples.english: Today's stock price is on the rise, unlike yesterday.

examples.japanese: 試験前の友人は、いつもとは打って変わって真面目に授業を聞いている。
examples.english: My good friend was seriously paying attention in class before the exam, which is completely different from usual.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに友人と会ったら、彼女は以前とは打って変わってオシャレな格好をしていた。
examples.english: When I met my friend for the first time in a long time, she looked completely different and more fashionable than before.

meaning: compared to; in contrast to; unlike; while; whereas ~
structure: Verb (stem) ます + つ + Verb (stem) ます + つ

examples.japanese: たくさんの亀が池の中を浮きつ沈みつしている。
examples.english: Many turtles are floating and sinking in the pond.

examples.japanese: どうしても欲しいゲームがあって、店の前を行きつ戻りつした。
examples.english: There was a game I really wanted, and I went back and forth in front of the store.

examples.japanese: 今日のレースでは、二人の選手が最後まで抜きつ抜かれつ一番争いをしていた。
examples.english: In today's race, the top two athletes kept changing positions fighting for the top spot.

examples.japanese: あのストーカーはカメラを持って、人気のアイドルの家の前を行きつ戻りつした。
examples.english: That stalker was walking back and forth holding his camera in front of a famous idol's house.

examples.japanese: 毎日押しつ押されつの満員電車に乗って会社に通うのは、正直しんどい。
examples.english: To be honest, it's hard to go to the office on a crowded train being pushed back and forth every day.

examples.japanese: 私と彼は持ちつ持たれつの関係で、子供のころからお互い助け合ってきました。
examples.english: He and I have been carrying each other and have helped each other since childhood.

meaning: the most / greatest … of all
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + 尽くすつくす

examples.japanese: 私は常に自分のベストをし尽くすようにしている。
examples.english: I always try to do my best.

examples.japanese: 彼は園芸の細かいことまで知り尽くす。
examples.english: He knows everything (all the details) about gardening.

examples.japanese: あれだけあった料理を彼は一人で食べ尽くした。
examples.english: He completely ate all that food by himself.

examples.japanese: 彼女が最善をやり尽くすだろうと思います。
examples.english: I think she will do her utmost best.

examples.japanese: 彼らはどちらも試合中ずっと全力をし尽くした。
examples.english: They all gave their best effort throughout the match.

examples.japanese: その医者たちは全力で患者を助け尽くしている。
examples.english: The doctors are doing their best to save the patient.

meaning: if only; I wish; I'm sorry it's not actually (regret)
structure: Phrase + ってばったら | Noun + (だ)な-adjective + (だ)

examples.japanese: ほんとだってば。彼女を見たんだ！
examples.english: I'm telling you it's true, I saw her!

examples.japanese: 遅いなあ。早くしてったら。
examples.english: You're so slow... Hurry up!

examples.japanese: そんなこと言われなくても、分かっているってば。
examples.english: There's no need to tell me that, I already know!

examples.japanese: ねえ、ねえってば。私の話、ちゃんと聞いてる？
examples.english: Hey, come on. Are you even listening to me?

examples.japanese: 分かったってば。うるさいなあ。
examples.english: I know that (already)! You're so annoying.

examples.japanese: まったくお兄ちゃんってば。
examples.english: Seriously big brother, what is your problem?

meaning: can't compare with ~
structure: Verb (casual) + うちに（は）入らない | Noun + の | な-adjective + な | い-adjective + い

examples.japanese: 日本語はちょっと複雑ですが、世界で一番難しい言語のうちに入らない。
examples.english: Japanese is a little complicated, but it is not one of the most difficult languages in the world.

examples.japanese: 毎日5つ単語を覚えるというだけでは、勉強のうちには入らない。
examples.english: Just memorizing five words every day is not enough to count as studying.

examples.japanese: あの頃の辛さと比べたら、今の状況は辛いうちに入らない。
examples.english: Compared to the pain of those days, the current situation cannot even be regarded as painful.

examples.japanese: このチャーハンの味はいいですが、美味しい料理のうちには入らない。
examples.english: The taste of this fried rice is good, but I can't say it qualifies as delicious food.

examples.japanese: 異性と二人で食事に行くのは浮気のうちに入らない。
examples.english: Going out for dinner with the opposite sex cannot be said to be infidelity.

examples.japanese: それだけしか食べないの？食べたうちに入らないよ。後でお腹空いちゃうよ。
examples.english: You're only eating that much? That amount doesn't really count as eating and you'll be hungry later.

meaning: not limited to; not only… but also ~
structure: Verb (dict.) + の/こと + はおろか + （もまですらさえ） | Noun

examples.japanese: 僕の地元はモールはおろかコンビニすらない。
examples.english: My hometown doesn't even have a convenience store, let alone a mall.

examples.japanese: 納豆は嫌いなので、食べることはおろか、匂いを嗅ぐこともしたくない。
examples.english: I hate natto, so I don't want to smell it, let alone eat it.

examples.japanese: 彼は敬語はおろか、簡単な日本語さえできない。
examples.english: He can't even speak simple Japanese, let alone honorifics.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分の会社はおろか住んでいる家まで失ってしまった。
examples.english: He even lost the house he lived in, not to mention his company.

examples.japanese: 事故で怪我をして、歩くのはおろか立つことすらできない。
examples.english: I was injured in an accident and can't even stand, let alone walk.

examples.japanese: 私の国の経済は不景気で、正社員はおろかアルバイトすら見つからない。
examples.english: The economy of my country is in recession, and I can't even find a part-time job, let alone a full-time one.

meaning: with the exception of; excepting ~
structure: Noun + はさておき

examples.japanese: この本、内容はさておき、タイトルはすごくいいと思う。
examples.english: As for this book, content aside, I think the title is very good.

examples.japanese: 彼女の料理は見た目はさておき、味はとても美味しいよ。
examples.english: Setting aside the appearance, her food tastes very good.

examples.japanese: 冗談はさておき、この件についての解決方法を考えましょう。
examples.english: Joking aside, let's think of a solution to this matter.

examples.japanese: 難しい話はさておき、今日は食事を楽しみましょう。
examples.english: Difficult stories aside, let's enjoy our meal today.

examples.japanese: この話はさておき、教科書の80ページを見てください。
examples.english: Moving on, please look at page 80 in the textbook.

examples.japanese: 新しいスマホはデザインはさておき、素晴らしい機能が充実している。
examples.english: Aside from the design, the new smartphone has a lot of great features.

pattern: はそっちのけで / をそっちのけで
meaning: without doing something
structure: Noun +（は / を） + そっちのけで

examples.japanese: 彼は勉強そっちのけで遊んでばかりいた。
examples.english: He doesn't study at all, he just plays around.

examples.japanese: 私の同僚は仕事をそっちのけでスマホ触ってばかりだ。
examples.english: My co-workers don't focus on work and are constantly touching their phones.

examples.japanese: 妻は家事そっちのけで猫と遊んでいる。
examples.english: My wife is playing with the cat instead of doing household chores.

examples.japanese: 生徒たちは先生の注意をそっちのけでおしゃべりに夢中だ。
examples.english: The students ignored the teacher's warnings and were caught up in their conversations.

examples.japanese: 大学4年生の弟は就職はそっちのけで、毎日パソコンゲームに没頭している。
examples.english: My younger brother is a fourth year university student who instead of searching for a job, is absorbed in computer games every day.

examples.japanese: 彼女は本業をそっちのけで副業に精を出している。
examples.english: She is devoting herself to her side business, leaving her main business behind.

meaning: no sooner than; as soon as ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + やや否や

examples.japanese: 先生が教室に入るや否や、学生たちはおしゃべりを辞めた。
examples.english: As soon as the teacher entered the classroom, the students stopped talking.

examples.japanese: 友達の赤ん坊が私の顔を見るや否や、泣き出した。
examples.english: As soon as my friend's baby saw my face, it started crying.

examples.japanese: 彼女が現れるや否や、大勢のファンが取り巻いた。
examples.english: As soon as she appeared, many fans surrounded her.

examples.japanese: 社長は部屋に入るや否や、静かになりました。
examples.english: As soon as the boss entered the room, it suddenly got quiet.

examples.japanese: 彼は電車を降りるや否や走り出したがどうやら乗り換えの電車に間に合わなかったようだ。
examples.english: He ran as soon as he got off the train for his transfer, but it doesn't look like he made his transfer in time..

examples.japanese: あの子どもは、それを口に入れるや、吐き出した。
examples.english: That child vomited the instant they put that in their mouth.

meaning: completely; absolutely; totally; (not) at all​ ~
structure: Verb (ます stem) ます + やしない

examples.japanese: 最近、息子は私の言うことなど、聞きやしない。
examples.english: Recently, my son doesn't listen to anything I say.

examples.japanese: うちの会社は日曜日なのに休みやしない。
examples.english: Our company doesn't take a day off even though it's Sunday.

examples.japanese: 大学時代に恋愛に夢中で勉強やしなかった。それでも卒業出来て良かったと今も思うよ。
examples.english: When I was in college, I was absorbed in love and didn't study. I'm glad I still was able to graduate.

examples.japanese: あの研修生は全くの役立たずだ。コーヒーの作りも知りやしない。
examples.english: That trainee is completely useless. They don't even know how to make coffee.

examples.japanese: 僕は病気があるからこんな強い酒を飲めやしない。
examples.english: I have a sickness, so I can't drink such a strong drink.

examples.japanese: 俺は結婚しているからあんなところに行きやしない。
examples.english: I'm married so I definitely won't go to that kind of place.

meaning: and; and the like; and so forth ~
structure: やれ + Noun + だ(の) + やれ + Noun + だ(の) + と | sentence + sentence

examples.japanese: やれ出張だの、やれ会議だのと、ゆっくりする暇もない。
examples.english: With business trips and meetings, I don't have any time to relax.

examples.japanese: 日本で部屋を借りる場合、やれ敷金だやれ礼金だと、いろいろなお金がかかる。
examples.english: When renting a room in Japan, it costs a lot of money from the security deposit to key money and other various fees.

examples.japanese: 日本でのやれ地震だ、やれ台風だと心配事が多い。
examples.english: There are many worries like typhoons and earthquakes in Japan.

examples.japanese: 彼女は最近やれ剣道だ、やれ茶道だとお忙しそうだ。
examples.english: She seems to be busy with Kendo and Tea Ceremony club lately.

examples.japanese: 妻はやれ仕事だのやれ家事だのとやったから、自分の時間があまりない。
examples.english: Between working and doing housework, my wife doesn't have much time for herself.

examples.japanese: 息子はやれハンバーガーだやれピザだと、健康に良くないものばかりを食べたい。
examples.english: My son only wants to eat foods that are bad for his health, like hamburgers and pizzas.

meaning: no matter; whether; even if [A] or [B]
structure: Verb (volitional) + がと（も） | Noun + だろう/であろう | な-adjective + だろう/であろう | い-adjective い + かろう

examples.japanese: 君が何歳であろうが関係ない。仕事が出来ればいい。
examples.english: As long as you can do the job, it doesn't matter how old you are.

examples.japanese: 誰と結婚しようが、私の勝手でしょ。
examples.english: Who I marry is my choice.

examples.japanese: あなたがどんなに謝ろうとも、今回は許しません。
examples.english: No matter how much you apologize, I'm not going to forgive you this time.

examples.japanese: このマンションはどんなに騒ごうとも、外からは何も聞こえません。
examples.english: No matter how loud you are in this apartment, you can't hear anything from outside.

examples.japanese: 必要だから、どんなに高かろうがこれを買わないといけません。
examples.english: It's necessary, so I will buy it no matter how high the price may be.

examples.japanese: 僕が何をしようが勝手だ。あなたに言う必要はない。
examples.english: Whatever I do is my choice and none of your business.

pattern: ようによっては / ようでは
meaning: in accordance with; depending on; whether or not ~
structure: Verb ます (stem form) + ようによってはようでは

examples.japanese: この絵は見ようによっては男性にも見えるし、女性にも見えます。
examples.english: Depending on how you look at this picture, it looks like a man or a woman.

examples.japanese: やりようによっては、その仕事は簡単に済ませることができる。
examples.english: That job can be done easily depending on how you do it.

examples.japanese: 見ようでは善にも悪にもなる。
examples.english: Depending on the way you look, there are good things and bad things.

examples.japanese: ここから目的地まで、道の混みようによっては１時間かかる場合もある。
examples.english: It may take an hour from here to the destination depending on how busy the road is.

examples.japanese: どんな道具も使いようによっては便利にも危険にもなります。
examples.english: Regardless of the tool, depending on how it is used can be useful or dangerous.

examples.japanese: 相手が強豪チームだとしても、やりようによっては勝てないわけではない。
examples.english: Even if the opponent is a strong team, it does not mean that you cannot win depending on how you do it.

meaning: there is a limit to what is acceptable; to go too far
structure: Verb(volitional / dictionary) + にも + Verb(ない potential) or(ない form)

examples.japanese: 風が強すぎて走ろうにも走れない。
examples.english: The wind was so strong that even if I tried to run, I couldn't.

examples.japanese: 結婚しようにも相手がいない。
examples.english: Even if I wanted to get married, I don't have someone to marry.

examples.japanese: 天ぷらを作るにも作り方がわからない。
examples.english: I want to make tempura, but don't know how to make it.

examples.japanese: 時間がないので友達と遊びに行こうにも行けない。
examples.english: Because I don't have time, even if I want to go out with my friends, I can't.

examples.japanese: 最終電車が行ってしまって、タクシーに乗ろうにもお金が足りない。
examples.english: The last train is gone and even if I wanted to take a taxi, I don't have enough money.

examples.japanese: 日本語の漢字は複雑すぎて、覚えようにも覚えられない。
examples.english: The kanji in Japanese is too complicated, I couldn't remember it even if I wanted to.

meaning: partly because; also because of; plus the reason for ~
structure: Verb (casual) + （が）ゆえ（に）（が）ゆえの | Noun + (である) | な-adjective + (である) | い-adjective

examples.japanese: 貧しさゆえに、彼は盗みを動いた。
examples.english: As a consequence of his poverty, he ended up stealing.

examples.japanese: 彼は性格がおかしいゆえに友達ができなかった。
examples.english: He couldn't make friends because of his strange personality.

examples.japanese: 悪天候ゆえに旅行は延期された。
examples.english: The trip was postponed due to bad weather.

examples.japanese: 日本語を知らなかったがゆえに誤解された。
examples.english: I was misunderstood because I didn't know Japanese.

examples.japanese: 女性であるがゆえに差別されることがある。
examples.english: You may be discriminated against because you are a woman.

examples.japanese: 彼が交通規則を守らなかったがゆえに、事故が起きてしまった。
examples.english: The accident happened because he didn't follow the traffic rules.

meaning: ending particle; indicates assertion
structure: Phrase | ぞ / ぜ

examples.japanese: がんばるぞ！
examples.english: I will do my best!

examples.japanese: さあ, 始めるぞ！
examples.english: Here goes!

examples.japanese: 一緒に勉強するぞ。
examples.english: Let's study together!

examples.japanese: 遅れてるぞ。
examples.english: You are too slow.

examples.japanese: 彼に逆らうと後悔するぞ。
examples.english: You'll regret it if you cross him.

examples.japanese: 止まらないと撃つぞ。
examples.english: If you don't stop, I'll shoot!

pattern: ずにはおかない / ないではおかない
meaning: must; will definitely; can’t help but to ~
structure: Verb (ない form) + で + はおかない | Verb ない (ない stem) + ずに | ※ する -> せずに

examples.japanese: やられたらやり返せずにはおかない。
examples.english: You must fight back if you are defeated.

examples.japanese: 帰りが遅くなってしまった。父に叱られないではおかない。
examples.english: I returned home late. I will definitely be scolded by father.

examples.japanese: 彼女の演技は見る人を感動させずにはおかない。
examples.english: Her performance move the audience without fail.

examples.japanese: 指名手配犯を目撃したのだから、警察に通報せずにはおかない。
examples.english: Since I witnessed a wanted criminal, I must report it to the police.

examples.japanese: 彼女の美しさは多くの男性を虜にさせずにはおかない。
examples.english: Her beauty cannot help captivating many men.

examples.japanese: この曲は聞く人の心を揺さぶらないではおかない。
examples.english: This song can't help but shake the hearts of listeners.

meaning: ended up not doing ~
structure: Verb ない (ない stem) + ずとも | Exception : しない -> せず

examples.japanese: 勉強せずとも誰でも満点取れるくらい簡単だった。
examples.english: It was so easy that anyone could get a perfect score even without studying.

examples.japanese: 現金を使わずとも、クレジットカードで決済できる。
examples.english: You can pay with a credit card without using cash.

examples.japanese: 無理して変わろうとせずとも、私は今のあなたが好きです。
examples.english: You don't have to force yourself to change, I like you the way you are.

examples.japanese: 出勤せずとも、この仕事は家にパソコンがあれば問題ないです。
examples.english: Even if you don't go to work, this job can be done from home with a computer.

examples.japanese: 彼があなたのことを好きだということは、言わずともわかる。
examples.english: Even without him saying so, it is obvious that he is in love with you.

examples.japanese: 今の時代は帰省せずともビデオ通話で両親の顔が見れるようになった。
examples.english: Nowadays, you can see your parents' faces by video call without going home.
